BJP state president Jai Ram Thakur said the party is giving special emphasis to youth power and to tap it, a special programme has been framed that would be monitored by a seven-member team, comprising president of BJP Yuva Morcha Rakesh Jamwal, Anurag Thakur, Govind Thakur, Randheer Sharma, Vikram Singh, Himanshu and Ramita Rahi.

"Conclaves would be attended by all big leaders of the party. The party is also preparing for the December 30 Vijay Sankalp Rally to be held by Prime Ministerial candidate, L.K. Advani," he said.

Heading: HSGPC puts off move to take over gurdwaras - Indian Express
Content:
Moving ahead with his ambitious plan to make Himachal Pradesh a carbon neutral state, Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal has convened a day-long session with top experts, NGOs, representatives of the industry and government officials here on October 16.

The session, which has on its agenda three contentious issues — effect of climate change, assessing carbon footprints (impact of human activities on environment) and opportunities in earning carbon credits.

The Department of Environment and Scientific Technologies has already prepared a draft policy on climate changes, identifying forests, hydro-power projects, industry, transport, renewable energy and waste management as key areas for carbon credits.

At least a dozen hydel projects, including World Bank-funded 1,500-MW Nathpa-Jhakri and three industrial units in Himachal Pradesh have already been registered with United Nations Framework Convention on Climate (UNFCC) for getting carbon credit benefit.

"The Chief Minister is very keen to see that Himachal, being a state with rich biodiversity and forests and less environmental pollution, takes a lead in the country to become a carbon-neutral state.

This session will help the government to step up the efforts to assess carbon footprints and implement clean development mechanism (CDM) projects involving all stake holders," said Dr Nagin Nanda, Director, Environment and Scientific Technologies.

Explaining the concept of carbon footprints, Nanda said, "By carbon footprints we mean assessing the impact of human activity on the environment in terms of amount of greenhouse gases produced. It's measured in units of carbon dioxide. The impact, whether individual or collective, contributes to global warming. The climate policy, which is under formulation, will address these issues."

Supplementing the efforts, the forest department on October 17 also proposes to hold a workshop on the issue of payment for environment cost (PEC) — a concept which some countries such as Costa Rica have already implemented. "Those who protect the forests and sacrifice their rights should get the cost for doing so," asserts Avay Shukla, Additional Chief Secretary (Forests), who was a member of the government delegation to Costa Rica recently.

According to Shukla, the forest department proposes to take up a pilot project on the issue in the vicinity of Shimla and create an innovative model to be subsequently adopted elsewhere in the state. Already, the government has taken a decision to utilise 10 per cent of the catchment area treatment (CAT) plan funds on this concept.

Nearly Rs 200 crore of compensatory afforestation management and planning authority (CAMPA ) is already lying un-utilised with the Centre. However, Himachal still claims to have nearly Rs 80 crore CAT plan fund for taking up afforestation works along the catchment sides of hydel projects.

Heading: State increases amount of marriage advance to Rs 1 lakh - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana Sikh Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (HSGPC) has postponed till November 20 its move to take over charge of gurdwaras in the state from October 8. However, the HSGPC has warned that if by then no decision on their demand for a separate SGPC for Haryana is taken by the Haryana government and the Centre, they would resort to an agitation again.

The move has come as a big relief to both the Haryana and the Punjab governments, as the takeover threat could have sparked off tension in both states. Talking to The Indian Express, Jagdish Singh Jhinda, president of HSGPC, said SGPC general secretary Prem Singh Chandumajra and Dr Daljit Singh Cheema, advisor to Punjab Chief Minister Parkash

Singh Badal, met them today, requesting them to sort out the matter through talks.

"We have decided to postpone the takeover of gurdwaras in Haryana, provided talks on the issue between SGPC members from Punjab and Haryana begin by November 10 and some concrete solution is reached by November 20,'' said Jhinda.

The HSGPC had given a one-month ultimatum to the Haryana government and the Centre on September 7 at its rally in Karnal to create a separate SGPC for Haryana, warning that otherwise they would take control of gurdwaras in the state.

Welcoming the postponement of the HSGPC move to take over control of gurdwaras in Haryana, SGPC president Avtar Singh Makkar said it has come as a big relief to everyone. "I welcome the move. We can sit and talk in a cordial atmosphere now,'' said Makkar, when contacted.

Didar Singh Nalvi, general secretary of the HSGPC, said talks were welcome, but the two sides must arrive at some conclusion by November 20 or else tension could brew again.

Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda said confrontation never solved any problem, but peaceful talks could. "The Haryana government has already constituted a committee headed by Agriculture Minister H.S. Chatha to seek the opinion of Sikhs of Haryana regarding formation of a separate SGPC for the state. The report of the committee is still awaited. Any decision in this regard will be taken on the basis of the aspirations of the Sikhs of Haryana,'' said Hooda.

Heading: State govt eyes big investments - Indian Express
Content:
A marriage advance of Rs 1 lakh instead of Rs 60,000 will be given to the state government employees, said Birender Singh, Haryana Finance Minister, today. The advance would be recovered in 100 monthly installments and recovery would start with effect from second issue of pay after the advance was drawn. The second or third marriage advance would be granted to government employee as per his admissibility under each category separately. The second or third marriage advance would be granted as per his admissibility under each category separately.

The marriage advance would be admissible to regular class-I, II, III and IV state government employees/officers. He said that the marriage advance would now be limited up to Rs 1 lakh or 15 month's basic pay of the employee whichever was less. In case of dependent sister's marriage advance, the employees would have to furnish an affidavit to the effect that the sister for whose marriage advance is being obtained is wholly dependent upon the employee and financial condition of the parents is such that they cannot perform the marriage themselves, said Birender Singh.

The names of other siblings of the employees, along with their respective departments should also be mentioned in the affidavit. The application for marriage advance, complete in all respect, should be sent to the Finance Department two months before the date of marriage.

Heading: CBI to investigate poaching case against shooting champ Manavjit Sandhu - Indian Express
Content:
With 260 IEMs in hand, govt trying to attract investment of over 4,000 cr

With 260 industrial entrepreneur memoranda (IEMs) in hand, the Haryana government is eyeing to attract an investment of over Rs 4,000 crore. It is for the first time that under the present Bhupinder Singh Hooda government such a large number of IEMs have been signed, overtaking the previous high of 208 IEMs in 1995. Out of this, the government has envisaged investment of Rs 150 crore from 59 non-resident Indians (NRIs).

All these NRIS have already been allotted plots in the state. The government is also expecting equal amount of investment from a leading textiles manufacturer that plans to set up a cement grinding plant at Panipat. "This has been possible due to consistent efforts by the government to provide better infrastructure and congenial atmosphere to

investors," said a

senior official.

Sources in the government said the Aditya Birla Group is also setting up a cement grinding unit at a cost of Rs 115 crore at Panipat. The Adani Group of Industries plans to invest Rs 150 crore to set up an inland container depot at Palwal. Besides, the government has offers for foreign direct investment from various big industrialists, including Rs 1,000 crore by Maruti Suzuki Vendors, Rs 650 crore by Suzuki Diesel Plant, Rs 250 crore by YKK Expansion, Rs 125 crore by S. Diagnostic Centre, Rs 115 crore by NTN and Rs 65 crore by Samsung.

The government has been successfully implementing the IEMs, though in many cases IEMs fail to materialise into actual investment. However, the state has still ranked first in the country in the implementation of IEMs, with a percentage of 54 as compared to the all-India average of 37 per cent.

The infrastructure projects are likely to have two to three times more investment as compared to that of industrial sector in the next decade. A National Institute of Food Technology Entrepreneurship and Management would be set up at Kundli with an investment of Rs 350 crore. A National Automotive Testing and Research Infrastructure Project would also be set up at Manesar with an investment of Rs 400 crore. The Central Institute of Plastic Engineering and Technology has started partial functioning in a rented building at Panipat. The setting up of the institute involved an investment of Rs 23 crore.

With all this in its basket, the Hooda government is aiming to give a major boost to industrial investment in the state. "We are hopeful of further improving our implementation graph of IEMs. Majority of the proposals are already under process and many of them have actually taken off in various parts of the state," said a senior official.

Heading: U-turn by school: ‘We did not ask rape victim to stay away from class’ - Indian Express
Content:
After his unsuccessful run at the Beijing Olympics, world trap shooting champion and 2007 Khel Ratna awardee Manavjit Singh Sandhu now faces another setback. Almost a year after a Chandigarh Forest Department inquiry report found him guilty of poaching, the CBI has accepted the case for investigation.

"The matter has been re-examined by the CBI. It has now been decided to take up the investigation of the case on the request of the Chandigarh Administration," states a letter from the Economic Offences Wing (Vigilance) of the CBI to the Chandigarh Secretary (Environment and Forests). Dated September 17, 2008, the letter adds that a formal complaint giving complete details of the case may be sent to the CBI's New Delhi office at the earliest.

Manavjit, now 31, and his father Gurbir Singh Sandhu, a former international trap shooter, were found guilty of killing Schedule I and Schedule III wildlife animals in a preliminary report submitted to the Chandigarh Forest Secretary by inquiry officer (Wildlife Warden) in 2007.

The inquiry report had recommended that there is enough evidence to establish a prima facie case of wildlife poaching under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, against Manavjit and Gurbir.

Also, it had suggested that since the alleged poaching had taken place outside the jurisdiction of Chandigarh and had inter-state ramifications, the investigation should be handed over to an appropriate state or central agency for a fair and speedy trial.

Following CBI's refusal to take up the case in May, the case was sent to the Chandigarh Police, which too had declined to take up the investigation. The Chandigarh Administration resent the case to the CBI Director directly in August to which CBI has finally given its nod.

In October 2006, during a raid at a flat of then Punjab MLA and arms dealer Arvind Khanna in Chandigarh (the flat had been let out by Khanna to Gurbir), the CBI had stumbled upon evidence of poached wildlife articles and nearly 150 photographs which reportedly show Manav and his father posing with arms and the kill. Sources said the photographs show poaching in different parts of the country, mainly in the south, of Schedule I wildlife animals such as leopard, black buck and bison besides Schedule III wildlife animals such as wild boars.

The all-India ban on hunting was imposed in 1991-92 and any hunting since then can be undertaken only on special permit for killing either wild animals declared vermin or man-eaters. According to this, any picture of Manav with the kills must date to before the shooter was 16.

Heading: Don’t ask students to repeat classes, CBSE to schools - Indian Express
Content:
A day after the 17-year-old girl, who was allegedly gangraped in Panchkula on September 16, said she was not allowed to attend classes after the incident, school authorities have denied the allegation.

In a complete u-turn, principal of Chaman Lal DAV Senior Secondary School, Sector 11, Panchkula, Anjali Marriya said: "We never asked the girl not to attend classes. Although, the girl was suspended for a week for bunking classes that ended on September 22. After that, she was free to attend classes but failed to turn up."

She has missed the half-yearly examinations but can join school once the exams end, added Marriya.

The victim reiterated her claim. "I was abused and insulted in the assembly by my teachers and told not to enter the classroom. I was asked to come for the final exams. Now, my brothers, who study in Class IX and KG in the same school, are asked all sorts of embarrassing questions," she said.

Meanwhile, a local NGO — Jeevan Mukt Nishulk Vidyalya — has come forward to help the girl. President of the NGO, Mansa Ram Ahuja, said: "The child has been wronged. At a time when they should support the victim, the school is shying away from its responsibilities. We will ensure that she gets justice and that her life is not spoilt simply because a school has denied her the right to education."

Heading: Again, stereos stolen from cars in one night - Indian Express
Content:
Taking a serious note of schools asking Class IX and XI students to repeat the classes, the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has issued notices to the heads of affiliated institutions. In a circular dated September 1, the Board directed schools to stop the practice and create a healthy environment for its students.

The notification reads: "The CBSE has received feedback about certain schools where the authorities forcibly hold back students in Classes IX and XI on various pretexts. The Board requires all heads of institutions to reflect on the long term objectives of imparting holistic education in schools."

The move has been welcomed by teachers. Asked about the practice, Dr Rakesh Sachdeva, principal of DAV Model School, Sector 15, said: "If the child is found to be lagging behind during the half-yearly examinations, we counsel and encourage her to study more, instead of forcing her to drop a year. The Board has taken a step in the right direction as it will help save one year for the child."

Neerja Jain, a teacher at Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 16, said: "Taking an exam is the right of every student and the school authorities do not have any business preventing a child from doing so. Educational institutions should realise their responsibility and in their selfish bid to better their results, not spoil a child's future." The notice further directs schools to address the problem of rising indiscipline among the youth with the help of programmes like the Adolescence Education Programme, Life Skills Programme and the Comprehensive School Health Programme, advocated by the Board.

Heading: Rural students get a feel of modern India - Indian Express
Content:
Stereos from as many as ten cars were stolen from houses in Sector 4 in Panchkula in the early hours of Monday morning. After Sector 2 and 16, this is the third such case where stereos were stolen from a number of cars within a night.

"Around 2.30 in the night, the siren of my car went off. I went out to check and saw my car intact but a taxi moving around in the area. I called up the police control room but no one answered it. I called up again and told them about the taxi. However, no police officer turned up," said one Om Prakash, a resident of the sector. It was in the morning that the thefts came to light, he added.

Another resident on condition of anonymity, said: "In all the cars, the glass pane had been opened and the stereos taken away. Despite being the third such episode in the city, the police have failed to prevent such crimes."

Talking to Newsline, Ajab Singh, Station House Officer of Sector-5 police station said: "After receiving the call, our constable did go to the spot to check if there was any taxi roaming about in the area but he failed to locate any suspicious vehicle. A case has been registered and the matter is being investigated." Sandeep Khirwar, Panchkula Superintendent of Police also visited the spot on Monday.

Heading: An amusement park in Sector 17 will lead to chaos: former mayor - Indian Express
Content:
Students from Gidderbaha taken on educational tour of Technology Park

Over 150 students from government schools in rural areas of Gidderbaha constituency in Punjab were taken on an educational tour to the campuses of Dell Computers in Mohali and Infosys Technologies in Chandigarh Technology Park on Monday.

The tour, which was organised by Punjab Finance Minister Manpreet Singh Badal (MLA from Gidderbaha), saw students between classes VIII and XII who had secured over 70 per cent marks in their last annual examinations. Also, accompanying them were their teachers.

"It is a way to teach children of what is happening in modern India. These kids are from economically backward families but they are ambitious and extremely talented. I am sure that this tour will not only be informative but will also spur them to achieve excellence," said Rishipal Singh, SDM Gidderbaha, who was accompanying the contingent.

In fact, the three-day-long tour, which started yesterday, also featured visits to the Vidhan Sabha, Punjab Tractors Factory, Sukhna Lake and the Fun City amusement park.

The students said they have learnt a lot. Parminder, a class VIII student, said: "I was always confused when people talked about call centers. How could some one sit in India and give directions to an American? I have a clear understanding after visiting the Dell office now."

Manpreet said that he was going to organise a similar tour for the students of his constituency to the Indian Military Academy next month. "You have to give the right encouragement. The fact that these kids have excelled in board examinations despite coming from unprivileged backgrounds shows their grit. Exposures like these will give them a better perspective of their goals and encourage those who have scored lesser marks this year, to score higher and be part of this trip next year."

Heading: WORDZMUN ’08: Simulating the UN Assembly - Indian Express
Content:
The proposed amusement park to come up in Sector 17 continues to invite the ire of a section of councillors in the Municipal Corporation as well as architects.

The councillors said that setting up of an amusement park in the area will lead to chaos.

The amusement park is to come up near the proposed site for an eleven-storey building envisioned by Le Corbusier.

Former chief architect of the city M N Sharma said that the amusement park should not be set up in the area.

"The site is not suitable for setting up an amusement park. The projects in the city are being set up without giving adequate thought. The proposal should be reconsidered," he opined.

Objections were raised in the House Meeting held recently.

Former Mayor Harjinder Kaur said that the project has been passed without keeping in mind the views of the majority.

She said: "It was finalised in an arbitrary manner in the meeting of the Finance and Contract committee. The objections that we raised in the House were dismissed. Having an amusement park in the middle of a busy commercial area will definitely lead to chaos."

She adds: "An amusement park could be set up in the southern sectors which have more space. These areas are completely neglected. There is no place where the residents can go to."

Another councillor said that with hundreds of people likely to visit the amusement park it will add to the traffic chaos.

The parking is inadequate and multi-level parking will require some time to come up. There will be no space to park vehicles.

Mayor Pardeep Chhabra, meanwhile, said that the objections being raised are uncalled for.

"We are coming up with four new parking lots. This will take care of the parking woes. The development of southern sectors is also been taken care of," he says.

Heading: ‘Responsibility comes from within’ - Indian Express
Content:
A three-day conference on social and economic issues starts at CII

Wordzmu '08, a three-day conference on social and economic issues, was inaugurated at the CII on Monday.

More than 200 students from different schools all over the country have come to participate in the event, which is organised every year by WORDZ Debating Society.

The inaugural function of WORDZ was held at St Stephen's School. Union Minister of State for finance Pawan Kumar Bansal was the chief guest on the occasion.

On the first day of the conference, students from states like Haryana, Punjab and far-flung areas including Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, brainstormed to find solutions to prevailing international problems.

The students will talk about subjects like prevention of outer space arms race, nuclear waste management to strengthening of women and children rights and unrest in Darfur.

Explaining the concept of WORDZ, Atin Batra, Secretary General of the WORDZ, said: "It is like a mock UN Assembly where countries are represented by the participants. The agenda is covered over three committees namely General Assembly, Security Council and Economic and Social Council. We will focus on problems that concern the entire world and not limited to a particular community or country."

The event provides a big platform to students to put forth their views in front of a large crowd.

"It is a good opportunity to sharpen one's public speaking skills. Apart from this, WORDZ also provides students exposure regarding the debating expression. In today's time, it is very essential that students command good power of expression," said Ashmita, Vice-President of WORDZ.

Heading: YPS mountaineering team conquers Shatidhar peak - Indian Express
Content:
Much has been talked about reducing the age limit for drinking from 25 to 21 years. If the youngsters have hailed this proposal, the elders have criticised it with their plea being that age reduction would make the youth more wayward.

I think the entire idea is only a hogwash the government is indulging in. Take a look around and you can find several under-age people consuming alcohol. Be it parties, social functions or any other occasion, "alcohol" has become an expression of celebration for the young. And if there is a feeling that they start drinking only after acquiring the legal age, I am sorry to say it is a misconception.

With social drinking becoming a norm with the "Generation Y", it is difficult to keep a tab on their habits by imposing an age bar. Most of the bars and pubs do not even check the age of their customers.

People argue that the age bar needs to be maintained as by 25, one is wise enough to know what is right or wrong and if they are given unchecked freedom, they will misuse it. The sense of responsibility comes from within and age has nothing to do with it. A 27-year-old man can be as irresponsible as a 20-year-old youth.

Unruly behaviour is human tendency. I agree that alcohol triggers the impulse, but, again it too is not age-bound. One needs to exercise restrain on oneself. Following or not following the age limit is a personal choice; what matters at the end is after drinking, how well behaved and sober we can be.

Heading: PCR vehicles missing from duty, cop tries to ‘hush it up’ - Indian Express
Content:
Twelve students from Yadvindra Public School, Patiala, scaled the Shatidhar peak (17,200 feet) in the Pirpanjal Range of Himachal Pradesh in a school excursion from September 27 to October 4.

The team was led by Anmol Nohria, a student of Class XI, and trainer Dalip Singh Shekhawat.

According to school officials, this is the first time that a school from Punjab has successfully completed the rare feat.

"The team was originally bound for the adjacent Friendship Peak (17,350 feet) but had to abandon the plan due to heavy snowfall. On their instructor's advice, they decided to scale the equally formidable Shatidhar peak," said principal Vinod Kumar Stanley.

The group left for Manali on September 27 and proceeded to Bakarthatch (30 km from Manali) the next day.

"We set up our base camp here (a height of 11,200 feet) and underwent three-day training for acclimatisation. Also, we participated in activities like hill walk, rappelling and rock climbing. We reached our destination the next day," said Shekhawat.

Noria said the ascent was exhausting.

"Our stamina seemed to crumble with the increasing altitude but none of us gave up. We were told that ours was the first team in the last two months to conquer the peak, after eight other senior and experienced groups had failed," he added.

Heading: Teachers protest non-payment of salary for six months - Indian Express
Content:
When the city is expected to be on high alert after the recent serial bomb blasts in the country, the Station House Officer (SHO), Sector 39, is alleged to have compromised with the area's security.

SHO Rajesh Shukla allegedly did not report about the four Police Control Room (PCR) vehicles missing on the night of September 28 and hushed up the matter.

The matter was recorded in the Daily Diary Report (DDR) in Sector 39 police station on the intervening night of September 28 and 29 for the PCR vehicles — Sugar 26, Romeo 23, Romeo 24 and Romeo 28.

"The SHO was supposed to inform his senior officers about the PCR vehicles and personnel absent from the duties but he settled the matter for obvious reasons. Thus, he is also liable to be punished for the misdeed," said police officers.

Sources said SHO Rajesh Shukla was reviewing the security in the area of the police station on the intervening night of September 28 and 29 but did not find four of the PCR vehicles at their scheduled points. He searched for them but could not locate them. He returned to his police station and recorded the incident in his DDR immediately.

"He was supposed to inform about the security lapse to his superiors the very next morning. Meanwhile, the personnel of the PCR vehicles, which were found missing from the scheduled spots, approached the SHO and urged him to hush up the matter. The SHO, in a closed room meeting, decided not to apprise the senior authorities about the lapse and hushed up the matter," sources said.

Officials said the matter is of grave concern and such lapse cannot be tolerated.

SHO Rajesh Shukla said he was not aware whether he had sent the report to his seniors or not and that he would be able to speak on the matter only after going through the records.

SSP S S Srivastava said he would look into the matter before making any comment.

Heading: Two killed in separate road accidents - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab private-aided schoolteachers are up in arms against non-payment of their salaries for the past six months, rendering them starving.

To express their anguish against the government apathy, the entire teaching staff of the private-aided schools in Mohali district on Saturday skipped work by availing themselves of a mass leave, the president and general secretary of their Mohali district union Narinder Nindi and Jagdish Singh, respectively, said here on Monday.

In a joint statement, the teachers' union leaders accused the ruling SAD-BJP combine of "backtracking" from their pre-poll promise made for the welfare of the private-aided schoolteachers in the state.

The protesting schoolteachers gathered at Khalsa Senior Secondary School in Kharar, where they held a massive demonstration against the state government.

The union leaders, including SN Verma, Avtar Singh Gill, Kuldeep Singh, Ravinder Kaur and Shruti Kant, rued that instead of fulfilling the pre-poll promises of lifting ban on new recruitments, 5 per cent interim relief and increase in medical allowance, the state government has pushed the aided schoolteachers to starvation without giving them pay for the past 6 months.

Heading: Letters from Corbusier: Memoirs suggest architect was victim of red tapism - Indian Express
Content: Two persons, including a beggar, died in separate road accidents at Kudda Kalan village and Ambala Cantonment on Monday. Rachna Ram (48) from Safera village was run over by a speeding bus at the Khudda Kalan bus stand. The police have registered a case against the bus driver. In another hit-and-run case, a car ran over a beggar killing him on the spot. Though the driver fled the spot, a case has been registered by the police.

Heading: Le Corbusier’s ‘experiment’ Chandigarh gets a centre to its creator, his dreams - Indian Express
Content:
Le Corbusier might have been the favoured choice of many for designing the city, but it appears this was not enough to save him from the clutches of red-tapism. A number of letters of Corbusier, on display in the Le Corbusier Centre, Sector 19, narrate the tale of the bureaucratic rigmarole that he had to go through on different issues.

In a letter dated December 15, 1960, addressed to the then Chief Minister of Punjab Pratap Singh Kairon, Corbusier states, "My drawings for Chandigarh Museum of Knowledge are made since two years. I ask you urgently, dear sir, to kindly admit that my research was not a superficial one."

On display is another letter from Kairon to the officials demanding an explanation. In another letter he says, "No decision has been taken for the renewal of my contract. The personal damage will not be considered by me, still it can be bad for the development of the city."

Corbusier also had to face the problem of delayed payments. He raised objections on the dismissal of two officials who were working on the Capitol Project, without him being informed. The letter for the same was addressed to the then Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru dated June 7, 1958.

A couple of letters also suggest that his selection of certain members to the Chandigarh Capital Project Control Board was not acceptable.

About working on the Capitol Project, he writes, "I have spent hours of anger, indignation and discouragement on the site of HC and Secretariat, not being able to give my orders myself. I had to transmit them to the Sub-Engineer who transmitted them to higher authority. The effects of these orders were not appreciable till fifteen days later. Therefore a problem of organisation has to be faced."

Corbusier also talks of the 11-storey building which was proposed to be set up in Sector 17. In a letter from Paris on February 3, 1959, Corbusier wrote, "I have been suggested a compromise! I will not accept it!"

He continues, "Our scheme implies the definitive foundation for an eleven storey structure; the scheme also implies the financing per customary and ordinary practice of the building of the eight other storeys, so as to reach from now on the definitive level which is a conspicuous part of the skyline of the capital. The enclosed document predicts failure should we persist in wanting to realise the eleven storeys in one operation."

Heading: Panel to develop infrastructure in Industrial Area - Indian Express
Content:
chandigarh is the biggest example in India of experimental architecture. It hits you on the head and makes you think. You squirm at the impact, but it has made you think and imbibe new ideas.

This is what late Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru had said about Chandigarh in a speech on March 17, 1959. The excerpt now stands framed inside the Le Corbusier Centre in Sector 19. The Centre was inaugurated on Monday to commemorate the 121st birth anniversary of the creator of the city. The centre has been opened in the work place of Corbusier and his associates.

In nine rooms, the centre showcases works of Corbusier and Pierre Jeanneret from 1952 to 1965. Documents pertaining to the creation of the city, original masterplan, paintings, sketches, models as well as archival records, are on display. The centre has a digital library where students can conduct research.

An exhibition titled 'A Dream Realised — An Architectural Overview of Ideas that Became Cities' is also on. It has been organised by the Embassy of Switzerland in India, Arts Council of Switzerland and Saakaar Foundation. The exhibition depicts life and work of Corbusier and Jeanneret.

While inaugurating the centre, Punjab Governor and UT Administrator General S F Rodrigues (Retd) said there is a need to conduct a research-based structural study by experts to throw light on the original concept and vision conceived by Le Corbusier to undertake the challenging job. He ordered for the constitution of a multi-disciplinary team of eminent experts for this project and emphasised that the endeavour must focus on establishing linkages of the conceptualisation of the city, the old civilisation of Harappa and the Indus Valley and its relevance to futuristic needs.

The Administrator was accompanied by Home Secretary Ram Niwas, Secretary to Governor MP Singh, Finance Secretary Sanjay Kumar and Director Tourism Vivek Attray.

V N Singh, the Nodal Officer of the Research Center, while explaining the objective of the center said it has three sections comprising museum and display gallery, research and publication and administration. The projects and components are: conservation of the old architects' office in the manner of an authentic resource that can be used for disseminating information about the experimental aim of modern architecture of Chandigarh.

UT Chief Engineer S K Jaitley slipped and fell down during the inauguration of the Centre. While he stayed for the inauguration, he had to be hospitalised later.

Heading: Realty developers woo with freebies this festive season - Indian Express
Content:
UT Administration General SF Rodrigues (Retd) constituted a committee on Monday comprising UT Home Secretary, Finance Secretary and representatives of Confederation of Indian Industries (CII), PHDCC and other industrial organisations for the development of infrastructure in the Industrial Area.

The committee will suggest a roadmap to strengthen support structure for the economic growth of the Industrial Area. The committee was constituted during the public hearing session held at the Secretariat.

Rodrigues also emphasised on the need to make provision for a permanent exhibition ground in the Industrial Area, which would be made a part of Industrial Area Development Strategy.

Expressing concern over encroachment on government land, General Rodrigues asked the Home Secretary and the Deputy Commissioner to review the functioning of the committee of the task force assigned with the job of removing encroachments followed with corrective steps wherever necessary.

Rodrigues asked the officials to follow the law and the decisions of the courts from time to time and take appropriate action for removal of encroachments. He also directed officers to remove encroachment on Timber Market and shift furniture business to an appropriate place.

Responding to the various individual grievances and problems of people in the public hearing session, General Rodrigues asked the officers to streamline the functioning in their respective departments so that the common man's problems are solved on the spot. "Help the people within rules and facilitate them to lead a life of dignity and respect. We should always adopt a positive approach for the common good," Rodrigues said.

As part of the programme to empower physically challenged people, General Rodrigues asked the Finance Secretary to chalk out a plan to give them booths or sites to enable them earn their livelihood.

Heading: With the flow - Indian Express
Content:
With the festive season on, real estate developers are leaving no stone unturned in attracting buyers with freebies and discounts.

Now expanding the horizon and trying out innovative ideas to lure the buyers, real estate developers have geared up this festive season by offering cash discounts, add-ons like four wheelers, two wheelers, consumer goods, waiver of interest rates on the period of construction and improving the specifications of the products like from marble flooring to vitrified tiles and many more.

"We are offering cash discounts between Rs 25,000 and Rs 30,000 for the flats. Besides, we are also providing improved facilities in the specifications. For instance, from marble flooring we have upgraded to vitrified tiles," said Rajit Kakkar, Managing Director Silver City, Dera Bassi. The price range of the apartments in this project is from Rs 18 lakh to 27 lakh.

Some of the developers have come up with add-ons instead of cash discounts. These add-ons vary from four wheelers, two wheelers to consumer goods like television, refrigerator, air-conditioner and other electronic products.

These freebies are either offered to all or through a draw of lots. The developers feel that the buyers are more attracted towards these items rather than cash discounts.

"The buyers will be offered add-ons like cars and scoters, this festive season. Thinking different and to stand out we are not offering cash discounts," said a sales official of Paras Built-tech Pvt Ltd.

Keeping the high cost of houses acting as a deterrent for sales, the developers have also come up with ideas to cut the cost by waiving off the interest on the construction period.

"The combination of consumer goods with waiving off the interests, the developers are attempting to bring some momentum in the market. It is though surprising that despite the high rates, they are forced to come up with these discounts," said Regional Director JLL Meghraj, Manoj Kashyap.

Whereas, due to the already shrinking profit margins there are some developers, who are holding on to their prices, hoping that the festivals, considered an auspicious time for purchase, will revive the market.

"We are not offering any discount in cash or kind to the buyers hoping to have good sale in the coming months," said one of the builders.

Heading: Celeb watch - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Redressal Forum has directed IFFCO-TOKIO General Insurance Company, Sector 28-A, Chandigarh, to pay Rs 2 lakh as compensation to Raj Rani, a resident of village Kamomajra Khurd.

The company has also been directed to pay litigation costs of Rs 5,500 to the complainant within 30 days from the date of receipt of the copy of the order, failing which, they would be liable to pay the same with an added interest at the rate of 12 per cent per annum.

The complainant's son, Rajesh Kumar Sharma, had purchased a TATA Indica car from one Manjit Singh, which was duly insured with the insurance company. The owner of the car was entitled to get Rs 2 lakh in case of accidental death.

It is averred that when Rajesh was going from Barara to Paunta Sahib in the above said car, three unidentified persons shot him to death.

The police registered a case and later recovered the body of Rajesh Kumar Sharma, which was sent for postmortem to the Indira Gandhi Medical College, Shimla. The accused were also arrested and the vehicle was recovered from Saharanpur.

A notice of the police complaint was sent to the insurance company, which refused to pay the claim. The claim was also repudiated on the ground that Rajesh Kumar Sharma had been murdered and, therefore, the claim is beyond the purview of the insurance policy.

The Forum held that the claim has been wrongly repudiated and therefore directed the company to pay the said compensation.

Heading: Let’s talk about - Indian Express
Content:
I Spy

The world's favourite spy, James Bond is back in action, and this time, he'll hit Indian territories first. James Bond's Quantum of Solace, people, will be seeing an India release first followed by the US. Come November 7, and Bond's 22nd film will fire up screens across the country while the US market will get to see it only on November 14. Says Kercy Daruwala, Managing Director, Sony Pictures Releasing, "We are delighted to have such a huge franchise in our line-up. James Bond has a huge equity in this country and Bond films have always been a hit here. November 7 will see the biggest roll out for any Hollywood film in India as we would like to give our audiences the thrill of seeing "Quantum of Solace" even before US does. Our endeavour is to make it the biggest, best Bond film ever."

A historic move, Sony Pictures will bring the charming and suave secret service agent Daniel Craig as James Bond with all his cars, gadgets, guns, gals, high octane adventures and his license to kill. Quantum of Solace is a sequel to 2006's Bond flick Casino Royale, which was based on Ian Fleming's novel. The film is directed by German-Swiss film maker, Marc Forster. It also stars Olga Kurylenko, Gemma Arterton, Dame Judi Dench, Jeffrey Wright and Giancarlo Giannini. This time the adventure goes behind his Casino Royale's lady love, Vesper and unearths the organization that blackmailed her. On a mission that leads him to Austria, Italy and South America, Bond in a minefield of treachery, murder and deceit, allies with old friends in a battle to uncover the truth.
