Heading: Dalit attacked for defying garba ‘norms’ - Indian Express
Content:
Village garbas still out of bounds for downtrodden

Even as the state government has gone out of its way to welcome the rest of the world into the folds of garba, Dalit women in many villages across rural Gujarat are not allowed to join in the festive dance.

"Like everyone, we too feel like doing the garba, but then we are never allowed," said Savita Rohit, a Dalit woman from Sunalpura village under Khambhat taluka of Anand district. "They simply throw us out if we try to get in there," she added.

Not only that, during the nine days of Navratri, the Dalits in the village are also denied milk, as the Bharwad community, that is largely in the milk business, avoids coming in contact with the Dalits during this 'auspicious' period. "We know it is wrong, but then nobody has ever complained about this ever. Why should we put our neck on the line?" Savita said.

Pushpa Solanki from Khorsam village at Chanasma block of Patan district, said: "On Thursday, a middle-aged lady asked about my caste when I went for garba. On learning that I am a Dalit, she asked me to leave the place saying that I have no right to participate in garba. Later, she physically dragged me out of the ring."

Nimisha Parmar from the adjoining Chanasma village has a slightly better story to tell. "They do allow us to dance in the village garba, but on the eighth night of Navratri, garba is held at the village Ramji Temple, where Dalits are denied entry," she said.

Pushpa Vahnia from Memka village under Wadhwan taluka of Surendranagar said they have their own separate garba at Dalitvaas, as they are barred at the village garba.

"Our women are thrown out and have to stand at a distance and watch the garba," said Pravin Vahnia from the same village.

Amrut Sendhav, a Patan-based Dalit rights activist said that such incidents are quite common in rural Gujarat, but people are too scared to voice their protests.

"Things perpetuate to this extent because most of the Dalits are landless labourers and work in the farms of upper caste people, who also help them financially during need. To say anything against the moneyed upper castes means jeopardising the minimal livelihood options for these people," Sendhav added.

Harji Bala, a Dalit Panchayat member from Targara village said that the situation is the same across Saurashtra.

Eminent sociologist Gaurang Jani called it an extension of religious discrimination. Unlike the cities, Navratri in villages is more religious in nature. As in most villages Dalits are denied entry in the temples, they are similarly denied entry in the village garba as well. "Not only garba, comparatively new festivals too are showing such discriminatory tendencies. In the Ganapati festival, which is rather new in rural Gujarat, a Dalit child will not be allowed to sit in the truck taking Ganapati for Visarjan," Jani said.

He added: "Those who sponsor garba in the villages are usually from the higher castes and naturally, they want to have the event all for their own people. Further, while the youth are allowed to mix freely during garba, intermingling with Dalit children may lead to possible inter-caste marriages, which too is not acceptable to people. They therefore, prefer to have Dalits at bay."

Babu Koli, sarpanch of Targara village under Botad Block of Bhavnagar district denied the charge. He said there is no such discrimination during Navratri. "Dalits have been organising their own garba separately and the practice has been going on for years," Koli added.

Convener of the SC/ST Cell of the BJP Atmaram Parmar also denied that there is any caste-based discrimination at Navratri.

Heading: Another Godhra carnage accused falls ill in custody - Indian Express
Content:
The youth was probably used by an upper caste group to implicate another

Ramesh Parmar had been to a village garba under Therada taluka of Patan district to light a lamp on Sunday evening. Instead, he ended up in a Patan hospital with a stab injury on his head.

The matter is not as simple as it seems. Dalits are not usually allowed to participate in village garbas, and Ramesh is paying the price for trying of defy the norm.

What makes it all the more intriguing is the fact that Ramesh was taken to the venue by a Thakore community group to settle scores with another, say the police.

"This is a simple case of rivalry between two Thakore groups, one of whom used this man as a pawn to implicate the other," said Sub-Inspector AG Ghasura.

"The idea was simple: take a Dalit to the village garba, there will be some trouble and then the protesters can be implicated in a case of atrocity," he added.

An FIR has been lodged in the case and the accused are absconding.

Heading: Six-yr-old raped, murdered - Indian Express
Content:
Yaad Mohammad admitted to jail dispensary with typhoid

Yet another arrested under the Prevention of Terrorism Act (POTA) in the Godhra train burning incident has been admitted to the Sabarmati Jail Dispensary, according to the family members of the accused.

Yaad Mohammed Shafi Mohammed Charkha (64), was arrested on February 27, 2002. "He was picked up five hours after the incident that day," said Hussain Yaad Mohammed, his son. A resident of Godhra locality, Charkha has been suffering from typhoid since last week.

Hussain said his father was moved to the dispensary on October 1 after he started vomiting. It was then that doctors found that he had typhoid, he added. Meanwhile, the bail application was rejected by the Gujarat High Court on October 3. "Our advocate had filed the application on September 12 as my father's health was deteriorating since the beginning of 2006," Hussain said.

Charkha's advocate, Ibrahim Saiyyad added that under Section 268 of POTA, only critical cases can be treated in hospitals outside the jail premises. "The provisions are such that one has to wait for the person to get to that critical stage to be shifted to a hospital," said Saiyyad.

On October 7, Hussain will file another bail application for his father. He said, "I am scared after [Mohammed] Dhobi's death, as I know it will take ages before the judgment finally comes."

Charkha had a flourishing leather business in the Polan Bazaar area of Godhra, but the train burning incident brought misfortune to his family. "Our mother has passed away and our father is in jail. Each of us four brothers visit him regularly in Ahmedabad," said Hussain.

Heading: No special sops, says Industries Dept - Indian Express
Content:
In a shocking incident, a six-year-old girl was raped and murdered by unidentified person(s) on the Sabarmati riverbed, just behind the Gaekwad Haveli Police Station, on Monday morning. The girl had gone missing from her hut in the Raikhad slums late on Monday night. Gaekwad Haveli police have registered a case of rape and murder against unidentified person(s) and begun investigations to nab the accused.

Gaekwad Haveli Inspector G H Khan said: "The girl went to bed around 9 pm. Her mother found her missing around 2 am, following which, she and the other family members began looking for her and even lodged a missing complaint with the police. The body of the girl was discovered around 7 in the morning."

Khan said the body of the girl bore multiple injury marks on her head, throat and eyes. "It seems that the rapist killed her to conceal his identity. The exact cause of death would be known only after the post-mortem report. As of now, it seems to be the handiwork of only one person. We'll get the full picture once we get the FSL report," he said.

The police have launched a manhunt for the suspects in the nearby slums. Batulbibi belongs to Banaras in Uttar Pradesh. She has been living in the Raikhad slums along with her parents and children ever since her husband abandoned her five years ago. The deceased is the youngest of her three kids. Her relatives told Newsline they believed it to be the handiwork of one of the slumdwellers.

Heading: Nano to bring cheer to Rajkot’s auto parts manufacturers - Indian Express
Content:
The state Industries Department has ruled out offering "special incentives" to Tata Motors if the automobile giant decides to set up shop in the state, it has been learnt; this despite the buzz in the corridors of the Sachivalaya over the Nano's entry into Gujarat.

A senior official said on Monday that successive governments in Gujarat have provided some "special sops" to mega industrial projects to attract a sizeable investment in the state in the recent past. "But, the incentive/subsidy regime has almost come to end with the concept of liberalisation and globalisation being accepted everywhere," he said.

"There may be reports of the government considering offering a huge chunk of land belonging to the Anand Agriculture University near a village in Sanand taluka in case the Tatas decides to set up their Nano car project there. But, the land in question cannot be given in a charity to any corporate house for commercial activity," he added.

When his attention was drawn to the fact that Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka were promising special sops, including free-of-cost land to Tata for setting up the Nano plant there, he said: "This is nothing but an unhealthy competition by such states to woo the Tatas. We will set a wrong precedent by giving special incentives to the auto giant for relocating its Nano project from Singur to Gujarat. If our government tries to sweeten its offers to Tata Motors, other industrial houses in Gujarat may also start claiming such incentives from the government. It will certainly prove a dangerous proposition especially when the biennial Vibrant Gujarat Global Investors' Summit is due mid-Janaury next year."

Even with speculations rife that the Tatas may make an announcement on the entry of Nano into Gujarat on Tuesday when Chief Minister Narendra Modi completes his seven years in office, senior government officials as well as ministers concerned, continue to remain tight-lipped over the issue.

Principal Secretary (Industries) Gauri Kumar said: I don't know anything about the Tatas' plan to set up their Nano project in Gujarat." Minister of State for Industries Saurabh Patel and Chief Secretary D Rajagopalan were unavailable for comments as they were busy in meetings throughout the day.

Heading: Exposed: A hidden water war that we are losing against MNCs - Indian Express
Content:
The destination could either be Ahmedabad or Bhuj, but when Tata sets up its manufacturing unit for the Nano in Gujarat, it will be Rajkot that will have all the reasons to cheer. The hub of the automobile parts manufacturing industry, Rajkot is now looking for a big boost in anticipation of Tata setting up shop here.

Rajkot has developed as a hub for the auto parts ancillary units and supplies parts to leading manufacturers like Tata, Mahindra and Mahindra, Mitsubishi and General Motors. There are 100 such units in Rajkot GIDC estate at Metoda with an annual turnover of Rs 1,500 crore. Of these, the supply to Tata comes to Rs 200 crore per annum, and supports around 50 units in a major way.

Kishor Kadvani, the owner of Kadvani Forging and president of Metoda GIDC said: "We expect the auto parts manufacturing industry of Rajkot to grow by over 30 per cent if the Nano comes to Gujarat."

He said at present, the parts manufactured in Rajkot are supplied to Khadagpur. "If the plant is set up within Gujarat, not only will the transportation cost go down, we will also get a 2 per cent Central Sales Tax relief. These two things will help Rajkot supply parts at lower rates compared to Ludhiana, Pune and Delhi manufacturers."

The fact that ancillary suppliers like A V Tech and Sona Toya, which will purchase parts from Rajkot to manufacture components for Nano, will also give a bigger boost to the industry here.

Unlike other auto parts hubs at Pune and Delhi, Rajkot has been functioning in isolation. "Cities like Pune and Coimbatore enjoy advantages of automobile giants being right at their doorstep. Contrary to that, Rajkot is located in a bit remote area and the auto companies have to take pains to reach here. The industry in Rajkot has been growing despite this disadvantage," said Hitesh Bagdai, president of the Rajkot Chambers of Commerce and Industry.

He said: "It's not a surprise that Tata's entry into Gujarat will encourage other auto giants to come here too. It will boost the growth of local auto parts manufacturing industry both in terms of business and creation of job opportunities."

Known for its engineering skills, Rajkot was earlier known as the hub for diesel engines and lathe machines. But in recent times, the city has made its presence felt in the automobile sector. The number of units manufacturing auto parts has increased from just five in 2002 to 150 now. With automobile giants like Tata Motors, Bajaj, General Motors, Ford, Mahindra and Mahindra and Mitsubishi procuring components from Rajkot, the industry has been growing at the rate of 25 per cent per annum. From a 100-crore business in 2000, auto-parts industry in Rajkot today has a turn over of over Rs 1,500-crore.

Heading: Congress MP Virji Thummar held for breach of election code - Indian Express
Content:
For those who take pride in rising privatisation and commercialisation of the Indian water sector, Alex Thomson, a research scholar from M S University (MSU) Economics Department has a significant study of Plachimada village in Kerala state, to share.

Thomson volunteered to protest against the overexploitation of ground water in Plachimada between 2000 and 2005 by Hindustan Coca–Cola Beverages Private Limited (HCBPL). Now he is in his final stages of submitting his thesis 'Commercialisation of water: A study on developmental issue and ecological concerns.'

He told Newsline: "There are two kinds of compensation, which a company can provide. One is the cost price, which is basically what a company can give to its employees as well as shell out for the raw materials being used. The second is an external cost, which might also have a negative impact on environment and the ecology of the area. This cost is not payable and can have a negative impact. The reason: it may also affect generations of people living in the area where an MNC has come up."

Plachimada, which was dominated by the tribals, had HCBPL consuming around 5 lakh litres of ground water daily. People argued that the MNC was contaminating water by 13 to 15 lakh litres from 16 bore wells daily, said Thomson who also volunteered to survey this area with Dr P R Sreemadevan Pillai, the author of the book, The Saga of Plachimada.

He said several uncommon diseases started emerging in Plachimada whose ground water had rich cadmium, chromium, manganese and sulphide more than the prescribed norms and regulations. There were reports of people being affected by diseases like hair fall to even asthma, he said. He added that HBPCL finally closed down its production in Plachimada in 2005 due to rising protests.

Thomson said his study is divided into three parts: Plachimada before the MNC came up, the impact and the situation after the closure.

"While, I have already submitted the first two parts of my thesis, I am studying the last chapter which shows a positive response of the people after the closure of the MNC," said Thomson. He added that the foremost question, however, remains is whether water is an economic good or a free good? "Who are the real custodians of nature's life blood? Who will protect water resources? If water is privatised who will buy it for Ecology?" he added.

Heading: Oil’s not well: State Cong leaders rush to Delhi to thrash out oil ban issue - Indian Express
Content:
Congress MP Virji Thummar was arrested here on Monday in connection with a case pertaining to violation of the code of conduct during the Gujarat assembly elections, police said.

Thummar had allegedly made some personal remarks against Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi and other BJP leaders during the campaigning for the assembly elections held in Gujarat in December 2007, the police said. A case was filed against him by elections officials at that time, police said. Thummar was later released by the court on bail, they added.

Heading: Consumer Forum orders insurance companies to pay claims to kin of dead policy holder - Indian Express
Content:
Matter to be discussed with PM, Sharad Pawar

State Congress leaders have rushed to New Delhi to join Union Agriculture Minister Sharad Pawar, to discuss the ban on export of edible oil, with Prime Minister Manmohan Singh. The ban has kept all the 24 marketing yards in Saurashtra closed for the sixth consecutive day and local Congress leaders have been under tremendous pressure to take up the issue with the UPA government.

The ban has come into effect from March 18 to cap the spiralling prices of edible oil and oil seeds. For the Saurashtra region, which has an annual average groundnut crop yield of nearly 15 lakh metric tonnes, it means settling for a lesser amount for the oil in the domestic market. For over 500 groundnut oil mills, it means the end of overseas business. With the kharif season about to begin, farmers and millers now want the ban to go soon.

Feeling the heat from farmers and millers to get the ban lifted, state leaders like MP Virji Thumur, who represents the Amreli constituency – a groundnut bowl for Saurashtra – is now leading the team with co-operative sector leader and Dhoraji-Jamkandorna Congress MLA Vithal Radadia.

"We want to represent the problems farmers and millers have been facing because of the ban," said Thumar. The MP and MLA are also roping in Union Textile Minister Shakersinh Vaghela and Union Minister of State for Railways Naran Rathwa to support them.

According to the local leaders, Pawar and the Prime Minister are scheduled to discuss the matter on Wednesday and they want to represent the case of Gujarat farmers and millers at the meeting. The delegation has got a charter of demands from the Bharatiya Kishan Sangh to be discussed in the meeting. The BKS, which has called for an indefinite strike, also wants to increase the minimum support price of Rs 400 for groundnut while removing the embargo on exports.

Heading: Coming soon: An abode where butterflies will breed naturally - Indian Express
Content:
The Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has ordered New India Assurance Company Ltd (NIAC) and two other firms to pay Rs three lakh with interest at the rate of nine per cent to a complainant, Dinesh M Kathrani, holding the respondents guilty of deficiency in service and negligence.

The petitioner, Consumer Education and Research Society (CERS), had sued NIAC as well as Vex Marketing Services and Vinal Insurance Benefit Pvt Ltd for negligence and deficiency in service, both individually and collectively. The Forum admitted the complaint and ordered the insurers to also pay Rs 5,000 towards the costs.

Dinesh Kathrani's brother Bharat had taken a Janta Personal Accident Insurance policy for 15 years from NIAC on January 29, 1999 and paid a premium of Rs 44,072. According to the policy, the nominee in the policy would receive Rs three lakh if Bharat dies in an accident.

Bharat had met with an accident on July 4, 2001 and died on July 15. Dinesh had filed a claim with the insurer along with copies of the First Information Report (FIR), panchnama, post-mortem report, inquest panchnama, death certificate, etc.

Dinesh stated before the Forum that neither did the insurers process the claim nor did they reject it. Several of his letters evoked no response. NIAC responded only after a personal visit by Dinesh and gave him a letter rejecting his claim. The letter explained that the policy floated by the insurer had been discontinued from May 1, 1999 and this had been advertised in national and regional newspapers. Dinesh was told he was not eligible to receive any amount from the policy, which was not in force when Bharat had died.

Dinesh complained that such a unilateral discontinuation of the policy was illegal, unreasonable and showed the insurer's deficiency in service and negligence. He drew the Forum's attention to Clause 5 of the policy relating to discontinuation of the policy and the procedure to be followed for it. The clause required the insurer to issue individual notice and refund the premium to the policyholder. The insurers had not done this, which implied that the policy continued till date.

The Forum passed a verdict in favour of Dinesh and said that the insurers had neither objected to the claim being made and the required papers being in order nor presented any proof challenging the sanctity or facts of the claim.

Heading: Trucks collide on NH-8; kill 8, injure 8 - Indian Express
Content:
A butterfly park will soon come up in the south Gujarat region to promote research and breeding of the exotic creatures. The park will be set up by the Gujarat Ecological Education and Research (GEER) foundation, Gandhinagar, an autonomous body under the state government's Ministry of Forests and Environment.

"The main purpose of this park is to provide a congenial environment for the butterflies to breed naturally. Though the project is still in the initial stages, but it will be completed soon," Director of GEER foundation C N Pandey said.

"We will be introducing different species of butterflies and study their breeding pattern and the environment necessary for it. Most of the breeding will be natural, but for some species of butterflies we will have to create a special environment," he said.

"This will also create a good research opportunity for scientists who want to study the breeding pattern of different exotic species of butterflies," Pandey added.

He said that the data collected during research will be further used to improve the ecological conditions required for natural breeding of butterflies and various patters emerging from it.

However, he did not divulge the exact time where and when the park will be operational, but said that it will completed soon.

Geer foundation was set up by the state government in 1982 for the promotion of ecological education and research, creating public awareness, sensitizing people about environment and carrying out ecology related studies.

India's first butterfly park was established at the Bannerghatta Biological Park, Bangalore, in 2006, which is spread across 7.5 acres of land. It comprises a butterfly conservatory, museum and an audio-visual room.

The butterfly conservatory has a polycarbonate roof and is a 10,000 sq.ft. circular enclosure, inside which the living environment has been carefully designed to support over 20 species of butterflies.

The environment has a tropical setting complete with the humid climate, an artificial waterfall and host plants and shrubs that attract butterflies.

The park also encompasses a butterfly rearing house, plant rearing house and host plant garden.

Heading: KPT scam: CBI keeps close watch on Customs officials - Indian Express
Content:
Eight people were killed and eight others were injured in a a major road accident on National Highway No 8 near Limdi in Surendranagar district on Monday morning when a rashly driven truck hit another truck while trying to overtake. Three women and four minors are among the injured. All the injured have been shifted to the Government Hospital in Limdi. One of them is reportedly in a critical condition.

The deceased have been identified as Dahyabhai Rathva (50), Dariyaben Rathva (30), Bhavesh Rathva (2), Savitaben Rathva (50), Chanchalben Rathva (45), Mukesh Rathva (4), Suresh Rathva (9) and Sandip Rathva (7)—all residents of Kavli village in Jambusar taluka of Bharuch district. The police said all the deceased and injured belong to Bharuch district and were going for labour work to Upleta town of Rajkot district.

According to the Joravarnagar police, the incident happened on the highway in the outskirts of Vadod village around 5.30 am. Following the accident, one of the trucks fell off the road while the other hit the road-divider and turned turtle on the other side of the highway.

Sub-Inspector H M Vala who is investigating the case said that the drivers and cleaners of both the trucks have escaped and efforts are on to nab them.

Heading: NABARD develops cold feet over disbursing micro-credit - Indian Express
Content:
The scam had resulted in a loss of several crores to the Centre and the Central Warehousing Corporation

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is keeping a close watch on some senior officials in the Customs Department, Gujarat, who are suspected to be involved in the Container Freight Station (CFS) scam at Kandla Port.

The scam had resulted in a loss of several crores to the Central Government and the Central Warehousing Corporation at Kandla.

The CBI has already filed a case of corruption and cheating against five people, including four senior officials of the Kandla Port Trust (KPT) in this connection. The agency said on Monday that some Customs officials of Gujarat Zone are suspected to be involved in the scam. "We are probing the role of some senior Customs officials in Gujarat zone," said a CBI official.

On Friday, the agency had filed a case of corruption against four KPT officials — former chairman of KPT A Janardan Rao, and department heads — Krishnan, R Revenkar and A Gadhkari. The quartet was accused of allegedly misusing their official position to facilitate the Jamnagar-based private firm, Seabird Marine Service Ltd., establish a CFS at Kandla in 2005.

The CBI elaborated that the said CFS was a violation of the agreement reached between KPT and CWC, according to which KPT will have to stop any competitor of CWC from establishing a CFS at Kandla.

CBI officials further said that the CFS was established after procuring a No Objection Certificate (NoC) from the Customs Department, Gujarat.

"It is being investigated whether the Customs officials who issued the NoC to the Union Ministry of Commerce, were aware of the agreement between KPT and CWC," a CBI source said.

Heading: Game is Booked - Indian Express
Content:
India Post was all set to expand the project, but due to the pending resolution of the credit risk rating, the plan has been put on hold for the time being

The National Bank for Agricultural and Rural Development (NABARD) has developed cold feet over the disbursal of micro credit to Self Help Groups (SHGs) as planned earlier, in Gujarat and seven other states including the North East, through the post-office network. The hitch, it is learnt, is over the sharing of exposure to credit risk.

India Post has already disbursed Rs 1.35 crore among 165 SHGs in five districts of Tamil Nadu on a pilot basis and no default was reported. India Post was all set to expand the project, but pending resolution of the credit risk sharing, the plan has now been put on hold at least for the time being.

The other states where the project was to be implemented are Bihar, Karnataka, Orissa, Madhya Pradesh, Kerala, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh.

Postmasters have been specially trained in nurturing SHGs and making inspections. A simple interest of 9 per cent is charged on the loans out of which India Post gets a share of 3 per cent, with the remaining 6 per cent going to NABARD.

The scheme helps the Postal Department in cross-selling its financial and insurance services to the SHG members, thus strengthening their financial and life security besides underlining the continuing relevance of rural post offices and their close interaction with the public.

If implemented on a full scale, the scheme will reinforce their relationship with the rural people. Post offices in the country have already disbursed about Rs 2,900 crore as wages to beneficiaries of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (NREGS) through around 15 million accounts in nearly 70,000 post offices.

D K S Chauhan, postmaster general (business development, technology and marketing), Gujarat, has opined that the joint venture will focus mainly on rural customers who are in need of loans but are unable to approach the banks. Chauhan said that in Gujarat, the postmasters were imparted training to handle the SHGs' applicants.

Murlidhar Rao, General Manager at NABARD said that things will take a concrete shape once the issue of risk sharing is resolved. He said banks were not very keen in credit disbursal with NABARD because they thought it was a costly proposition. There are 88,000 SHGs in Gujarat and post offices are going to be an attractive destination for credit expansion to them, he said.

Heading: Beautifully Simple - Indian Express
Content:
His life resembles the reels of Chak De! India, but former India hockey coach Mir Ranjan Negi now reveals it all in a book

When Kabir Khan's motley team of girls won the imaginary World Championships in Chak De! India, there was a collective sigh of relief in the cinemas. But for one viewer, Mir Ranjan Negi, it was as though a moment of his life was blown up on the screen. Negi did not share Kabir Khan's sexy bearded looks, but somewhere the pain matched. "Shah Rukh Khan acted exceptionally well, but I had actually lived out those sentiments," says Negi.

There have been endless discussions on whether or not Negi's life inspired the blockbuster, but this time he has decided to do the talking.

The 50-year-old former goalkeeper and coach is ready with his autobiography, From Gloom to Glory (Popular Prakshan). The origin of gloom is in the 1982 Asian Games. Negi was the goalkeeper of the Indian hockey team which was badgered 1-7 by Pakistan. The country wept — and then fumed against Negi for conceding the goals. Almost ostracised, Negi slunk away — but not quite.

He redeemed his destiny 16 years later — when the men's hockey team he coached won the gold in the 1998 Bangkok Asian Games. Four years later, the women's team trained by him won the gold at the Commonwealth Games.

"I have no complaints about hockey. It gave me the worst days of my life but it also made me redeem my fate," says Negi, going on to reminisce the two moments of agony and ecstasy.

"I feel I could have done things differently. For instance, while stepping on the field for the match against Pakistan in 1982, froth was spilling from my mouth. I shouldn't have played that day. Also, I had chances of slyly injuring the main Pakistani player, but hesitated. This might have cost us the game. I did not speak much after our loss against Pakistan since I was stopped by the hockey federation," says Negi, "I felt vindicated only when the men's hockey team won the gold at Bangkok."

From Gloom to Glory comprises a series of anecdotes and Negi's diary entries after the 1982 games, but the book doesn't begin there. It starts with a personal loss — the death of his eldest son Abhi in a motorcycle accident three years ago. And then he goes on to his brief Bollywood days when he became associated with the making of Chak De! India.

"I was offered the project of Chak De! days after my son's demise. I was in a dilemma whether to accept the offer or not. But after a little convincing I accepted it," says Negi, who had finished the book well before Chak De! India happened. The draft was later tweaked to include the experience of working on the film. He writes: "Chak De! turned my life on its head. From relative anonymity I came under the arc lights."

Negi has hung up the boots though he put on the dancing shoes for a while for a season of Jhalak Dikhla Ja. The distress has returned, though, after watching the Olympics where India did not even qualify. "I wish glamour would come back to hockey, something like Twenty20."

Heading: Back in Business - Indian Express
Content:
'Beautiful Inside' -- a painting exhibition by Arpita Bhavsar and Riddhi Shilpi -- surely puts up the beauty of nature and life at its simplest best. Nature and life have been inspirational to many an artists and so has also been the case with Arpita and Riddhi, but it's the way nature and life expresses itself in their paintings that call for art lovers' attention. While the lily has become Arpita's muse, Riddhi is completely in love with the art of the Warli tribe.

Arpita's canvases have become playgrounds for the lilies, which appear to be interacting with 'nature' in their own way. While you see leaves cuddling in a group, you also find branches romancing the flowers 'silently'. Whether it's midnight or rains or a foggy day, the flowers seem to express their moods accordingly. "Before starting the lily series, I spent a good time exploring nature and its beauty. It carries hardness and softness together. So, I feel that it is very much like our life itself -- full of happiness as well as sadness," said Arpita, a passout of Sheth C N Arts Colleges. In her paintings in acrylic, she uses the bamboo sticks and branches to symbolise rudeness, harshness in human life.

From nature to man living in harmony with nature -- the Warli tribe. Says Riddhi, "This is simplest tribe and yet so expressive. Though it is a two-dimensional art, but it expresses all their activities in simple, symbolic forms. Their life revolves around nature. The only thing is that I have tried to make it more colourful." Although Riddhi is an interior designer, she took to painting out of sheer passion. She was honoured with the Young Artist Award for best painting during her undergraduation and was also awarded the Jalaram Timber Trophy for Best Design by the Sophia Polytechnic, Mumbai.

The exhibition is on at Beyond Exhibition Gallery, Abhishilp (Vastrapur) from 4 pm to 7 pm till October 8.

Heading: Chatterati - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister led from the front, had Advani's blessings

What West Bengal lost has now turned out to be Gujarat's gain. But before bagging the prestigious Nano car project from Tata Motors, the Gujarat government under Chief Minister Narendra Modi had adopted a two-pronged "backdoor" strategy.

Since the day Ratan Tata announced his decision to withdraw the Nano car project from Singur, Modi and his team of "chosen" bureaucrats swung into action.

All through, the negotiations Modi and his team of senior bureaucrats had with Tata Motors executives and its chairman were kept under wraps; so much so that many of Modi's ministerial colleagues and officials in various departments concerned were not aware of the ongoings. Even the media had a tough time digging out information on a day-to-day basis about the development.

The "deal" was kept a closely-guarded secret till Monday night when Tata officials informed the Chief Minister's Office (CMO) about the final decision taken at the Tata Motors' Board of Directors meeting at Mumbai that night, sources said. A proposal sent to the CMO was later approved at the Cabinet meeting on Tuesday morning.

It was sometime in mid-September that Tata Motors Managing Director Ravi Kant was reported to have made a secret visit to Modi's official bungalow in Gandhinagar, where the first round of talks on the Nano project took place. Later, the CM began talking to Ratan Tata directly over the phone at regular intervals, convincing the auto czar about how the state government was ready to extend full support to the company to set up its small car project in the state.

Sources in the CMO said that Modi established a direct rapport with Ratan Tata by constantly talking to him over the phone.

Elsewhere, he appointed two of his trusted bureaucrats – newly appointed Chief Secretary D Rajagopalan and Principal Secretary to the CM K Kailasnathan – to hold regular negotiations with senior Tata Motors executives including Ravi Kant.

Apparently, Modi had entrusted the job of negotiating the deal with the Tatas to Rajagopalan when he was still heading the state Finance Department, much before he was elevated to the coveted post of Chief Secretary in place of Manjula Subramaniam, who retired on September 30.

Being credited for successfully handling the three consecutive Gujarat Vibrant summits, Rajagopalan had been in constant touch with Ravi Kant and other senior Tata Motors executives. He arranged the visits of the Tata teams to identify various sites in Gujarat – Savli and Padra in Vadodara district, Mehsana and Prantij in north Gujarat, Halol in Panchmahals and Mundra in Kutch.

Besides, Modi reportedly also roped in his political mentor and NDA's Prime Ministerial candidate L K Advani, urging the latter to throw his weight behind the government's efforts to bring the Nano project to Gujarat.

Sources in the state BJP said Advani personally called up Ratan Tata and persuaded him to set up the project in "investment-friendly" Gujarat.

A senior BJP functionary told Newsline that Advani himself started evincing a keen interest in the small car project since the day he learnt that Tata Motors had zeroed in on the Sanand site near Ahmedabad to relocate the project from Singur. Significantly, the Sanand Assembly segment falls under Advani's Gandhinagar Parliamentary constituency after the delimitation.

Soon after the Tata team zeroed in on the Sanand site, Modi brought in his Principal Secretary Kailasnathan on the scene. Since both

Rajagopalan and Kailasnathan originally hail from south India, they started keeping a close tab on every move the two southern states of Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka had initiated to woo the Tatas to set up the project in their respective states.

Both the Gujarat cadre IAS officers successfully used their contacts in the bureaucracy of these two states to apprise Modi of the day-to-day developments on the issue. In fact, Rajagopalan was in constant touch with his counterparts in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, said a senior official.

As Modi relied heavily on these two senior officials, Principal Secretary (Industries) Gauri Kumar was asked to handle the lower rung Tata officials, whenever they visited Gujarat in connection with the Nano project.

Despite the best of incentives offered by Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, the main factors that are believed to have weighed in favour of Gujarat are political stability, good infrastructure and industrial peace in the state.

Since the Assembly polls are due in Andhra Pradesh next year, the Tata think tank was not sure which party would come to power there, and what would be the fate of the project if it is relocated there.

In the case of Karnataka, barring the areas in and around Bangalore and Mysore, no other place in has proper infrastructure or logistics in place, sources in the CMO said.

Moreover, Modi has offered to provide all necessary infrastructure to the Tata Motors at Sanand for its car project and also the ancillary units.

Although Modi did not promise tax incentives and land at concessional rates to the Tatas, his assurance to the auto company to dole out indirect benefits by way of providing infrastructure convinced the automobile giant to set up the project at Sanand.

Sources said the estimated cost of the land purchased by the Tatas to set up shop at Sanand is put between Rs 300 crore and 400 crore. The government has, however, asked Tata Motors to make a staggered payment towards the land cost.

Heading: Industrialists arrested for protesting against VAT hike   - Indian Express
Content:
Talking of Michelangelo

Ashish Balram Nagpal loves to nurture the link between Bollywood and art, which is why the after party to celebrate the opening of artist Gagan Vij at the JW Marriott (Mumbai) had more actors than artists present at the do. Vij was seen explaining his sculptures, one of the works were brought to the venue for the benefit of the guest, to Dino Morea and Manoj Bajpayee were captive listeners while posing for the shutter-bugs. Jackie Shroff made an elaborate entry spiffily dressed in a denim shirt with formal coat and trousers to top off the look. Expectedly, Shroff drew more attention than the art works. Also spotted at the do were Sushant Singh, Kapil Sharma, Yuvraj Parashar and Rajendra Rathod who insisted on wearing jodhpurs to the party-sans horse, but chic nonetheless.

Bummer Can we have more of the art please? The show at The Courtyard needs more visitors ASAP.

Heading: Mayawati’s ‘poor’ politics annoy Opposition, confuse her men - Indian Express
Content:
Over sixty members of Indian Industries Association (IIA) were arrested on Monday. They were holding a demonstration against the hike in VAT rate in the state. The police released the industrialists after three hours.

"UP must be the first state where industrialists are arrested," said D S Verma, Executive Director IIA. 

"The industrial associations have been putting forward their demands in a peaceful manner. But seeing no response by the government after so many days, we had to resort to a public demonstration," he added.

Demanding parity in VAT with the neighbouring states, the industrialists had planned to take out a two-kilometer car rally in the city. The rally was supposed to end at Patel Park where the industrialists had to observe a dharna. The IIA members had also planned to hand over a memorandum of their demands to the chief minister. "We wanted to request the CM to withdraw the hike on VAT and to reduce the entry tax as it obstructs the industrial growth of the state," said Verma.

Over 250 cars had gathered in front of the Moti Mahal Lawns in the morning. After being denied by the district administration to hold the car rally, the industrialists began a march. The administration, however, did not grant the IIA members a permission to walk through the market.

The annoyed members then carried out a protest and were arrested by the police.

The detainees included chairman of IIA-Lucknow Chapter Rajat Mehra, senior vice president Anil Gupta, general secretary Mukesh Tandon and two former presidents Ganesh Chaturvedi and VK Agarwal.

Inspector of Hazratganj police station Ajit Singh Chauhan said the protesters were detained but were released after they signed a personal bond that they would not indulge in any activity which might cause law and order problem.

Heading: Samajwadi Party gets on BSP turf,  eyes Dalits - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Mayawati's decision to suspend the state-wide survey that demarcated the population living below the poverty line has put a question mark on the legitimacy of the exercise as the leader has begun to pull out 'eligible' names from the list, putting in fresh ones.

Most district magistrates do not know which criteria decide whether a name stays on the below poverty line (BPL) list, or is removed. District Magistrate of Kanpur Dehat Ramashankar Sahu said: "How do we do it? Our quota for BPL families is 1.83 lakh. Nearly 11,000 people who were on the old list have now been excluded. However, these people are now complaining they fulfill the criteria to be on the list. Those freshly included say the same." Sahu added the district administration had been asked to remove the 'illegitimate' names. "But how do we determine who is eligible unless we don't conduct a fresh survey?" he asked.

Sources said the original survey, which was based on government-approved norms and completed on September 30, had left many unhappy. Complaints started pouring in, particularly from the BJP, when the lists were being compiled, forcing Mayawati to suspend it last Saturday.

At the root of the problem, sources said, is politics. A family on the BPL list is the beneficiary of numerous welfare schemes for the poor, and no party wants to miss the opportunity of being generous to its votebase.

Most complaints were similar: the undeserving have been included, while the eligible have been left out.

The BJP complained of largescale anomalies in Unnao, Hardoi and Kanpur Dehat districts.

Additional District Magistrate (Revenue) of Unnao C P N Upadhyaya said a particular set of guidelines for the survey was decided before it began in 2007. "But there will be a lot of confusion now," he said. District

Magistrate of Mirzapur S P Dixit said if all complaints were accepted, the list would be lengthier than the district's quota of BPL families: 1.35 lakh.

This survey, sources said, has used a set of new norms to identify BPL families, norms set by the Centre and also the state. Strangely, it was decided in advance that the number of BPL families would remain unchanged at 99 lakh families — the same as found in the last survey in 2002.

Mayawati now wants district magistrates to delete thenames of those who do not qualify according to the central norms.

She also wants to maintain the total number of beneficiaries, though many more new names will now have to b included. That would mean a complete revision of the lists — which cannot be done without a fresh survey.

Heading: Azamgarh clerics form council to protest arrest of Muslim youths - Indian Express
Content:
With the Lok Sabha elections round the corner, the Samajwadi Party (SP) is reworking its election strategy by wooing the Dalits to enhance its vote bank.

Addressing a meeting of the state executive here on Monday, party chief Mulayam Singh Yadav claimed that the SP had always been pro-Dalit and had worked for their upliftment more than any other government in the state. "No dalit faced injustice during our rule," he added.

To underline the anti-people ideology of the ruling party, Mulayam recalled how the Bahujan Samaj Party government snatched away the jobs of 22,000 policemen and stopped the allowance of many unemployed youth. He termed the ruling party as the most corrupt government in the history of Uttar Pradesh politics.

Mulayam exhorted his party workers to stand up against the BSP and get set for the big fight in the coming elections. "Our aim should be to oust this government and ensure a that a democratic environment prevails in the state," said Mulayam.

He also reviewed the organisational strength of the party at the district level and asked the party leaders to start working for the Lok Sabha elections on a war footing.

Addressing the executive office bearers, Mulayam pointed out several issues like the increase in VAT, grim power scenario, police action in Azamgarh and explained the partymen in which way these issues should be presented to the public to create an anti-ruling party wave before the elections.

Meanwhile, party state president Shivpal Singh said the party has already finalised the candidates for all 80 seats for the Lok Sabha election. But the names would be made public only after the poll notification.

Heading: BJP, Congress war cries play out in slogans - Indian Express
Content:
A group of Muslim clerics in Azamgarh have constituted an 'Ulema council' to protest against the arrest of youths in various blast cases and the killing of two youths in an encounter in Delhi.

Convener of the council Maulana Mohammad Aamir Reshadi, who is also a former SIMI member, said: "The council is not influenced by any political outfit and has no affiliation with anyone. We, the clerics, are convinced that the youths of Sanjarpur and Sarai Mir areas were framed in fake cases."

Deputy Inspector General (Azamgarh range) Vijay Kumar said: "I am aware of the council and that the group would protest against the arrests and the encounter deaths. The police have been keeping a watch and we will not allow anyone to disturb law and order."

The DIG confirmed that the police records showed that Reshadi was a former SIMI member and a case was lodged against him at Kotwali

Azamgarh after the outfit was banned in 2001.

The charges against him included promoting enmity between different groups on grounds of religion and causing public mischief. "I was arrested in 2001. After spending six months in jail, I got bail and trial of my case was stayed by the High Court," said Reshadi.

Sources said he was close to senior SIMI leader Shahid Badr Falahi and held enormous clout in the organisation after Falahi was elected president of SIMI in September, 2004. Falahi, however, was replaced by Misbahul Islam of Karnataka in February 2006 and the members close to Falahi were asked to keep away from actively participating in the organisation, the sources said.

Asked about the council, Falahi said: "Though I was not informed about the council, this would help in seeking help from the authorities regarding framing of innocents in fake cases."

Heading: Family of Mehrauli blast victim donates organs to AIIMS - Indian Express
Content:
Kanpur has become the battleground for Congress and Bharatiya Janta Party members to settle their scores through derogatory hoardings and slogans.

Before the June 27 rally of Lal Krishna Advani, the district BJP members had put up a hoarding that portrayed Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and Congress president Sonia Gandhi as demons of inflation. Last Saturday, the Congressmen struck back and put up a hoarding at Bada Chauraha, showing Advani, dressed as a tiger and dreaming about the Prime Minister's chair. The hoarding carried the slogan, "Laashon par rajniti maboori hai, kyunki Kursi bahut zaroori hai( Greed for power forces us to do politics of death)." 

The hoarding called BJP as 'hypocrite patriots' and listed attacks on Parliament, Akshardham Temple, Raghnunath Temple and Red Fort during the NDA regime. The Kandahar incident, in which the government had released three terrorists including Maulana Masood Azhar, was highlighted as one of the major failures of the BJP-led NDA government to check terrorist activities in the country.

The anti-encroachment squad of Kanpur Nagar Nigam (KNN) removed the hoarding on Sunday, even though it was a non-working day. District Congress members alleged that the KNN removed the hoarding on the directives of BJP Mayor Ravindra Patni. Subsequently, the Congress members set on fire the effigy of the mayor. Following which, a delegation of senior BJP members met the district magistrate and submitted a complaint about the incident.

On Monday, District Congress president Mahesh Dixit slammed the mayor for the removal of the hoarding. "When BJP members put up hoardings targeting senior Congress leaders it is never considered objectionable but when we made a sincere attempt to apprise people about the reality, the hoarding was removed within a day," he said.

Dixit said at least 50 hoardings targeting Advani will be put up in the city soon. "The BJP members and the mayor cannot carry out their agenda. It is time they are taught a lesson," he added.

Patni termed the entire episode a political gimmick by the Congress. "The drive against illegal hoardings is being carried out by KNN officials and I have no role in the issue," he told The Indian Express.

"On Sunday, nearly half a dozen hoardings of the Bahujan Samaj Party were also removed from Bada Chauraha, but no one held me responsible for it." He claimed that Congress leaders are looking for issues to appease their vote bank for the upcoming Lok Sabha elections. "Instead of pointing fingers at the BJP stalwarts, Congress should review its own performance," added the mayor.

Former minister of state for urban development, Satish Mahana said the facts mentioned in the hoarding were misleading and sent a wrong message to people. "The slogan aimed at a senior BJP member was derogatory," said the BJP leader.

"We will oppose such acts of the Congress so that these are not repeated in future," said Mahana. While the BJP hoarding targeted Congress on the issue of inflation, Congress attempted to level baseless allegations at a senior BJP leader, he added.

Heading: First meet of Nobel laureates’ to be recorded by IGNOU and UGC - Indian Express
Content:
Even though Deepu lost his life in the Mehrauli blast, his family did not let go of the chance to serve others, as they decided to donate his organs to the Organ Retrieval Banking Organisation in the All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi.

Twenty two-year-old Deepu, a resident of Raipur village in Mohanlalganj, died on Thursday after fighting for six days with a head injury that he sustained during the blast in Mehrauli on September 27.

"Of my three sons, only he dared to venture out despite not having a proper education. He managed to find a job for himself," said Deepu's father Bhaagu Lal.

Lal said it was difficult for him to manage a large family with the small land that he had at his disposal. "We have only 15 bigha, which is barely enough for us to meet our basic needs. So, Deepu decided to go to Delhi, where his cousin Sanjay was working as a gardener and assured Deepu of a job there."

"After working as a security guard for several months, Deepu got a job of a gardener in a farm house at Gadaipur in Mehrauli," said Deepu's elder brother Samsher.

On the fateful day, Deepu, who resided in Bheem Basti near Mehrauli, went to buy clothes from the market. "He had promised to come home on Diwali, and for the same he went for shopping for the family," said Lal.

When Deepu failed to come back on Sunday, Sanjay started searching for him and came to know that he was injured in the blast. "Sanjay found unconscious Deepu at AIIMS Trauma Centre, where doctors said that Deepu had been in coma ever since he was brought to the hospital," said Lal.

"On Wednesday, after sensing his chances of survival to be rare, the doctors asked us to donate his organs," said Lal. Without any hesitation, they decided to ahead with the aim to serve the society.

The family, however, declined to accept the compensation granted by the Delhi government.

Heading: 796 schools will turn computer savvy from December - Indian Express
Content:
Stakes are high for the first ever meet of Nobel laureates in the country that will take place at Indian Institute of Information Technology, Allahabad (IIIT-A) between December 15 and 21.

To record the invaluable knowledge imparted by 14 living legends from across the world during the conference, IIIT-A administration has granted the permission to Indira Gandhi National Open University (IGNOU) and the Consortium for Educational Communication (CEC) of University Grants Commission.

The proceedings will then be used for developing e-content to be broadcasted by CEC through its 24-hour channel — Vyas — on higher education and by IGNOU through its educational web cast.

"This is being done to present the repository of knowledge before the generations to come," said Dr M D Tiwari, Director, IIT-A.

He added the permission for the recordings had been granted by IIIT-A, but the copyright of the content will remain with the institute. "Both IGNOU and CEC have agreed in principle to acknowledge the support of IIIT-A in the development of the e-content and broadcasting of the talks," said Tiwari.

Preparations for the meet are in full swing. Some important sessions, including the inaugural and the valedictory sessions of the meet, will be broadcasted live by the two organisations through their satellite uplinking facility, Tiwari added.

The CEC, an inter-university centre, was set up in 1993 by UGC to use electronic media for the development of higher education in the country.

It has 17 Educational Multimedia Research Centres in various parts of the country and is responsible for the use of new technologies for the improvement of standards in higher education in the country through the use of multimedia and e-content creation.

Heading: LU to start grading system: Science dept first on the block - Indian Express
Content:
Come December and 796 primary and upper primary schools in the state Capital will have access to computer education. Courtesy: "Education For All" scheme launched by the state government in 2007 with the aim to make students in primary schoolsand upper primary schools computer literate. It could not, however, take off due to the absence of electricity in many schools.

Now, the Lucknow Electricity Supply Administration (LESA) has been asked to give electricity connections to these schools by the end of next month so that the computers can be installed in these schools.   

"We are now speeding up the work to provide computer literacy to schools and this process will begin soon," said Rakesh Shrivastava, Basic Shiksha Adhikari.

In the first phase, 779 schools have been shortlisted for the electricity connection with the remaining to receive it soon. We did not install the computers in these schools earlier as they would have been useless without electricity, said Shrivastava.

A letter was written to the LESA on September 2 this year, asking it to give connections by the end of next month, he said.

For the purpose of providing installations, services of only registered electricity department contractors will be taken.

Heading: Police raid LU hostel, arrest two illegal occupants - Indian Express
Content:
Following the precedent laid by the IITs across the country, Lucknow University has now decided to introduce grading system in its examination process from the next academic session. The system will be introduced initially in the Science department, followed by others depending on its response.

To work out the modalities of the system, the university has formed a three-member committee comprising V K Tandon, Dean, Science faculty; Dr Dinesh Kumar, Head of Botany department and Meenakshi Srivastava, Head of Zoology Department. This decision was taken on Monday during a meeting of the deans and heads of various faculties and departments. The committee will be preparing a report regarding its implementation, which will be submitted by January 2009. "In the new system, grades will be awarded to the students depending upon the marks scored. But on the mark sheet, only grades will be displayed," said Dinesh Kumar, university spokesperson.

The university, meanwhile, has also decided that the first semester exams for the Post Graduate courses of this session will be held between December 1 and 15. It will be responsibility of the head of the departments to prepare the schedule of the examination and obtain an approval for it from the V-Cand the examination controller.

Heading: Former BJP MLA’s house robbed - Indian Express
Content:
To keep a check on illegal occupants in the Lucknow University (LU) hostels, the district police conducted a raid in the wee hours of Monday morning and arrested two illegal occupants.

The occupants — Rahul Singh and Vijay Anand — were arrested from the Narendra Dev hostel for occupying rooms which were allotted to some other students.

According to the proctor's office, the accused Rahul Singh, a student of BA Part II and Vijay Anand, who completed his MA this year, were found occupying rooms originally allotted to Gyanendra Kumar Gautam from Sitapur and Kuldeep Kumar from Ambedkarnagar.

The raid took place after a student of the university reported the matter to the police.

Heading: FIR lodged against Azamgarh hotel - Indian Express
Content:
Some unknown miscreants fled with a licenced revolver and some jewellery from ex-BJP MLA Kusum Rai's house near D Block Puliya in Talkatora police circle on Monday night.

According to police, the incident took place in the absence of Rai, who has been in Benaras for the last five days. The police, however, informed her of the incident over the phone.

Circle Officer (CO) Bazarkhala, Chiranjeev Nath Sinha, said, "Rai's neighbours informed us that the doors of her house had been broken. Initial investigations have revealed that a revolver and some jewellery, including a chain and an ear ring are missing."

Heading: Will Paddy plump for youth too? - Indian Express
Content:
With the previous Vengsarkar-led Mumbai selection committee giving youngsters adequate exposure, it will be interesting to see how Shivalkar & Co go about their business in the upcoming Ranji season

The Mumbai Cricket Association's (MCA) Cricket Improvement Committee (CIC) recently appointed Padmakar Shivalkar as chairman of the selection committee after Dilip Vengsarkar made his exit. But the biggest question on everyone's mind is - will the small and slender-made Shivalkar - the most talented dynamo-spinner to miss the India bus - perfectly step into Vengsarkar's imposing shoes?

A former left-arm spinner, Shivalkar, who was unfortunate to not play for India, will definitely have a tough task ahead. Though it is too early to predict the mindset of the new MCA selection committee, but it will be interesting to see how they come up with their first squad for the Mumbai Ranji Trophy team later this month.

The last selection committee showed plentiful confidence in youngsters without being unduly worried about results. And apart from selection, it also saw the entry of Pravin Amre as Mumbai coach, especially when his name was not even in the list of contenders.

The earlier selection committee had dared to drop Mumbai's most experienced spinner Nilesh Kulkarni and chose 17-year-old Iqbal Abdullah instead. And recently, 15-year-old left-arm spinner Harmeet Singh was given a chance in the Buchi Babu tournament and the committee had divided the pool of youngsters in two groups which went on to play different tournaments.

When Vengsarkar took over from Milind Rege as the chairman two seasons ago, he gave opportunities to quite a few youngsters, as a result of which the likes of Ajinkya Rahane, Sahil Kukreja, Rohit Sharma, Dhawal Kulkarni, Abhishek Nayar and Iqbal Abdullah were all able to don the Mumbai Ranji cap. Apart from Rohit, who made his international debut, all of them managed to book a berth at India A level.

Looking at the past two seasons, one can easily say that Mumbai cricket was in fact revamped under Vengsarkar's tenure.

Will Shivalkar continue with the same policy of backing youth or will he pull out something altogether different from his hat? Will the new selection committee give another chance to veteran spinners like Nilesh Kulkarni or will leg-spinner Sairaj Bahutule, who left Mumbai and joined Maharashtra after much consternation, get another opportunity to represent his former team?

Vengsarkar, who is also a member of the CIC, feels that every new selection committee will certainly have some ideas and plans of their own in place. "It is too early to talk about it. I will be holding a meeting with every selector soon so that we all can serve Mumbai cricket better. Shivalkar has been chairman of selection committee earlier too and he knows what's to be done," he says of the 68-year-old. With BCCI having paid selectors finally, the MCA too have decided to pay Rs 50,000 to their selectors annually. Mumbai coach Praveen Amre is schedule to have meeting with new selection committee soon and when quizzed how much difference it would make to convince new selectors, he said, "We will give all data to them and will discuss how to go about it in the forthcoming season."

Apart from Shivalkar, the CIC has appointed Ismail Abdullah as one of the selector after Kiran Mokashi joined the MCA academy as coach. It will be interesting to see whether Shivalkar & Co will continue with Amol Muzumdar as skipper or will appoint Wasim Jaffer to lead Mumbai in the coming season.

Content:
Araldite Kenkre FC continued their resurgence in the MFL Elite Division League by beating Indian Navy 3-1 in a Group A match at the RCF Sports Complex in Chembur on Monday.

By virtue of this victory, they put themselves in a position to qualify for the Super 7 to be held later this month. In another Group A encounter, RCF allowed Akbar Travels to crawl back into the game after Nigel D'Souza had put them ahead in the 37th minute. Ezekal Okuwlum equalized for the latter in the 65th minute.

Kenkre FC, who impressed in their win over Akbar Travels last weekend, however were leaden footed in the last 45 minutes of the game after Grenville Murzello (7th minute) and Rajeev Ayyappan (45th minute) had put them ahead.

The sailors dominated the second half and could easily have run away winners if they had converted the chances they made for themselves. Sumesh converted a penalty in the 64th minute for them, but Shaji D'Silva and company could not convert any more goals till Kenkre's substitute Adhikarimayom scored in the 89th minute off a counter attack.

RCF started off in attacking fashion, but Nigel D'Souza and Allan Dias missed some sitters.

Veteran Prosenjit Barua, who came in as a substitute, placed a perfect pass for Nigel D'Souza to run in and score.

Jonathan 'Bobo'could not do much against the tight defence of RCF and was substituted.

Nusrat Kamal, RCF's right back blundered in missing a header at the centerline and allowed the Akbar left half to run in, and even as stopper Baleshwar Sharma slipped and fell, the ball was relayed to Okuwlum for him to finish past the RCF custodian.

Kenkre FC now has eight points from four games, the same as RCF. Akbar Travels and Indian Navy however languish at the bottom of the rung in Group A.

Content:
Here's where you must go to pay obeisance to pure vegetarian food during Navratri

Swati Snacks

Tardeo

When it's Swati Snacks, it's always a good time. Don't be misled by the name; you can make meals out of the snacks served here. However, it's most famous for its snacks, street-style spicy food. It's easy to get there; just get to Tardeo and say Swati Snacks to anyone. Panki, Dal Dhokli, Gatta nu Shaak are some of the popular dishes here. Food critic Rashmi Uday Singh swears by this place and says, "It is one of the best places for Gujarati food in town. The snacks are unbeatable, all-time eats." Waiting time is usually half-hour, all days of the week. An important Gujarati address, this one is a must-go during Navratri time.

Rating Excellent

Call 5660 8405

Govinda

ISKON Temple, Juhu

No onions, no garlic is the mantra they apply to this wonderful restaurant at ISKON temple, Juhu. The food is Sattvic so is the ambience. They insist on using only pure ghee and the freshest ingredients for their 556-item food list. Homemaker Shilpa Bhatnagar, a regular says, "It's a no-fuss place. Just buy coupons and then eat as much as you can. Besides the food, they have a good variety of drinks and sherbets which I like very much." The food is delicious and is offered to Lord Krishna as bhog to begin with. Devotional bhakti music completes the experience.

Rating Very good

Call 2620 5214

Bhagat Tarachand

Kalbadevi

Some places run out of food but never of eager diners. Bhagat Tarachand in Kalbadevi is one such place. It started out as a small lunch joint, today there stand three Bhagat Tarachands in one line. "Here, you should know to ask for food without onions and garlic. There are lots of Jains and Gujarati frequenting this place. I recommend their paneer preparations. Everything here is good," says Reema Jain, an executive with Indiainfoline, who visits the place every now and then. The other USP of the place is chilled chaas served in beer bottles.

Rating Very good

Call 2240 6158

Soam Chowpatty

For many a trip to Babulnath Temple also includes a trip to Soam. It's a pure vegetarian food space that sells fasting food by the kilos. They say that if you want to eat truly good food, go to a place that Gujaratis throng. Try out their Sabudana khichdi (Rs 60) Sabudana chilla (Rs 55), Rajgira puri with shrikhand (Rs 95) and Kesar shrikhand (Rs 65). If you're in for a thali, go easy on the farsan or you may not be able to do justice to the food. It is also a good idea to make a reservation. You don't want to wait to break your fast, do you?

Rating Very good

Call 2369 8080

It's Mirchi,Ramee Guestline, Juhu

The dandiya sticks and colourful dupattas suspended on the walls for decoration are a bit much but the food in this restaurant is quite good. They have a Gujarat-Marwar special cuisine. They too have omitted onions and garlic from the spread. Rich Marwari specialties like Dry tomato preparation, tomato curry, gatte-ka-saag and rich sweets are quite yummy. Other vegetables like karela and potato are also good. So are the kachoris. They have live chaat counters as well. For lack of patience, we skipped the counters and went straight for the food.

Rating Very good

Content:
Donburi

(Pronounced dohn-boo-rhee)

Quite simply, Donburi is a Japanese rice bowl dish. Stews made out of fish, chicken, pork or other meat are served over rice in bowls (also called donburi). These bowls are oversized and synonymous with donburi meals.

There are several varieties of donburi. Scrambled egg mixed with sweet donburi sauce and served over rice, deep-fried pork cutlets with onion, tempura shrimp and vegetables on rice, beef and onion on rice, and grilled eel on rice are some of the popular variations.

Donburi meals are popular as they can be made out of any ingredients. For this reason they are served steaming hot at inexpensive kiosks in Japan. In Mumbai try the donburi meals at Tiffin, The Oberoi and Wasabi by Morimoto at Taj Mahal Palace and Tower.

Heading: Forward block - Indian Express
Content:
After grabbing the spotlight as a model, this 23-year-old now makes her big screen debut in Fashion

You are lucky!" exclaim my male friends, envious of my lunch date with Mugdha Godse, the dusky model who is set to make her Bollywood debut with Madhur Bhandarkar's Fashion this Diwali. We are to meet at Masala Mantar in Andheri, her favourite hangout in this part of the city.

Godse keeps her word and sails in at 1 pm, sharp. Dressed in a black Adidas singlet and denims, she is a sharp contrast to her glam avatar; her minimalistic look lends her a girl-next-door look.

"I hope I didn't keep you waiting," she exclaims as she drinks in the colourful interiors. "I love its rustic look. Whenever I have time, I drop in for the spicy Punjabi fare they serve."

As we take our seats, a chance to take a closer look at this bubbly 23-year-old reveals signs of exhaustion. Juggling between ad shoots, promotions and film dubbing has kept her on her toes. "But I am so excited and nervous. Ever since the promos started on TV, the expectations have gone up," she confesses.

In the movie, Godse plays Janet Sequeira, an unsuccessful model. Fashion, starring Priyanka Chopra in the lead alongside Kangana Ranaut and Arbaaz Khan, is a Diwali release and will face competition from EMI and Golmaal Returns.

But Godse remains unflustered as "They all have different target audiences". Her faith in her director adds to her confidence. "The movie is about the emotional journey of models at different stages of their careers and Madhur has captured it aptly," she asserts.

Between posing for photographs, Godse reveals that she had no idea she could act before she faced the camera. Hers has been the typical small-town-girl story.

"I studied in a Marathi medium school in Pune. It was at Symbiosis College that I understood the basics of grooming. I would make friends and go partying so that I could learn to conduct myself."

Her ambitions drove her to become a part-time gym instructor and then a model. From modelling to movies, however, was simple. Bhandarkar spotted her at an ad shoot.

It was after Godse signed the film that the grill began.

She attended a crash course in acting at Anupam Kher's acting school and enrolled for Kathak classes, which she claims have helped her synchronise expressions, moves and feelings.

Recounting her first time in front of the camera, she boasts at having given her first shot in just two retakes. "And once the shot was done, everybody on the sets applauded. I can still hear the sound of those claps," she adds.

The debutante is clearly focussing on her acting career now. She has cut down on her modelling assignments and has been attending various script-reading sessions.

Her three-movie deal with Percept is also in the pipeline. "But you will see me at the forthcoming Lakme Fashion Week—this time as a showstopper," she promises.

Success has clearly not affected her. Nibbling on tandoori brocolli, the petite model admits that at heart she is still the Marathi mulgi who is enamoured by the drama and dhishum-dhishum in Bollywood films and loves her varan bhaat with ghee and nimbu.

Right then, just like a genie, the waiter appears with a platter of another favourite, masala corn.

Bon appétit .

Heading: Guessing game - Indian Express
Content:
Shelly Jyoti contemporises Mithila painting, presents a fusion of Zardosi and block prints

She paints women, their relationships and their inner space, while serving up a colourful palette of traditional Mithila paintings with an urban twist. Shelly Jyoti, a self-taught artist, displays both skill and sensitivity while dealing with her medium of acrylic and ink on archival paper. "I have always been interested in the decorative aspect of art. I add my own personal narratives to a style of painting, I feel I am bringing tradition alive," says Jyoti, who was born in Delhi in the year 1957. She is having her first solo in Mumbai—Beyond Mithila: Exploring the Decorative at Jamaat Art Gallery in Colaba. "As far as I go, Mithila appeals to my senses, rather than my intellect. I also think it's important to reconnect with art done by women, involving art that welcomes ornamentation instead of eschewing it," says the Baroda-based painter.

Mithila is relegated to the realm of craft but many contemporary artists are revisiting the style and imbuing it with new narratives.

"When I was invited last year by Women Made Art Gallery, in Chicago, I felt that I wanted to share the heritage of India with the people in America," says Jyoti who had a hearty response with 250 people turning up for the opening at the gallery.

"My current body of work explores a new medium, Zardozi textile, block printing with some of the motifs I use in my paintings," says Jyoti who also writes poems to accompany her paintings. They read as a lyrical artist's statement about the works.

In one of them she compares her mother to a tree.

"My next show is looking at a more political issue, the narratives of Indigo workers, who have been exploited through during Colonial times," says the artist who plans to collaborate with an American artist. "Collaboration is good because it brings in different cultural contexts and I am always open to fusion. However, much about this show is yet to be decided," says the artist who prices her paintings between Rs 3,500 to Rs 1 lakh.

Meanwhile, the current show is on at Jamaat till the end of October.

Heading: Know great shakes - Indian Express
Content:
The acclaimed German play, Mr Kolpert, returns to Mumbai stage riding on youthful energy

What can you say about a group of urban 20-somethings huddled together and talking about intense boredom? Either they are plotting how to get rid of this feeling or discussing the fate of Mr Kolpert in the eponymous German play by David Gieselmann. In this case, both.

For, the latest production of First Ray Theatre Group, Mr Kolpert, is about a couple, Ralf Droht and Sarah Kenner, who are bored. They invite Edith and Bastian—who are completely unaware of the Drohts' plan to amuse themselves by pretending that a trunk at their house contains the body of a colleague.

This German play had Anshuman Jha, its director, interested in it for some years now. He had staged it in Mumbai for the first time in 2003, at the Thespo festival. "I'm reviving this black comedy with some changes in the cast," says Jha, who for a 23-year-old leads a busy life of an assistant director doubling as theatre director-actor.

How do he and his cast—all in their early 20s—relate to the tale of such murderous boredom? Jha comes up with a number of instances of urban ennui. Actors Amrita Puri and Nisha Lalvani chip in. "We haven't experienced that but can relate to it," they say. Lalvani talks about her bike-happy acquaintances who slap people on the street while speeding ahead, just for fun.

The play a fine example of European absurdist theatre, however, is not just about boredom. It mixes black humour, violence and horror to dish out an excellent exploration of the chaos theory at work in Germany today.

So enamoured is Jha by this dark comedy that he plans to make his directorial debut on the big screen with this. And for its cast, the names featuring on his wish-list are Farhan Akhtar, Rahul Bose,

Shefali Shah and Neha Dhupia. "The one-and-a-half hour play doesn't give much background of the eventful evening. But my screenplay will throw more light on that," says Jha.

Would Indian movie-goers relish a dark comedy? "Why not? And I will never make it boring," says the young director. We can believe that.

(Mr Kolpert will be staged at Prithvi Theatre on Tuesday and Wednesday.)

Heading: 15 news faces of terror: all educated men, some with highly-paid jobs - Indian Express
Content:
Popular night clubs keep you on your toes with various exciting dance forms

Ever wished you could just walk on to the dance floor and make heads turn with your moves? Now you can gain that confidence at the dance floor itself. Popular night clubs in the city have introduced dance classes in salsa, tango, hip hop and belly dancing and what's more, they are running a full house too.

It was Zenzi in Bandra that first introduced salsa and belly dancing classes. "We wanted to conduct activities nobody else does and then look for professional teachers and start it. The numbers are also unlimited and we do not charge fees," says Matan Schabracq, partner, Zenzi. Thanks to its rising popularity, they have added two more dance forms to the list - traditional Argentine Tango and Lindy Hop every Monday and Wednesday.

These World dances are performed and taught by Tim Collins of USA and Malou Meyenhofer of Switzerland. The classes that are conducted in a professional career will help you get a solid grasp of rhythm, musicality and moves that you can pull out on any dance floor. "Zenzi has a cool club feel and that really charges the atmosphere during the classes. We do have an occasional need for mirrors and for that we have rented a second space so we can balance between the night club and a dance studio," says Collins. Lindy Hop, the tougher of the two is danced to old-school swing and jazz music. But Collins advises, "Everyone must start somewhere, and our teaching system is very methodical. Whether it is two-left feet or an experienced dancer, there is something for everyone at our classes."

Although both these classes attract a substantial number, it is the all-time favourite couple dance salsa that attracts a large number. Schabracq says, "Salsa is by far the most popular and hence we have these classes on Sundays."

Cashing in on Salsa's popularity is hip club Blue Frog, Lower Parel, which conducts monthly workshops. Kaytee Namgyal of Salsa India Congress who conducts regular salsa workshops at the club feels this is the best way to advertise a particular dance form. "You cannot earn a dance degree at these workshops. But we help you familiarise with the dance form, educate you with the basic steps and generate interest," says Namgyal, who has had many more students enrolling, post these workshops.

Banana Bar and Tangy Tamarind, Bandra, too conduct basic salsa classes for all its guests. "It is an hour-long class, which gives you a chance to interact with others," says Shivangi Bose, a regular.

Time to get those shoes on then.
