Submitting that the High Court cannot direct it to pay the passenger, the airline said an important question of law is raised with regard to the operation of flights and the obligation of operators in the event of cancellation and delay of flights due to technical reasons.

While both the district forum and Delhi Consumer Dispute Redressal Commission had asked the airline to pay compensation for deficiency in service to the passenger, the airline contended the consumer fora acted outside their jurisdiction.

Heading: Pubs under watch in area where Soumya was murdered - Indian Express
Content:
A senior Class I central government officer allegedly jumped to death from his office on the fifth floor of Udyog Bhawan. Police said, he was suffering from depression due to health problems.

According to police officers, H S Kanthuria, Deputy Industrial Adviser of the Department of Chemicals, took the extreme step about 2 pm, a senior police officer said.

Kanthuria had met with an accident about two years ago and was not keeping well for a long while, the officer said, adding that he was depressed due to his health problems.

Kanthuria reportedly jumped from the window above the air-conditioner in his office. The room was locked from inside and the key was in Kanthuria's pocket. The window from which the victim reportedly jumped is a small one and is at a great height.

A senior official of with the Department of IPP at Udyog Bhawan said, "We found his shoes inside the room. It seems that he first got on top of the showcase placed under the air-conditioner and then crawled out from the window to jump to his death, as the opening is quite small."

Police said Kanthuria was a resident of Mayur Vihar Phase II, SFS Flats and his wife works as a manager with a bank. He is survived by two sons who are settled abroad.

An Udyog Bhawan official said, "One of his sons lives in the USA while the other is in Saudi Arabia. He did not have any problems with anyone and we are still being not able to fathom what happened."

Heading: New role, same goals - Indian Express
Content:
Clueless South Delhi police were keeping an eye on late-night pubs and bars near the area Soumya Vishwanathan was shot dead in Vasant Kunj.

According to a source, Delhi Police sleuths in civil clothes are paying visits to late night bars and are monitoring the activities of the people.

"We are trying to find any lead from the bars because we suspect some rogue local elements might be behind the incident," police sources said.

Sources added they are closely monitoring the activities of visitors to late night bars and are scrutinising the ones who possess weapons.

Soumya Vishwanathan was found dead in her Zen car on September 29 at Nelson Mandela Marg.

Till now, at least three witnesses have approached the police in connection with the case, however, their narration of events and what they saw has not helped in making a breakthrough.

A senior police officer said, "As it is a blind case we are trying to explore every possible measure. We have deputed men during late-night bars in Vasant Kunj and adjoining areas."

Heading: DDCA throws a surprise: Chopra gets the captain’s band - Indian Express
Content:
Former men's national coach Rajender Singh is busy sharpening girls' skills now

Four years ago, he was the man who was expected to set India's recent dismal Olympic record straight. Less than a month before Athens, he was sent home packing, in between games in Europe. He went back to where he came from, working in the shadows, training youngsters at the Union Academy in Delhi.

Now Rajender Singh is on another mission: posted at the SAI academy in Chandigarh, the man is in charge of the development of their women's hockey team. The first step was taken when his team — Government Model Senior Secondary School — pumped in 25 goals past a hapless the Government Girls Higher Secondary School, Raigarh (Chattisgarh) in their opening match of the Nehru hockey girls (under-17) tournament at Shahbad on Tuesday. Captain Reena Khokhar scored eight of those, Manmeet Kaur scored five, Sandeep Kaur scored three, Monika, Shivani Singh, Gurpreet Kaur and Navdeep Kaur had two each against their names, while Ritu Shah Arya scored one.

But Rajinder Singh is far from happy. "This might be a good beginning. But once we move ahead in the tournament and play against better teams, things will get difficult. A scoreline of 25-0 does not mean this team is something special," he says bluntly.

Maybe not for someone who has worked with perhaps the most talented Indian men's line-up in recent times. A while later, though, he admits it is a refreshing difference working with girls. "They have infinite patience," he says with a laugh. "There are no complaints on the amount or hardship of training. On the flipside though, since I am used to working with boys, the different speeds and reaction times sometimes rankle. But that will come with practice, I guess."

Rajinder took charge just over three months back, and he admits to the problems he has been facing. We have just 14 girls, despite trying hard to get more. And during selections, there is more emphasis on fitness than skills. That makes things more difficult for me, as I have to work much harder on making sure they get the basics right," he says.

Despite the shortage of time, Rajinder Singh has been able to organise matches for the girls against the better known team from the Shahbad Academy. "Players like Reena, Monika, Shivani Singh and Ritu are talented, they can be in the national team in a couple of years with proper training and exposure," he says.

But he knows better than to promise anything, having been on the receiving end of an administration that doesn't believe in continuity. "I hope to get around 40 girls by next year. I can produce at least a couple of talented players for the Indian team. But I can't say how long I will be here. Tomorrow I might be transferred somewhere else," he signs off.

Mizoram school thrash Vadodara girls
In other matches of the day, Government Lallengunga High School, Thenzawl (Mizoram) thrashed Don Bosco High School, Vadodara (Gujarat) 27-0. Leading 15-0 at half time, Ramngaihzuali scored nine goals, Lalbiaksailovi scored eight, Lalhmingmawii scored thrice, Lalnunchami and R. Lalnunsangi scored two apiece and Lalsawmpari, Lalrothuami and Julie Tluangi scored one each. Duruelo Convent High School, Mumbai beat NCC Directorate (Punjab) 4-1 in another match. Anita Kapadiya, Bhagyashree Agarwal, Tosha Kamath and Jemima Moteiro scored for the winners while Ruchika Raghav was the lone scorer for the losing team.

Heading: Aayush upsets 10th seed Nischay - Indian Express
Content:
If it ain't broke, don't fix it. Adhering to the axiom, the new DDCA senior selection committee has refrained from major chopping and changing while announcing the list of 28 probables for defending champions Delhi's 2008-09 Ranji Trophy campaign. However, the Chetan Chauhan-led committee couldn't resist throwing in a surprise, naming Aakash Chopra as captain ahead of Mithun Manhas.

"In the absence of Virender Sehwag and Gautam Gambhir, who will be with the Indian team for the Australia and England series, Aakash Chopra will lead the side," selection committee convenor Sunil Dev said in a statement.

Normally in the past, Manhas has assumed the responsibility whenever the Sehwag and Gambhir are performing national duty. Naturally, the move has left him a bit dejected.

"I think I have successfully led the team in the past. Be it the initial phase in the Ranji Trophy last season or guiding North Zone all the way to victory in the Duleep Trophy, I have repeatedly proved my captaincy credentials," Manhas, who is nursing his sore back in Bangalore, told Sportline over the phone.

"Since Aakash and I are very good friends, it won't be and issue but, yeah, I am surprised and a bit disappointed too."

For his part, Chopra is surprised too, albeit pleasantly. "Well, the news is a little surprising that it (the captaincy) came to me," the former India opener said. "However, I had been sounded out and was asked if I was interested. I said 'yes'," Chopra, who is in Kochi to promote his book, said.

"I'd been approached in the past but I was wary of taking it up because of obvious reasons in the DDCA. But now, the things are better. My form is good too and I am confident that I can handle the responsibility."

Meanwhile, Shikhar Dhwan was appointed the vice-captain, even as the top 17 picked themselves. Among others, Sahan John, Raman Sachdeva, Avtar Singh and Amandeep Singh were the new faces, unheard of earlier, while Pradeep Chawla, Varun Kumar and Suhail Sharma failed to make the cut.

Heading: Read the Metre - Indian Express
Content:
With its walk-in wine cellar, hot canapés and retro rock, InSomnia recalls another age

It is circa 1930 at The Taj Ambassador's InSomnia Bar and Lounge. Carrying forward the colonial ambience the Taj Ambassador is known for, InSomnia comes as a carefully selected package that exudes an air of past glory. The décor is colonial Art Deco with a contemporary touch. Sweeping curves (check out the ceiling with its bold circular designs around the lights) and stepped forms dominate the decor as the lavish velvet, chenille and leather upholstery adds to the overall plush feel. Giving a traditional Indian element is the ornate brass partition at the entrance and on the windows that surprises you with its familiarity.

While the food menu, though European, is limited, it is compensated by the extensive drinks menu and a walk-in wine cellar where connoisseurs can look for a vintage to go with their smoked duck and lamb shanks. The bar stocks over 120 fine-wine labels, costing Rs 1,200-25,000 per bottle, and boasts some rare whiskies like Bruichladdich and Dalmore.

We started with InSomnia Margarita (Rs 500) and Virgin Mojito (Rs 450). The margarita came with a distinct almond flavour while the mojito, with its minty texture, was just a variant of the common Adam and Eve mocktail. The Espresso Martini (Rs 500) was not a bad choice even though its taste lingers somewhere between the pleasantness of coffee and its raw bitterness.

For starters, we chose hot canapés — Smoked Duck Rolls with Orange and Cointreau Dip (Rs 500) and Spicy Cottage Cheese and Tapioca Cakes (Rs 425). The former was a delight, with the duck perfectly smoked and tasting even better with the flavoured dip. So were the tapioca cakes, served with fruits sprinkled with chillies that surprisingly brought out the taste of sago in a novel way. For the main course, Braised Lamb Shanks Over Glazed Onion Risotto (Rs 625) is a must-try, as the slowly simmered lamb is amazingly succulent. And the sauce is soaked up by the risotto, which is served with vegetables and garlic bread. Though the menu gives hardly a choice for vegetarians, Cheese Baked Open Ravioli with Wild Mushrooms Ragout & Parmesan (Rs 550) is a mild, melt-in-your mouth Italian-French dish, generous with parmesan and fleshy mushrooms packed in the open, thin pasta dough. InSomnia offers only two choices for desserts (Rs 250). Frozen Caramel Parfait on Tropical Salsa scores over Sugar Free Banana Chip Bread Pudding, which can be given a miss unless you don't mind the sour orange sauce of the experimental dessert.

To go with the food, InSomnia has a one-man band that plays retro/rock 'n' roll. On Tuesdays, a jazz band plays while Thursday nights are reserved for country music.

Heading: Go See Gabo - Indian Express
Content:
Jeet Thayil on bringing together some of the finest poets in an anthology

Jeet Thayil mentions this Macaulay moment in poetry when W.B. Yeats, after praising Rabindranath Tagore much, revised his opinion and wrote to friend William Rothenstein, "Damn Tagore. We got out three good books, Sturge, Moore and I, and because he thought it more important to see and know English than to be a great poet, he brought out sentimental rubbish and wrecked his reputation. Tagore does not know English, no Indian knows English. Nobody can write music and style in a language not learned in childhood and ever since the language of his thought." Nobody asked Yeats if he wrote in Gaellic. Indian poets who followed Tagore, though not necessarily in the footsteps of his sangeet, sometimes tried to explain the need to write poetry in English. And then they stopped bothering.

60 Indian Poets (Penguin, Rs 499), edited by Thayil, brings together some of the finest poets of post-independence India, all writing in English — from Nissim Ezekiel's "You want one glass lassi?/ Very good for digestion/ With little salt, lovely drink/ Better than wine;/ Not that I am ever tasting the wine" to Daljit Nagra writing of "cos up di stairs is my newly bride/ v share in chapatti/ v share in di chutney/ after vee hav made luv/ like vee rowing through Putney".

If you have been stumped by a lack of poetry anthologies after you have gone through R. Parthasarathy's Ten Twentieth Century Indian Poets, this one bravely tries to fill the gap. The idea of the book was suggested to Thayil when he was leaving America for India in 2004. "Philip Nikolayev, editor of the literary journal Fulcrum, suggested that since I was returning to India, I could work on an anthology of contemporary Indian poetry. It wasn't supposed to be too much then, but it consumed the entire 500-page journal," says Thayil, now based in Bangalore.

While working on the anthology, Thayil read and re-read works of poets he had known and those he had missed out in his years abroad. "It wasn't too difficult to choose. There were names I knew just had to be there and it was a matter of finding some others whom I included because of my preference for craft," says Thayil. As for the number, he just thought 60 was big enough to encompass what is essentially "an introduction to an undeservedly little known literature".

The book begins with Ezekiel, and then it spans across the country and beyond. The usual suspects are there Dom Moraes, Arun Kolatkar and Kamala Das as well as other well known names like Vikram Seth, Amit Chaudhuri, Dilip Chitre, Keki Daruwalla, Adil Jussawalla, Gieve Patel and Eunice de Souza. But the book also gently reinstates the works of forgotten poets like Gopal Honnalgere, Lawrence Bantleman, Srinivas Rayaprol and G.S. Sharat Chandra.

"Unlike a Bangla poet, English-language poets in India don't have a distinct readership," says Thayil. And, sadly, they don't share the limelight set aside for Indian novelists. "Poets receive no advances, their books are usually out of print, it's difficult to find publishers. These are difficult conditions under which Indian poets produce original work," says Thayil.

If you can set aside the debate over the title — shouldn't "Indian Poets" include those in regional languages? — then gently surrender to the verses. Damn Yeats.

Heading: Konkan Coasts to Success - Indian Express
Content:
Catch a glimpse of Aracataca and everything Marquezian at this exhibition

He made Macondo the most famous fictitious address in Latin America. So one shouldn't really be surprised when people far away in Alappuzha talk of Gabriel Garcia Marquez as though one evening they had all wandered out of their homes to say hello to him, under the shadow of his crumbling ancestral house in Aracataca. If you have glimpsed Aracataca and everything Marquezian in feverish dreams generated by words and an imaginary Colombian sun, now is your chance to see the real thing on large black-and-white photographs displayed at the exhibition "Gabo: The Writer" organised by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Colombia and the ICCR.

Sinthya Rubio, cultural head of the Colombia Embassy, points to a photograph of macondo, a tree whose wood is used for making canoes, and which inspired the fictitious town where an entire clan of Buendias flourished. On the walls are images of an impassive, 14-year-old Marquez in Bogota, "such a grim city", where he arrived in a shirt made of black blanket and hat with a metal trunk; a middle-aged Marquez dressed in a sweater with wife Mercedes; and the family together in bed with the boys Rodrigo and Gonzalo. There is also an effervescent Marquez with his customary warm smile with writer Jorge Luis Borges, "one of the authors I read the most and maybe disliked the most". Then there is the coastal town of Aracataca with its shanties; the Barranquilla Group with a youthful Marquez standing with three friends; a boy in a panama hat playing the accordion as people look around with a desultory air; and Gabo's grandparents Nicolas and Tranquilina Iguarán who influenced his early years. The 78 images record Marquez's life till 1982 when he won the Nobel Prize for literature.

"The travelling exhibition was organised in the 1990s by Ministry of Foreign affairs of Colombia and since then it has travelled to Chile and European countries. From here, it will now go to China in the second week of November," says Rubio. As one visitor points out, "In Colombia, everybody tries to establish a connection with Marquez. Old people waiting for their salaries compare themselves to the batty Colonel Buendia who refused his 'pension in order to get rid of the torture of waiting for it'."

The best known citizen of Colombia now lives in Mexico with his wife, but on the coast of Colombia, "Aracataca is still the same. Nothing has changed," says Ambassador of Colombia Juan Alfredo Pinto Saavedra. And you feel the afternoon sun on your spine.

The exhibition is on at Azad Bhavan till October 11

Heading: This Navratri, Forest Dept tells a musical tale of conservation - Indian Express
Content:
A mix of suspense, comedy and songs, Konkani musical or tiatr has all the elements that make up a popular stage act. So it wasn't a surprise when the audience sat through a four-hour-long tiatr Police, performed by Augustino Temudo and his group of 17 actors, flown in from Goa by the Goa Art and Culture Department.

Most tiatr actors are accomplished singers and give intermittent vocal performances during the play. While a live band, including a saxophonist, trumpeter, keyboardist, bassist and drummer, gave an electrifying and dramatic background score to the play, Police told the story, quite sensationally, of a policeman whose sister gets raped by a known criminal who is shielded by the chief minister of the state. Even as the play played on something sinister — the criminal-police-politician nexus — the comic scenes involving the constable (played by Temudo) and a local cycle-repairman kept the audience rolling in the aisles.

"Comedy has become a compulsory aspect of tiatr these days, taking up as much as 75 per cent of the script, as the audience gets bored otherwise. Also, we know that the audience is smart and so we have to work hard on keeping the humour fresh so that the audience doesn't outwit us by guessing it all," says scriptwriter-director-actor Temudo, who has been involved with tiatr for over two decades and completed the 128th show of Police in the span of seven months, with his latest performance. But it doesn't stop here, as the group is all set to tour the UK, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain and Dubai, courtesy of the efforts of the Goan diaspora.

Heading: From industry captains to FM channels, Nano is theme of the day - Indian Express
Content:
Sasan Gir Maan Garje Sawaj, Dala Matthe Vanraj. Ache Hariyalu Gujarat. Game, Game Upwan shobe. Chede, Cheda Ugya Jhad. Ache Hariyulu Gujarat…

"In Sasan Gir roars the lion with long mane, this is green Gujarat; where every village flaunts a garden, every corner a tree, this is green Gujarat…" goes the song penned by Natwar Hadau Gujarat Ecological Education Research (GEER) Foundation and District Forest Officer (DFO) C N Patel. It is one of the many songs that have become popular in Junagadh and Bhavnagar districts, this Navratri.

For the first time in Gujarat, the state Forest Department has struck a different chord to spread awareness about the flora and fauna of the state during the ongoing Wildlife Week.

They have distributed more than 100 CDs containing garba songs in all the forest circles in the state and even a few garba organisers in Gandhinagar.

The Wildlife Week is celebrated from October 2 to October 8 and coincides with Navratri.

"Garba has its own cultural significance. This time, we decided to spread awareness about the ecology and environment through folk arts that are traditionally well known," said N P Majmudar, Public Liaison Officer (PLO), state Forest Department.

Renowned Kathiawadi folk singer Bhikhudan Gadhvi has sung the songs penned by Hadau and Patel. Hadau has been writing poetry about for quite sometime now.

The five garba songs contained in the CD are of more than 30 minutes duration.

They talk about the rich wildlife in Gujarat—from Ghudkhars (Wild Ass) of Kutch to the thick bamboo forests in the Dangs.

The Forest Department has, meanwhile, asked several forest officers to get feedback on the songs after nine days.

Heading: Family members cry foul over - Indian Express
Content:
Corporate groups see it as an opportunity to take the state's development further

Tata's decision to shift its Nano plant from Singur to Chharodi near Ahmedabad has given both the corporate groups in the state and the locals a reason to smile. While industry captains see it as an opportunity to take the state's development further, the general public consider it a matter of pride.

According to Gautam Adani, Chairman of the Adani Group, the move will provide a fillip to the engineering and auto ancillary industry in Gujarat besides opening up employment opportunities for a large number of skilled and semi- skilled individuals.

"Nano will also benefit by the extremely cost effective infrastructure facilities available in Gujarat," said Adani.

Parimal Nathwani, Group President (Corporate Affairs) of Reliance Industries Limited and a Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha), also welcomed the move to set up the plant at Chharodi.

He said: "Tatas and Gujarat were inseparable because of Tata's presence at Mithapur near Dwarka for several decades as Tata Chemicals. The entry of Nano into Gujarat would further boost prosperity and progress of both the Tatas and the people of Gujarat."

While the state government shook hands with the Tata Company, locals burst crackers to celebrate the arrival of the country's most economic car in their hometown.

"It is a matter of great pride. Gujaratis are fond of cars and Nano will be the most preferred vehicle in the coming days," said Anand Modi, a student of H L Commerce College.

Also, radio stations in the city did not miss out on the opportunity to celebrate the occasion in their own way. Jingles like "Nano lag gayi hai to manwa ma kasak hoi be kari" and "Nano ki mat suniyo re, nao thag lenge" kept on running on the air.

Jignesh Vasavda, Station Head of Radio Mirchi, said: "We are making parodies of the songs. The idea is to have complete fun. We are also taking views of locals to capture their happiness."

(With inputs from Tanvir Siddiqui)

Heading: Railway guard, two others arrested for parcels’ theft - Indian Express
Content:
Lawyer of Godhra case accused plans to approach NHRC

The death of Hussain Mohammed Dhobi, who was arrested under the Prevention of Terrorism Act (POTA) in connection with the Sabarmati Express carnage case, has once again raised a question mark on the medical services provided at the Sabarmati Jail.

Dhobi died on October 4 in the V S Hospital after being shifted from the jail for paralysis treatment. While the authorities claim that all inmates of the jail get proper medical treatment whenever needed, family members of the deceased and those who are ill accuse the state government of adopting a biased approach. Dhobi's family members allege that the jail authorities did not give him proper treatment until his condition became critical.

"Dhobi's is not the first case. Earlier also several representations were made about the improper medical services provided to the inmates. In 2003, the then POTA court judge Sonia Gokani had taken note of this problem and had instructed the jail authorities to ensure all possible medical assistance to the inmates," said advocate A A Hassan who is providing legal assistance to the accused.

He added: "An inquiry was also ordered in this connection. Now, we are planning to approach the National Human Rights Commission to ensure proper treatment and granting of bails on medical ground."

According to Hassan, of the 86 accused, 85 had filed bail application in March 2007. "A special bench was constituted to take up the bail applications. On September 30, when hearing into the case took place, the government pleader sought adjournment and it was granted. The next hearing is scheduled for October 16," he added.

Public prosecutor Sudhir Brahmbhatt, on the other hand, asserted there has been no lapse in the medical services provided to the accused. "At times, we have spent nearly Rs 5 lakh on treatment of a patient. Their health checkups take place on regular intervals. Interestingly, during video conferencing, those seeking bail give ill health of their family members as the reason."

Another official who is involved in the investigation told Newsline: "The medical services available at the Sabarmati Jail are very good. Death during the trial period is not something which is happening in the Godhra case alone. Every year, a large number of prisoners die in different jails, but when it comes to the Godhra case, things are different."

Patients in lock up

* Hussain Mohammed Dhobi – Suffered from paralysis and died on October 4

* Fakhruddin Yusuf Musalmaan (35) – Suffered from lung disease and died on April 20, 2003

* Siraj Abdullah Jamsa (30) – Suffered from blood cancer. He was granted bail and shifted to a private hospital in Vadodara where he died in December 2003

* Gulzar Agnu Ansari (22) – Suffered from Tuberculosis. He was given treatment after court order but died in 2008

* Yamohammed Shafi Mohammed Chhakda – Suffered from brain tumour and was operated for the same

* Idrish Charkha (33) – Suffering from Tuberculosis and is out on bail

* Mohammed Ansari Kutubuddin Ansari – Suffering from lung disease

Heading: Modasa blast: cops zero in on timeframe - Indian Express
Content:
The Railway Protection Force (RPF) claimed to have busted a racket of parcel thieves and arrested three people, including a railway guard, at Anand on Monday.

The three have been accused of stealing valuables from the parcels of coaches of different trains in the last few months. They been booked under the provisions of the Railway Property (Unlawful Possession) Act, and sent in police remand for seven days.

They have been identified as M A Qazi (41), his son Saeed Qazi (21) and Nirmal Sewakramani (47), all residents of Anand.

According to the RPF officers, M A Qazi is a railway guard whose job is to ensure the security of parcels carried in train coaches.

RPF officers said the accused were caught red-handed while they were stealing valuables from the parcel coach of the Rajkot-Secundarabad Express.

Inspector K D Patel said: "For the last 2-3 months, we were getting a lot of complaints of theft from the parcels in the railway coaches. Following this, we started keeping a vigil on the parcel coaches. We got a tip-off that M A Qazi is involved in the crime. So, we mounted surveillance on the trains in which he was posted as guard and caught him on Monday."

Patel said the three had adopted a sound modus operandi for stealing the contents of the parcels.

It was repacked in such a way that no one would know that the parcel was tampered with.

"Being the only guard, M A Qazi ensured an easy entry into the coach," said Patel.

After the arrest, the police also raided Qazi's residence in Anand and recovered several stolen valuables such as cardamom and clothes worth more than Rs 1 lakh. Patel said that investigations are now on to find out the role of the three in other such cases of theft from the railway parcels.

Heading: Surat ophthalmologist to be felicitated by Vyas - Indian Express
Content:
Police officers investigating the September-29 Modasa blast in Sabarkantha district, have received information that the bike on which the bomb was planted, was parked in the Suka Bazaar area between 8.30 pm and 9.10 pm.

They, however, said the information may not lead to a breakthrough, as the information is based on eye-witness accounts.

The blast that rocked the heart of the Muslim-dominated area of the town, had killed one person and injured around 10 others, just a few days before the festivals of Navratri and Eid.

A senior district police officer said: "Earlier, no one was ready to come out and speak to the police about who had parked the bike, or at what time it was parked. But now, people have given their account of the timeframe during which the bike was spotted at the place."

As per their account, it seems that the bike was parked between 8.30 pm and 9.10 pm, he added.

Attempts are now being made to find out those who may have seen the person who parked the bike, he said, adding, "Based on that information, we can make his sketch and reach the person who planted the bomb."

District Superintendent of Police R B Brahmbhatt, however, said: "This is an outcome based on the eyewitness accounts of people present in the Suka Bazaar area. But, nothing concrete has come out so far. We are also waiting for the FSL reports to establish the identity of the stolen bike was used in the blast."

The Improvised Explosive Device used in the blast was installed in one of the glove compartments of the bike.

Heading: Saurashtra oil merchants may be compelled to end strike - Indian Express
Content:
Dr Divyesh Shah, a city-based ophthalmologist and Medical Superintendent of the Old Civil Hospital in Surat, will be felicitated by State Health Minister Jay Narayan Vyas for his achievements in conducting the maximum number of cataract operations between April 2007 and March 2008.

Dr Shah (37) will be honoured on the occasion of World Sight Day on October 8. He conducted as many as 3,337 cataract operations over a span of one year.

In addition, he has also conducted 30,000 cataract surgeries and lens implantations during his medical job in the government sector for the last ten years.

The majority of patients who come to Dr Shah are tribal and poor people. The ophthalmic surgeries on these patients are conducted at Primary Health Care Centres, Community Health Care Centres and Civil hospitals in Ahwa, Vyara, and Surat.

Dr Shah said that he regularly visits tribal areas and also participates in the awareness programmes.

"I feel that to be felicitated by the State Health Minister is a big achievement for me. We submit the statistical data of the number of cataract surgeries conducted by us to the State Opthalmic Department in Ahmedabad every year," he said.

He added: "We conducted a survey in different villages in Uchhal taluka in Surat district a couple of weeks ago and found that around 400 people have cataract problems. We will send our vehicles to get the tribals for operations."

Heading: Traffic police block intersections to ease congestion - Indian Express
Content:
Fiifty-three marketing yards to resume work following poor response from Centre, piling up of stock

The strike by 53 marketing yards of Saurashtra region, which began on October 1 to protest against the Central government's policy to ban the export of edible oil, is now likely to be over in a day or two.

Two main reasons are being cited for the early pack up of this indefinite strike.

Firstly, the Centre has given a poor response to the ongoing agitation; and secondly, there has been a backlog of fresh crops at all the yards in Saurashtra due to the strike.

A yard president said on condition of anonymity that leaders of all the marketing yards of Saurashtra have been camping at Delhi for the last 3-4 days. But Union Agriculture Minister Sharad Pawar and Trade and Commerce Minister Kamal Nath have not given them even an opportunity to present their case.

On the other hand, with no selling taking place at the yards due to the strike, the crops are on the verge of getting spoilt. Many marketing yards have now threatened the agitators to start auctions from Wednesday.

The Visavadar yard, one of the major yards, began the auction of crops on Tuesday, signalling the end of the strike. At Amreli and Rajkot yards though, the auctions are yet to commence.

Hardevsinh Jadeja, president of the Rajkot Marketing Yard and the Marketing Yard Federation, which has given the call for the ongoing strike, said: "We are in Delhi and will meet the Prime Minister in the evening. Ministers Sharad Pawar and Kamal Nath could not meet us due to their busy schedules. We have decided to end the strike from Wednesday as we are hoping that the Prime Minister will accept our demand by either lifting the ban on the export of edible oils or by providing a high support price for groundnut crop."

He added: "We are hopeful and have been promised by other Congress leaders that our demands will be accepted. But even if the demands are not accepted, the strike must end by tomorrow because if the crops are not sold within a day or two, they will get spoilt. Our agitation is for the benefit of the farmers only. If they suffer as a result of the strike, then the agitation must stop immediately. The yard will start functioning normally from Wednesday onwards, and the auction of all the commodities will begin, including that of groundnut. If the Central government breaks its promise, we will decide on our future course of action accordingly."

Heading: To Nano or not to Nano, that is the question - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to ease congestion on the arterial roads, the traffic police blocked three intersections on the R C Dutt Road in the Alkapuri area of the city on Tuesday. The blockades, however, became a bone of contention between several vehicle owners and the traffic police, as many had to take a detour of 500 metres to reach their offices.

Joint Commissioner of Police Praveen Sinha said the move was initiated on the request of many commuters who had complained of difficulty in crossing these intersections.

"We have introduced these blockades on an experimental basis in order to avoid congestion, after a lot of people complained. We will have to see if it is a success and whether it ensures a smooth flow of traffic," he said.

In the afternoon, some businessmen blocked the road near the intersection close to Alkapuri to protest against the introduction of barricades.

According to the J P Road police, the commotion lasted for half an hour as a group of businessmen did not want to take the detour to reach to their shops. The police said that no one was arrested and the area was cleared off within half an hour.

Heading: Singur’s loss becomes Chharodi’s gain - Indian Express
Content:
As Chharodi was swaying to the drumbeats of percussionist Savabhai Kachrabhai Parmar on Tuesday to celebrate the Nano deal, Parmar himself was upbeat about it.

"I come with my drum whenever there is an occasion. But such occasions are rare and most of the time I end up doing casual labour to sustain my family," said Parmar. He said if Nano comes to Gujarat, his life will change.

Parmar is not alone in this exultation. But, there is a silent majority that has had bad memories of outsiders coming into the state and setting up manufacturing units with unfulfilled promises to offer jobs to locals. As for Parmar, he believes he will get any small job at the Nano factory and that will change his life for the better.

The land opposite Chharodi village on the other side of the highway will see the Nano factory come up.

With the Nano deal, expectations have soared among people. But all the rejoicing has more to do with the rekindled hopes of getting employment than Gujarat's winning the race for Nano.

No one, however, is sure about how many manual jobs the project will offer to the locals.

Nevertheless, celebration is in full blast. Television channels have also joined in the party.

On the flipside, Chharodi is in bad shape with essential services lying diseased, without maintenance. The place is littered with garbage, open drains, polluted water, courtesy chemical units nearby, and no road for a kilometre from the railway track.

Will the Nano change all of this and the lives of the locals after what the world sees as a landmark in the industrial history of Gujarat, is one question that has intrigued the public mind. As of now, the people are hovering between hope and despair.

Heading: Meanwhile, Nano leaves a trail of despair in Singur - Indian Express
Content:
As Nano drives into Ahmedabad's neighbourhood, locals hopeful of major job openings

Their smile could not get any wider when locals knew for sure that Singur's loss had ultimately become Chharodi's gain. But even before the Nano made its grand entry, local farmers had already signed the land transfer papers — much before Tata sealed the big deal in Gandhinagar on Tuesday.

With this, the small village — 25 km from Ahmedabad — has found a place for itself on the world's automotive industry map. Local farmers, many of them Muslims, virtually made a beeline and surrounded GIDC officials on the spot for signing documents to complete the land transfer procedure.

The interaction between villagers and officials had been going on for the last five days. The activity picked up pace with every passing day, and even before the Tatas could land at Ahmedabad on Tuesday afternoon, the GIDC officials were ready with their share of work — the complete paperwork.

Village sarpanch Nazir Pathan, who himself has parted with two acres, appeared the happiest man having liaised between government officials and the village folks. "So what if we are Muslims and our land goes for a project that is going to earn (Narendra) Modi credit… the development will reflect in the growth of our future generations," he said when asked as to what convinced him about the project that his counterparts in Singur have rejected.

Peer Khan, Hayat Khan Pathan and his brother Shamsher offered 18 bighas "for the sake of the overall development of the place" that they hoped would translate into job opportunities for locals. Paddy and wheat are the two crops taken here in two seasons and no one has any qualms about losing the yield of 80 maunds per bigha of wheat and 50 maunds of paddy.

"It is our good fortune that this place has been chosen for this ambitious project. Atleast the future of our coming generations is secure," said Pathan, whose words were endorsed by Kanuji Thakor, a fellow villager. Pathan said the villagers had been assured of jobs by the locals.

However, a few village seniors were a little apprehensive about such oral assurances. "The village panchayat should get the assurance in writing from the private company. Government officials or politicians cannot be trusted on this," said Babubhai Parmar, who had a bitter experience with a Korean multinational that had set up a unit in the vicinity.

He said the Korean firm had sacked him after he was injured while on duty. "I was not even allowed to enter the factory when I went there to plead my case," he added.

Expectations of getting jobs are high also because the success of agriculture here depends on Narmada waters for which farmers have to pay charges. Their experience with Anand Agricultural University in this regard is not very memorable either. "If there is no Narmada water, there is no other job apart from being employed as a casual labourer," said a government employee.

He further said there are certain things that would be discussed with villagers because disclosing them to outsiders might have a negative impact on village welfare.

Heading: How Modi’s men fought battle of wits… and won - Indian Express
Content:
A few days before the Pujas, the news that the Tatas are relocating their small car project in Gujarat has come as a rude shock to the people of Singur. It has not only tarnished the image of the town, its residents have also lost their jobs.

Many of them had hoped that despite Tata Sons Chairman Ratan Tata's announcement to shift the project, the company might change its decision. But with the joint announcement made by Tata and Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi about relocating the project to Gujarat, all hopes have been lost. Those who thought of earning a livelihood out of the project seemed demoralised.

"I was hopeful that I would support my family with the job provided by the Tatas, but now I do not know what to do," said Asim Ruidas, a youth of Beraberi Madhyapara. He had undergone an apprenticeship course organised by the West Bengal Industrial Development Board and the Tatas.

His brother Akul said: "We had hoped that the Tatas might come back later and resume the project. But now, since the factory is being shifted to Gujarat, all hopes are lost."

Manas Khatua, who runs a small tea stall at the main gate of the factory premises, is also clueless. "I had invested my entire savings to set up this shop. I thought that the stall would do well and I would later expand it. My main customers were Tata employees. I have lost my clients," he said.

The unwilling farmers are also demoralised. "We had hoped that if we got our land back, we would either resume farming or sell it off at a good price," said a farmer. The local CPM has not lost all hopes though. Dibakar Das, a local CPM leader, said: "We know that the Nano project has been shifted. But, Tatas never said they would not build any industry here. We will request the government to persuade the Tatas to set up any other industry here."

Locals are, however, not so optimistic. Sheikh Jiarul, a resident of Joymollah village who willingly gave his land for the project, said: " Some people are saying that the Tatas might set up something else here. But I think that the Tatas have gone forever, at least as far as Singur is concerned." The local youths, who supplied building materials and other minor items to the factory and the ancillary units, carried out a procession in Singur market on Tuesday. They sat on dharna outside the Tata factory's gate and decided to approach the Governor and the Prime Minister to intervene in the Singur issue. "We want the Tatas to come back," said Raju Mal, a youth.

Heading: Maiden Innings - Indian Express
Content:
With 20 films under his belt, at a reported fee of Rs 12 crore each, a new production house and political ambitions ahead, meet the new and improved Sanjay Dutt

A Career going great guns and a seemingly happy personal front, life is coming up roses for Sanjay Dutt. Kidnap, his first big film of 2008, released on Thursday and the actor has a long line-up of films like Blue, EMI and Aladin in the last quarter of the year.

Dutt has also turned a producer with the launch of his own banner, Sanjay Dutt Productions. Two films, an action adventure directed by Soham Shah and another action film directed by Milan Luthria, are scheduled to hit the floors next year.

Talks are also on with five more directors, which make it seven films in all. And Dutt will act in all of these.

The 49-year-old is also committed to a couple of film assignments for Balaji Films. In all, the actor has almost 20 films in various stages of production. "I'm very charged about life and want to do a lot of good work. Thankfully, I'm still getting it," he says with characteristic nonchalance.

There are other things that Dutt is contemplating. Promoting boxing is one, ever since Vijender Singh got home the medal from the Beijing Olympics. And trying his hand at politics is also on his wish-list, but that when the work pressure is less.

Directing a film is also part of his future plans. "I haven't yet thought about it seriously, but I will definitely be taking it up in the near future," he confides.

In Kidnap, the high action drama, has him essay a multi-millionaire whose daughter is held for ransom. The role is special for Dutt. It is for the first time that the actor is playing father to a teenage girl, close to his daughter's age. This is one of the reasons he was considered for the role.

"Sanjay Gadhvi saw me with my daughter Trishala on a show and said that he could think of no one but me to play the part."

"There are times in a person's life when all the money in the world can be of no use. Working for this high drama between father and daughter was a very emotional experience for me. I also enjoyed working with Imran Khan who I found to be a very confident actor and a grounded person," Dutt says.

The actor hotly denies that relations between him and his daughter are strained because of his marriage to Manyata.

"Trishala was with us in the Bahamas when I was shooting there for Blue, and even otherwise we are on the Net every day. She also shares everything she does with me. She is studying Forensic Sciences and just the other day she called to say that there was a dead body with a bullet in its head lying in front of her. She appeared so cool about it, but it really blew my mind," he smiles indulgently.

Heading: ‘When it comes to health, people like to spend less’ - Indian Express
Content:
Former cricketer Manoj Prabhakar is making the most of his beauty business

It's something you wouldn't think a former cricketer can be eloquent about. But Manoj Prabhakar speaks about pimples, acne and pigmentation with the same ease as he would if bowling a medium pacer! It's a role, the cricketer says he has slipped into rather effortlessly. "I have after all being doing this for 13 years now," tells Prabhakar who is the managing director of Naturence, a Delhi-based company that's into manufacture of beauty products and cosmetics. In Chandigarh to launch a new range and conduct a beauty workshop, Prabhakar was happy to dish out all you need to know about hair and skin treatments! "I am totally into beauty...you have to in order to run a successful beauty enterprise," says the former cricketer who along with wife and cosmetologist Farheen Prabhakar have been training beauticians across the country for many years now. "I don't address them as beauticians but as beauty doctors since they know skin and hair problems inside out," Prabhakar points out. So what got him interested in the business of beauty? To this the former cricketer bowls a straight answer: "It seemed like the right thing to do. With my wife being a well-known and well-travelled cosmetologist, we make a good team."

With an increasing number of cricketers deciding to air out their hidden talent, there's the likes of Sreesanth, Harbhajan and Irfan on a dance reality show on television to others making the most of Bollywood connections (remember Ajay Jadeja?), Prabhakar has been a trendsetter of sorts. "As long as a cricketer's focus is his game, there should be no eyebrows raised on his off the field activities," feels the bowler who hasn't really let go of his cricket. "Not many are aware but I am the coach for the Delhi Ranji team and I would like to be given responsibility for much more," the cricketer finally speaks up. But lots changed since his times. "Yes, there's ICL and IPL now. Though both might be at loggerheads, I feel it shouldn't be. The idea behind both is the same, why should the BCCI act tough with ICL players," he makes his opinions loud and clear. For someone who has had enough controversy to deal with, the player's moved on well. "I am straddling life both as a businessman and as a coach. Cricket will always be a part of my life. It's my first love after all," he says before heading off for the beauty workshop to elucidate on ways to deal with hair fall and dark under eye shadows!

Heading: Don of Design - Indian Express
Content:
The Avantha group, earlier known as the Thapar group, plans to invest Rs 100 crore in the next three years for expansion in the technology education sector in Punjab and Chandigarh.

Thapar University's director Abhijit Mukherjee said that the Thapar Technology Campus, comprising Thapar Polytechnic, Thapar Centre for Industrial Research and Development and the Thapar University, plans to expand its existing campuses in Punjab and Chandigarh and start some new courses.

Mukherjee said apart from taking the present student strength from 2,000 to 6,000 in the next three years, the Avantha group plans to set up a medical education centre in Dera Bassi, near Chandigarh. The group has 14 acres of land in Dera Bassi, where it plans to start health care management courses jointly with the PGI in Chandigarh.

Besides, it plans to start a new campus in Chandigarh's prestigious Education City project. The group is setting up its new campus in six acres of land, where new courses are set to start soon.

New courses in MBA (Energy), Social Sciences and MPhil in Economics and Psychology have also been proposed to start soon. Mukherjee announced the expansion plan at Thapar University's 22nd convocation, which was addressed by A Sivathanu Pillai, distnguished scientist and chief controller, Research and Development, DRDO and MD, Brahmos Aerospace.

Heading: Avantha group to invest Rs 100 crore in education sector - Indian Express
Content:
'First Resident Engineer of Chandigarh', Mahendra Raj, takes us through the making of this city

Let's go back 50 years. To the time of wilderness, greenery and patches of agricultural land. No concrete structures, no roads and no sectors. "Chandigarh was what a virgin land would look like," Mahendra Raj, the "First Resident Engineer of Chandigarh" and Structural Engineer for projects like The Punjab and Haryana High Court and UT Secretariat, rewinds to '49, when he first stepped on the land, which was to be the capital of Punjab. To the first "experiment" that Le Corbusier conducted and to the project that Raj was to spearhead as the Structural Engineer.

"Resources were limited and constraints many," he recalls how strategies and plans were chalked out to get a simple thing like cement and the way they got construction material rationed. Technology, a far-fetched word, here he stayed in Chandimandir and in tents to give shape to structures that now give the city its very character. "Open, peaceful and green," he defines the thought that went into the conceptualization.

The designs once decided on, the feasibility was for him and the Chief Engineer Gulzar Singh to check upon. "Unlike the way we can solve thousands of equations with a computer now, we could only analyze about eight to ten permutations and combinations,'' Raj, who is here from Delhi for Le Corbusier Memorial lecture at Chandigarh College of Architecture, tells us, as he heads to the all-new Le Corbusier centre and stops to give a long look to the sketches. "The modular dimensions developed by Corbusier were derived from the fully grown human body," he explains the drawings and reels how tough the making of sun breakers in front of the rooms of judges and the Chief Justice was.

Bringing about slight changes where required, Raj says, "Canopy parasol of the High Court was one such instance. The initial design of flying, cantilever shell roof had to be replaced by the present cantilever beam and slab structure on our insistence." Raj tells us those were the times when engineering took an independent turn and developed into full blown structuralism evident in several buildings of the '70s and '80s.

Ensuring that designs satisfy given design criteria, predicated on safety, serviceability and performance, "Creative manipulation of materials and forms, mass, space, volume, texture and light saw the inception of Chandigarh," Raj smiles and walks towards where his first office was in Sector 19 (now the PWD building), satisfied with the way the city has grown and progressed. "Despite all the pressure of population, politicians, bureaucrats, commerce and industry, it's holding well and will do so for many years to come." You heard him!

Heading: GMADA axe falls on four industrial plots - Indian Express
Content:
Cash and jewellery worth Rs 10 lakh were stolen from a house in Sector 10 today. The cash belonged to an NRI family from Austraila, who had come to attend a wedding in the city.

"We came to Panchkula four days ago to attend my brother-in-law's wedding, which was scheduled for Sunday. While the ceremony was on, we noticed a girl between 5 and 10 years, roaming around. Though we were a little suspicious, we ignored her thinking somebody must have invited her. My wife kept the bag on the chair to participate in the ceremony. After some time, however, we noticed both the girl and bag missing," said complainant Pradeep Verma.

He added that upon enquiry, it was found the girl had been seen leaving the room with a bag in her hand.

"It was then we realised that the bag had been stolen. While we have no records of the girl in the video tape, she is there in the photographs," he added.

A case has been registered into the matter. He also met Sandeep Khirwar, Superintendent of Police, Panchkula, and apprised him of the situation. Taking to Newsline, a police officer, on condition of anonymity, said the case has been registered and the police are investigating into the matter.

Heading: Trial proceedings awaiting apex court’s verdict adjourned - Indian Express
Content:
Cracking the whip on marriage palaces owners for the gross violation of allotment terms, the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) resumed four industrial plots in Mohali.

The resumption proceedings were also underway against another industrial plot in Phase VI, which was also being used as a marriage palace.

Confirming the action, GMADA Estate Officer (EO) Sukhjeet Pal Singh told Newsline that the resumption orders were issued after giving enough time to the allottees to comply with the allotment terms and conditions, failing which plots were resumed as provided in the allotment letters.

The resumed plots measure over 1 acre each and were allotted at meager prices in early 1980s but presently their cost was running into several crores each. They are situated on the National Highway-21 near Verka Milk Plant.

"The resumed plot owners were entitled to challenge the resumption orders before the Additional Chief Administrator, following which eviction proceedings will be initiated," said GMADA EO.

The use of marriage palaces in the resumed industrial plots was causing great hardship to the residents, who were constantly complaining of widespread nuisance and safety concerns due to largescale parking of vehicles on roadsides, loud music, use of liquor.

Heading: Make tree-plantation drive a mass movement: Badal - Indian Express
Content:
A Mohali Special Court on Tuesday adjourned till December 5 the ongoing trial proceedings in a corruption and disproportionate assets case against Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, his wife Surinder Kaur, son Sukhbir Badal (ruling Shiromani Akali Dal president and Faridkot MP) and others.

The case was registered in Mohali by the Punjab Vigilance Bureau during the previous Capt Amarinder Singh regime in June 2003.

None of the three members of the Badal family appeared in the court. While Badal senior and his wife Surinder Kaur were already exempted from personal appearance, Sukhbir was in Indonesia after taking prior permission from the court.

Following the appearance of the co-accused in the case, Special Judge S K Garg fixed December 5 as the next date for further proceedings in the trial of the case, awaiting the Supreme Court verdict in a petition filed by former Capt Singh seeking transfer and re-trial of the criminal case involving the Badals outside Punjab.

Already, the Supreme Court bench headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan had restrained the local Special Judge from recording statements of the accused under Section 313 of the CrPC till the final disposal of the petition.

Amarinder had submitted before the apex court that after Badal assumed power as the chief minister of Punjab, all senior counsels and special public prosecutors were withdrawn from the matter "in public interest". Amarinder had levelled personal allegations against the present public prosecutor claiming that the officer has committed "overt acts of sabotaging the case of the prosecution". He has submitted the court orders to prove his claim.

According to him, all the witnesses had turned hostile. "The public prosecutor has consciously given up crucial witnesses and the special court had recorded the statements of the public prosecutor to this effect.The investigating officer of the case has also turned hostile . The public prosecutor has done nothing to confront the investigating officer," Amarinder had stated in his affidavit.

Heading: Bomb scare in Panchkula again - Indian Express
Content:
Concerned over the increasing air pollution, Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal on Tuesday made a clarion call to make tree plantation a mass movement in the state. He urged the public and Forest department to join hands and make Punjab "clean and green".

Addressing a gathering after laying the foundation stone of Forest Complex, to come up over 2 acres of land at an estimated cost of Rs 38 crore in Sector 68, Badal emphasised the need to make the masses aware about the importance of trees in daily life. "We must strive hard to conserve our forests because deforestation at a largescale has resulted in imbalance in the eco-system," he said.

Badal asked officials of the Forests department to motivate people to plant trees to clean the environment that has been polluted by heavy emission of deadly industrial and other gases.

The chief minister also announced special prizes of Rs 5 lakh and Rs 2 lakh for the best green village and town selected through a statewide competition organised by the Forest department to encourage people to grow trees and inculcate the aesthetic sense to nurture them with utmost care.

Badal regretted that most of Punjab's area under the forest cover had gone to Himachal Pradesh after reorganisation of the state in 1966. "It is high time to plant trees on a large scale to strike a balance in ecology besides protecting the environment from global warming," he said.

Cooperation Minister Capt Kanwaljit Singh said that the new forest complex would be instrumental to encourage the masses to adopt the green building technology in order to popularise the concept of clean and green environment.

In his address, Forest Minister Tikshan Sood said the new forest complex will be constructed on the principles of green philosophy to propagate the concept of "Green Building Design" to preserve and protect the environment.

Forest Complex

* Height: 100 feet (7 storeys)

* Comprise: Conference Hall, Training Centre, Forests and Wildlife Gallery, Document Centre

* Supervision: Punjab Small Industries and Export Corporation

* Quality Control: Punjab Engineering College

* Completion Date: November 30, 2009

Heading: That’s IIT! - Indian Express
Content:
An abandoned suitcase found at one of the busy traffic junctions of the city in Old Panchkula, near Suraj Theater, generated panic among commuters on Tuesday. The bomb disposal squad was rushed to the spot and the entire area was cordoned off. It was, however, found later that the bag contained cheque books in the name of a Chandigarh-based resident.

"A call was received at the police control room that a bag was found lying at the Old Panchkula Chowk, near Suraj Theater. A team, led by Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Ram Chandra Rathi along with the station house officer, Sector 5, Ajab Singh, reached the spot and got the area cordoned off. The bag was searched but no explosive was found in it," said a police official.

Heading: Insurance firm to pay Rs 2 lakh compensation - Indian Express
Content:
Visiting about 200 educational institutes across India, students of IIT Kharagpur stop by in the city and invite all to their annual fest Kshitij

If the world has become a global village, India is just a small colony in it, one which students trot across to participate in the fest of other colleges and to invite them. With PEC sending delegations across the country to invite all to their annual fest, this time round we have visitors from as far as Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur, giving the invites for their fest 'Kshitij'. "I have visited colleges in Punjab, now I am heading to colleges in Chandigarh," says Ashish Modi, member of the core organising team of Kshitij, as he hands out a brochure to us, which is complete with over 45 events, guest lectures and workshops packed in a span of four days.

Starting on January 29 to February 1, they tell us, like last year they are expecting over 3500 outstation and 6000 internal participants. "With prize money worth Rs 50 lakh to be won, students from various IITs, IIMs and NITs along with from Stanford and Princeton University among others have been visiting us since the inception of the fest in 2004," he says they see a lot of participation from Chandigarh and Punjab. "Students here are very talented and so we try to rope in as many as possible," he smiles.

Providing a melting pot to intermingle, collaborate to conceive and execute ideas, plans and presentation and to show and see talent, Modi says here students get to know about new cutting edge technologies and managerial methodologies being used world wide. "From categories like coding, mechanical, electronics, structures, robotics, entrepreneurial, quizzing to new events like car design, refrigeration, senate, zero hour to el dorado we will have et all," he reels. For the computer junkies, they have hack and kryotech as the new additions.

With online registrations open for Kshitij 2009, the deadline for the first round of submissions is December 16. As for the online events like woodstock and forex, they start on October 15. For more information log on to ktj.in.

Heading: Hospital-acquired infections to be compiled at PGI - Indian Express
Content:
Made in Heaven

There is an extraordinary love story in every ordinary Jodi. So goes the tagline of Aditya Chopra's Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi. We bring you the first look of this yet another romantic flick from the Yash Raj stable. Written and directed by Aditya Chopra, who makes a comeback after his DDLJ, the film stars Shahrukh Khan, Anushka Sharma, Anupam Kher, Fardia Jalal and Vinay Pathak. We hear Kajol makes a special appearance and that King Khan will be seen in a double role. Here's looking forward to double mazaa!

Heading: Retired from Admn? You might have to vacate govt houses - Indian Express
Content:
With no objective data available on the infections acquired by patients while undergoing treatment at the PGI, the institute has decided to compile the data in a monthly bulletin format. The PGI has a Hospital Acquired Infections Control Committee to monitor such infections.

Talking to mediapersons, medical superintendent of PGI, Professor A K Gupta said that institutes like AIIMS, New Delhi, have already compiled such data for closer monitoring.

"Though no reliable data of hospital-acquired infections is available for Indian hospitals, there are estimates that if these infections are brought down by just one per cent, health expenditure to the tune of Rs 6000 to 7000 crore annually could be saved in the country," said Prof Gupta, claiming that the PGI has a reasonably lower rate of infections due to the hygienic environs.

In the USA, added the professor, as many as 80,000 patients lose their lives annually due to hospital-acquired infections.

"According to the WHO, such infections should not be more than 2 per cent of the total cases as some infections are inevitable in the hospital wards. But we would see from our objective data, how much deviation is observed from the set standards," added Professor Gupta.

It is patients in the ICUs, including cancer patients, burns and accident victims and gynecology patients, who face a higher risk of acquiring infections due to the nature of treatment, which either involves greater use of instruments and incisions or the patients have low immunity.

Two-day conference on administration from Saturday

Nearly 400 delegates from various corners of the country are expected to participate in the two-day long national conference being organised by the department of hospital administration, PGI, beginning on Saturday. The focus areas include — recent trends in hospital administration, strengthening of healthcare institutions, hospital disaster management, role of the hospital administration in the control of HIV and outsourcing of hospital services.

Tussle for faculty positions at premier hospital continues

With the last date for application for the post of professor and assistant professor at the Cardiology department of the PGI having expired on October 4, the controversy regarding the promotion of faculty refuses to die. With the advertisment of new posts of faculty, the case of the present head of the department, Dr Yash Paul Sharma, continues to remain unclear. So much so, that the HoD has submitted various representations with the authorities, to expedite his case.

Sharma was the sole candidate to have appeared for the selection of additional professor and professor, after the institute advertised for the same last year. Representing his case, Sharma argued that since he was the only candidate to have faced the board and was eligible for both the posts of additional professor and professor, his name should be considered for the same, before taking new people. Sharma, who is now the additional professor, in his representation to the Director Prof K K Talwar, had quoted instances where interviews were held for promotions even when the candidates expressed their inability to attend the personal interviews. The PGI Director, meanwhile, was unavailable for comments.

Heading: Tapping row: HC disposes petition; judges switch to BSNL after SC order - Indian Express
Content:
In wake of the increasing waiting list for government accommodations, UT Home Secretary Ram Niwas has asked Assistant Estate Officer Ashwani Kumar to draft a proposal according to the house allotment rules so that the backlog for government houses' allotment could be cleared.

"Once an officer is retired from the post, he or she should surrender the official accommodation and apply afresh, after he or she has got another post-retirement position in any department in the city," said Ram Niwas.

At present, according to official figures, there are nearly 33 such government accommodations, which are occupied by officers, who though have retired from the UT but have retained their houses as they have been reappointed in some other position.

The Chandigarh Administration is contemplating on barring such a practice by senior officials. "For instance, even if an officer, after retirement from a post in UT, joins any other department such as Information Commission or any other government position, he looses the right of staying in the same government accommodation. Apply afresh, get in the queue and if your turn comes, take the official accommodation," explained Niwas. While talking to the mediapersons at the UT Secretariat, Ram Niwas mentioned that he has received requests from various people, who are entitled to have official accommodations, but have been waiting in the queue for years.

Heading: ‘We faced political pressure while building city’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court judges have switched over to Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) from Airtel. This is, however, not due to the so-called apprehension of their (judges) mobile phones being tapped by any investigating agency, as wrongly reported by one of the English dailies.

The news report which appeared on August 30 under the head "Judges feel bugged", was rubbished by the governments of Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh. Terming the news as totally unfounded, the Chandigarh Administration had rubbished the tall claims of the English daily. An affidavit was also filed by Inspector General (IG) of Police S K Jain on behalf of the UT Administration.

The news report had claimed that post the judge-bribery case, a few High Court judges were suspicious that their mobile phones were being tapped. A new series of mobile phone numbers of BSNL had been given to the High Court judges last week. As per sources, the new numbers have been given in light of a Supreme Court directive which holds that government services should be availed by the judges and not due to any apprehension.

One of the judges of the High Court had taken suo moto notice of the news report after which it was sent to the Court of Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur. The suo moto notice was treated as a petition and notices were issued to Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh. Taking on record the replies of the three states denying any ounce of truth in the news report, the division bench of the High Court headed by the Chief Justice has disposed of the petition.

While disposing of the petition, the division bench headed by the Chief Justice observed that there is indeed no basis for the report and no directions are required to any of the governments on this issue.

Claiming that the apprehension had set alarm bells ringing in the High Court, the news report without mentioning any state agency simply stated "some state agency has not only placed the incoming and outgoing numbers of judges under surveillance, but is also listening to their conversations. The issue has become the talk of the High Court".

The High Court judges had been using Airtel services till date. Their previous Airtel connections will be disconnected in a short while.

Reiterating the stand taken by the Punjab government that no mobile phone of any judge has been tapped, the Haryana government had also submitted the same. S K Joshi, IAS, Special Secretary to Haryana government, had filed a reply confirming that no phone of any judge has been tapped.

The petition has been finally disposed of by the High Court with the finding that there was indeed no basis for the news item.

Heading: Vacant OBC seats: After SC directive, PU awaits written order - Indian Express
Content:
Mahendra Raj, delivered a memorial lecture on Le Corbusier, at the Chandigarh College of Architecture, Sector 12, as a part of the Chandigarh Heritage Festival today.

He said: "We resisted a lot of political pressure while building the city and selecting its site. Now, it's for the future generation to fight the pressures created at all the corners in the city. The relevance of Chandigarh lies in the fact that it is a symbol of modern architecture for the whole of India."

He added: "The modular concept was developed by Corbusier just three years before the start of the Chandigarh project and I had problems in understanding the concept due to its tedious dimensions and controls set by the master architect himself."

Eminent architect Sen Kapadia, made a presentation on the architectural works undertaken at various places.

The Principal Prabhawalkar memorial award was awarded to Mayank Ojha, while the Anita Sharma Memorial award for the overall topper was presented to Jasmeet Kahlon.

Heading: Upgraded, but most govt schools still without principals - Indian Express
Content:
The implementation of the 7 per cent Other Backward Classes (OBC) quota (the first phase of the prescribed 27 per cent) has made the admission process at the Panjab University a tediously long process.

While the Supreme Court guidelines direct that seats, left vacant, have to be converted into general seats, the Panjab University authorities are still awaiting written orders for the same.

The Supreme Court's guidelines on converting the vacant seats into general category seats had raised hope among aspirants seeking admissions in the university.

Talking to Newsline, Professor R C Sobti, vice-chancellor, Panjab University, said, "We are going by the law and are waiting for any written orders by the University Grants Commission, following which we shall go ahead and convert the vacant seats."

The implementation of the quota has already delayed admissions in the varsity, and with the classes having started, those still seeking admissions are at the losing end.

Ankur, one of the students seeking admissions said, "The Supreme Court has announced that the vacant seats can be converted, but with the Panjab University not doing the same, it is a loss for the students."

The university has, meanwhile, postponed the exams to give students extra time for preparations.

Heading: 75% attendance minimum for taking exam - Indian Express
Content:
More than a year after some government high schools were upgraded to the level of senior secondary schools, they are still functioning without institution heads. While officials from the Education department say that principals will be appointed soon, those working as headmasters in these schools are unhappy with the delay.

Government high schools located in Sarangpur, Behlana, Khuda Lahora, Kaimbwala and Raipur Khurd were elevated as senior secondary schools last year. As per rules, all the schools of the senior secondary level should have principals to manage their affairs. But some of these schools do not even have the post of a principal, leave aside anyone assuming the office.

While the Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sarangpur, has Mohinderjit Kaur working as the Headmistress, the school in Behlana has Ramesh Kumar officiating as the Headmaster against a non-existent post.

"It has been more than a year that the school was elevated to the senior secondary level and I continue to work as its Headmaster. They have neither promoted me nor appointed any principal for the school," says a principal requesting anonymity.

Government Senior Secondary School, Kaimbwala, too does not have the post of a principal, though Surinder Kaur is the officiating head. Similar is the case of Government Senior Secondary School, Khuda Lahora, where Amita Khanna is the head.

Taking note of the situation, Vinod Sharma, president, Government Teachers' Union said that regular appointments should be made at the earliest.

"Any school without a principal is bound to suffer. The department should make selections as per the Departmental Promotions Committee so that these schools improve," said Sharma.

Talking about the issue, Director Public Instructions (School) Samwartak Singh said that the department will work on the issue after receiving the details.

Heading: Terrorist activities will hit tourism sector: Ambika - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has issued notifications to all the heads of its affiliated institutions that students from Classes IX to XII must maintain a minimum of 75 per cent attendance in order to be eligible for taking the promotion examinations.

The circular, dated September 22, states, "No student from a school affiliated to the Board shall be eligible to take the examination unless he has completed 75 per cent of attendance counted from the opening of class IX/X/XI/XII up to the first of the month preceding the month in which the examination commences in the subject of internal assessment."

Anu Kumar, Principal, Stepping Stones School, Sector 37, says, "We do face attendance problems from students, particularly of Class XII, since they have coaching classes to attend simultaneously. But we are strict with the 75 per cent attendance rule. Students should realise the significance of being regular. The orders are in the right spirit."

The order has clearly mentioned that every year in February and March, the Board receives letters from a large number of candidates with pleas to the chairman to consider shortage of attendance.

The notice further states that a shortage of only upto 15 per cent of attendance may be condoned by the chairman, on the recommendation of the principal of the school.

"The candidates/parents while representing the matter to the Board invariably state that their school has never informed them about the shortage of attendance. In view of this, the condition of completion of 75 per cent attendance should be brought to the notice of candidates as well as parents," reads the notification.

Students, however, are not happy with the guidelines as they find it difficult to shuttle between school and private tuitions.

"I have to attend coaching classes also, some of which are held during school hours. Since I am preparing for competitive examinations, I cannot afford to miss them. No matter how hard I try, it is difficult to attend school most of the time," says Mohit Bansal, a student of Class XII.

Heading: At heritage walk, Rodrigues bats for active participation to preserve city’s splendid culture - Indian Express
Content:
Inaugurates tourism complex at Attari border

Union Minister of Tourism and Culture Ambika Soni today said terrorist activities would definitely hit the inflow of foreign tourists to the country. Soni, accompanied by Punjab CM Parkash Singh Badal, today inaugurated a tourist complex, Aman Umeed Bhawan, at Attari-Wagah border. She said as safety of foreign tourists was their prime concern, the police departments in all states have been directed to be extra-vigilant.

When asked about the decline in number of tourists visiting India in the wake of the blasts, she said they were compiling data and as terrorism has affected the world, India could not remain unaffected. "But this gives us a strong resolve to fight terrorism and join hands with the countries facing similar problem. I also welcome the statement of Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari that terrorists are operating in Jammu and Kashmir," she said.

Badal said the tourist complex, constructed at a cost of over Rs 1.2 crore, would give a fillip to the tourism sector. "We have a number of other projects lined up, including integrated joint border checkpost and institute for hotel management," Soni said.

Badal, who was accompanied by his cabinet entourage of Hira Singh Gabria, Bikram Singh Majithia and Gulzar Singh Ranike and BJP MP Navjot Singh Sidhu, said they would provide land to any new project started in the area. Badal said the border residents have suffered a lot ever since Partition and later during Indo-Pak wars, but now friendship with Pakistan would prove to be a boon for tourism and trade between the two countries.

The complex, built on about 10,000 square feet with facilities for domestic as well as foreign tourists, especially from Pakistan, would help in further promoting peace between the two countries, said Soni. She added that tourism has vast potential in employment generation and the Centre would provide all the help required to establish a convention centre in Punjab.

She said Amritsar has been selected as one of the mega destinations, out of the 22 identified by the Ministry of Tourism in the country, for integrated development. She said the Union Ministry of Tourism has earmarked Rs 4,802.32 lakh during the Tenth Five Year Plan and Rs 1,983.42 in the first two years of the Eleventh Five Year Plan for Punjab. She said private-public-partnership (PPP) was the new mantra for tourism growth and the 2010 Commonwealth Games would change the face of the industry with new mega-projects coming up in Delhi and outside that would provide jobs to three lakhs youths. She said the Visitors' Gallery at Attari border that receives about 20,000 tourists daily would be further widened.

'Party keeping an eye on Bir'
