He spoke to Police Commissioner Satyapal Singh and Deputy Commissioner of Police Satish Khandare and Assistant Commissioner of Police RS Khaire and requested the police to leave the court premises to restore sanity. The lawyers roughed up many policemen before pushing them out of the court premises, said policemen standing outside the court premises.

Angry lawyers also shouted slogans condemning the policemen. DCP Khaire, DCP Khandare and ACP Pote met judges presenting the court and discussed how the situation could be brought under control. The policemen were equally seething with rage and told reporters outside the court that they will not tolerate the lawyers' behaviour.

The entire drama began when assistant police inspector Ashok Randive was roughed up by advocate Rajendra Shinde and some other lawyers accompanying him on Saturday. API Randive was taken before the principal judge by the lawyers. In a retaliatory on Sunday night, as many as 100 policemen in 15 vehicles swooped down on the Parvati home of advocate Shinde and arrested him while he was in his underwear. He was booked under section 353 of the Indian Penal Code for obstructing a government servant on duty. When Shinde was brought to the court premises on Monday ,he was crying loudly and alleging the police had thrashed him severely during interrogation.

Heading: Bharati Vidyapeeth’s D.Litt to Prez Patil - Indian Express
Content:
A survey conducted by Sudhakar Kunte of the department of statistics, University of Pune, has concluded that astrology cannot be considered a science.

An initiative by Kunte, the survey supplied astrologers with 200 horoscopes in random order. "Hundred out of the 200 horoscopes belonged to intelligent people and the remaining 100 to mentally challenged persons. The astrologers, with the help of the horoscopes, were supposed to predict various factors, such as the intelligence and sex of the person that the horoscope belonged to.

The results, however, compelled us to conclude that astrology is not a science. The findings of this survey hardly support the claim of the predictive power of astrology on the basis of the horoscope, at least for the question regarding the intelligence of the person." Kunte said while announcing the results at a press conference here on Tuesday.

Refuting that the survey was conducted with a preconceived notion, Dabholkar said, "We have tried to prove this on the basis of science. Further, if astrology can predict the future of a person, it should also be able to say what his or her past was, he said. "We are open to astrologers approaching us to prove if they can tell us about people's past."

Commenting on the seminar organised by Nandakumar Jakatdar of Brahan Maharashtra Jyotish Mandal to challenge the survey, Dabholkar said, "If astrology is to establish itself as a science, it cannot escape validation by surveys like ours. Further, this is the conclusion of this survey and we are open to conduct more surveys. The results might be different and we are open to the possibility."

The astrologers, however, have a different take on the issue. Meanwhile, in another press conference, Siddheshwar Maratkar, an astrologer who participated in the survey, said, "Astrology as a science depends upon a number of factors. There are times when even the predictions by so-called scientific methods fail. This does not mean that the science is no longer a science. Statistics and numbers cannot be applied to astrology."

Heading: PMC completes Baner subway in record time - Indian Express
Content:
The Bharati Vidyapeeth Deemed University will confer Doctor of Letters (D.Litt) Degree to President Pratibha Patil during their 10th convocation ceremony on Sunday. Governor of Maharashtra S C Jamir and Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh will be the guests of honour at the function.

Nineteen students will be presented the gold medal and 21 students will be awarded the Degree in Philosophy. A total of 3,217 students have registered for the convocation, said vice chancellor of the University Shivaji Kadam.

Patil will attend the centenary birth celebrations of Sant Tukaram at Dehu and platinum jubilee celebration of Sadhana weekly at Balgandharva Rand Mandir on October 11 and inaugurate the Commonwealth Youth Games at Balewadi on October 12.

Patil will also visit Gawdewadi village in Ambegaon Taluka near Manchar on Pune-Nashik highway — which had been awarded Indira Priyadarshini Vrikshamitra Award, Nirmal Gram Puraskar and Mahatma Gandhi Tantamukta Ahiyan Award — to witness various development projects like vermicompost, percolation tanks and types of bunds. "The President will also interact with a few reverse migrants from the village," said Mohan Dharia, president of Vanrai, a non-governmental organisation, that was instrumental in the development of the village.

Patil is also expected to visit the village school's computer laboratory, interact with self-help groups and visit the gram panchayat office.

Heading: CYG baton arrives to a grand welcome - Indian Express
Content:
The Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) officials are glad as they have managed to complete the Baner subway, along with the necessary road work in the city, in time. The Baner subway was hailed as the most daunting task before the civic body among all development works planned ahead of the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG). In order to complete this project, the PMC had even sought help from the private developers, whose 1,000 labourers worked day and night to complete the mission.

The subway has been constructed under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) and has cost Rs 7.26 crore. The subway measures 41 metres long, 23.5 metres wide and 5.5 metres high. This has facilitated the vehicles to cross the national highway without dangerously posing any obstacle to the highway traffic.

The construction has been done in compliance with the Indian Roads Congress (IRC) standards, which means that even large and heavy vehicles like a double-decker bus or big trailer can easily pass through it. Addressing the mediapersons on Monday night, during the site visit, Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi lauded the efforts put in by the civic departments. "All the civic departments — land acquisition, electricity and garden — worked in sync with each other. Therefore, the work could be finished in time," Pardeshi said.

PMC city engineer Prashant Waghmare said that the PMC has completed the task in about seven months. "The work order was given in February. Though the work had been given to a contractor, we employed additional labourers in the final phase of the subway. The contractor's labourers were 450, while the labourers from the private developers were about 1,000. We had to employ machinery on a large scale. There were 40 JCB machines and 15 transit mixers."

He added, "It was only after 17 days of laying the slab of the subway, we confidently allowed the traffic to move above, whereas normally the road is opened to public only after 28 days. This was because, the slab got more than the required strength in a quick time."

Heading: Signal Group celebrates 11th Raising Day - Indian Express
Content:
Heavy rain on Tuesday afternoon did not deter Puneites from giving a grand welcome to the Youth Baton Relay of Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG). A procession of cyclists carrying flags of 71 participating countries brought the baton into the city from Khadki cantonment area.

Thousands of school students from various schools carrying placards with messages related to environment conservation like save tiger and globalisation were standing en route the YBR. The children gave a loud cheer and claps when Jigrr, the CYG mascot, waved out to them. The baton was then sported on 71 boats carrying flags of 71 participating countries that travelled from Harris Bridge at Dapodi to Bund Garden. MP Suresh Kalmadi, his wife Meera Kalmadi, Mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosale and others led the boats. Groups of curious onlookers were standing at strategic locations hours before the boats reach Bund Garden. While many got to witness them, some others standing opposite Rajiv Gandhi Hospital in Yerawada and nearby areas were disappointed for not being able to see it.

After this, the relay passed by Deccan College, Alandi Road, Airport Road, Gunjan Talkies chowk, Aga Khan Palace, Ramwadi octroi post, Wadgaonsheri, Chandan Nagar, Kharadi, Magarpatta Road, Hadapsar, Fatima Nagar, Wanavdi, Ghorpadi, Koregaon Park, Wadia College chowk, Pune Station and reached B J Medical ground. The baton halted at Rajeev Gandhi Zoological Park in Katraj. The baton relay came to the city after traversing thousands of kilometres across nine states. It completed its 67-day journey that began from New Delhi on August 1 and will head for the final venue at Balewadi on October 12.

On October 9, there will be a grand carnival starting from Baburao Sanas ground to Balewadi. The route is — Bajirao Road, Vishrambaug Wada, Vishrambaug Wada, Laxmi Road, Alka Talkies chowk, Deccan, F C Road, Agriculture College, Pune University, Aundh and Baner.

Heading: Capgemini wins football c’ship - Indian Express
Content: Ghorpadi-based Signal Group celebrated its 11th Raising Day on Sunday. Brig Ajeet Bajpai, Commander of the group, inaugurated the event which comprised games organised for the families of jawans attached to the group. Col (retd) H N Shivakumar, the first Dy Cdr of the group, raised on October 5, 1998, and his wife were present on the occasion. The Signal Group was raised by Brig (retd) R K Bhatia in Madhya Pradesh and has since participated in Operation Vijay and Operation Parakram. It also won laurels during the largest military exercise held by the Southern Command this year.

Heading: ‘Armed forces, industries need common platform’ - Indian Express
Content:
Capgemini beat Mphasis 4-3 in the tiebreaker to win the OM Developers sixth inter-Information Technology football championship trophy organised by the Maharashtra Krida held at the Range Hills Football Ground, Khadki, on Saturday.

Both teams were deadlocked at a goal apiece at the end of regulation time.

Stanley Fernandes gave Mphasis the lead after scoring a good goal in the 10th minute of the game. Dhirendra Kumar then equalised for his team in the dying minutes of the game to take the match into

penalties.

Heading: IMA’s new building to be inaugurated tomorrow - Indian Express
Content:
The armed forces, research and development organisations and the private industry need to work together on a common platform and facilitate better collaboration, Southern Command General Officer Commanding-in-Chief Lt Gen Noble Thamburaj said here on Tuesday.

"Research and development organisations and the industry need to explore new areas and generate innovative polymer-based technological solutions for the armed forces," Thamburaj said during a seminar on 'Applications of polymers in defence,' organised by the defence sub-committee and polymer sub-committee, in collaboration with the Mahratta Chamber of Commerce, Industries and Agriculture (MCCIA). Pointing out that polymers were a crucial component of several defence-related applications, he said the recent technological advancements in this field and invention of new materials, particularly nanocomposites, have opened up new possibilities. "It is essential that defence equipment is constantly upgraded by incorporating state-of-the-art technology and 'new age' material to pull off a technological asymmetry over hostile elements," Thamburaj said.

Reiterating this viewpoint, S Radhakrishnan, deputy director, National Chemical Laboratories (Sc 'G'), said, "Modern warfare involves a lot of state-of-the-art technology, which requires various hi-tech materials that contains polymers."

Heading: Dist election office announces final voters list - Indian Express
Content:
This Dussehra, doctors under the aegis of the Indian Medical Association (IMA) will move into their new building at Tilak Road. The new IMA building will have modern equipment and facilitate the coordination of community training programmes as several specialists' and doctors' associations are located here.

Speaking to media persons, Dr Avinash Bhondwe, president of the city unit of IMA, and Dr Devendra Shirole, president of the Maharashtra unit of IMA said a function has been organised on Thursday to officially inaugurate the new building.

Dr Jayant Navrange, secretary, IMA, the Pune branch of the association has entered its 80th year of existence and over the years played an important role by organising conferences, training programmes and encouraging doctors in various activities.

There are plans to introduce new programmes like training in resuscitation during accidents and tie-ups have been planned with KEM hospital and others.

Meanwhile, the IMA has decided to intensify its agitation against assault on doctors and will strike work on October 10, Dr Shirole said. Citing recent instances like destroying hospital property and humiliating hospital staff at Malad,Amravati, Beed and Chandrapur, Shirole said the IMA has urged doctors to shut their OPDs on October 10. However emergency services will not be affected. "We are concerned about the safety of doctors. They need to be assured of a safe environment to provide relief to patients," he said.

IMA doctors have demanded and urged Home Minister R R Patil to bring out an ordinance in Maharashtra taking a cue from other states.

Heading: International award for Harbinger Group - Indian Express
Content:
The district election office announced the final voters list in the district as 57.08 lakh on Tuesday. The election office is also planning to issue notices in a week to sort out repetition of names. With 21 assembly constituencies after the delimitation, the final list of Pune was announced after checking additions, deletions, corrections and transfer from one constituency to the other. Officers in the election department said that the draft rule had 54,81,885 voters and after addition of 2,54,673 voters, the total went upto 57,08 445. 28,113 names were deleted from the voters list. On Tuesday, the list was publicised at various polling stations and from Wednesday it would be publicised at the Pune Municipal Corporation(PMC) and Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC).

For the 10 constituencies in the rural areas, the list will be put up at the tehsildar's office and the Sub Divisional Office.

Heading: Indira Group excels among business schools - Indian Express
Content:
Harbinger Group, Pune, a global provider of software products and services, has won the gold award at the 2008 Learning in Practice awards sponsored by the Chief Learning Officer magazine. The prestigious CLO Learning in Practice Awards program recognizes those industry vendors and leaders who have demonstrated excellence in the design and delivery of workforce learning and development programs. The award was handed to Harbinger at the Fall 2008 Chief Learning Officer Symposium held in San Diego, California last month.

Harbinger won the award for "Clinical Challenges," an innovative online learning project with Philips Healthcare, pioneering gaming in healthcare education. The objective of Philips while conceptualising "Clinical Challenges" was to create a learning environment that would leverage cognitive benefits of game-based learning, in a manner that is cost-effective and rapid to build. Harbinger partnered with Philips to provide the technology and services that fulfilled this objective.

"With the help of Harbinger's thought leadership on game based learning development and its innovative product Raptivity, Philips has started a new paradigm in providing a unique learning experience in healthcare, " said Vikas Joshi, chairman and managing director of Harbinger Group.

Heading: Max New York ties up with Pune co-op bank - Indian Express
Content:

Indira Group received the maximum number awards amongst all the participating business schools across the country. In all, Indira Group won awards in over 14 different categories.

Indira Group chairperson Tarita Mehendale accepted the prestitious best busienss school award from Harish Mehta, chairman,Onwards Technologies on the occasion.

Other prominent awards which were bagged by Indira include the Visionary Award for chairperson Tarita Mehendale, best teacher general and strategic management award for Group director Chetan Wakalkar and Renu Bhargava, director, Indira School of Business Studies.

The other awards include:

* Best teacher human resources : Renu Bhargava

* Best teacher marketing management – Pandit Mali

* Best placement brochure contest: Indira Group of Institutes.

Heading: ‘Quality education is a fundamental right’ - Indian Express
Content:
Max New York Life Insurance, a leading life insurance companies and the Pune Peoples Co-operative Bank have announced a strategic referral tie-up. Max New York Life Insurance will utilise the branch network of the bank to sell its life insurance products. The tie up with Pune Peoples Co-operative Bank will further strengthen Max New York Life Insurance's presence in Pune and adjoining districts, stated a release.

Max Life Insurance's products will be sold through a network of 14 branches of The Pune Peoples Co-operative Bank. This alliance enables Max New York Life Insurance to reach its customised life insurance solutions to more than 20, 0000 customers of Pune Peoples Co-operative Bank. With deposit base of Rs 345 crores and loans to the tune of Rs. 171 crores, the bank has a share capital of Rs. 4.98 crores. The key objective of the bank has been to serve the people by providing financial assistance., release said.

Heading: Go for upgradation, SMEs advised - Indian Express
Content:
Padma Bhushan advocate P P Rao has emphasised the need of quality education which is fundamental right but which needs to be based solely on merit.

"Rural areas need more schools, better teachers and better facilities so that those children can come into the main stream and contribute to country's growth," he said at a discourse on "Constitution -- then and now" held at the New Law College, BVU, recently.

Highlighting the importance of the Indian Constitution, Rao praised the leaders who drafted the Constitution after great deliberations.

He however lamented that the great document "has not been able to contain the menace of terrorism which is growing in the country."

Mukund Sarda, dean and principal of the New Law College and director of foreign cell Jagannath Patnaik were present on the occasion. Rao was introduced by the principal and felicitated by Patnaik. Rao also interacted with the students of the college.

Heading: ‘Pick-and-choose’ taint on Tehbazari drive - Indian Express
Content:
SME's should upgrade from being a mere component manufacturer to system developers and should play a greater role in the indigenous manufacturing of various systems and sub-systems for use of defence establishments, said V K Saraswat, scientist and chief controller, R&D (MSS). He was delivering the keynote address at the DEMA Awards 2008 held in the city recently.

DEMA awards are hosted by DEMA Manufacturers Association for recognising the contribution of individuals and member companies in the field of development and manufacturing related to Defense. In his address, he made the DEMA members aware of the various challenges for DRDO while following Dr. Kalam's Vision 20-20 and also mentioned about the various opportunities for the small and medium companies so that they can come forward to contribute substantially in defence related manufacturing. He called for SME's greater participation in making high quality sensors, actuation systems and Radars systems.

Sarasawat also launched DEMA's website www.demaindia.com. All the awardees of the DEMA awards 2008 were honoured by Saraswat during the programme.

The DEMA Appreciation awards 2008 were given to Surendra Kumar, outstanding scientist and director, ARDE Pashan, Subbir Kumar Chaudhary, outstanding Scisntist and Pravin Kumar Mehta, project director, Agni Governed Systems, R&D Engineers, Dighi.

The DEMA Excellence Awards were given to Symtronics Automation Pvt. Ltd for the development, manufacturing and supply of diesel monitoring systems for Submarines, Wavelet Group for multifunction display for fighter Aircraft, Arien Inc. for variable time based fuses for Armament. The DEMA Commitment Awards for the year 2008 were given to Badave Engineers Pvt Ltd for their continued support to Prithvi Missile Project, Padmasree Electronics for their long and consistent support Ground Instrumentation and control for missile launcher and Jahagirdar Aero Products for their support to moving targets for missiles and armament.

D S Kamlpurkar and Shirish Deshmukh, president and vice-president DEMA also addressed the gathering on the occasion.

Vishwas Udpikar, member, executive committee, DEMA made a presentation about various products and systems developed by DEMA members for defence establishments.

Heading: DMCH offers free counselling for weight-loss surgery - Indian Express
Content:
The Tehbazari team today removed illegal unipoles from Jagraon bridge area and for a change, the politicians were helping them in this drive. However, many boards were still not removed indicating pick-and-choose policy of the authorities.

Senior deputy mayor Parveen Bansal, councillors Gurdeep Neetu and Sakshi Julka had come to the spot to get the work done at a faster pace. Zonal commissioner Kuldeep Singh was also present on the spot.

The structures of few unipoles were also removed from the area. Apart from this, even illegal boards were also removed from outside Nikkamal Jeweller shop at the Mall road area. The jeweller had displayed his illegal board reportedly 'with permission.

Heading: Montage Capital opens regional office - Indian Express
Content:
For individuals who have been unable to achieve significant weight-loss through diet modifications and exercise programmes alone, DMCH is providing free consultation and pre-screening for those who will get themselves registered for weight-loss surgery, also known as Bariatric surgery, till October 30. The appointment for the weight-loss surgery can be taken from the Public Relations Office of DMCH by contacting at the telephone numbers 4687510, 4687514

According to the treating surgeons, Bariatric surgery refers to various surgical procedures performed to treat obesity by modification of the gastrointestinal tract to reduce nutrient intake and/or absorption. In general, weight loss surgery success is defined as achieving loss of 50 per cent or more of excess body weight and maintaining that level for at least five years. Excessive obesity is a known risk factor for chronic diseases including heart disease, diabetes, high blood pressure and stroke.

The Department of Surgery has taken a lead to start this procedure in the institution.To start with, the surgery will be performed by Dr P.S. Nain and Dr Ashish Ahuja in the presence of renowned Bariartic surgeon from Pune, Dr Shashank Shah. The cost for this surgery is nominal.

The patient can be discharged within one or two days after the surgery and can resume his normal routine within a week's time. The surgery will help in controlling health-linked diseases like diabetes, high blood pressure, breathing trouble, joint pains besides bringing about an over-all improvement in patient's physical fitness.

Heading: 20 youth given training on fabrication of metal bins - Indian Express
Content:
Montage Capital Markets Ltd. opened its regional office at Malhar road on Tuesday. The office was inaugurated by former state minister Jagdish Singh Garcha. The company is an NRI investment advisor and ECB consultant with associates and offices in London and Singapore, Delhi, Mumbai, company's regional manager Harjinder Singh Garcha said.

Garcha said that company was extensively involved in the project and financial advisory services and innovative funding solutions for various PSUs, state governments and industrial houses for their big-ticket developmental projects. The company aims to clock business worth Rs 1,000 crore till March 2008.

Montage Capital Markets Ltd has provided funding solutions to state governments, blue chip companies in India, power projects, export houses, oil companies and road and township development projects.

Heading: City businessman put behind bars for bounced cheque - Indian Express
Content:
Extension Education Department of Punjab Agricultural University in association with Indian Grain Management and Research Institute, Ludhiana, organised a 10-day training course at Bharsinghpura village in Jalandhar district. The course, aimed at imparting skills of fabrication of metal bins for better storage of grain, provided training to 20 youths from the village.

Apart from practicals, the trainees attended technical sessions also. They were made aware of the importance of grain storage to avoid wastage of food grains. The trainees were awarded certificates as well stipend in cash.

According to Dr C.S. Arneja, senior extension specialist, emphasis was laid on entrepreneurship development. He urged the participants to be computer literate to face the global challenge. He also warned the youth against declining work culture, trend of cheating in exams and increasing drug addiction in the state.

Dr A.K. Aggarwal, senior agriculture engineer from IGMRI, Ludhiana, shared his views on grain storage and emphasised the need to protect the grain in stores. Two of the trainees also expressed their views regarding five golden points for grain storage and importance of grain storage, respectively.

Dr D.S. Dhillon professor and head of the Department of Extension Education, informed that the training was organised under the scheme 'Identification and development of farmers/farm women/youth key communicators/opinion leaders for agricultural development of Punjab state" of the department.

Heading: Lions beat Warriors in practice game - Indian Express
Content:
The court of judicial magistrate, Charanjit Arora has sentenced Baldev Singh Toor, a local resident, to one year imprisonment in a cheque bounce case.

The court has also directed Toor, the proprietor of Toor Poultry Farm, to pay a compensation of Rs 1 lakh to the aggrieved complainant.

Sham Sunder Aggarwal, the proprietor of M/s Kamsun Traders of Bharat Nagar Chowk here filed a complaint through his special attorney and submitted that the accused used to purchase poultry feed from him and as per the account books maintained by him in its regular and ordinary course of business, an amount of Rs 1,24,000 was outstanding against the accused. In order to discharge his liability, the accused issued Aggarwal two cheques vide dated September 11, 2000 and September 2, 2000.

It was assured that the cheques would be encashed on its presentation. But to his Aggarwal's utter surprise, when the cheque was presented for encashment, the same was dishonoured by the banker of accused with remarks "Exceeds arrangements" vide memo dated September 12, 2000 and October 16, 2000. Thereafter, a legal notice was served upon the accused, requesting him to make the payment of dishonoured cheque. But he failed to do so, added the complainant.

On the other hand, the accused pleaded innocence and claimed false implication.

After hearing the arguments of both the sides, the Judicial Magistrate, Charanjit Arora held that it was established that the cheques had been issued for discharging the liability raised due to purchased goods from the complainant. Pronouncing the verdict, the judge held that the prosecution had successfully proved the guilt of accused, who had been sentenced accordingly.

Heading: Angry parents flay cricket coach - Indian Express
Content:
A quick-fire 61 runs off 37 balls by Lou Vincent helped Chandigarh Lions overcome Dhaka Warriors by 29 runs in a practice match played at Tau Devi Lal Stadium on Tuesday.

Chandigarh Lions batted first after the coin was tossed. The opener duo of Matthew Elliott and Lou Vincent could not give a goods start to the Lions as Matthew Elliott was bowled by Tapash Mishra when he was on individual score of seven. Then Lou Vincent and Munish Sharma scored at a brisk pace and added 75 runs for the second wicket. The Chandigarh Lions captain and coach Chris Cairns showed that he was in good touch as he blasted 45 runs in just 24 balls. He struck three boundaries and four towering sixes with ease. Opener Lou Vincent's innings of 61 runs included seven boundaries and three huge sixes. The Chandigarh Lions' innings ended at 187 runs in 20 overs for the loss of six wickets. Musharraf scalped two wickets for the Dhaka Warriors.

In reply, openers Shariar Nafees and Nazimuddin put on 24 runs for the first wicket before Nazimuddin got out for 18 runs. The Warriors' middle order crumbled owing to some fine bowling by the opposition team. In the later part of the innings, some fire-works by Mahbubul Alam (31 runs off 17 balls) and Nafees took the score-card past 150-mark. Dhaka Warriors fall short by 29 runs in the end despite a fine half century by ShariarNafees. He made 77 runs off 54 balls with the help of nine boundaries and two towering sixes. Karanveer emerged as the highest wicket taker for Chandigarh Lions as he bagged three wickets for 17 runs.

Dhaka Warriors will leave tomorrow for Hyderabad to participate in the second edition of ICL championship.

Results:

Chandigarh Lions: 187 for 6 in 20 overs (Lou Vincent 61, Chris Cairns 45, Gourav Gupta 24, Musharraf 2 for 25); Dhaka Warriors: 158 for 8 in 20 overs (Shariar Nafees 77 no, Mahbubul 31, Karanveer 3 for 17).

Heading: U-15  team announced for Sri Lanka tour - Indian Express
Content:
Some parents have criticised Chandigarh Education Department's move to put Nagesh Gupta, a cricket coach contracted with the UT Administration, on the job to conduct Under-14 trials on September 22 for National School Games held at GMSSS-32 in Chandigarh.

Parvin Sharma, father of an 11-year-old cricketer said, "We were surprised to see that Nagesh, who is a coach at St John's High School, was conducting the selection trials. He ignored other wards and just kept asking players from his school to bat and bowl in the nets during the trials."

It is pertinent to mention that according to the rules, only NIS qualified coach can take the trials while Nagesh is just BCCI Level-II coach. Rules also say that the coach taking trials should not have direct affiliation with any school whose players appear in the trials.

But these rules were flouted by the concerned authorities. Another father of a cricketer, Ravinder Singh said, "We don't consider these trials valid. We will move to court if these trials are not conducted again with an NIS coach."

Reacting to the complaints, DPI Schools, Samvartak Singh said, "If some rules were flouted during the trials then it is against the spirit of the game. I will look into the matter and see what has to be done."

Last year Harish Sharma, an NIS qualified coach, had taken the selection trials.

Heading: MNSSS Rai corner glory - Indian Express

Heading: Two arrested for producing fake Class XII certificate - Indian Express
Content:
FIRING IN COURT COMPLEX: Metal detectors installed at entry points; complex to get CCTV cameras

Following the firing incident in the judicial complex on Monday, the police have started face-saving exercise by increasing security measures in the complex.

After the incident yesterday, eminent personalities, including the District and Sessions Judge, GK Rai and MP Sharanjit Singh Dhillon had condemned lack of security in the court complex.

The police installed four metal detectors at the entry points today, to prevent the entry of weapons in the complex. Besides, special commandoes have also been deployed to keep surveillance in the complex. These commandoes today took several rounds of the complex to restore the confidence of litigants and lawyers.

SP Rupinder Singh held a meeting with the office-bearers of the District Bar Association (DBA) to seek their suggestions on the safety arrangements in the complex. DBA President Parupkar Singh Ghuman put forward the suggestions and demands on behalf of the lawyers.

Ghuman sought round-the-clock security in the complex and installation of CCTV cameras in the complex. He also demanded that the parking lot of litigants and visitors should be different from that of lawyers.

He said that only those vehicles, which carry stickers issued by the DBA, should be allowed in the parking lot for lawyers. SP Rupinder Singh accepted these demands of the bar members and assured them that action would be taken soon on their suggestions.

SP Rupinder Singh further assured the DBA members that soon the boundary walls of the judicial complex will be raised so that anti-social elements cannot enter the complex.

SSP RK Jaiswal told Newsline that the CCTV cameras would be installed in the complex soon.

He said that security had already been stepped up in the complex.

He said that the police had been strictly instructed to be alert and vigilant in performing their duties.

No arrest made

Even a day after the firing incident in the court complex, the police have failed to arrest any of the four accused.

Meanwhile, the condition of injured Manveer Singh, who was operated at the DMC hospital late last evening, is stated to be out of danger. According to sources, the police parties were conducting raids to nab the accused who had fired at Manveer Singh. The police had booked Inderjit Singh, Bhagwant Singh, Jasbir Singh and Gurdeep Singh (all residents of Sehjadpur village under Sudhar police station in Jagraon) in an attempt to murder case.

SSP R.K. Jaiswal told Newsline, "We are raiding at all the possible hideouts of the accused and hope to arrest them soon."

Lawyers stay away from work

TO protest over Monday's firing incident in the judicial complex, lawyers observed a strike today. The DBA executive had passed a resolution to this effect and had requested all the lawyers to observe strike to show solidarity on this issue.

Heading: Complainant questioned as formal probe begins - Indian Express
Content:
The police have registered an FIR against two youths for allegedly producing a fake Class XII certificate. One of the accused is a student of Class XII of Nankana Sahib Public School on Gill Road, while the other is a village shopkeeper.

Sadar Police Station SHO Jangjit Singh said, "On the complaint of Nankana Sahib School Principal Harmeet Kaur, the accused have been booked under Section 420 of IPC and the case has been forwarded to the Economic Offence Wing for further investigations."

The SHO said, "During preliminary investigations it came to light that one of the accused, a student, alleged that a village shopkeeper helped him in procuring the fake certificate of Class XII of CBSE by charging Rs 90,000. We have registered an FIR against both."

Harmeet Kaur said, "The said student could not clear Class XII this year. On August 18, he came to me to get a character certificate and told me that after revaluation, he had been declared pass. As I saw the pass certificate, I got suspicious and kept the photocopy of the certificate.

I immediately faxed the document to the Regional Office of CBSE, Panchkula, for verification. Within half an hour, D R Yadav the Regional Officer CBSE, Panchkula, confirmed that it was a fake document and asked me to lodge an FIR against the individual for submitting a fake certificate in the school."

The principal lodged a complaint against the student on August 19 at Merado Police Station. Harmeet Kaur said, "I kept perusing the complaint and was told that it has been forwarded to Sadar Police Station. It was on September 20 when I had a word with R K Jaiswal, Senior Superintendent of Police, that the FIR was registered."

Heading: Traces of pollutants found in ‘treated’ industrial water - Indian Express
Content:
The inquiry into the sexual harassment case in the Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) formally began today after the complainant was questioned by a special committee formed to investigate the charges against Director Students Welfare Dr Dulcha Singh Brar.

On September 14, a woman employee of the university had lodged a complaint with Vice-Chancellor Dr MS Kang alleging sexual harassment at the hands of Brar.

The complainant had also maintained that prior to filing the formal complaint she had verbally informed the authorities.

Following the complaint, the V-C withdrew the charge of girls' hostel from Brar.

The complainant was asked to be present for the inquiry today by the committee headed by the Dean, College of Home Science, Dr Neelam Grewal. The questioning continued for two hours in the Home Science College.

However, no details were available as to what transpired between the committee members and the complainant at the meeting.

Sources said Brar will soon be summoned to present his side of the story to the committee.

Dr Grewal, meanwhile, reiterated that the inquiry into the complaint would be wrapped up at the earliest. When asked whether the inquiry would be completed this week, she declined to comment.

Meanwhile, the Punjab Agricultural University Teachers' Association (PAUTA) seems to be going soft on its overt support to Dr Brar. Dr Mukesh Siag, the General Secretary of the union said the association does not 'support any of the contesting parties in the sexual harassment case'.

Heading: Realty blues hit home as GLADA auction draws a blank - Indian Express
Content:
Although sewerage treatment plants (STPs) of Bhattian, Jamalpur and Balloke are operational, the monthly test reports have indicated that cadmium, nickel and arsenic level in the treated water is much more than the permissible limits.

Owing to lack of proper treatment of industrial effluents, the water having byproducts of the electroplating industry is further flown into the Sutlej.

A K Mahajan, superintending engineer, Punjab Water Supply and Sewerage Board, said, "Monthly tests, which are being conducted by PAU, have proved the presence of adulterants in water. Our STPs can only treat sewer water but the industrial effluents will have to be treated by an industry on its own. This is a clear indication that treatment is not up to the mark."

Not only the industrial effluent but the corporation sewer is also polluting the Sutlej.

Information revealed that Bhattian STP, which has the capacity to treat 111 million litres of sewer water per day (MLD), is treating not more than 75 MLD of sewer water because MC sewer lines are chocked at Transport Nagar, Miller Ganj. Hence, the remaining water flows in to the Buddha Nallah.

At Jamalpur, the capacity of the plant is to treat 48 MLD of water but the industrial water of more than 80 MLD is released every day. Mahajan said, "Industry is releasing more water than the capacity of the plant. Hence, water is not being treated properly and the remaining water is thrown in the river without treating it."

While the sewer board plans to give the treated water to villagers for irrigation purposes, Mahajan said, "Villagers are apprehensive whether the water might destroy their crops. Though lines for giving water in villages have been laid, it looks knotty whether the rural masses will accept the treated water or not."

Talking to Newsline, DS Malhotra, SE Operation and Maintenance cell, Municipal Corporation, said, "We are desilting our sewer lines across the city. Earlier, only 55 MLD water was reaching Bhattian STP but now the flow has increased and within a few days the condition will improve further."

Mahajan said that the industry has been asked to follow the zero-discharge policy, for which two months grace period has been given. "After the expiry of the grace period, no unit in the city will be allowed to discharge waste in the sewer water."

Heading: Durga Ashtami celebrated with fervour - Indian Express
Content:
It seems that slump in property business has started now. A perfect example was seen today when no bidder came to attend process of the auction of 16 shops situated opposite the civil hospital.

The officials of Greater Ludhiana Area Development Authority (GLADA), which organised the auction, kept waiting for the bidders the whole day but with no result. The reserve price for these shops was in range of Rs 51,000- 54,000 per square yard.

GLADA officials are now planning to organise another auction near Diwali. They are blaming the development on crash in the share market besides slump in property business in general.

Meanwhile it needs to be mentioned that even in the past, auctions for this site have not yielded much response to authorities which also suggests that buyers were either not happy with the location or were finding the reserve price too steep.

However it needs to be mentioned that even in the last auction organised by GLADA for old courts land, the highest bid had gone 33% above the reserve price which was also not as per the expectations of the authorities.

Real estate business is no longer enjoying the same boom now.

"In many areas, prices are stagnant for the past many months while at some a mild increase has been reported. Moreover inflation is also another factor which is stopping people to invest in property business," said a GLADA authorities.

Heading: 40-year-old man found murdered - Indian Express
Content:
The festival of Durga Ashtami was celebrated with enthusiasm in the city on Tuesday. Devotees started visiting the temples, which were decked up with beautiful flowers and lights, early in the morning. It was also the day of "Kanjak poojan" and little girls carrying lot of gift packets in their hands were awfully busy visiting for "Kanjak poojan."

As majority of schools in the city open between 7 and 7. 30 a.m., people faced problem in arranging for the Kanjaks. At some places, residents were seen requesting the school-going children to visit their house first.

Some students opted to take a leave from school. "I did not feel like going to school today as it was the Kanjak day. I love this festival," said Nidhi Kumari, a fourth standard student, even as she proudly displayed the four gifts she had received during the ceremony.

Eight-year-old Manu said, "My mother told me yesterday itself to take leave from school due to Kanjak Poojan at home."

Lot of hustle and bustle was observed near temples where children, especially of migrant labourers, waited eagerly for the parsad of Kanjak Poojan. Sitting with big polythene bags in their hands, these children were also singing religious songs related to Goddess Durga.

Heading: Gold rush for Pooja, Joshua - Indian Express
Content:

Heading: Air-India, Mumbai Police sail into semi-finals - Indian Express
Content:
Street Style is a soccer battle without the ball being kicked on a large patch of grass or without a man under the bar to be beaten, and it is all set to capture the imagination of India's soccer fans. Glimpses of the new format in which the players are called 'ballers' was evident in the rectangle courtyard of the St. Xaviers College on Sunday evening and eventually Delhi's Michael Keishing beat a field of 16 to win the India finals.

Keishing will now travel to the country famous for coffee, Samba and of Pele and vie with qualifiers from 47 countries in the Red Bull Street Style World Finals at Sao Paulo, Brazil in November. The 2007 event was restricted to Latin Americans; this year the new format has been thrown open to the rest of the world.

Lightning and thunder intervened at the South Mumbai venue with a superb back-drop, but the young collegians all attired in colourful dress roared their approval for the neo-variety of freestyle soccer as the qualifiers exhibited their skill, control and creativity and style. In what was a virtual battle between the teenagers from Mumbai and Delhi, the capital's Keishing outclassed rivals balancing the ball on the big toes, employed the in-step and out-step with dexterity, lobbed the ball to be stationary on a bent body, rolled it on his hands and chest; all in a contest against rivals spanning 3 minutes. As per rules the rivals passed the ball after showing tricks for 20 seconds, increased to 30 seconds in the final. In short it was juggling with the ball on various parts of the body with some of them dribbling the ball with their legs raised in a particular yoga position.

It was a true test of the limbs and body, coordination of the eye and ball with an accompanying break-dance and hip-hop music and on a stage the size slightly smaller than on which rock stars perform. Keishing was declared the winner by virtue of his capacity and ability to demonstrate the best tricks using imagination, balance and athletic moves while keeping control with the ball and showing creativity and stylish finesse.

Delhi had six finalists and Mumbai seven. Bangalore had two and Chennai, one. The panel of judges were Abhishek Yadav, Terrance Louis and DJ Nasha. There are no physical contacts as one-to-one battles seen in wrestling, boxing or even in traditional soccer. In the years to come Street Style juggling with the ball is bound to turn into a massive spectator sport; just like IPL's Twenty20 has done to cricket the world over.

Final standings: 1. Michael Keishing (Delhi), 2. Vishnu Kumar (Mumbai), 3. Manik Misra (Delhi).

Heading: Gala in quarters - Indian Express
Content:
Fancied Air-India easily beat holders Bharat Petroleum 30-14 to advance into the semi-finals of the Rajaram Sheth Lad Gold Cup Kabaddi Tournament. Joining them there will be Central and Western Railway along with Mumbai Police. The tournament, which is a part of the Shivneri-URL Foundation organized Kabaddi festival in Dadar, saw Central Rly prevail 14-7 over Mahindras in a lackluster contest. However, their counterparts Western who trailed MS Police for most part of the match turned the tables on their opponents to win the match 23-14 in convincing fashion. Mumbai Police who sealed a last-four berth then entertained the 3000-strong crowd with some good attacking play. They won 29-20 against new-look Union Bank of India (UBI) after a bitter fight.

Air-India led by internationals Gaurav Shetty and Dinesh Kumar found the going easy against a depleted Bharat Petroleum (BPCL) who had lost a couple of top players to the state team preparing for the Nationals. The airmen quickly gave a 'lona'to jump to a 10-1 lead and when they wiped out their opponents, the second time around; it was curtains for BPCL with the score reading 28-11. Ashish Mhatre and Sachin Patil were the only ones who made some impact for BPCL which wasn't good enough.

Western Rly kept themselves within striking distance of the policemen throughout the first half, trailing by a couple of points at the most. Once they equalized at 12-12, they drew away from their opponents giving a 'lona', which boosted them to 19-13 with five minutes left on the clock. Brothers Ravi and Hemant Radke proved to be the railmen's mainstay. Dharamveer and Saurajya also impressed for Western. The police outfit, which had done well due to Mahesh Magdum and Prakash Ambre faded away.

Shekhar Patil and Anand Alawane, the raiding duo of the Mumbai Police team, did most of the damage against UBI. The bankmen played well with Nilesh Chindarkar netting three points in one raid at a crucial stage but the failure of Rohit Sheth counted in the end. Siddharth Gaikwad of UBI showed good potential with his raiding.

Central Railway have the tall Naresh Kumar to thank as he turned the tide in their favour with a raid that yielded five points. He got all the three Mahindra men out and that gave his team two additional points with a 'lona'. From 5-4 at half time in their favour, Central did enough to ensure a win. They now run into Western while Air-India meet the city cops in the semi-finals.

Meanwhile on Monday, Western Railway and Mumbai Police booked their berths in the knockout stage of the Rajaramsheth Lad Gold Cup in the Shivneri Seva Mandal -URL foundation Kabaddi Festival. The railmen made light of the rain affected court to demolish Bank of India (BoI) 30-13 while the city-cops had to toil a bit more to overcome Mumbai Port Trust (MPT) 19-15. The railmen thus won two matches in Group 'D' whereas Mumbai Police won all their three matches in Group 'C'. The cops finished on top while the railmen face Air-India in a match to decide the top two places.

In a first round match of the Mohan Naik Cup for 'A' division teams Dena Bank beat Aishwarya Electronics 21-19. Shree Bharati Muklund Masurkar shone for the bankmen in attack and defence while Mithun Bhoir and Prashant Kadam ended on the losing side despite a good display.

The railmen were cautious initially as the 10-7 lead they got at the break indicates. But once the raiding duo of Ravi Radke and Kunal Yadav got going it was curtains for BoI. Sainath excelled in defence for Western Rly. Mumbai Police were well served by Shekhar Patil and Anand Alawane who have been in the forefront in all their encounters. Their raiding has proved to be an asset for the policemen. Shekhar was at his best claiming three victories in one raid. Pankaj Mhatre and Sandeep Bhat tried their best to keep MPT afloat but to no avail.

Gurukul, Chiplun made it to the finals of the URL Cup Inter Collegiate Tournament beating Khalsa 22-5 with consummate ease. Rajesh Mhatre, Sanjay Shinde and Satish Khambe simply devastated Khalsa. Gurukul will take on the winners of the other semi final between Khar Education and Thakur College. Khar Education beat A D Kale 21-20 in a thriller while Thakur beat Ruia 20-8. Adesh More, Manoj Jagtap did well for Khar education. Prashant Wadkar , Dinesh Parab and Ganesh Sawant flexed their muscles for A D Kale who came close after being down 8-14 at the interval.

Heading: Words worth - Indian Express
Content:
A dictionary that no mnemonics can rescue

There rests a solid dictionary on every substantial writer's desk. In the last few years, it may have moved to the Desktop but the lexicon still spells the final word for us. This is also the reason why the dusty, pink and colossal dictionary in our office is more wanted than the mafia is in Mumbai. Each one of us could kill for it. The dictionary is so important to us; the written word is so sacrosanct.

The Oxford University Press website states that previously, it was considered a formidable task to have a single generation of editors and staff work on setting up a dictionary. Given the amount of time, labour and precision that went into it, the dictionary emerged more than just a glossary. It emerged as the gospel truth.

Until the endemic entrepreneur arrived, that is. Start-ups are in fashion and everybody is in a hurry to start something new. A result of such haste is mnemonicdictionary.com.

Mnemonics are a memory tool that helps people by giving associations of words. A mnemonic can be a visual, a key word, an acronym or anything that can relate new information to something that is previously known. Mnemonics (or entrepreneurship?) are the premise on which this online dictionary works. It hopes to educate/ enlighten people in a fun way. It's highly interactive and has lots of features like games, a comprehensive GRE wordlist, word tests, chat and discussion forum, SMS and e-mail words of the day. The creators have a taken up a great idea. An idea, however, does not make a dictionary. I don't even need mnemonics to come up with the two words that denote the website; peripatetic and precipitated.

To begin with, mnemonics are given by the users. Under ordinary circumstances it would be called being user-friendly. However, the contributors are extra-ordinarily frivolous and unabashed. This is how they recommend you remember the word 'abase'—in Hindi, 'abey' is used to humiliate a person. So remember it is a word used to slight someone. There are many such inconceivable options suggested by the users.

Old crosswords from The New York Times and fun word-games are the saving grace of the site. Or so I thought until the time I kept getting the same crossword again and again. I still feel it's a good mind exercise. If you're lucky, perhaps, a quiz won't repeat. As for the GRE wordlist, there is nothing yet that will replace that revered tome called Barron's anytime soon.

To use a euphemism, mnemonicdictionary.com needs a reboot urgently. In its current state, it is best erased from memory.

Heading: In Hermes we trust - Indian Express
Content:
For 60 years, Scrabble has managed to string together people from around the world

From being a simple word game to a cultural icon, Scrabble has created history by upholding its magnificence for six decades. A popular birthday gift and a family favourite since 1948, Scrabble's meteoric rise began after an out-of-work architect Alfred Mosher Butts from Poughkeepsie, New York decided to invent a board game. He attempted to create a game that would use both chance and skill, by combining features of anagrams and crossword puzzles. Initially turned down by two companies because of the fear of lack of commercial potential, the game's journey has been one of the most fruitful chapters in history.

In a world where the shelf life of a board game isn't more than two years, it is a huge achievement for Scrabble to have survived 60. "What has actually helped it survive is the edutainment value it generates and the group play it involves," says Rahul Bhowmik, head of marketing, Mattel Toys India. FYI, since 1994 it is Mattel that has taken over the manufacture of Scrabble outside of USA and UK.

To mark the 60th year, Hasbro games, (owner of Scrabble in USA) launched the diamond anniversary edition game. From the sleek folding case to the two slide-and-store trays, there has never been a more convenient way to enjoy a game.

As a popular board game of all time, Scrabble has had a large impact on the Indian pop culture scene. Mattel is conducting quizzes on Scrabble's history and the Scrabble Association of India (SAI) has held a national tournament to celebrate the game's success. "It is not merely about word power today. It is a memory game which requires learning superfluous words," says Udayan Grover, committee member and Scrabble player, adding, "We have a tournament coming up next month in Pune which will part of the celebration. Also, a new committee has been established to bring about a few altercations."

The game instills healthy competition and has been a favourite with cricket commentator Gautam Bhimani as well. "I reckon playing it from the age of 10. It was an exercise to form newer words that are not just superficial but genuine. During your formative years it is the best way to build your vocabulary." While it was a convenient way to spend time with friends, to make it more interesting, a few conditions were added. For instance, forming words related to cricket; like bat, ball, stump, pitch and so on. Retired english teacher Dorothy Mascarenhas, swears by the game and encourages parents to gift their children a set each. "While the best way to improve your English is read good books, Scrabble comes a close second."

While it is essentially a team game, played by two to four people, celebrity make-up artist Clint Fernandes at times plays it all by himself using two sets. "It is my favourite hobby and it jogs my mind a bit. Recently, I bought the

Hasbro online version of the game, which I can travel with anywhere I want," he smiles. Prior to this, many have launched online versions of the game, the most popular being Scrabulous.com launched by the Agarwalla brothers, Jayant and Rajat. "But none have been able to compete with the original," says Bhowmik.

Heading: Caution: curves ahead - Indian Express
Content:
Two years ago, all of Mumbai's high society was giggling about a socialite who lives in a Worli bungalow and claimed to have walked into an Hermes store in Milan and walked out with a Birkin. "Does she not know that they have a two-year waiting list?" cackled one. "It's obviously a fake," tittered the other, fiddling with her yellowed two-carat solitaire earring.

The Birkin Bearer seems to be having the last chirp as the waiting list is no more than a fable. All she had to do was to appear classy and spend some serious Euros at the Hermes store and the Birkin would be hers. Rather unlike many of our Indian Page-three Peroxide Pals who trundle in, ask for it, get refused and sign up on a register no one will probably look up.

But all of the newspapers covering last fortnight's India Couture Week spent more time Birkin-papping rather then trends-spotting. So we now know that Anu Dewan, Shilpa Shetty, Kaykasshan Patel and Anisha Chaturvedi have joined Haseena Jethmalani, Vanita Bhandari, Laila Lamba, Nisha Javeri, Anita Khilnani, Anju Taraporvala in the Birkin Bearers club. Many of these have signed and re-signed the register, others have called friends in important places, jumped the queue, but few have truly 'earned' themselves a Birkin (or even two).

I've just put down Michael Tonello's superfabulous Bringing Home the Birkin, an honest-to-God account of a Boston-based make-up artist who found himself jobless and work permit-less in Barcelona, a city he fell in love with and found love in. In order to stay on, he had to earn his bread the quasi legit way: he became a reseller on eBay. When he found his old Prada coat and Polo Ralph Lauren scarf sparked a passionate rivalry amongst online bidders, he knew he had cooked a damned good "career chopsuey".

Hermes' Birkin, named after the actress Jane Birkin, is the world's most coveted handbag because Hermes wants it to be so. (In a recent interview to a fashion magazine, Birkin's daughter, the denim-pushing Lou Doillon claims she never owned one herself; but she did buy a fake one in Morocco.) It isn't available off Hermes' orange shelves, it's kept there to see and touch, but right next to it is a sign that says 'Reserved'-and that word alone is enough to set the moneyed on an acquisition spree. This is something that all luxury companies know of, so they come out with a limited edition range every year. But Hermes cleverly stretched the story and capitalised on the attraction to the unattainable.

Tonello skipped the bigger stores and went for the smaller boutiques in beach towns in Spain and Italy. He togged himself in a Prada suit, Jil Sander tie, Giorgio Armani shoes and an Hermes chaine d'ancre bracelet and Ulysse notebook for style. At the stores, he shopped for several notebooks, beach towels, scarves, watches and notebooks, before asking, "Would you have a Birkin?" Soon enough, one or two large orange bags were carried out from the staff room.

Over a year and a million dollars later, Hermes caught on to him and wrote him a letter stating they were "out of quality leather" for his orders! But by then, Tonello had made his buck and Birkins were everywhere. Even in India.

Interestingly, as a Birkin aficionado will tell you, owning a Birkin isn't the last word. The ones that have been papped so far are what they call "the starter Birkin"; available for $ 8,000 (about Rs 4 lakh). The really coveted ones are those made in crocodile or ostrich skin, and can cost up to $ 30,000 (Rs 14 lakh). I know of only two women who own these here: Natasha Poonawala, my fave little fashion fiend, has a brown croc and Veenu Dalamal has one in a beautiful bleu roi. There's also a limited edition Birkin, with real diamonds on the palladium, that costs Euros 100,000 and is waiting to be photographed soon. Until the Next Big Thing comes along.

(namrata.sharma@expressindia.com)

Heading: Peerbhoy did a course on ethical hacking, found it ‘mind-boggling’ - Indian Express
Content:
Knew their roles well, were in touch with absconding Indian Mujahideen founder: Police

All 20 alleged members of the Indian Mujahideen arrested so far in connection with the New Delhi and Ahmedabad bomb blasts and terror emails were on Tuesday booked under the stringent Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) and remanded to police custody till October 21.

A battery of police officers who appeared before the magistrate's court claimed that all the accused were part of an organised crime syndicate involved in committing terrorist activities.

The remand application says that the arrest of Afzal Mutalib Usmani, a known car thief, from Uttar Pradesh led to the arrest of the others. Usmani broke down before the police and confessed to having stolen the cars from Navi Mumbai that were later used in the Gujarat terror attacks. Usmani, who also allegedly confessed to being a member of the Fazl-ur-Rehman gang, has a MCOCA case pending against him. Under MCOCA, at least one accused must have a minimum of two chargesheeted offences registered against him in the last 10 years. Usmani has nine cases registered against him.

Information given by Usmani also led the police to the prime accused Mohammad Sadiq Israr Ahmed Shaikh (33), who is believed to be one of the founding members of the IM.

Claiming that the accused all knew their roles well, the remand application says they aided and abetted one other knowingly in different cities across the country since 2005. Though religion was the primary motive, pecuniary benefits also lured them, the application says.

The remand application also repeatedly states that all the accused had been in touch with absconding accused Riyaz Bhatkal alias Roshan Khan, founder-member of the Indian Mujahideen, and his brother Iqbal Bhatkal, who are both closely involved in setting off explosions at Jaipur, Ahmedabad, Hyderabad, Varanasi, Lucknow, Delhi and Mumbai's serial blasts aboard local trains in July 2006. The 20 accused were arrested from different parts of the country after two rounds of combing, the remand application states.

Claiming that all the perpetrators of these crimes have not yet been nabbed, the prosecution demanded that the accused all be handed over to police custody for further interrogation on the whereabouts of these person.

Heading: Six organisers of Juhu pub rave party arrested - Indian Express
Content:
Last July, when this 31-year-old software engineer completed a course in ethical hacking and cyber crime, he posted his feedback on the website of the firm that played host to the programme: "Mind-boggling," wrote Mohammed Mansoor Asghar Peerbhoy, or Mannu. "Really unleashes the power of information."

A software "architect" at the Pune office of the Yahoo! India-owned firm Zimbra, Peerbhoy attended the six-day course on network security at internet security solutions firm E2Labs, located in Banjara Hills, Hyderabad. "It was a crash course on network security, and Mansoor had already done some courses on the subject," said a spokesperson for E2Labs. "It was a corporate training programme which he completed successfully. The training was conducted by global experts in the field and included training in how organisations can protect their information security and on cyber law."

Newer threats to connected environments, deeper levels of security, encryption-based technologies and an understanding of phishing, hacking, identity theft and online fraud were also part of the course curriculum. Among the others who attended the course — it was a one-time course, the spokesperson said — was a computer crime investigator and forensic analyst with the Andhra Pradesh State Forensic Laboratory. Peerbhoy's online feedback, in bullet points, also said: "very well-designed course (obstacle race); very helpful people; very hands-on".

A senior official of the Mumbai Police Crime Branch confirmed that investigations were on in this regard.

Speaking to Newsline on the phone, Peerbhoy's brother Adil who works as an architect said, "We came to know about the allegations against Mansoor only yesterday from the press. We do not know anything at all about this, and, therefore, cannot comment on the claims being made by the police on his associations and activities. We have never heard of any Riyaz Bhatkal or the other names being mentioned. I cannot comment on this whole affair, as it would not be proper at this stage. My family is going through a very tough time now. We ourselves want to verify details so that we can get to the bottom of this. Only then will we be able to say anything."

While colleagues at the eSpace IT Park office of Zimbra refused to speak about the man who Mumbai Police have said earned Rs 19 lakh per annum, an official spokesperson for Yahoo! India said: "We are very concerned about these events and will fully cooperate with the law-enforcement agencies, consistent with local laws." Zimbra, set up in California and taken over by Yahoo! India last year, offers the Zimbra Collaboration Suite software, a groupware product for messaging and collaboration, emailing, group calendars, web document management, etc. It also provides software to sync mobile devices.

The Mumbai Police have said Peerbhoy, an extraordinarily talented software developer and resident of Pune and belonging to a "highly educated family", travelled several times to the United States on work.

Russian engineer Igor Sysoev, whose opensource software "nginx" is used by Zimbra, said in an emailed response to Newsline: "I know Mansoor as Zimbra developer because Zimbra software uses my opensource software nginx mail proxy server. However, I do not know him personally and until now I do not even know his religious commitment."

(With inputs from Mustafa Plumber)

Heading: Salem won’t be tried for murder, conspiracy in Dewani case - Indian Express
Content:
DJs playing trance music under scanner, cops to get training to deal with drug users

Acting on the information provided by the nine peddlers arrested after the raid on Juhu pub Bombay 72 degrees East on Sunday night, officers of the Anti-Narcotics Cell (ANC) on Monday night arrested six people who were allegedly involved in organising the rave party.

The six people were arrested from various parts of the city in a night operation which was conducted in a matter of few hours. The arrested have been identified as Stanley Fernandez (41), Kashish Malkani (23), Vijay Harlankar (24), Yunus Sheikh (20), Ilias Sheikh (26) and Nikesh Gune (20). All six were produced before the metropolitan magistrate's court on Tuesday afternoon along with the other nine arrested on Sunday. While Rahul Karmarkar, who has a previous drug record, and Ben Simone, the Israeli DJ, were remanded to police custody till October 13, the others were sent to judicial custody but later granted bail.

Talking about the 231 youths who were detained after the raid on the pub on Juhu Tara Road on Sunday night, DCP (Anti-Narcotics Cell) Vishwas Nangre-Patil said, "We had released the 231 youths after collecting their urine and blood samples. The samples have been sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory at Kalina for testing. Though the results will take at least a month, I can confidently say that around 90% of the youths will test positive for drug use." Once the test results are out, those who test positive can be charged with consumption of narcotics and will face six months in jail.

Nangre-Patil informed that in most such parties where trance music is played, there are evidences of narcotics use. "Keeping this in mind, we have decided to keep a special watch on DJs in the city who play trance music. Even in this case, Ben Simone, the Israeli DJ, who was in India on a tourist visa, was dealing in drugs while working as a DJ. Many of the DJs in the city suspected of having drug dealings are not full-time employees of any club but are specially called in to play trance music," he said.

Talking about the ways to tackle people involved in the drug trade, Nangre-Patil said, "Drug users and peddlers cannot be handled like ordinary criminals and in order to combat the apprehensions faced by the policemen, we have come up with a new training schedule to be adopted for police personnel dealing with people in the narcotics trade."

According to Nangre-Patil, most of the drug users in the city are infected with HIV. "Our officers used to fear the risk of infection as while making arrests, these drug addicts would either attempt to bite them or spit on them or even defecate," he said.  "We shall be providing gloves to the officers and also will be training them about the ways to hold the drug users."

Heading: Families of Indians aboard hijacked vessel seek PM’s intervention - Indian Express
Content:
Extradited gangster Abu Salem, once believed to be a prize catch among wanted gangsters brought to India by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), will now be tried for lesser charges in the sensational Ajit Dewani murder case of 2001. On Thursday, the prosecution will move an application before the special Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) court requesting the court to drop, alongside MCOCA charges, also charges under Section 302 (murder), 449 (house-trespass in order to commit offence punishable with death), 452 (house-trespass after preparation for hurt, assault or wrongful restraint), 212 (harbouring offender), 120-B (criminal conspiracy) and 34 (common intention) of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 25 and 27 (possession of weapons illegally) of the Arms Act.

A magistrate will now try Salem for sections where the maximum punishment is seven years. The sanction to drop charges was given after the Union Home Ministry directed the Mumbai and Delhi police, at the request of the Central Bureau of Investigation, to drop the stringent charges against the gangster as they violated conditions of the extradition treaty between India and Portugal.

Special Public Prosecutor Jimmy Madon said: "I will be doing as the state wants me to do." The move could also bring some relief to six co-accused in the case who are in custody since 2001, since there is no direct evidence against them. Most have now filed bail applications in the MCOCA court, their prayer being that their role is limited.

Defence lawyer Subhash Kanse, appearing for four of the accused, said: "The main assailant Deepu who had given the confession describing everyone's role is not before the court so his evidence can be ruled out." Deepu is now absconding.

Dewani, actor Manisha Koirala's secretary, was killed on June 30, 2001, with a 9 mm pistol, allegedly by accused Deepak Singh alias Chotu alias Deepu at Dewani's office in Oshiwara. Salem had allegedly demanded an extortion sum from Dewani, which the latter had refused.

Don't deny our marriage: Salem to Monica Bedi
Abu Salem, meanwhile, has served a legal notice on actor Monica Bedi saying that he is "deeply hurt and distressed" by her statements denying their marriage. Salem claims the duo got married in a Los Angeles mosque in November 2000.

Bedi, in several interviews given after her exit from reality TV show Bigg Boss, had said that she had known Salem for many years but had never actually married him. Salem's notice claims his anguish had been "multiplied manifold" since he was unable to communicate with Bedi due to his imprisonment. Salem has been lodged at Arthur Road jail ever since his deportation from Portugal in November 2005. If Bedi wants a divorce, he would "though heart-broken, soulfully pronounce a talaq" according to the notice. On a romantic note, the notice also says Salem found "peace, solace and comfort in reading Bedi's letters and cards" sent to him.
— ENS

Heading: Police rope in college students to get info on peddlers - Indian Express
Content:
After running from pillar to post and eventually having exhausted all options, family members of the 18 Indian hostages onboard the Hong Kong flagged and Japanese owned chemical tanker, Stolt Valor, led by Seema Goyel, wife of Captain Prabhat Goyel, wrote a petition to the Prime Minister asking for his intervention in the matter.

The delegation of family members along with representatives of the Seafarers Union and Capt. J.C Anand, Chairman, Indian Register of Shipping (IRS) met Captain Manmohan Baggi, Nautical Advisor to the Ministry of Shipping (MoS), Y Venkatraman, Deputy Director General (DG), Ministry of Shipping (MoS), Sabyasachi Hajara, Chairman & MD, Shipping Corporation of India (SCI) and Naveen Passey of the Foreign Ship Owners' Association to convey their restlessness over the ongoing crisis.

Members conducted a symbolic peace march before the meet. "My brother has had fever for the last three days and was crying over phone while talking to his mother. He said that the hijackers pick them up at midnight and harass them. He also said that food and water on the ship was very scarce and was only given some medicine on October 5," said Roshni Rodrigues, whose brother Allister Fernandes is a cadet on the Stolt Valor.

"We cannot leave the sailors at the mercy of the Japanese owner and therefore a representative from the government's side is required to spearhead the negotiation process," said Murad M Burondkar, whose twenty-year-old son Naveed happens to be the youngest cadet onboard. "It was his first voyage," said Burondkar who believes that a committee to track the issue on a daily basis should be formed by the government or else the issue will die out. Similar views were expressed by other family members. "The government needs a dhukk (push) every time and then it takes a few steps and then it needs another one," said Seema Goyel who has been leading the crusade against the government's inaction on the issue.

"Even if we talk on commercial grounds, apart from the 18 hostages, even the commodity on the ship was meant for Indian companies," said Goyel underlining the fact that the phosphoric acid, which the ship is carrying, is meant for Kandla based Indian Farmers Fertilizer Cooperative Limited (IFFCO).

According to Goyel, the hijackers have reduced their demand to two million dollars from six, that they had asked for earlier. J.C. Anand, who has formerly headed the Indian National Shipowners' Association, said that it was the duty of the ship-owner to protect his crew. "By now the ship owner should have put the money in the negotiator's escrow account to secure the hostages' release which they still haven't done," he said. Also according to Anand, there is an anti-hijacking insurance available to ship owners. "Why don't they have it when they know that the Gulf of Aden is an endangered route," said Anand.

Government officials however were on the defensive and maintained that it was trying its best to secure the release of the hostages. "We're making all efforts and are in touch with the ministry of external affairs (MEA) over the matter. We are highlighting the seriousness of the matter to the government and will pursue the matter on an hourly basis," said Venkatraman. The families denied getting any assurances from the government.

The Gulf of Aden & the Shipping trade
One of the world's most important waterways, the gulf is an important shortcut that saves shipping time and fuel costs. According to Sabyasachi Hajara, Chairman & Managing Director, Shipping Corporation of India (SCI), the route is responsible for transporting as much as 4% of the world's daily oil consumption. "Half of the world's container trade is carried on through that route and one-third of the world's dry bulk trade is carried out through the route. In addition to this almost 4 billion barrels of oil passes through this area everyday," he said. The waterlines fall between Yemen on the south coast of the Arabian Peninsula and Somalia and it also connects the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean .

Ever since the hijack of the Stolt Valor on September 15, Seema Goyel, wife of Captain Prabhat Goyel, has been at the forefront of the entire hostage crisis. It is only because of her efforts that the families, today, stand united in their fight for the government's attention on the issue.

According to Goyel, she not only keeps a tab on her husband's wellness but on that of the entire crew. Mentioned below are her efforts to get the issue highlighted in the national media:

* October 1: Goyel met the Shipping, Road Transport & Highways minister, T R Baalu and briefed him about the ongoing crisis off the Somali Coast. Along with Baalu, Goyel also met Shipping Secretary APVN Sarma and Captain PVK Mohan, Chairman of National Shipping Board. Subsequently, a letter was sent from the ministry of Shipping (MOS) to the ministry of external affairs (MEA) & ministry of defence (MoD).

* October 2: Seema sought appointments with President Pratibha Patil, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and Rahul Gandhi along with Foreign Secretary Shiv Shankar Menon, National Security Advisor, M.K. Narayanan and the Ambassador of Japan.

* October 3: Goyel managed an audience with Rahul Gandhi who, according to Goyel, was well aware of the matter and promised to take up the issue with the concerned ministry. Also on the third afternoon, Bijendra Singh, family member of one of the hostages, met Haryana Chief Minister, Bhupinder Singh Hooda and was assured by the CM of action. Hooda also fixed the family members' appointment with Minister of State for External Affairs, Anand Sharma.

At 5:30 on the same evening, Seema Goyel met N. Ravi, Secretary, MEA (East) for more information about government's action on the matter. At six on the third evening, Goyel got a call from Anand Sharma's office and heard the plight of the hostages' family members. Goyel also got support from Deepender Hooda, MP from Rohtak who made a representation on the families' behalf to Sharma.
- Shashank Shekhar

Heading: 9 held for selling fake Continuous Discharge Certificates - Indian Express
Content:
Having visited as many as 70 colleges in the city and suburbs, officers of the Anti- Narcotics Cell (ANC) are slowly building a network of college students who can pass on information to the department on possible drug peddling activities at popular night spots and discotheques.

"We have achieved great success in such projects many times; the students approached us and provided information on suspected drug peddlers on college campuses and also pubs and such places from where they have received information on drug peddling activities," said DCP Vishwas Nangre Patil, who led the raid on a pub in Andheri where a rave party was going on last Sunday night.

"Whenever we get information on drug activities in places like pubs and discotheques, we send a decoy to confirm the information and it's quite obvious that we cannot send police officers. People can easily make out the presence of police due to their typical 'cop appearance'. In such cases, we mostly use civilians, especially students from colleges apart from under-cover officers. After decoys pass on the information about the use of drugs inside, the raiding party swoops in," said Patil.

Patil also said that he had personally visited as many as 5-6 colleges in the city to talk to students on the ill-effects of drug use and the necessity to combat it. Apart from me, many other ANC officers have visited over 70 colleges across the city and spoken to a section of students on this issue," he said.

Elaborating on the use of college students in their operation against narcotics, Patil said, "Drug peddlers target the college students as they are not matured enough to understand the dangers of the drug use. Hence, peddlers usually approach such people during parties at pubs or even on college campuses. To tackle the issue, we thought of fighting it by talking to college students and seeking their help in identifying and apprehending drug peddlers."
