Heading: Dimpy murder: bullet fired from Rocky’s pistol, say police - Indian Express
Content:
2 years on, Nayagaon Nagar Panchayat still 'powerless' to check encroachment

No construction existing in the Nayagaon municipal limits in the periphery of Chandigarh is authorised. Illegal constructions raised without getting building plans approved by competent authority have eaten up almost 80 per cent area of Karoran, 60 per cent of Kansal and 20 per cent of Nada villages, which constitute the Nayagaon Nagar Panchayat.

The facts came to light after Newsline filed an application under the Right to Information Act, 2005, seeking information from the civic body with regard to constructions in Nayagaon.

The civic body has not yet identified any encroachment in Nayagaon. Neither has it initiated any action against those responsible for raising the unauthorised structures. Reason: even two years after coming into being, the civic body does not have the power to regularise buildings, approving building plans and issuing no-objection certificates required for procuring power and water supply connections.

It may be mentioned that top politicians and bureaucrats own vast chunks of prime land and structures in the area.

In September, the Mohali Deputy Commissioner banned all new constructions in Nada and Karoran, besides refusing power, water supply connections and ration cards.

In his reply to the RTI application, the Public Information Officer of the Nayagaon Nagar Panchayat said with no major source of income, the civic body had to raise a loan of Rs 20 lakh from the 'cash-rich' Mandi Gobindgarh Municipal Council to meet its expenditure. The meagre development work taken place so far had been undertaken with the help of government grants.

In these two years, the Nayagaon Nagar Panchayat has received 27 building plans from Kansal area, but no plan could either be approved or rejected due to the restriction. The fee of Rs 29.73 lakh received with the building plans, however, was kept pending, which constituted a major income of the civic body since its establishment in October 2006.

Apart from that, the municipality earned Rs 52,000 from octroi on electricity, Rs 6,000 as rent and Rs 2.81 lakh from other sources to take its total revenue to Rs 53.12 lakh, the PIO said in his reply.

The total expenditure of Rs 46.01 lakh included Rs 22.25 lakh on salaries, Rs 3.53 lakh on stationery, office furniture and fixtures, Rs 16,000 on telephone and fax, Rs 1.28 lakh on miscellaneous, Rs 9.93 lakh on solid waste management, Rs 8.5 lakh on construction of streets and drains, besides Rs 1.05 lakh on streetlights.

The Nayagaon Nagar Panchayat received a grant of Rs 50,000 under the MP Land Area Development Fund in August 2007 for construction of a drain for waste disposal in Karoran. It could not be utilised due to restrictions imposed by the Punjab Land Preservation Act (PLPA).

Besides, the civic body got Rs 12.25 lakh grant for solid waste management and database computerisation in August and December 2007, of which Rs 3 lakh is yet to be spent. Another grant of Rs 6.19 lakh was received in June this year, of which Rs 1.37 lakh was spent on purchase of a water tanker, a carrier container system while Rs 4.75 lakh is lying unused.

Heading: Dengue cases lead to blood scarcity - Indian Express
Content:
The bullet, which killed gangster Prabjinder Singh alias Dimpy in Chandigarh two years ago, was fired from the same pistol that was recovered from Jaswinder Singh alias Rocky, an Uttar Pradesh-based gangster. Rocky was arrested in connection with the murder earlier this year. The Central Forensic Sciences Laboratory (CFSL) confirmed this, the Chandigarh Police said on Wednesday.

The US-made .45 bore pistol, which is issued to the soldiers of the US Army, was recovered from the possession of Rocky when he was arrested. He had allegedly given the sophisticated weapon to two shooters for eliminating Dimpy on July 7, 2006. The UT police had sent the pistol to the CFSL for examination.

"During interrogation, Rocky confessed to giving his pistol to two shooters who were assigned the task of eliminating Dimpy. He said the two gave it back to him after executing the task," said a senior police officer.

Heading: Heritage trees in city need to be protected: survey - Indian Express
Content:
Demand has shot up to 100 units a day from 35 at PGI; situation no better at private blood banks

With cases of dengue fever gripping the region, blood banks in the city have been coping with a severe crunch for the last one month.

At PGI, where the demand for blood ranges between 35 and 40 units a day in normal days, the requirement has now shot up to 90 to 100 units. The situation is worse at private blood banks.

"The demand has definitely gone up since September, the season for the onset of dengue. It will last till the end of November. Our patients are largely taken care of by the donations from their relatives and also voluntary donors, but we get repeated requests from nursing homes and blood bank societies to provide them with additional units," said Dr Neelam Marwaha, head of transfusion medicine at the PGI.

While the UT Health department says the city has recorded over 26 cases of dengue so far, in this season, and that more than 250 cases have been detected in the nearby towns and cities of Haryana and Punjab, the actual figure may be much more, going by the long queues at the blood banks.

Adding to the city's burden are cases from the region, surging the demand for blood units and platelets.

The Blood Bank Society, an NGO, made a formal appeal to the public on Wednesday to donate blood for dengue patients.

"We get five to six new requests each day for platelets. Increasing cases require a large supply of these life-saving platelets, which can only be available from freshly donated blood. Significantly, they have a life span of only three days and have to be extracted within five hours of donation. Blood banks cannot store these. Only one dose can be extracted from fresh blood given by five donors at a time," said Neeti Sareen, general secretary of the Blood Bank Society.

Society director Col R S Shah, who held a one-day camp at Yamunanagar on Wednesday, highlighted upon the extent of the demand. "We collected 20 units at the camp and already 18 have been allotted to the patients waiting for platelets. We are now left with just two units to care to the new requests," he said.

Platelets, a component separated manually or through machines from freshly donated blood, are required to treat severe dengue cases. The machines that can separate the components in a concentrated manner (where one unit is capable for extracting more platelets) are available at the blood banks at PGI, GMCH-32 and Fortis Hospital, Mohali.

"Not all dengue cases require platelets. Some dengue fever cases are treated by medication. In severe cases, the platelet count drops significantly," added Col Shah.

Heading: UT functioning may suffer as senior officers on way out - Indian Express
Content:
The condition of over 1,000 heritage trees across the city is deteriorating considering that they have been neglected in the past. A survey conducted by the volunteers of Yuvsatta has revealed that trees like neem, peepal, mango and others need to be protected.

The 500-year-old mango tree in an ashram in Maloya is the oldest mango tree in the city. Among other such varieties is a 350-year-old banyan tree, located in a park in Sector 9.

While a number of such trees are located in educational institutes, their condition too is bad. With a parking lot in Sector 17, a 300-year-old banyan tree does not have enough space for its roots to expand.

The trunk of a peepal tree was severed in 1972 to make space for a gurdwara in Maloya.

One problem that plagues such trees is of residents, who engrave their names on the trunks and branches of trees. Such examples can be found at various places, including the Sukhna Lake.

Certain regulations have been recommended to protect the trees from possible problems, which include the installation of lightening conductors, the construction of an earthen platform among others. It has also been suggested to install signboards in English, Hindi or Punjabi near the trees, highlighting its history.

Parmod Sharma, co-ordinator, Yuvsatta said: "The construction of more houses in the southern sectors should be checked. The green areas too, need to be maintained. The sites where trees exist should be made the centres of tourist attraction."

Heading: MC volunteers to redress woes of women - Indian Express
Content:
The UT Administration is going to face a serious crunch of officials in the coming few weeks with some of the key officials on their way out.

While UT Director (Tourism) and Director Public Relations, the Haryana Civil Services (HCS) officer Vivek Atray will be relinquishing his charge next week, as he joins a consulting firm Price Waterhouse Coopers (PWC); Raji P Srivastava, the Punjab cadre IAS officer who was holding the charge of Special Secretary (Education, Finance ) besides being Director Public Instructions (Colleges) will be joining as Director, Census, after her repatriation to her parent cadre.

Atray, who had received an official nod from his parent cadre — Haryana — will be proceeding on a three-year long leave from the next week. Atray remained as Director (Information Technology) from 2000 to 2006 and also worked as Director (Tourism, Public Relations and Technical Education), during his eight years term, in two stints with the UT Administration.

On the other hand, UT Chief Engineer SK Jaitley sustained a serious hip-fracture on Monday when he tumbled during the inauguration of Le Corbusier Centre here in Chandigarh. Jaitley is admitted at Government Multi-specialty Hospital, Sector 32, and is likely to be operated on Thursday. According to the senior administration officials, Jaitley is likely to take at least six months to recover from the injury. Kishanjeet Singh has been given an additional charge of the UT Chief Engineer, for the time being.

The Punjab government had already sent a panel of four officers to replace Raji P Srivastava. While the panel includes two officers of the 1993 batch, Anurag Verma and RK Rangta; Jaspal Singh belongs to the 1992 batch. Another officer Vikas Pratap, who also figured in the panel of officers for the post of CITCO Managing Director, belongs to the 1994 batch. The post of CITCO Managing Director is vacant since the last couple of months, ever since the Punjab cadre IAS officer JS Bir was repatriated to his parent cadre.

"The Administration will definitely miss its senior and competent officers who were holding key positions once they are gone. We are looking for their replacements, but it would take some time," said UT Home Secy Ram Niwas.

Heading: A historic landmark... lost in time - Indian Express
Content:
The Women Empowerment Committee of the Municipal Corporation is identifying women from different wards to determine and solve problems being faced by women in different areas.

Around 10 women in each ward are being identified, many among them being the active workers in their wards. Their job will be to talk to other women in their wards and identify the major problems being faced by them.

Councillor Dr Pam Rajput, who heads the Women Empowerment Committee, had found during visits to slums and colonies that the majority of problems being faced by women was of alcohol addiction in their spouse. The men in such families were found to spend a substantial part of their income on liquor.

Councillor Anu Chatrath said: "We are identifying the problems that women in different wards face. The issues that are in the purview of the Municipal Corporation will be solved here and the rest will be taken up with the Administration. The level of personal hygiene is also low in slum-dwellers. Efforts will be made to improve this." The committee is also planning to organise regular medical camps and also lay stress on maintaining cleanliness.

In a recent House meet, Dr Rajput had stressed on the need to highlight the problems faced by women, especially in slums. She said a manifesto listing out issues that were important for women could be made. She also expressed concern on security of women in the city.

Heading: Retail investment takes a hit as sensex continues to plummet - Indian Express
Content:
Given the historical relevance of the place, it is a surprise to know that a very few people in the city are aware of the Lily Garden.

While the name suggests it is a place where lilies bloom, it's anything but that. Tucked away in the heart of Sector 9's residential area, the place, at first seems like any other garden with cemented paths and towering trees. There's nothing here — no boards or signages — that gives you a lead regarding its importance. This, until you literally stumble upon a huge cuboid-like structure housed just off the middle of the garden. Made from cement, it boasts of two dilapidated plaques that have certainly seen bad weather.

The iron bar circling it on the ground along with a thick undergrowth make it difficult to take a closer look — you can squint and just about make out what it reads. 'Jawaharlal Nehru, Prime Minister of India, saw the layout of Chandigarh from this spot on 2nd April in the year 1952' it says across a black granite slab.

That's how important a place it is!

Circle the square and there's another plaque, in an equally regretful state. It reads: 'This memorial was inaugurated by M S Randhawa, Chief Commissioner, Chandigarh on Februrary 27, 1967.' Finally, you realise that Lily Garden actually houses a memorial to Nehru's vision of planned urban development.

But there's nothing left now to celebrate the importance of this place.

Interestingly, a hundred metres or so, you notice another structure. This one is tall like a tower and has huge iron frames surrounding it from four sides. Here too, there is no mention of what the tower is or its significance. As one enters the area, you notice something's amiss.

"There were plaques here too. See the missing spots. They've been gone for a long time," says the neighbourhood dhobhi from across the street." All you see now are empty spaces with moss all over and broken steps. With no one to fill us in on the place, we turn to M N Sharma, former chief architect of the city, who has worked closely with Le Corbusier and M S Randhawa, former Chief Commissioner of the city. "It's called Lily Garden?" questions Sharma as we quiz him about the place. "Is there a pond now?" he asks us and we tell him there isn't one.

"Did you go up the tower? There were wooden steps I remember," says Sharma as he remembers being at the garden the day Pandit Nehru surveyed the city that was to be Chandigarh. "The tower had steps leading to it. It had four sides and Pandit Nehru looked around from each. This is a very important place for the city and needs to be highlighted," he says. Strangely, while the garden itself looks cared for with its wrought iron benches, cemented footpaths, flower beds... the sites of importance are in neglect.

Heading: Passengers to bear the brunt as airlines get ready to scrap travel agents’ commission - Indian Express
Content:
The first timers prefer to stay at a distance, the seasoned rue the huge losses already suffered and the usual trading sessions are now left with a few active participants. As the Sensex continues to plummet further, breaching all the previous lows, retail investors are neither coming forward for daily trading nor for long-term investment.

The opening of the new demat accounts has completely shrunk, say the city brokers, and the day trading sessions have gone down to a mere 20 per cent of the usual active participation.

"The retail investor is obviously scared to enter," said M L Batra of the Angel Broking at Panchkula, gauging the overall sentiment in the market, while adding that business has reduced by 30 per cent.

"Compared to the beginning of the year, when there was a huge waiting list of newcomers getting their demat accounts opened, the requests to open accounts has practically disappeared," he added.

Batra still manages to give a bold advice to investors — of going in for quality stock pickings at cheap rates available in the market. "There is definitely scope for some intelligent buying," he said.

The scenario is bleak for investment in the markets, says V Kumar of the V Kumar of the Viksons Finance and Investments Limited.

"From opening 1,000 demat accounts a day, we now get an occasional request from one or two people, willing to start investment in the market. Things are definitely getting from bad to worse and the scenario may change in at least 3 - 4 months only," he says.

"The day trading sessions was earlier a hectic affair but now the number of people coming has gone down," he said, while adding he is advising the retail investors to hold to the cash and let the markets stabilise before investing again.

But as the markets tumble time and again and with the investors' wealth eroded up to 50-60 per cent, people are now increasingly opting for investment in gold or keeping their money in safe fixed deposits, especially with the banks offering handsome interest rates, generally in double figures.

"I have some investments in shares, where the values have corrected up to 50 percent. I can hold these. But since I cannot afford anymore investments in this bleak scenario, gold appears a good option for investment if the markets recover. Otherwise, for salaried person like me, fixed deposits are the most attractive option at the moment," said Sanjeev Sharma, working in the private bank here.

Heading: Cong’s Sood defects to INLD - Indian Express
Content:
The airlines industry, in an attempt to recover from the prevailing crunch, has decided to scrap the travel agents' commission of five per cent from November 1 this year. While the travel agents in the city are opposing the move of the International Air Transport Association (IATA) passengers will now have pay the transaction fee that is charged directly by the travel agents.

"The shrinking profit margins are the main reason for this move by the airlines who trying to reduce the cost incurred by them and make some savings. The decision will be implemented from November 1," said an official of the Indian Airlines.

If things go right this time — as earlier this guideline was to be implemented from October — instead of travel agents' commission, the passengers will have to pay a transaction fee or service charge to the agents for the services provided. This move will have an extensive affect in the city as around 95 per cent of the tickets are booked through travel agents and only 5 per cent are booked directly.

The move will marginally affect domestic passengers but significantly hit the international flyers as the transaction fee for international flights will be in three slabs — Rs 1,200 to Rs 2,400 for economy class, Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 for business class and Rs 5,000 to Rs 10,000 for first class. The passengers will be at the suffering end with this fee being charged by the travel agents as earlier the commission was calculated on the basic fare, which usually forms the lowest percentage of a ticket cost.

The passengers; both domestic and international, are concerned about the scrapping of the commission. They believe that in the absence of any guideline for the travel agents, regarding the transaction fee for the services charged by them, it is likely that the charges will be random and unjustifiable. "Also, now, with slabs for international flights, we have to pay extra for each ticket as earlier this was inclusive in the ticket only. We are so dependent on the travel agents due to their 24-hour customer friendly services as against the airlines," said Gurpreet Singh, an NRI.

While the airlines have accepted that they are facing resistance from the travel agents, the community of travel agents in the city is upset with this attitude of airlines. "The travel agents have provided a ground and market to the airlines. Now, when they have an established market, they are trying to compete with the travel agents," laments Sumant Kapoor, Managing Director, Khanna Enterprises.

He added that the profit margins of the travel agents whose business solely depends upon ticketing will shrink to a considerable percentage in the long run.

Heading: Relatives of gangrape victim ‘harassed’ - Indian Express
Content:
In a serious blow to the Congress, Zila Parishad, chairman Umesh Sood joined the Indian National Lok Dal (INLD) on Wednesday. Sood, however, managed to save his seat of the chairman.

Around nine members in Zila Parishad reached the Mini Secretariat to submit a no-confidence motion against Sood yesterday. As Deputy Commissioner Rajinder Kataria was not at his office that time, the programme was postponed for today.

Alleging threat to his life form the Panchkula deputy commissioner and additional deputy commissioner, Sood said at a press conference that he was compelled to leave the party as both were interfering in his office and the chief minister failed to take stock of the situation.

The prominent INLD leaders present on the occasion were: Sher Singh Barsami, former INLD state president, Pardeep Chaudhary, district president, Manoj Aggarwal, city president and Amardeep Chaudhary, general secretary of Panchkula.

The friction between Sood and Deputy Commissioner Rajinder Kataria and Additional Deputy Commissioner Parvin Kumar, surfaced during a meeting last month, after which, the matter was brought to the notice of Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda, who was visiting the town that day.

"Both the officials are relatives of high profile politicians in the state and when I raised objection to their interference in the working of the Zila Parishad, they started threatening me in public view," alleged Sood.

Heading: Post polythene ban, traders shift to manufacturing paper bags - Indian Express
Content:
The relatives of the 17-year-old girl, who was allegedly gangraped in Panchkula on September 16, have claimed that they were harassed by authorities of Chaman Lal DAV Senior Secondary School, Sector 11.

The uncle of the girl had gone to the school to meet the principal and inquire about the victim's future course of studies. He was, however, made to wait for more than an hour by the school authorities.

The principal met the relatives only after seeing media persons around and asked them to send the girl to school from Monday.

"We were told initially that the principal is busy and may not meet us. I had come to ask when the girl can start attending school again. It has been a traumatic time for her and the school is behaving in an irresponsible way," said a relative on condition of anonymity.

On the other hand, principal, Anjali Marriya, refused to comment on the issue. "I have never denied anything to the girl and she is always welcome. I would not like to talk about the issue now," she said. The 17-year-old was allegedly gangraped on September 16 by youths in a Balero car. Two of the accused are behind bars.

Heading: United India Insurance to pay up to Mandi Board - Indian Express
Content:
Considering the recent ban on polythene from October 2, most of the traders have now shifted to maufacturing paper bags. They are, however, happy with this switch as the sale of paper bags has gone up by almost 15 per cent.

Many traders say that the ban has given them a cause to celebrate as the demand for paper bags in the city has gone up. Talking to Newsline, Rajesh Gulati, owner of Venus Stationary in Sector 20, who also manufactures paper bags says: "The ban has been a boom to the sale of paper bags. Earlier, we received very less number of orders for paper bags, but now, there is a sudden increase in its demand since the ban. Earlier, the sale for paper bags was hardly 10 per cent and has now gone up by almost 50 per cent."

With this sudden increase in the demand, however, the traders are busy struggling to complete their orders. They say that with limited orders earlier, they had limited labourers, due to which, they are now having problems in meeting the deadlines. Another trend that has been witnessed is that traders, who earlier dealt in plastic, have now shifted to paper bags.

Vinaj Kansal, owner of Davindra Cottage Industry in Sector 20, who has shifted to the business of making paper bags, says he suffered a loss of Rs 4 lakh due to the ban as he could not sell the stock of plastic goods. Talking to Newsline, he said: "The ban has definitely created problems for customers who have to carry their purchases in paper bags. But from the business point of view, it has come up as a good opportunity for traders. Though I suffered loss owing to the unsold stock, the paper bag business is going fine."

Heading: Forum directs water filter dealer to refund amount - Indian Express
Content:
In a significant judgement, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum disposed of 298 complaints of the Punjab State Agricultural Marketing Board employees who were allegedly denied claims.

The forum has directed the secretary of the complainant board to constitute a committee comprising representatives of insurance companies who would 'consider, process and dispose of' cases of claimants.

While some of the complaints were dismissed on Wednesday, the consumer forum directed United India Insurance Company to pay Rs 1,000 to the successful complainant as litigation expenses. The company has been directed to pay Rs 10,000 in cases pertaining to death claims.

"The company shall additionally pay Rs 10,000 in cases pertaining to death claims and Rs 2,500 in case of loss of one/two limb(s) to each such claimant," the forum ruled.

The Punjab State Agricultural Marketing Board (Mandi Board), subject to the provisions of the Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1961, expressed its willingness to accept Rs 15 lakh as premium for carrying out personal accident insurance of farmers, farm labourers and mandi workers throughout Punjab as per the provisions of its Insurance Scheme for the year 1989-90.

As per the scheme, Mandi Board conveyed its decision to take up personal accident insurance provided by the United India Insurance Company for a period of one year from April 13, 1989 and co-terminus with April 12, 1990 for a net premium of Rs 15 lakh.

As per the rules, the scheme would cover farmers, farm labourers and mandi workers against all accidents arising out of the use of agricultural machinery, agricultural implements, digging of tubewells, electric current, while watering the fields and even snake bites.

The scheme was implemented throughout Punjab through its market committees. The amount of claim which was the financial assistance received by way of cases through market committees would be paid by the insurance company in the office of the Mandi Board.

As per the complaints, despite receiving the receipt, the company was not releasing the amount of the claim, that is, financial assistance due in the office of the Mandi Board. Therefore, Mandi Board served a notice to release the claims.

In its reply, the United India Insurance pleaded that the concerned forum had no jurisdiction to entertain the complaint, as it was not filed by a person authorised to institute the complaint. It was pleaded that the premium calculated was initially Rs 15 lakh, but the matter was referred to the head office and instructions were received which were communicated to the complainant.

As per the instructions, the premium would be Rs 1.25 crore for the above risk. The complainant was either to remit an amount of Rs 1.10 crore towards balance premium to enable the company to assume the risk, or advise the company so as to refund the Rs 15 lakh already paid.

Heading: 2 killed, 1 hurt in separate accidents - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed a dealer of a water filter company to refund Rs 3,600 charged towards a defective water filter.

In addition, the dealer has been ordered to pay Rs 1,100 as penalty for causing mental and physical harassment to the consumer.

The complainant, one Krishan Kumar Bansal, purchased one water filter of Aqua Fresh for Rs 3,600 from New Milan Associates in Sector 45.

The water filter carried a one year warranty at the time of purchase. The said amount was to be paid in installments of Rs 600 each, for which Bansal issued cheques.

However, Bansal has alleged that the water filter stopped working on the very next day of the purchase. He then informed the dealer, who sent his official to repair the machine after three days. But the water filter broke down once again.

This time, the official of the company took the filter with him and fitted an old filter in its place. However, he did not turn up for five days.

Moreover, the old water filter also stopped working on the very next day. Thereafter, the complainant approached the dealer and requested him to take back the water filter and return his cheques, but to no avail.

The forum said that New Milan Associates were grossly deficient in service.

Heading: Kharar civic body takes over Sunny Enclave - Indian Express
Content:
Two persons were killed and one sustained severe injuries in two separate accidents in the city on Wednesday. Pradeep Kumar, a Bapu Dham Colony resident, succumbed to his injuries after being hit by a speeding car near Sat Sang Bhawan in Sector 26, Madhya Marg, this morning. He was rushed to PGI where he later died.

In another incident, a pillion rider on a motorbike succumbed to his injuries after an unidentified truck hit the motorbike late on Tuesday evening near Needle Factory, Industrial Area Phase-I. Amandeep Singh, a Mohali resident and Onkar Singh a resident of Manimajra, sustained severe injuries and were rushed to GMCH-32, where Onkar died and Amandeep is in a critical state.

The police have registered cases but no arrests have been made till now.

Heading: Air warriors celebrate a year of achievements on Air Force Day - Indian Express
Content:
In a major decision involving responsibility to cater to the needs of thousands of residents, the Kharar Municipal Council has taken over one of the most inhabited township — Sunny Enclave — located on the busy Kharar-Mohali stretch of National Highway-21 in Desumajra village.

Kharar Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Rajeev Kumar Gupta, who is also the MC Administrator, has accepted the proposal of Bajwa Developers Limited. The same was rejected by the previous elected body of the Kharar MC at its meeting on January 30, 2008.

Overruling the previous rejection, the SDM-cum-Administrator adopted a resolution on September 26 to hand over a major responsibility to the civic body, which was still finding it difficult to satisfy the residents of vast areas already under its control.

The bureaucratic decision taken almost two weeks after the election of the new civic body raised many eyebrows, besides questioning the urgency of the matter when the new MC House was about to take charge shortly bringing an end to the Administrator's rule.

The SDM-cum-Administrator justified the decision on the grounds that the developer has given an undertaking to maintain the township for the next seven years. "The case was lying pending since May due to the poll code and the decision was subject to final approval by the Director, Local Government," reasoned Gupta, while referring to the MC Executive Officer for further discussion on the matter.

However, Sunny Enclave developer Jarnail Singh Bajwa said the previous civic body had certain property dealers as councillors, who remained instrumental in rejecting his proposal. "I have been trying for years to hand over my township to the MC just to get back my bank guarantees deposited with PUDA," rued Bajwa while claiming that since he was bound to maintain the area for seven years, handing over Sunny Enclave will serve him no other purpose except enabling him to get back his bank guarantees.

Contrary to the claims of the SDM-cum-Administrator and Bajwa, the accepted proposal read that the developer will maintain roads, footpaths, parks and trees in the township for five years from the issuance of development license, which dates back to 2001 and 2002 for major parts of Sunny Enclave.

As per the accepted proposal, Bajwa Developers will transfer to the MC all non-saleable open spaces in all its six extensions of Sunny Enclave, where 500 streetlight points, 36 parks, a gurdwara and a temple exist. The developer undertook to construct a community centre and school on the earmarked sites in extension 4.

Heading: Security stepped up in Patiala ahead of Dussehra - Indian Express
Content:
This year has been a remarkable one for the Air Force Station, Chandigarh (12 Wing). The officials, while celebrating Air Force Day on Wednesday, looked back at the achievements during the year and appreciated the good work of their fellowmen.

The station had pressed into service its aircrafts and men to provide disaster relief to earthquake victims in China and bomb attack victims at the Indian Embassy in Kabul. The base also accomplished the challenging task of landing an AN-32 aircraft at the world's highest airfield called Daulat Beg Oldie (DBO) in Aksai Chin. The air warriors of this station also undertook a high altitude trek in Himachal.

The station acts like a bridge connecting Jammu and Kashmir with the rest of the country. When the road links to these regions are unavailable, the aircrafts of this base serve as the lifeline of the valley.

On July 7, 2008, the Indian Embassy in Kabul was hit by a massive suicide bomb attack, which resulted in the death of four embassy staffers including the Defence Attaché, a Brigadier of the Indian Army, and an IFS officer. The IAF was called upon by the Government of India, to provide immediate assistance by way of launching a relief mission. Air Force Station, Chandigarh responded with alacrity and efficiency and dispatched an IL-76 aircraft to Kabul via Delhi with medicines and rescue personnel in less than two hours. The aircraft returned to Palam at midnight the same day.

On 15 May 08, one IL-76 of 25 Sqn was tasked for a Humanitarian / Disaster Relief (HA/DR) mission to the People's Republic of China (PRC), which was reeling in the aftermath of a massive earthquake in Sichuan province in the south-western part of the country. A total of 96.2 tonne of relief material comprising tents, blankets, food, medical supplies and sleeping bags were airlifted.

Apart from these, units of the Chandigarh base actively participated in flood relief operations in Bihar recently.

Heading: Decks cleared for Sarangpur Education City - Indian Express
Content:
In view of the recent terror strikes in various parts of the country, the city police will be on high alert during Dussehra on Thursday. Police sources said that security measures have been stepped up to avert any mishap.

"Metal detectors and CCTV networks have been installed at certain places. Also, policemen in plain clothes have been deputed at critical places to avert any mishap during the festival season," said an official. Dussehra celebrations will be held at various places across the city. Hence, the job of the policemen has become tougher, given the recent terror waves in various parts of the country.

However, the routine works of the police have been affected, as majority of the policemen are busy with the security arrangements. "Almost half of our force has been busy for the last one week at the Kali Mata temple due to the heavy inflow of pilgrims. This means that routine works like passport verification, investigations and other cases are lying pending in the police stations," said a senior police officer.

Senior police officials told Newsline that they are not taking any chances and security is the prime concern for them.

Heading: Sociology students of CBSE Class XII to have practical projects from 2010 - Indian Express
Content:
Chandigarh Administration signs MoUs with three companies

The Chandigarh Administration on Wednesday cleared the decks for setting up of an Education City at Sarangpur Institution Area, by signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with three parties.

Present on the occasion, UT Administrator S F Rodrigues said the project of Education City had been conceived to create world-class educational infrastructure, with the main focus on empowering children and sharpening their skills to make them professionally competent as well as confident individuals.

"Special emphasis has been laid on providing assistance, in the form of scholarships and low-cost quality education to committed and intelligent students belonging to the disadvantaged sections, who cannot afford to pay normal fees in other institutions," he said.

The three companies whose representatives signed MoUs with UT Home-cum-Education Secretary Ram Niwas included NMIMS (Narsee Monjee Institute of Management Studies), Chitkara Education Trust Chandigarh and Indian Express Newspapers (Mumbai) Limited.

Sources said the Education City also has effective linkages with the Rajiv Gandhi Information Technology Park, Film City, Theme Park and Medicity to share infrastructure support.

Rodrigues said being one of the mega projects to come up at the Sarangpur Institutional area on the UT's periphery, Education City will help in making Chandigarh a regional hub for extending support to the people of the region.

"Chandigarh is emerging as the regional hub to extend support to 60 million people of the region with its various new projects like the international airport, Mass Rapid Transport System, a super-fast train service between Delhi-Amritsar via Chandigarh and a modern terminal market for agriculture in the pipeline," added Rodrigues.

Dr N M Kondap, Vice Chancellor, NMIMS, assured to play an active role in various societal endeavours for building a prosperous life in the region.

Besides eminent educationists, Sanjay Kumar, Finance Secretary and Vivek Atray, Director Tourism and Public Relations were present on the occasion.

Heading: ‘Unhealthy’ beep on cell phone radar - Indian Express
Content:
Taking a note of the changing education trends, the Central Board of Secondary Education has decided to include a 20-mark practical project in sociology for students of Class XII.

It will be implemented in the Board examinations to be held in 2010. The project has been introduced in Class XI from this academic session onwards and shall be implemented for the students appearing in their Class XII examination next year.

New textbooks of sociology were introduced for Class XI in 2006-07 and for Class XII in 2007-08, in view of the revision of the syllabus according to the directions from the National Curriculum Framework 2005.

The CBSE through its circular has mentioned that sociology as a discipline is more a mode of inquiry rather than a fixed body of knowledge and hence the importance of the project.

Clarifying about the marks, the CBSE, has said that both the practical project as well as the theory paper shall be evaluated by external examiners.

Rakesh Sachdeva, Principal, DAV Senior Secondary School, Sector 15 said: "Sociology is a very interesting subject and projects like visiting old-age homes, slums, will provide an in depth knowledge of the subject. Students will be able to have a clearer picture of the social setup."

Vinita Arora, Principal, Bhavan Vidyalaya, Sector 27, said: "The practical aspect of any subject is a welcome move as it will give a better perspective to the students. Since the concept of education is moving more towards practical knowledge, students will definitely benefit from this."

Heading: ‘Students from small cities will get a huge exposure at WORDZ’ - Indian Express
Content:
A study with an aim to sensitise the general public on the ill effects of excessive cell-phone usage caused by electromagnetic radiation has been recently conducted at Panjab University (PU).

The study has shown that eggs exposed to four working mobiles become half-boiled in very little time. Not only this, the study has also informed that the Sectors 8, 9, 17, 18, 21, 23, 27, 30, 32, 33, 34, 35, 38, 44, 45, 46, 59 and 51 in the city are exposed to electromagnetic radiation released by the mobile phone towers, far more than the prescribed limit (as per a petition filed in the Supreme Court).

Prof V P Sharma, Dr R K Kohli and Dr H P Singh have conducted the study. While both Dr Kohli and Dr Singh are from the Department of Botany, Prof Sharma is from the Department of Zoology.

"We conducted research with an aim to sensitise the general public and make them aware of the fact that long hours of talking over cell phones can really damage the ears," Dr Kohli told Newsline.

The study has shown that mobile towers have two kinds of effects: thermal effect and non-thermal radiation effect. These effects are being studied simultaneously by the university on plants, honeybees and chicken eggs.

Meanwhile, the ENT department of the PGI has also conducted a similar study and found that spending long hours on the cell phone may result in loss of hearing. Some international studies also say that it can cause brain tumours.

Prof S Prabhakar, Head of the Department of Neurology, PGI, said, "The study has definitely shown that excessive cell phone usage is harmful. However, the exact nature of harm caused to the human body is yet to be ascertained. I believe phones should be used only to the extent of their requirement."

Heading: Dussehra celebrated in schools - Indian Express
Content:
More than 200 schools from across the country are participating in a three-day conference, WORDZMUN, at the Confederation of Indian Industries. This is the first time that the city is hosting the programme.

Atin Batra, Secretary General, WORDZ says: "WORDZ has mostly been held in cities like Delhi, Bangalore and Mumbai. We wanted to expose students of Chandigarh and nearby areas to this concept. Thus, we have invited schools from towns like Nabha, Hisar, Ambala to participate in the programme."

In the programme, students representing different countries discuss globally relevant issues like prevention of outer space arms race, nuclear waste management, strengthening of women and children rights, unrest in Darfur, among others.

"Students from small cities will get a great amount of exposure at WORDZ, which will help refine their public speaking skills. The reason that we have students representing countries rather than themselves, is that, through this, they learn to look at a particular problem from another's perspective. Though it is difficult to remove personal biases, WORDZ is worth a try," said Ashmita, Vice-President, WORDZ.

The three-day conference, concluded at a function held at St Stephen's School today. Dr BC Gupta, Principal Secretary (Home), Punjab, was the chief guest on the occasion.

The three-day conference saw the participation of more than 20 teams, where students discussed issues of global importance. While the best delegation award went to the team from GD Goenka Public School, the students from Delhi Public School, RK Puram, received the maximum number of prizes.

Students unhappy
The programme, has, however, come under criticism by some participants due to the cost factor involved. Each student had to deposit a fee of Rs 1,000 as expenses for their boarding, lodging and food. The students were also required to wear business suits to give a 'complete' look to the seminar. A participant said: "They could have held the seminar in school uniforms. It was an unnecessary expenditure of a few thousand and I am not sure if I will wear this ever again."

Heading: High-voltage compensation for Rajpura thermal plant - Indian Express
Content:
The students and staff of the Aryans Institute of Management and Technology (AIMT) today celebrated Dussehra at the college. After burning the effigy of Ravana, sweets were distributed. Over 100 students of BBA and BCA participated in the function. Anshu Kataria, Chairman, Aryans Group of Institutes (AGOI) presided over the function. The students presented a cultural programme which included solo songs, plays, jokes, brain teasers, group songs and couplets.

St Kabir Public School, Sector 26
The students of St Kabir Public School, Sector 26, Chandigarh, celebrated Dussehra with much fervour. Students dressed up as Lord Ram, Sita, Laxman and Hanuman spoke about the significance of the festival. The students also made masks, crowns and puppets and made sketches of Ravan. Addressing the students, principal J P Singh said students should be aware of the Indian traditions and celebrating such festivals in schools was a good way to do so.

Small Wonders School, Mohali
The weeklong celebrations marking the Dussehra festivities at Small Wonders School, Phase 7, Mohali concluded today. During the Mythological Week, many events and competitions were held. The students learnt about Indian mythology and importance of the festival. The festive events organised at the school campus included narration of mythological tales to the children, enactment and depiction of Ramayana by students and the symbolic burning of effigy of Ravana showing the triumph of good over evil.
A poster-making competition on "Say no to crackers" was also organised to encourage students to celebrate Dussehra and Diwali in a less polluting and harmless manner.
Speaking about the festivities, Sandeep Singh, Director, Small Wonders said that the festival season in India is long drawn and offers excellent opportunity to relate to Indian traditions. "Dussehra and Diwali celebrations are the most exciting events in Indian festival calendar which should be aptly utilised to sensitise students towards Indian values.

Heading: Only VIP sangat gets darshan here - Indian Express
Content:
State likely to announce over Rs 40 lakh per acre

After Rs 1.50 crore per acre for international airport in Mohali, the Punjab Government is likely to offer the second highest compensation of over Rs 40 lakh an acre for setting up the thermal plant in Rajpura.

Sources said the committee formed under Patiala Deputy Commissioner Vikas Garg for awarding compensation for 1,078 acres has given its final report to the government. The committee has recommended Rs 40 lakh per acre, which would include Rs 34.5 lakh per acre as compensation and rest as displacement and employment allowance.

The compensation will have a binding, whereby farmers will not be allowed to move court for higher award. The Revenue Department has issued notices for acquisition of land in seven villages, including Nalas Kalan, Nalas Khurd, Rangia and Sadhraur.

"The report was submitted to the Power and Irrigation Department, which forwarded it to the Chief Secretary. Now, it is lying with the Chief Minister, who has to give the final nod. Then, the file will be placed before the cabinet," said an officer. The last day of receiving bids for the 1,320-MW thermal plant is November 14.

Meanwhile, 2,432 acres have been identified along NH-15 on the Bathinda-Abohar road, near Gidderbaha in Muktsar district, for 2,460-MW Gidderbaha thermal power plant.

The site study contract has been finalised and the Irrigation Department has started the process for water allocation. The application for long-term coal linkage has been made and Railways has given clearance for transportation.

The state government had also acquired 2,100 acres for the 1,980-MW Talwandi Sabo plant at the rate of Rs 16.5 lakh per acre.

For the Goindwal thermal plant, the state government acquired 1,100 acres at Rs 16.50 lakh per acre.

An officer said, "The government acquires the land, while the companies pay the compensation."

Heading: Akal Takht Jathedar miffed with Harbhajan - Indian Express
Content:
Only a select few had the privilege of attending Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal's Sangat Darshan in Kapurthala and Jalandhar. The residents who had come with grievances raised slogans outside the tent when the police did not allow them to meet the CM.

"This Sangat Darshan is eyewash, as only selected panchayat members were allowed to meet the CM," said Paramjit Kaur of Shahkot Sanghwal village. Even inside the tent, the women who had lined up to meet the CM, were stopped by the cops mid-way. They said they had directions from higher authorities.

"We wanted to ask the CM that he had announced compensation for the flood-affected farmers, but what about the farm labourers, who are sittings idle at home," said Paramjit Kaur.

Sukhjinder Kaur of Mandhala village said she wanted to ask the CM when would the state implement National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme, under which 100 days of assured employment is given to the jobless in villages. "I was not allowed to meet the CM, who was sitting 50 yard away," she added.

Bibi Baksho of Giddarpindi had come with a demand of waiving farmers' loan taken from the co-operative banks, but she too had to return empty-handed. A group of women later raised slogans against the CM.

Similar was the scene at the Sangat Darshan held at Bharoana village in Kapurthala district.

Badal met 17 panchayats in Kapurthala and 12 in Jalandhar. The cavalcade of the CM blocked the entire Jalandhar-Makhu Road for hours together, causing inconvenience to commuters.

Heading: Wildlife Week: Minister says forest cover in state depleting - Indian Express
Content:
The cricketer and actress Mona Singh dressed as Ravana and Sita for a TV dance show

Akal Takht Jathedar Giani Gurbachan Singh has taken a strong exception to off-spinner Harbhajan Singh and TV actress Mona Singh dressing up as Ravana and Sita on a television dance show.

The Jathedar said though they have received no written complaint against the two celebrities, no one can mock at the religious traditions and Gods.

Certain sections of the Hindu organisations have also taken an umbrage at the show. "How can Ravana and Sita dance together? There has to be an end to such parodies," said Gurbachan Singh.

He said both Bhajji and Mona were Sikhs, and he, as the head of the community, would not like its members to mock at religious personalities. "We believe in respecting all religions," he added.

"I am waiting for a written complaint and a report will be filed thereafter. And if the two stars are found guilty of religious misconduct, action will be initiated against them," said the Jathedar.

Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee chief Avtar Singh Makkar said he was not aware of the episode, but feels that personalities who were role models for the coming generations should desist from such mischief.

Makkar said the Akal Takht Jathedar was entitled to act against them if they had done something wrong.

Heading: Denied permission to hold Dusshera function, Congress MLA cries foul - Indian Express
Content:
The Wildlife Week held with a view to sensitise people towards preservation of flora and fauna ended on a sad note today, with Minister for Forests and Wildlife Preservation Tikshan Sud accepting that the forest cover of Punjab was depleting fast.

The minister said the practice of associating trees, birds and animals with religious beliefs could prove fruitful in wildlife preservation.

Sud said more trees had been felled in the state than planted.

"The government has earned a revenue of Rs 15 crore by selling trees felled along the roadside since it came to power more than a year ago," he said, adding that the green cover inPunjab has been reduced to 5.5 per cent.

He, however, quickly added that these trees mainly comprised those which had either dried up or had to be removed from the roadsides to facilitate widening of roads and other developmental projects.

"Efforts are being made to compensate felling of trees by planting more, but the government alone cannot do much in this regard," he said.

Stressing the need to spread awareness about environment, Sud said the government proposed to promote ecological tourism in the state.

Chief Wildlife Warden, Punjab, HS Gujral said the government has notified 12 wildlife sanctuaries and two community reserves in the state for wildlife conservation.

Others who addressed the gathering included Financial Commissioner, Forests and Wildlife Preservation, RC Nayyar, Baba Sewa Singh from Khadoor Sahib and Tarn Taran Deputy Commissioner Khushi Ram.

Heading: Special schemes take toll on teaching in schools - Indian Express
Content:
Politics will cast its shadow over Dusshera celebrations at Chheherta grain market, as Congress MLA Om Parkash Soni alleged that the ruling SAD-BJP leaders and the district administration have not allowed him to hold a function.

He said last year too, he was denied the permission despite the fact that he had been organising the function for the past many years at the same venue.

Notably, last year, a clash between the Congress and the SAD workers took place and several persons were injured. Soni warned the ruling party and civil authorities not to put a spanner in the function or else he would ask his supporters to forcibly occupy the ground.

DC KS Pannu said they provide the ground on first-come-first basis and would maintain law and order.

Heading: Finally, CCI starts cotton purchase - Indian Express
Content:
The state government's various schemes launched to improve primary education in Punjab has lead to a situation where teachers are finding it hard to take out time for the main subjects.

As the teachers are busy in the implementation of various schemes, the main syllabus is being taught for hardly an hour a day.

Presently, the school timings are 9 am to 2:25 pm, out of which, 9 to 9:30 has been set aside as the prayer time; 9:30 to 12 pm is the time for 'Padho Punjab' classes, 12 to 12:30 pm is for the much-in-news 'Radio Programme', and then comes the break for the mid-day meal.

This practically leaves the teachers with only one hour and five minutes (1:20 pm to 2:25 pm), in which they have to take the classes of other subjects. Earlier, there used to be 45 minutes devoted to each subjects.

A teacher said, "The time we get is inadequate to finish the syllabus."

"The government should make it clear whether the exams would be taken on the basis of the innovative new classes or the syllabus of the five subjects meant for primary education," said various primary school teachers.

When contacted, District Education Officer (DEO), Primary, Joginder Das, said the schemes were launched as per the government's directions and he could not comment on them.

Heading: KN Hospital to be shifted to IGMC - Indian Express
Content:
The Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) today finally entered the market, giving a relief to the farmers, who had been selling their produce to private players at a price lower than the MSP of Rs 2,800 per quintal.

The CCI today purchased 5,020 bales from more than 15 locations in Bathinda, Mansa, Faridkot, Muktsar and Moga districts. The prices offered ranged between Rs 2,700 and Rs 2,800 per quintal, said NS Sidhu, Cotton Officer, Bathinda.

Since the cotton started arriving in Mandis from September 15, about 1.11 lakh bales had been purchased by private players till yesterday, said an official of the Punjab State Agricultural Marketing Board (PSAMB).

Even as the CCI went into an overdrive to purchase cotton, farmers at some of the locations expressed apprehensions over uniformity in purchase pattern by the CCI. "No doubt, farmers are feeling relieved today, but we don't know whether the CCI would keep the momentum on in the coming days as well," said Jagroop Singh of Narang village, who had come to Rama Mandi with his produce.

"We are not even sure if the tempo would be maintained during the later half the day today, what to talk of tomorrow," said another cotton grower, Inderjit Singh. Sidhu, however, said the CCI was committed to continue the purchase.

Earlier, the CCI started purchase in Rama Mandi in the presence of PSAMB chairman Ajmer Singh Lakhowal, who also inaugurated a shed on the occasion. Answering media queries, Lakhowal said the market waiver proposal was under government consideration. Different farmers' bodies of Muktsar district, under a common banner, submitted a memorandum to Lakhowal, listing their problems.

Heading: Judicial inquiry into Tihar deaths - Indian Express
Content:
Move to shift the women and child care facility part of series of reforms

The government has decided to shift Kamla Nehru Hospital, a women and child care facility, to Indira Gandhi Medical College (IGMC) and Hospital.

Though no formal announcement to this effect has been made, senior IGMC doctors and principal Dr Surinder Kashyap are understood to have been informed about the move.

At present, the Kamla Nehru Hospital could be housed in the unoccupied new block of Government Dental College, just next to the IGMC complex. Dental college principal Dr Ashu Bhardwaj is learnt to have been told about the decision and asked to help in accommodating the patients of Kamla Nehru Hospital.

Principal Secretary (Health) Deepak Shanan, who is the brain behind a series of medical sector reforms, confirmed that the government is thinking of re-structuring the women and child care facilities.

"Following reports of deaths of infants or mothers, who sometime are required to be shifted to IGMC in emergencies, the need to shift Kamla Nehru Hospital closer to IGMC was felt," he said.

Sources said sitting BJP MLA Suresh Bhardwaj, who earlier had also been a Rajya Sabha member, has been persistently struggling for shifting of Kamla Nehru Hospital either to the newly-built Government Dental College or the IGMC itself.

Right now, under the plan, the Dental College will stay at its present location, but space is being made for indoor patients, OPDs and operation theatres, beside doctors' rooms of the Kamla Nehru Hospital.

Subsequently, the government proposes to appoint a consultant to prepare a report for complete restructuring of the IGMC building and streamlining functioning of various units of clinical health care.

Heading: ‘Saina is a top-five material’ - Indian Express
Content:
Tihar jail officials are set to face the heat as a city court holds judicial inquiry on the deaths of two jail inmates, with medical reports hinting at negligence in treatment.

In the first case, 45-year-old Sohan Singh, who was jailed for involvement in a drugs case, died on October 3 owing to multiple wounds in his liver. He was referred to DDU Hospital after a whole month, for better medical care. According to sources, the medical report suggests that it was a case of sheer negligence by jail personnel. In the second case, 55-year-old Sohan Kaur, who was in custody since August 22 for alleged complicity in a cheating case, died on October 1 due to complications arising out of abnormal blood pressure. Kaur was declared dead on arrival at the DDU hospital; doctors cited the swelling up of her liver and lungs as the cause of death.

Sunil Gupta, Tihar's PRO, however said both inmates were provided adequate medical care and the magisterial inquiry was a routine affair as laid down under the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Heading: Why overhaul a winning unit? - Indian Express
Content:
Prakash Padukone thinks that Saina Nehwal has arrived as a complete player. Currently ranked No. 11 in the world, the shuttler has the potential and, as he succinctly put it, has "the right temperament and attitude" to reach the top-five in a couple of years' time. But the legendary badminton player has a piece of advice to offer: "Pick and choose your tournaments. That is what separates a mature player from the also-rans," said Prakash after inaugurating the Punjabi Bagh Club prize-money tournament here this morning.

Admitting that Saina is the best thing to happen to Indian badminton, Prakash said it is up to the current crop of players to keep themselves fit. "But that is only possible if a player is able to pick his or her tournament properly because playing in more tournaments would mean suffering niggles as tournaments takes place every week."

Giving credit to Saina's coach, Prakash said that Pullela Gopichand, who is also the national coach, has aptly planned her schedule and it is paying rich dividends. "Badminton these days has become more demanding and players will have to work on their fitness accordingly. Otherwise, players could end up suffering one injury or another which can keep them out of action for quite some time," he warned.

Talking on Anup Sridhar and Chetan Anand, the former All-England champion said he was following Anand's recent exploits and was immensely pleased. But he said he would not say that great talents have emerged in the country. "Yes, these players have been able to change the scene quite a bit with right kind of exposures but, by no stretch of imagination, I would say we have arrived."

Prakash was suggesting that India have quite a long way to go despite improvement in the game. "For that matter, we should say that every sport has improved. But in terms of the popularity of the shuttle game we have still miles to go. "

Recalling his days, Prakash said there were fewer tournaments abroad and still fewer competitions at home. He also said that there was only one academy in Bangalore that he floated after retiring from the game. "But today, there are academies in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Delhi. Clubs organizing tournaments like here is another good example of how the game is gaining in popularity."

But he rued the fact that India were unfortunate not to produce players in multiples. Citing the example of Nandu Natekar, Syed Modi, Gopichand and now Sridhar or Anand, he said it has been India's problem because no more than a single player dominated at a particular point of time. Prakash was a loner when he dominated the game in the 80s until he retired.

"Unlike in China, Indonesia and Malaysia or in the European nations where badminton is a big-time game, India have never thrown up a combination of players at any specific juncture. We haven't had more than a single player doing consistently well to give tough competition."

Speaking on his experience, particularly his deceptive game, when he went to play in Denmark — he stayed in Copenhagen for six years — after winning the All-England champions in the 80s, he said he had gained much after playing the likes of Martin Frost. "Yes, it was a good experience but the youngster (Frost) was able to sort me out after a few years. But I must admit I had gained more and I have no regrets whatsoever."

Heading: One-stop shops - Indian Express
Content:
DDCA opts for a new selection committee which, in turn, picks a new captain

A ranji Trophy victory was supposed to put things in order but, as it happens in the Delhi & District Cricket Association (DDCA), last season's triumph has only triggered disorder within its ranks. It began right from the top and trickled down, infecting all quarters — the selectors, skipper and, finally, the list of probables.

While Arun Jaitley's elevation as BCCI vice-president is great news, there's an emergent need for the DDCA president to have a re-look at the cricketing affairs in his own backyard.

First up, the complete lack of recognition to the senior selection committee that picked a champion side last season is appalling. This despite a fervent plea by Virender Sehwag and Gautam Gambhir in person to the DDCA top brass to retain the same set for sake of continuity.

Instead, the sports committee removed two selectors Vinay Lamba and Vivek Razdan, demoted Manu Nayyar to under-22 and appointed three fresh selectors in their place. That the three new appointments were previously relieved of their duties midway by Jaitley is all the more intriguing, so is the lack of initiative or intent on the executive committee's behalf to overturn arbitrary decisions.

In its very first meeting, the new selection committee spotted a 'fault' at the top of the team list, and 'corrected' it by replacing existing skipper Mithun Manhas with Aakash Chopra. While the decision to sack Manhas — who has stood in for Sehwag, when the regular captain and his deputy Gambhir are with the Indian team — has spread acrimony within the senior players, it has also sent out wrong signals as well.

Chairman of selector Chetan Chauhan, however, insists that the decision to appoint Chopra was unanimous. "We wanted someone with Test experience as a skipper. Besides, everyone thought Chopra is having a great season and this responsibility can pep him up further. So when the question to appoint a stand-by skipper in absence of Sehwag cropped up, everyone immediately agreed on Chopra's name," he says.

However, the insiders say Manhas's removal was handwork of sports committee. Manhas has a good track record as skipper leading Delhi and North Zone and had refused interference in team selection. That went against him.

"If they think Chopra will agree to certain players being picked, they are mistaken. No player would like to undo his reputation including undeserving players. Chopra will have our backing, no doubt, but again the manner in which seniors are treated, even after winning, is humiliating," says a senior player.

Coach Vijay Dahiya says the change in command will not affect the morale of the team. "I would say a new set up has come and there's a change of thought. And the change of skipper is just a reflection of that. The team will still be together, I don't think it will affect the players in any way. Our path this year will be just the same as last year," he says.

That Delhi are the defending champions should provide a perfect platform to rectify all wrongs, but it's being used by some as cushion to reduce the impact of their misdeeds.

Heading: Twin strokes - Indian Express
Content:
Want to rustle up an exotic menu at home? Step into any of the exclusive outlets for your ingredients and more

A trip through the winding alleys of INA market was once firmly inked in the to-do list of every traveller, expatriate and local resident fancying an exotic meal at home. But Delhi's one-point stop for scrumptious goodies has now got competition from a string of region-specific stores that offer everything from homegrown food products to native pots and pans.

For instance, if you plan to pair a bowl of steaming homemade noodles with something exotically Korean, a drive to A-Mart can solve your kitchen worries. The spacious store in Mahipalpur has South Korean food as its forte. Run your eye through the racks, and you will spot tins of egg tuna in soya sauce, silkworm pupa (Rs 135 for a can), snail tuna (Rs 185) and black rice (Rs 600 a pack). A large freezer in one corner is layered with packs of meats including shrimp nuggets (Rs 380 for 500 gms) and ready-to-eat momos. "There are over 5,000 Koreans staying in Delhi and NCR and many are regulars at our store. Japanese and Chinese expats too flock in as do patrons from MNCs in Bangalore and Chennai," says Ellen Lee, general manager, A-Mart, adding that the products are flown in every month.

At Hauz Khas village, a bright red banner announces Northeastern. A fleet of stairs leads to an equally bright shop on the second floor. The recently opened shop is laden with black pottery and (Rs 500-Rs 4,000) colourful tribal jewellery (Rs 50 for a pair of ear rings and Rs 3,000 for a neckpiece). Set up by Ashim Pearl, a professional potter, the store has found a loyal clientele among the well-heeled crowd that struts the posh village market and wants to furbish kitchens with ethnic pottery. Though footfall has decreased at Hauz Khas of late, Northeastern still boasts a number of patrons.

A Manipuri, Pearl came to Delhi in 2000. "Black pottery is a dying art form and I thought Delhi was the best platform to revive it," she says. At her workshop in Mahipalpur, five artisans from her hometown spin out beautiful kettles, flower vases and candle stands. "Initially, it was difficult to get raw materials, but now I rely on friends travelling home," says Pearl, who will also be participating in a group exhibition at India Habitat Centre next month.

The Sikkim Organic Store in Pamposh Enclave offers fruits, pickles and teas that have come all the way from the hills. Set up by the government of Sikkim and Sikkim Apex Grower Association, the store boasts goodies like Nakema ginger, Dallae chilli, Lapsi or Ningro pickle and fermented mustard leaves for garnishing soups. There are packs of Temi tea (Rs 65 for 125 gms) and a bamboo basket holds Iris flower buds (Rs 15 a piece). The store also offers flowers like lilium and anthurium. Awareness about the benefits of organic food makes the store a popular stop. "We get lots of customers from south Delhi," says Kiran Rai of the store.

At Safdarjung Enclave market, Yamatoya could be your stop if you plan to roll out a Japanese meal. Options here include nori sheets, sushi mats, lacquered soup bowl, packs of dried baby sardines, a variety of tinned food and sauces like teriyaki, hashed beef, and oyster sauce (Rs 250 onwards). Spread over two levels, the shop is a favourite haunt of expats and locals.

"There are a few shops in Munirka too that sell typical Northeastern food and most of my friends in Delhi go there," adds Pearl. These apart, popular chains like Food Bazar, Spencer's and Le Marche are the new hotspots for picking up bonito shavings, scallops and salted salmon. Looks like, there won't be a trip to INA market soon.

Heading: All in the Family - Indian Express
Content:
The artist duo from Kolkata is forging a path into a controversial territory

The young man, a kind of Adonis, is dressed in rich robes and wears a crown of leaves. He gently looks down at a bunch of flowers in his hand as if to contemplate and compare his own beauty with that of the flowers. The colours in the frame are bright, the young man too life like to have been inside the painting, his sexuality and beauty contrasted with the flowers. In case this work, titled Flower Vass, reminds you of the French gay duo Pierre and Gilles, don't mention it to Suman Samajpati (32) and Sourav Roy Chowdhury (30), the Kolkata artists who go by the group name Taxi.

"We're arguably the first duo to be doing photo-paintings in India and the essence of our work is completely different from Pierre's and Gilles'. And we're not gay," says Roy Chowdhury emphatically. Samajpati and Roy Chowdhury are exhibiting their works as part of Outer Circle, the inaugural exhibition by the new arts collective, Religare Arts Initiative.

Photo-paintings or paintings on photography has captivated the boys for as long as they can remember. While Samajpati is a trained graphic artist from NIFT, Kolkata, Roy Chowdhury works as a commercial photographer with several advertising agencies. They began collaborating in 2005 and formed Taxi to break new ground in the Indian art scene. "Taxi symbolises a journey for us, a destination to be reached, a score of people to meet and experiences on the way," smiles Samajpati.

The experiences haven't been great so far. "The Kolkata art scene is very conservative and what we do is not considered art at all. To make things worse, our first collection is based on gender relations and exploring sexuality. Delhi, fortunately, is far more appreciative and informed about contemporary art and our work is being recognised here," says Roy Chowdhury.

Each work begins with the duo bouncing ideas off each other, while Samajpati prepares a storyboard. Artifice is central to their work— human subjects are set in floral, elaborate poses against alluring backdrops.

The artists draw inspiration from a host of influences, from mythology and cinema to classic lithographic shots to family albums. "Our work serves as a fanciful documentation for an array of subjects, each with its own stories. We are interested in looking at different lifestyles, cultures, gender relations and sexuality from our perspective," says Samajpati. And they paint a pretty picture while at it.

Outer Circle is on at 7, Atma Ram Mansion, Scindia House, Kasturba Gandhi Marg till October 31

Heading: RAIL TRAIL - Indian Express
Content:
Students of Summer Fields School, Gurgaon, take part in the heritage walk at Lodhi Gardens conducted by The Indian Express in association with INTACH and ASI

A schools' initiative from The Express Group
Quest is a project conducted by The Indian Express in schools in and around Delhi. It covers more than 50 schools in Delhi and NCR.

Quest aims at stirring awareness and opinions. Today, when all that children see are shopping malls and cineplexes, we at The Indian Express want to show a completely different picture of this city to them. Delhi has changed beyond nostalgia and recognition since Independence. How many of these kids know of the 'Seven Cities' of Delhi or the stories of the pigeon fliers of Old Delhi? The idea behind such an activity is to create awareness about the various structures and monuments that the students do not know about. This is a specially designed programme, which will help the students appreciate the rich culture and background of this city. In association with INTACH and ASI, this is a small effort on our behalf to depict a phase of our national life and the decay of a whole culture, a particular mode of thought and living. The visit is followed by the students sending in articles, pictures, poems, paintings, and collages to express their experiences about the heritage walk.

A mix of our heritage and nature's beauty
It was a pleasant and sunny day, and after getting stuck in traffic for some time, we finally reached our destination: the Lodhi Gardens. We were helped with information along the way by our guide, Ms Harika. Built in the 15th and 16th centuries by the Saiyads and the Lodhis, the vast grounds of the gardens, once a village, and the structures standing there, have been beautifully maintained and preserved. Various medieval monuments like tombs and mosques give the gardens a mystical charm. The tomb of Muhammad Shah is built in an octagonal pattern, with a central octagonal chamber, verandahs, arched openings on each side, and sloping buttresses. Apart from this, there is the Bara Gumbad, which is a square tomb with an imposing dome. The Sheesh Gumbad is also built in the square pattern, with a double-storied appearance, and looks much like the Bara Gumbad. Its ceiling has incised plaster work with floral patterns and inscriptions from the Quran. One can still see traces of the blue tiles that once adorned it and gave it its name. The tomb of Ibrahim Lodhi is built in the octagonal pattern, much like that of Muhammad Shah. Apart from the historical structures, I was very impressed by the environmental issues that have been taken into consideration by the government. The gardens have a variety of plants and trees, and me and my friends were impressed by the tall and huge Neem, Deodar and Chir trees, as well as herbal plants. We also learnt about birds that are commonly seen here from the billboards displayed but did not see any ourselves. I would like to thank The Indian Express for this memorable experience, which was a fun-filled way of getting close to our heritage.
— SURUCHI GUPTA, X D

An informative walk
The Lodhi Gardens are home to many tombs built by the Saiyads and the Lodhis in the 15th and 16th centuries. The gardens are well maintained and the huge variety of trees and plants here make the surroundings attractive. The gardens were once a small village. Under colonial rule, these gardens were called Lady Wellington Park and got their present name after Independence. The tombs of Muhammad Shah and Ibrahim Lodhi, along with the Bara Gumbad, have many arches, chhajjas, domes, and verandahs etc. All these structures are very beautiful. The Sheesh Gumbad resembles the Bara Gumbad and caught my eye because of the use of green and blue colours, usually used in Islamic monuments, giving it a glazed appearance. It was a great experience to be close to our heritage.
— MEENAL GANDHI, X B

Revisiting the Past
I went to the Lodhi Gardens along with my classmates for a heritage walk on September 24. The name 'heritage walk' had me thinking I was in for a boring history lesson. But the gardens and the monuments took me by surprise and before I knew it, I was enjoying myself. Built in 15th and 16th centuries, the Saiyads and Lodhis built many structures in the vast grounds of the Lodhi Gardens. The first thing we explored was Muhammad Shah's tomb and Sikander Lodhi's tomb. In the middle of the gardens stand the Bara Gumbad and the Sheesh Gumbad. The Bara Gumbad consists of a three-domed mosque and a residence around a central courtyard. The area seemed to posess unusual charm and adventure. The plush and well- kept gardens were truly a treat for the eyes and offered a peaceful and tranquil environment away from the hustle and bustle of city life.

The grandeur of the complex is truly breathtaking. It proved to be a very enjoyable and fun-filled trip.
— ANUBHA GUPTA, X D

Beyond books and classrooms
Enough of 123 , ABC…….
Out of the books, we Went to see
What we knew as the Medieval age
An essential part of our Heritage
Built in 1500s in Delhi;
Built by the great rulers- the Saiyads and the Lodhis
It was a knowledge enriching experience for all
Also, we were told about the Western Wall.
It made us to know Allah more closely,
As we went into the mosque built beautifully.
The concept of doors which were built odd
For making it even was the job of God.
We applauded the engravings on pillars
We cribbed about those who spoilt them in the Name of love.
The short trip was a memorable one,
All of us had loads of fun!
It was the best way to learn
About the kings and the other ranks,
So we students say thanks!
Cause the school gave us this chance
To know Indian heritage at a glance!
— PRIYANKA NAGPAL, X D
