Heading: DU goes to colleges for opinion on semesters - Indian Express
Content:
THE MAKING OF A MUSEUM
Indian Railway history was created on October 7, 1971. On this day, the foundation stone for the first ever transport museum in India was laid by the President of India, V V Giri. Also present on the occasion was the Minister for Railways K Hanumanthiya. Thus the Rail Transport Museum, now called the National Rail Museum, came into existence.

The President, in his address, said: I am sure this Museum will draw not only the students and those directly interested in the growth of the Railways but also ordinary men and women and thus be of considerable educative value. Railways are a great unifying factor in the country. This museum, I am sure, would go a long way in depicting the history of our Railways and create a feeling of public ownership and involvement in the development and well- being of the Railways... In a vast country like ours with long and rich heritage of Railway systems and operation, it should be possible for us, in the years to come, to set up such museums at various important centres in the country so that people get first hand knowledge of the working of the Railways... The Indian Railways have come a long way. To preserve and present India's rich rail legacy, Railways have set up regional rail museums in the Eastern Region at Calcutta, in the Southern Region at Madras and Mysore and a museum specialising in Narrow Gauge at Nagpur. The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway is showcased at the museum in Ghoom. A new regional museum for the Western Region is being set up at Lonavala. The Indian Railways remains committed to protecting, preserving and presenting for future generations its rich legacy.
— Meera Madhusudan,Former Guide Lecturer, National Rail Museum

THE FIRST INDIAN AT THE HELM
Driving down Cuffe Parade and turning onto Wodehouse Road in the southern tip of Mumbai, you will see a housing enclave on your left. Called "Badhwar Park", it is the colony where senior officials of the Indian Railways live when posted to the city. The complex has been aptly named after Shri Fateh Chand Badhwar, the first Indian chairman of the Indian Railway Board. Since its inception in 1925, all chairmen of the Railway Board had been Britons.

Taking over as chairman in 1951, he faced the onerous task of amalgamating the large number of rail systems in the country — ranging from government owned to private ownership by the Princely states. He successfully merged these diverse railways into a single unit, the Indian Railways, during his four-year tenure at the helm. A civil engineer by qualification, he used his technical background to reduce the dependency on imports, primarily from the UK, in keeping with the Nehruvian policy of self reliance. He was one of the first Indians to be recruited as an engineer in the erstwhile East Indian Railway in Calcutta in 1925, at a time when there were virtually no Indians manning the technical services.

Badhwar was a man of many facets. Apart from overseeing the consolidation and operations of the Indian Railways in the tumultuous days following Independence, he was a keen birdwatcher and mountaineer. He passed away in October 1995.

Locomotives in Steam
In the next thirteen weeks we will take you through the fascinating world of Indian steam locomotives, showcasing their development as depicted, where possible, through postage stamps issued both in India as well as abroad, from time to time. It was during the construction of the Solani Aqueduct, part of the Ganges Canal conceived in the 1840s by Colonel Sir Proby Thomas Cautley that the first steam locomotive ran in India. During its construction, British engineers wanted to bring a large quantity of clay and other materials from nearby Piran Kaliar area, situated 10 kilometre from Roorkee. This need to bring earth and other materials compelled the engineers to think of the possibility of running a train between the two points. The line laid was a 4 feet, 8-and-half-inch gauge. An engine was brought from England in 1851. It was known initially as "Jenny Lind" after a famous singer of that period. Designed by David Joy, Jenny Lind was an EB Wilson Well Tank type engine, with a wheel configuration of 2-2-2. The engine was renamed Thomason after the then Lieutenant Governor of the North West Provinces. Initially, two wagons were attached to the engine with a capacity of 180 to 200 tons. The train used to cover a distance of two and half miles between Roorkee and Piran Kaliar in 38 minutes with a speed of four miles per hour. The train remained operational for nine months until the locomotive caught fire one day in 1852. But by the time, construction on the aqueduct had been completed. After that steam locomotives continued to be the mainstay of Indian Railways.The steam era finally came to an end when WL 15005 hauled the last broad gauge steam train between Ferozepur and Jalandhar onDecember 6, 1995. Production of steam locomotives had stopped much earlier than that. The last steam loco, WG 10560, christened "Antim Sitara" was commissioned at CLW in June, 1970.

DID YOU KNOW
* The Hyderabad-Shadipalli line has the unique distinction of a broad gauge line being converted to a metre gauge line in 1901.
* During World War I, Gaekwad's Dabhoi Railway sent four X 0-6-2 locomotives to Mesopotamia (modern day Iraq).
* The Nalhati-Azimganj line, constructed in 1863, had the unique distinction of being a four feet gauge.
* The Shahdara-Saharanpur light railway, opened in 1907, was the first and only narrow gauge railway to have originated from Delhi.
* At the time of Independence, the Tenali-Repalle line had the unique distinction of being owned by a district board.
* The Tezpore-Balipara light railway was subsidised by the local board of Tezpore for transportation of tea in Northeastern part of the country.
— VIKAS SINGH, RAIL ENTHUSIAST

Heading: Low-floor ‘scam’: BJP MLA files case - Indian Express
Content:
After the conclusion of its emergency meeting at 3 am on Wednesday, the Academic Council of Delhi University has decided to seek the opinion of affiliated colleges before taking a decision on the semester-based examination system at the undergraduate level and starting integrated four-year dual degree courses.

"While no one has negated the semester system, feedback from the staff councils of the 80 colleges will now be sought," said Professor Pradeep Kumar, member of the Academic Council.

The semester system is already in place in postgraduate courses and will be implemented at the undergraduate level by 2010. A final decision will be taken in the Council's next meeting, in November. "A majority of Council members have consented to a semester-based examination system. After more planning and working out the infrastructure modalities, it should be implemented by 2010," said Deepak Pental, Vice-Chancellor, Delhi University.

"A resolution has been passed to forward the matter to the staff council of colleges for wider and detailed discussion. Colleges should be taken on board as the system is to be introduced at the undergraduate level," said Jaspali Chauhan, a member of the Academic Council.

On the other hand, the Academic Council decided to continue discussions on the four-year dual degree programme. The integrated course will help students master two subjects.

Heading: HUDA to civic agencies: hit the roads, repair them - Indian Express
Content:
Vijay Jolly, Delhi BJP MLA from Saket, on Wednesday filed a complaint with the Lokayukta's office alleging corruption in the purchase of low-floor buses in the Capital. The post of the Lokayukta has, however, been lying vacant for past seven months, with the last Lokayukta, retired High Court judge Justice Mohammad Shamim retiring in March this year. Senior officers at the Lokayukta's office said that in the absence of a head, not much can be done on the complaint filed by Jolly.

Jolly had earlier levelled the allegations in the Delhi Assembly on September 12. In his petition to the Lokayukta, Jolly claimed that despite the presence of other bidders with competitive prices, the order to purchase these buses was issued in favour of Tata Motors.

The petition claimed the low-floor buses were purchased at rates causing a loss of nearly Rs 153 crore to the government. Jolly has further claimed that more buses are being bought at inflated rates from Tata Motors at an expenditure of about Rs 1,750 crore , leading to misappropriation of more public funds.

The Delhi BJP had raked up this issue earlier. Delhi BJP President Harsh Vardhan had also demanded CBI enquiry in the case.

Content:
Gurgaon, rejoice. The roads are set to get better. In a recent order, Financial Commissioner, HUDA (Urban Development and Town Planning), D S Dhesi has instructed agencies like HUDA, Municipal Corporation of Gurgaon and the PWD to repair roads across the city.

Dhesi has also deputed a chief engineer to HUDA's Gurgaon office. A senior official at the district administration office said: "For expenditure up to Rs 4 crore, a chief engineer needs to sanction the amount after it is passed by the government. For projects costing more, civic agencies need approval from the state government directly."

Pankaj Kumra, HUDA Superintending Engineer, said: "There was a general discussion on the work in progress and a future plan of action." MCG commissioner Rajeev Sharma said he was unaware of the discussion that took place in the meeting.

Heading: JNU students turning campus to no-smoking zone - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi Police gave a clean chit to a youth who emerged as a suspect in the Soumya Vishwanathan murder case after the broken mirror of his BMW was found at spot where the TV producer was killed.

Mudit Jain, son of businessman Dinesh Jain, came under scrutiny after investigators collected pieces of the rearview mirror of his BMW from the crime spot in Vasant Kunj. Investigations revealed Mudit travelled on the route at 8.30 pm on September 29, almost seven hours before Soumya's body was found. He had gone to the DLF Emporio Mall on Nelson Mandela Marg.

DCP (South district) HGS Dhaliwal said mall CCTV footage showed the broken mirror and the timing of the footage corroborated Mudit's statement.

Heading: Delhi most unsafe for women working at night: Survey - Indian Express
Content:
As the JNU administration is yet to take any concrete step to check smoking, students have now taken upon themselves the responsibility of ensuring that the campus becomes a no-smoking zone.

A group of students have come together and formed a platform to sensitise students against smoking in public. The group, 'Breath of Life', has planned a series of demonstrations inside the campus to spread the message.

"We have vowed to save lives of innocent passive smokers," said Vijay Pal, convener of the group.

"I had earlier written to JNU administration to take tobacco free initiatives on the campus in the context of this year's slogan 'Tobacco Free Youth' by WHO. But I did not receive any response till now," he said.

Even after the government banned smoking at public places, the trend still continues in the campus. It is evident in TV rooms, canteens and 'dhabas', he said.

He cited the India Global Health Professional Student Survey (2006), which said about 73 per cent students are exposed to second hand smoke in public places.

"We are getting good feedback from students. They are sharing their concerns in this regard with us," said Vineet Kumar, the co-convener and a MSc student.

The group has planned a demonstration, 'Breath of Life Celebration' on campus, where they will symbolically dump tobacco products in a pit near Ganga Dhaba.

"This is just a start. We will take the matter to JNU administration again," he said.

Heading: 7 months and a transplant: Doctors at city hospital operate on a success story - Indian Express
Content:
The national capital, infamous for crime against women, has been polled in an industry survey as the most unsafe city for the fair sex working in night shifts with companies in IT and ITeS, aviation and media sectors and hospitals.

A majority of 65 per cent of women in Delhi interviewed said they felt insecure working in night shifts, while the figure was the least for Mumbai at 26 per cent, according to a survey by industry chamber Assocham.

The study comes nearly 10 days after, Soumya Vishwanathan, a scribe working with a television news channel, was murdered while driving home from office in the wee hours of September 30. Police investigating the case have so far drawn a blank in the case.

Bangalore is the second most unsafe place for working women with 56 per cent of those polled expressing a sense of insecurity, the survey said. In Hyderabad and Chennai as many as 35 per cent and 28 per cent respectively shared similar feelings, it added.

The survey covered women working in companies engaged in business process outsourcing, IT firms, airlines, hospitals and media. It said the safety concern related to the movement outside their office premises and most of the women expect their employers to make security arrangements.

The chamber has suggested strong measures to improve security for women, especially those who move at night.

"Government should make it mandatory installation of the Global Positioning System (GPS) in cabs used not only by BPOs but also other industries employing women at night shifts," Assocham Secretary General D S Rawat said.

Female employees in the small scale sector are more vulnerable to security risks than their peers in bigger units, the survey said. As much as 48 per cent of them in small firms were found "extremely worried" while the number was smaller at 23 per cent for those employed in big companies.

It also showed that women employees are the most vulnerable and prone to both physical and non-physical attacks.

Due to inadequate transport arrangements by employers, 86 per cent of women face commuting problems at night. In Kolkata, Mumbai and Pune, women face the maximum commuting problems compared with those in Delhi, Hyderabad and Ludhiana who face the least, the chamber said.

"The companies should ensure security of their women employees," it said.

Heading: After years, housewarming time for CGHS home owners - Indian Express
Content:
At seven months of age, Sivojit Paul has become the youngest Indian to undergo a successful liver transplant. The baby was born with a congenital liver disorder called Biliary Atresia — in which the bile cannot be excreted, as the liver and intestine are not connected.

Sivojit came to Indraprastha Apollo Hospital here from Kolkata with jaundice two months ago after a surgery to connect the intestine and liver had failed. He became "lethargic and contracted jaundice after the first surgery," his mother Munmun Paul told the media on Wednesday. That's when, she said, "doctors in Kolkata referred us to Delhi as Sivojit's condition began deteriorating rapidly."

Liver transplants are not attempted until children complete 12 months but in Sivojit's case, his condition was critical and doctors at Apollo said they could not have waited for another three months to perform a transplant. "Operating on a newborn is always difficult but was especially high-risk in Sivojit's case because his general condition was weak. His blood vessels are very tiny because of his age," paediatric gastroenterologist Dr Anupam Sibal of Indraprastha Apollo Hospitals said.

Doctors say Biliary Atresia is the most common reason of end-stage liver failure in babies. This condition affects one in 12,000 babies across the world.

"Due to jaundice, high bilirubin was making Sivojit lethargic and he was refusing to be fed. That made his case a huge challenge for us," said Dr Subhash Gupta, senior consultant (liver transplant) at Apollo.

A part of his father Indranil Paul's liver was taken to perform the transplant. "Both his parents were willing to donate a part of their liver but his father's liver was found to be more suitable on primary investigation," Dr Gupta, who performed the surgery, said.  

Sivojit underwent the liver transplant surgery on September 12 and doctors expect a full recovery within a month. "He has already been sent home and is now quite energetic and playful," Dr Sibal said. "He will have a completely normal life but will have to be on anti-resistance medication all his life."

Heading: Resident docs to govt: raise pay or face strike - Indian Express
Content:
Frozen in 2004 after scam, DDA begins allotment of flats

Naresh Nagpal will now be able to apply for a passport, for he finally has a "permanent address". One of 6,000 CGHS flat owners awaiting allotment since a scam was unearthed in 2004 and all allocation frozen thereafter, Nagpal received allotment for his flat in Great Layallpur housing society in Dwarka.

Besides Nagpal, 73 other owners got their due — a flat they had bought years ago — following the draw of lots held at the DDA's Vikas Sadan headquarters. Their housing complexes completed in 2002, most were paying EMIs on home loans all these years even as they stayed in rented accommodation.

Today's allotments came after the Registrar of Cooperative Group Housing Societies (CGHS) cleared them for allotments earlier this year. Allotments of all CGHS flats had been frozen since 2004 when the Rs 4,000-crore scam was unearthed; the scam involved 135 societies.

The societies were under CBI probe and were also being scrutinised by the Delhi High Court. The probe found then CGHS Registrar Diwakar had initiated the scam (see box).

While today's allotments did not involve these 135 societies, the day was significant as the government had frozen allotments on all societies till the matter was cleared. The first batch of allotments, involving eight out of 48 societies cleared, began today.

Present Registrar U K Wohra is, meanwhile, yet to clear a second group of 57 societies, and they cannot be allocated till the go-ahead comes. Registrar UK Wohra had earlier told Newsline that these are societies in which "flats had been constructed but the High Court had imposed a ban on allotment till now". The Registrar office, he had also said, would "expedite verification but these societies need to apply first".

On Wednesday, flats were allotted at Great Layallpur and Delhi Transporters Society. According to officials, draw of lots for other housing societies would be held on a weekly basis.

'Relieved, excited'
Recuperating in hospital a day after a gall bladder operation, Anjani Kumar, a member of Delhi Transporters Society, called it "one of the biggest days" of his life. "I had great plans to celebrate this occasion but that matters little," Kumar said. "I am really excited that finally I will get to live in my own house."

Like many others, Kumar had been paying rent as well as EMI against his loan of Rs 20 lakh all these years. "It has been a frustrating wait. It hurt me financially, mentally and even affected my health."

Dr Rajnish Gupta, working with the Ministry of Agriculture and staying in government accommodation all this while, said: "I went with my family to the DDA office at 3 pm for the draw of lots. Tomorrow, we will go to the temple to thank God."

Nagpal, though, is still cautious: "Many allottees are celebrating but I will wait for another 15 days. Then, all of us will have a massive party together. This has been a long, hard struggle for us, and it feels even better that this occasion came ahead of Dussehra."

At last: The draw of lots...
Delhi Transporters Society has 180 members, and today's draw of lots was taken for 162 members; Great Layallpur had 75 members and draw was done for 74. The other members had either not completed their verification documents or failed to pay their dues. The registrar of society will wait for the next 15 days in case any member wants to raise an objection.

This will be followed by confirming the allotment. As per rules, the owners can move in a month's time.

...At first: The housing scam
In its investigations, the CBI probe found that Diwakar, the then CGHS Registrar, had colluded with officials of the Registrar's office, DDA, builders, and office-bearers of cooperative societies across the Capital. According to CBI investigators, the scam involved fraudulently reviving "defunct" housing societies to get land from DDA at concession.

Post-probe, two significant decisions came this August: HC directed the Registrar of CGHS to clear all housing cases, and then the Registrar cleared allotment for 48 societies on August 22.

Heading: Blast casualty: footfalls fall in Puja pandals, Ramlilas - Indian Express
Content:
Resident doctors in government medical colleges in the Capital threatened to go on strike from Saturday unless their demands on revising pay scale are met by Friday, the doctors said after a meeting with the Health Secretary on Wednesday. The doctors had earlier threatened to launch their stir from Friday.

Unhappy with the government for not revising their salaries, doctors said after Wednesday's meeting that though the authorities have met most of demands, they are waiting for acknowledgement of the rest.

Medical services in 21 hospitals across the city are likely to be affected if the resident doctors stay off work.

Representatives from all medical colleges in the Capital were at the Health Ministry till late Wednesday evening, discussing possible solutions to avoid the strike. The decision to notify authorities about the strike was taken unanimously by the resident doctors, who were promised a salary hike in October," Dr Kumar Harsh, member of the Resident Doctors' Association at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), said.

"Their (government's) carelessness is shocking," Dr Harsh said. "The Union Health Ministry simply forgot to send a notification for revision of salary. The Pay Commission has specifically mentioned the recommendation for resident doctors but the ministry is sitting on it.

"Except for Delhi, all other states have implemented the Commission's recommendations."

The government does not have any idea about the packages that are due to resident doctors, a doctor from Lok Nayak Hospital said.

"While all other doctors get non-practicing allowance, resident doctors in Delhi are not given that allowance. We are also not allowed to work privately," Dr Kuldeep of LN Hospital said. "Certain issues have still not been clarified but the government has given the order to increase our salaries as per recommendations of the Pay Commission."

Heading: A year on, memorials in place, Maya fails to keep other promises - Indian Express
Content:
From the Durga Puja pandals to the usually open-air festivity of Ramlilas, and from the upscale malls of South Delhi to the alleys of Daryaganj, the common element missing from the party is the crowd.

The blasts, it seems, have found another victim: Delhi's spirit.

Sharda, 57, who travels from Jamnagar in Gujarat to sell junk jewellery at Kali Mandir pandal in Chittaranjan Park every year, says "something" is missing in the celebrations this year. He cannot pin it down to any reason in particular, but "even yesterday there were not as many people as you would normally see on Ashtami at this pandal. Even those seemed to be looking around themselves — people sure are enjoying themselves; just that it's a little different this time round."

But Sonali Mukherji, a volunteer at the pandal, puts the attendance at normal — "like every other year". She says, "The nominal drop is because there is no weekend during the Pujas this year. There must be about 6,000 people here already, and more should come for aarti at 7 pm."

The Navratri period is normally lean for restaurants, and it's no different this time, says Moi, the hostess at Piccadelhi in Connaught Place. Manoj, the manager, says the restaurant has reduced its stock of non-vegetarian fare and liquor for the Navratri period. "Sales would probably pick up from tomorrow; we expect people to go out more," he adds.

Pawan, of Mithas restaurant in Daryaganj, blames the blasts, and the scare in their aftermath, for the drop in sales. "We have a special Navratri thali which is doing alright but not many people have come out since the blasts," he says.

The movie theatres have also seen an alarming drop in footfalls. Officials at PVR Plaza in Connaught Place say though ticket sales usually drop to about 50 per cent of capacity during the Puja-Navratri period "but sales have really slumped since the blasts".

Pawan Kumar, who runs a paan shop in the PVR Anupam complex in Saket, says, "People do not sit around in the complex anymore. Sales have thus taken a huge hit."

The Ramlilas, too, have not escaped. Even at the popular Ramlila Grounds in Daryaganj, attendance has dropped significantly. The joint military secretary of the Indraprastha volunteer board, Satish Verma, says minimum attendance at the grounds has been around 50,000 this year. "Usually, the number on any given day during Ramlila is more than 80, 000," Verma says. He says many people who usually come from far-flung parts of the Capital have given it a miss this year.

Hope still floats, though. "Maybe more people will come later this evening and tomorrow," Verma says with pursed lips.

(With inputs from Akshay Kumar V and Pallavi Jain)

Heading: Madrasa students to learn English through radio broadcast - Indian Express
Content:
Last year, Chief Minister Mayawati had launched 12 projects, costing Rs 3,987 crore on Kanshiram's first death anniversary, but except the memorials, most other projects are yet to take off.

The 12 projects announced were Kanshiram Museum, Kanshiram Yaadgar Vishram Sthal, Kanshiramji Memorial, Kanshiram Multi-Specialty Hospital, Kanshiram Smriti Upwan, Kanshiram Nagar Yojna (later named Kanshiram Shehri Gareeb Awasiya Yojna), Ramabai Ambedkar Maidan, Kanshiram Child Hospital, Basic Services for Urban Poor (Housing) scheme, Kanshiram International Convention Center, Kanshiram Medical College at Saharanpur and Kanshiram International Sports Award.

Of these, three projects of public utility have not even started. These are multi-specialty hospital, child hospital and the medical college. Work on the convention centre has also not begun.

Aiming to provide free treatment to poor, the 500-bed multi-specialty hospital was to be developed at a cost of Rs 300 crore on an area of 15-acre near Sultanpur Road in Lucknow. Kanshiram Child Hospital was to be constructed in the same premises at a cost of Rs 14 crore.

Near these hospitals, Kanshiram International Convention Centre was to be developed on 20 acres at a cost of Rs 100 crore. An auditorium with a capacity of 1,500 seats and a hotel along with a shopping complex-cum-mall were also to be constructed.

The Kanshiramji Government Medical College was to be built in Saharanpur at an estimated cost of Rs 300 crore.

Director General of Medical Education, MC Sharma said,

"As far as I know, the land was available for the college. But I have no idea what is the current status of the project."

Work on the BSUP scheme has, however, begun. In all, 23,112 houses were to be built all

over the state. In the state Capital, the Lucknow Development Authority is developing the houses in its Hardoi Road and Mansarover schemes.

But the name of the Kanshiramji Nagar Yojna has been changed thrice, without any work actually taking place. First it was renamed Kanshniramji Sahahri Samagra Vikas Yojna. Now it has been again renamed as Kanshiram Shehari Gareeb Awasiya Yojna. On Thursday, Mayawati will inaugurate the work on the project.

Asked about the delays in various projects, Housing Secretary Ashtbhuja Tiwari said, "The land is available for all projects that are to be developed on public-private partnership model. But these are taking time to start because selection of consultants and hiring private developers is a long drawn process. Construction work on all such projects will start very soon."

In contrast, work is going on full swing on Kanshiram Memorial and museum that will be constructed on 60 acres at a cost of Rs 253 crore on Jail Road, and Ramabai Ambedkar Maidan.

The construction of Kanshiram Yadgar Vishram Sthal on a 4,224 sq mt plot at 13A, Mall Avenue, is on the verge of completion at a cost of Rs 12 crore.

The government had decided to redevelop the Kargil Smriti Upwan and Bangla Bazaar as Kanshiram Smriti Upwan.

After facing legal hurdles, 80 -acre land adjacent to Smriti Upwan is going to be developed as Kanshiram Sanskritik Sthal where cultural programmes will be organised. The sports award has also been instituted.

More projects on cards this year
On the occasion of the second death anniversary of BSP founder Kanshiram on Thursday, Chief Minister Mayawati will announce several development projects, including a housing scheme for the urban poor. There will be no rally on the occasion, unlike last year.
Under the Kanshiram Housing Development Scheme for the Urban Poor, the government will construct 1.10 lakh houses in 71 districts. As many as 19 development authorities have got land for launching the project. Land is also available in 24 other places, where the Housing and Development Board will undertake the work.
Government sources said the Chief Minister will lay the foundation stone of a new jail on Mohanlalganj-Gosaiganj road and the Shakuntala Mishra Viklang University on Mawana Road. She will also open the newly constructed OPD building in Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital to the public.
Mayawati will also inaugurate several newly constructed roads and bridges across the state, and also the new Media Centre in the Secretariat Annexe Building.
Sources said the government plans to house the Lucknow district, Lucknow Model jail, the Nari Niketan and the Jail Training Institute in the new building that is planned to come up on Mohanlalganj-Gosaiganj road.
The proposed Shakuntala Mishra Viklang (Physically Challenged) University is named after the mother of BSP's national general secretary Satish Mishra.
All inaugurations will be done by Mayawati by remote control from her residence. The foundation stones will be kept where the inaugurations are supposed to take place, and the chief minister will unveil these by pressing a button.
The projects have been directly cleared by the Chief Minister's office. But none of the projects is named on the invitation card of the function, nor has any official announcement been made.
— ENS

Heading: Raid at ex-MLA’s house: cops suspended - Indian Express
Content:
Interactive English Learning through radio broadcasts will soon be a part of the curriculum of nearly 360 madrasas recognised by the state government.

District Institute of Education and Training (DIET) has sent a proposal to Minority Welfare Department (MWD) to introduce the programme in the minority institutions. While the plan is to implement the course in all the minority institutions, madrasas are being targeted in the first phase.

At present, the course is a part of the curriculum in nearly 500 state-run primary schools of the state Capital. It was launched in August and has been popular among children and teachers.

DIET Principal Lalita Pradeep said: "We are in discussion with the MWD to introduce the programme in minority institutions." MWD Secretary Dr M A Khan said: "The course will help students to gain command over English. We are planning to implement it shortly in minority institutions."

The programme will be introduced in Class VI and VIII of the madrasas. Initially, the scheme will be implemented in Lucknow and later it will be extended to 17 other districts that receive the radio signal.

The programme will focus on spoken English skills and will also ensure participation of students in dramas, songs and language games. Special training will be given to the teachers to conduct the course effectively.

Heads of madrasas have welcomed the idea. "Though English is being taught in several madrasas at present, it is an optional subject. The introduction of the radio programme will make it a compulsory subject for all the students of madrasas. This will enable them to compete well with others," said Maulana Khalid Rasheed of madrasa Nizamia in Aishbagh.

Maulana Mushtaq of Mazhur Islam madrasa said, "Even private madrasas will benefit from the programme."

At present, the Lucknow station of All India Radio is broadcasting the programmes. The DIET has implemented the scheme with the help of Centre for Learning Resources, a Pune-based NGO, and United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF).

Heading: At Ayodhya, Durga Puja scores over Ramlila - Indian Express
Content:
Two policemen have been suspended for conducting a raid on the house of Mohammad Azhar Alvi, son of a former Congress MLA from Azamgarh, on Monday night without following proper procedure.

Alvi had lodged a complaint with the SSP, alleging that some policemen had raided and ransacked his Gomti Nagar residence and taken away the cellphone of his wife. "After an inquiry conducted by ASP (Trans-Gomti) Ashok Prasad, Sub-inspector Pankaj Verma and constable Kanta Prasad were found guilty of carrying out the raid without making an entry in the police general diary. Further, they failed to communicate the reasons of the raid to the family," said SSP Akhil Kumar. Even senior police officers were kept unaware of the raid, thus causing them embarrassment, he added.

Heading: Termites eat up Board’s documents - Indian Express
Content:
While effigies of Ravana and his clan will be set on fire all over the country on Dussera on Thursday, no such event will take in Ayodhya, the birthplace of Lord Ram.

Over the last 18 years, Durga Pujas have edged out Ramlilas and the burning of demons' effigies in this town.

"The last Ramlila was held here in 1990 or 1991, after that Durga Pujas invaded the town," said Anirudh Narain Jaiswal, who used to play Hanuman in the Ramlilas of the city. His troupe separated in 1991.

Ramchandra Tiwari, owner of a local theater which performed Ramlila for several years, has an interesting observation. "The popularity of Durga Puja increased as the Ram Temple movement gained strength," he said. And the reason behind it, said Tiwari, was simple economics. "Organising Durga Puja brings more money to organisers than the traditional Ramlila," said Tiwari.

"Putting up a stage, payment of wages to Ram Lila artistes, who start rehearsals couple of months before Dussera, managing their costumes—- it requires a lot of money," Tiwari said. "Add to this the expenditure on effigies, each of which cost not less than Rs 1.5 lakh, and you get an idea of the money required for a Ram Lila," he added.

Durga Puja pandals, on the other hand, are not very expensive. "You don't have to pay any artistes, buy costumes, make effigies or arrange other paraphernalia," said Tiwari.

This makes Durga Puja economically viable. "While Ramlila organisers were always worried about raising money even to meet their expenditure, Durga Puja organisers end up in making money," he added. With the Ramlila and Dussera celebrations pushed in corner, old timers rue the loss of a centuries-old tradition. "The Ram Lila was our tradition, which the young generation doesn't even know. It was the celebration of lord Ram's victory over Ravana, the victory of good over evil. Now we bow before the power of Durga," said Jaiswal.

It has also led to the eclipse of certain old crafts. For instance, Ram Murat Agrawal used to make effigies of Ravan, Kumbhakarn and Meghnad. "We had been doing this job since generations," he said, adding that after the invasion of Durga Puja, the family was forced to adopt other businesses.

Heading: Evicted by landlords, students take shelter in campus - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh Madhyamik Shiksha Parishad or the UP Board — Asia's largest school board — has failed to preserve over 500 million documents, including marksheets and certificates of students.

A majority of these documents have already been damaged by termites, moisture and improper upkeep.

Set up in 1921 at Allahabad, the Board has so far conducted 98 board exams.

To preserve records of its students' marksheets, certificates, scrutiny results and other such documents, the Board had established a micro filming unit since its inception. But due to the official apathy, most of the records have been destroyed, sources said, adding that several proposals to preserve the records have been gathering dust in the absence of administrative will.

"I am a 1965 pass out. But I later, lost my originals. I was supposed to show my date of birth for getting insurance, but when I approached the Board for getting duplicates, the attending clerk categorically refused to entertain me stating that all records of that year have been damaged," said a worried S K Tripathi.

"Records of 21 years (from 1959 to 78) of the Board have been completely damaged and could not be retrieved now. If immediate measures are not taken to preserve the existing documents, nearly 500 million students would not be able to get their duplicate marksheets and certificates," said a Board official.

For 35 years — from 1923 to 1958 — the Board had preserved the records through micro filming. Since the cost of the process was very high and the preservation method inefficient, the Board decided to drop the idea.

Of late, the Board had decided to preserve the records through digitisation and had sent a proposal in this regard to the state government in 1998 but the proposal could not see the light of the day.

It has been learnt that the government had forwarded the proposal to Uttar Pradesh Development Systems Corporation Limited (UPDESCO), which demanded Rs five crore for the project.

Considering the seriousness of the matter, the Board recently sent another proposal to the government explaining the need of preservation and the expected loss if immediate measures were not taken. The state government again sent the proposal to UPDESCO which this time quoted Rs 2.50 per page for scanning and preservation. This would cost the Board around Rs 100 crore, sources revealed.

Secretary UP Board Prabha Tripathi said that documents are being destroyed in the absence of proper record management.

Heading: A ‘snake’ robot to reach corners of nuclear plants - Indian Express
Content:
Fifteen students of a college were accommodated in the Lucknow University campus after they approached the authorities claiming that they were evicted by their landlords allegedly due to their Azamgarh background, a top varsity official said on Wednesday.

"We have made arrangements for 15 students in an academic staff college guest house. I don't know whether these students belong to Azamgarh or not, but we have provided them accommodation on humanitarian grounds," Prof Nishi Pandey, Dean, students' welfare, Lucknow University, told PTI.

The students of the Arts College, affiliated to the University, approached their Principal Rajiv Nayan on Tuesday claiming that they were asked by their landlords to leave with all their belongings due to their Azamgarh connection.

The landlords, on the other hand, alleged that the students were asked to leave as they were not cooperating in police verification, which is mandatory. Prof Pandey, when asked, said the students had not given any application for securing a room in university hostel. "If they apply and fulfill all criteria, they will be provided a room after police verification, as per rules, when the university reopens on October 17," she said.

Azamgarh had been in news recently after the arrest of Ahmedabad blasts mastermind Abu Bashar from the district.

Ragpicker dies in blast
A ragpicker was killed when a crude bomb exploded at a garbage dump in Kwarsi area of Aligarh on Wednesday. The boy was trying to open a polythene gunny bag containing crude bombs when it exploded.
The police later found six live bombs in the bag.

Heading: Let us be, cry family and community - Indian Express
Content:
The Centre for Mechatronic at the Indian Institute of Technology-Kanpur (IIT-K) has designed a robot which can perform repair and maintenance tasks inside nuclear plants, where the emitting radiation can pose danger to human.

Named VASUKY — acronym of Versatile Articulated Snake Using Knowledge-domain of Yantrika — the Robot has eight joints which enable it to navigate around the obstacles at various degrees. In nuclear plants there are several locations where it is not possible for scientists and maintenance staff to stay for a long period of time due to the radiation. On most occasions, the radiation machine has to be shut down to permit humans reach such locations. VASUKY, however, is designed to single handedly carry out maintenance and inspection tasks.

Bhaskhar Dasgupta, Associate Professor, Department of Mechanical Engineering IIT-K told The Indian Express, "Besides, inspection and maintenance works, VASUKY can also record events and take photographs." He claimed that there would be no need of shutting down the radiation machine for VASUKY to operate. "The robot has been made of steel, and can withstand radiation for a much longer duration than a human being," added Dasgupta.

He asserted that unlike other robots, the major challenge in this project was to check the ability of the robot to reach a cluttered environment. "Several experiments have confirmed that the snake-like structure of the robot could help it repetitively in executing tasks in a cluttered environment," Dasgupta said.

The project to make the robot was given to the IIT-K by the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE). The DAE had also given Rs 19.55 lakh to the institute to design VASUKY.

Heading: Muslims attack terror but want bait identified - Indian Express
Content:
Father of key suspect feels the pressure

Mohammed Mansoor Asghar Peerbhoy's family feels hounded. "First the police, then the media, and now the society is after us," said a family member, two days after Peerbhoy's arrest.

The Mumbai crime branch calls Peerbhoy (31), a software engineer, the "head of the Indian Mujahideen's media wing". His father, Asghar Ali, describes him as "a gem of a person who respects all religions".

"We are shattered. The police have made allegations against my son but there is no evidence," Asghar said. Of the media, he said, "We believe he is innocent but media reports about his alleged involvement with terrorist activities are causing us problems. We are highly disturbed."

As for Central Park Society in Pune Camp, where the family lives, it added to the pressure by calling the police when the family was away. The cops broke into the house.

Asghar defended his son: "I've never seen my son even slapping anyone. He is a brilliant student, topped his university exams and has studied the Gita and the Bible."

Most members of the family are in Mumbai, meeting police officers to understand the allegations. "The police have not told us but we are sure my son is not involved in any serial blasts. We had never heard the names of the others arrested with him. All we know is he had many friends," Asghar said.

The housing society convened an emergency meeting on Tuesday to discuss security. On Tuesday, while the family was in Mumbai looking for a lawyer, a society member called the police to examine Peerbhoy's jeep parked for months on the premises. A team of Bund Garden police got a locksmith but he could not open the jeep or the house. The cops broke into the house, searched it, smashed the jeep windows and seized some papers.

Yet Peerbhoy's brother Alim, who is a doctor, said after returning, "We will support the police."

Alim later said there was a misunderstanding with the society members. "The problem has been sorted out. Our jeep is damaged. We had not been using it for a few months," he said.

The police returned on Wednesday afternoon and spoke to the family.There will be no more media harassment, with the society deciding that journalists would be kept out.

Peerbhoy has been a software pro for 10 years. He joined Yahoo! last year. "We don't know where he was working before that. But all were reputed software companies," his brother said.

"Police are treating my son well and allowed us to meet him for two minutes. He said the police are not using tough questioning tactics," Asghar said.

Peerbhoy married three years ago and has two children. His wife is a homoeopath. Brother Alim is a doctor, while another brother is an architect.

Heading: Left out, Pune police say congrats Mumbai - Indian Express
Content:
When an educated Muslim youth gets involved in terror, his community reacts in two ways. They condemn what he has been doing and, at the same time, want to know what had prompted him.

The spate of arrests has seen several sections of the community going out of their way to condemn the suspects and even helping the police in bringing them to book. Poona College officials trained cops in Urdu to help them in their investigations, while Muslim clerics are preaching secular education at madarsas.

Yet the community feels insecure with "more and more innocents being detained for alleged terror links". While calling for punishment to the guilty, they have also demanded to know the suspects' motive. Police are not the only answer, they say: politicians need to look into their grievances.

"I wonder why such a highly educated software professional as Mansoor Asgar Peerbhoy should commit such a heinous crime," says Dr P A Inamdar, president of the Maharashtra Cosmopolitan Society. Nobody is talking of the motives behind the terrorist acts, says Inamdar, who feels the problem lies within the system.

Inamdar's society runs Rangoonwalla Dental College; arrested terror suspect Mohammad Honali used to teach there. "We are not here to defend terrorism and you cannot blame a college for what a student or teacher does," says Inamdar.

Poona College registrar Mohammed Chiraguddin feels the same. He points out the college's role in teaching Urdu to 20-25 cops.

Cleric Maulana Nizamuddin Fakhruddin, member, All India Muslim Personal Law Board and president of the Jamia Nizamia Trust, says secular education is imparted to children in 20-odd madarsas. He agrees terrorists should be punished but he too has the same question about "the system".

Razia Patel, a social activist with the Rachana Trust that looks into issues of minorities, says Islam is against terrorism. Yet, she feels, an atmosphere of insecurity prevails as Muslim youths are being picked up at random. "People look at us with doubt. We need to understand why the government has failed to address this issue," she says.

BREAK POINT
Expert view: Dr Mushtaq Margoob, a psychological trauma expert from Government Medical College, Srinagar, explains why and when even highly qualified people can get involved in terrorism

Trigger: When the person is pushed to the wall and has been exploited to a great extent

Critical stage: When he is swayed by his emotions and stops caring if he or others get killed

Collective identity: Can get formed when a number of such people are exploited by a cohesive group; they identify with the group rather than with their individual identities

Cerebral condition: The emotional part of the brain dominates, does not listen to logic and reasoning

Heading: Baner residents bristle at what build-up made them go through - Indian Express
Content:
The Pune police, who had not been involved in the crackdown on a terror module in the city, complimented the Mumbai police on Wednesday. Police Commissioner Satyapal Singh said he was happy for his Mumbai counterparts. "After all, the detection was made by the police," he said.

"We will get a report on the suspects in a week and will then decide how to proceed. The Mumbai police are investigating the matter and we will not interfere," he added.

On his own force, he once again cited lack of manpower but says his men were being trained. "The present strength of 7,000 cops for the entire city is certainly low. But I believe this manpower can be utilised more effectively. There is no point in having a huge force with low skill. I would prefer fewer but trained and healthy staff," he said. "We have started training the city police for gathering information on terrorist activities. Two training sessions have already been held," he said.

On Tuesday, The Indian Express highlighted that the city police were not involved in the arrest of any of the terror suspects with Pune links.

The commissioner expressed concern over educated youths joining terrorist outfits. "We need to find the reason why doctors and software professionals are joining terrorism. Mission Mritunjay has been launched with this aim," he said.

Singh praised the city's Muslims: "Police are getting inputs about SIMI from Muslims. Since the media reports on my statement that the city has over 300 SIMI activists, the police control room has got calls from nay informants, mostly Muslims.We are working on the inputs," he added.

In view of the communal riots in Dhule, the Police Commissioner appealed to Pune's citizens to maintain harmony.

Heading: Quarrel with lawyers has ended, says CP - Indian Express
Content:
Babsy Bilimoria loves sports. She played professional hockey in the '50s and the '60s and has been associated with women's hockey and cricket associations all her life. Sport dominates the lives of her entire family; her daughters have represented the state in the junior nationals and cricket, while one of her granddaughters is swimming captain in college.

Yet Bilimoria, now 71, will boycott the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) in her own city. This will be a mark of protest against Suresh Kalmadi, local corporators, the Pune Municipal Corporation and other utilities such as Maharashtra State Electricity Department Corporation Ltd (MSEDCL) and Bharat Sanchar Nigam Ltd. She holds them responsible for turning her life into a civic nightmare in the run-up to the CYG.

Bilimoria, living at Baner for 14 years, saw residents suffering ever since the civic administration undertook the work to redo the road. Cables frequently snapped, leading to telephone disruptions and power cuts running into days. Even water lines were snapped.

"I am interested in all sports. You name it, I watch it," Bilimoria said. "But we are certainly not going to watch the CYG events. Given what we have been put through, we are no way going to buy the tickets and add to their revenue." Other Baner residents including Rejy John-George, former state and national hockey player, will join the boycott.

They faced a 65-hour power cut from September 18 morning to September 20 night. Earlier that week, they had gone through 25 hours of loadshedding. "Just when we were recovering, it failed again on Monday (September 22) afternoon for another 30 hours," said Amar Singh, a 70-year-old resident.

The next evening, furious that not a single civic official responded to their complaints, residents parked their cars across Baner Road to block traffic. Since then power supply has been at best erratic. Now, 23 Baner residents have filed an application with the MSEDCL, demanding Rs 2,000 each as compensation.

Residents are not against the CYG; but against the civic authorities for leaving construction work till the last month before the Games. "The work has been going on for three years, but only after the rain this time did the pace pick up. They went at such a hectic pace that they were unable to look after the cables," said Sushil Bijlani of Eves Garden.

For months, the arterial route to Baner was dug up. One would have expected them to work lane by lane, but because of lack of time the entire road was blocked. Residents had to take a 9-km detour for two months via Baner-Sus Road, Pashan-Sus Road and Pashan Road, none of which even had a proper surface, Bijlani said.

Heading: Chief Minister will decide forest officer’s fate, says Pachpute - Indian Express
Content:
The tiff between lawyers and police is expected to end with the interference of Police Commissioner Satyapal Singh. A day after lawyers beat up a police constable in the premises of the Shivajinagar court, city Police Commissioner Satyapal Singh told media persons here that the dispute has ended.

"A delegation of lawyers met me. Now, there is no dispute between lawyers and police," Singh said. The Shivajinagar police lodged offences against 25 lawyers for manhandling police constable S M Veer on Tuesday. The lawyers have been booked under various sections of Indian Penal Code of causing disturbance in government work and manhandling a policeman on duty.

According to the police, the complainant constable, Veer, had gone to the court with assistant sub inspector U M Gajmal for obtaining details of the lawyers' meeting on Tuesday afternoon. The lawyers had called the meeting to condemn the way the police treated advocate Rajendra Shinde, who was 'badly beaten' by the police on Monday. The lawyers found constable Veer noting down the details of their meeting, after which they manhandled him. When asked if the lawyers booked in this case would be arrested, Singh declined to comment. Meanwhile, police sub inspector G N Garad of Deccan Gymkhana police station is investigating the case.

Heading: Baner-Balewadi DP: Activists to suggest changes - Indian Express
Content:
State Forest Minister Babanrao Pachpute on Wednesday said Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh would decide the fate of deputy conservator of forests (Pune division) Ashok Khadse, who was issued suspension orders for having illegally sanctioned no objection certificates (NOCs) for sale of reserved forest land and private forest land in the Pune division.

Pachpute said the case would be put before the Chief Minister. He however refrained from saying that the suspension order stands. "The matter will be investigated," he said.

According to forest department officers, Khadse was suspended for violating the Forest Conservation Act 1980 and giving nearly 82.87 hectares in Kondhwa (Khurd), Mohammedwadi, Undri, and Kondhwa (Budruk) to builders.

When contacted, Khadse refused to comment on the issue. Principal Chief Conservator of forests Jwala Prasad, who is the competent authority, also declined to comment on the matter but confirmed the suspension orders. Earlier, Prasad had asked Pune divisional commissioner Nitin Kareer to give a list of such private lands in the area, to which Kareer, when asked, said his department would soon compile and provide the list.

Forest department officers said Khadse had issued the NOCs without seeking permission. They said that acquired private land, which is deemed as reserve forest land, cannot be transferred. "Khadse has no powers to transfer the land,'' said an officer, adding that the powers rest with the government.

The Pune district is divided into three divisions: Junnar division, Pune division and Bhor subdivision. Junnar, Ambegaon, Khed and Shirur areas fall under the Junnar division, while Pune division comprises Wadgaon Maval, Mulshi, Haveli, Baramati, Indapur and part of Velhe. Purandar, Bhor and Velhe fall under the Bhor division. According to the forest department, there are a total of 92,362 hectares of forest land in the Pune division. The forest department had 55,594 hectares under reserved, protected, unclass and compensatory forest land while the revenue department had 36,768 hectares. The Pune division itself is divided into nine ranges.

Heading: NDA celebrates Air Force Day - Indian Express
Content:
The Green Pune Movement, an association of activists, has framed a sample letter for sending suggestions and objections about the Baner-Balewadi green development plan (DP).

The association is supported by former mayor Advocate Vandana Chavan, Aneeta Beninger, founder-director of Centre for Development Studies and Activities and Pune Municipal Standing Committee chairman Sham Deshpande. "The sample letter will help citizens in two ways –understanding the format of sending suggestions and objections in the prescribed format as needed to the government and the major points on which objections can be raised," Beninger said. She added that the core members of green pune movement are also working on the detailed objections that will be ready in a couple of days.

Vandana Chavan said that this is the last chance for Pune citizens to save Pune's green cover by sending their suggestions and objections. Satish Khot, president of National Society for Clean Cities (NSCC) said that citizens with a group of about 25 members could approach them for holding a meeting and explain the nitty-grittys of the DP. Those interested may contact the members at 304, Narayan Peth or call on 24441666, 24441777 or send e-mail to greenpunedp@gmail.com . Citizens can send their suggestions and objections for 60 days , starting last week of September.

Heading: 27-year-old woman jumps to death - Indian Express
Content: The 76th anniversary of the Indian Air Force (IAF) was celebrated with great enthusiasm on Wednesday at the National Defence Academy at Khadakwasla here. NDA Commandant Air Marshal T S Randhawa was the chief guest.  An oath-taking ceremony was organised for all the IAF officers and personnel below officer ranks posted at NDA in the Air Force Training Team premises of the academy. Meanwhile, in a separate initiative, the NDA, in the year of its diamond jubilee celebration, is donating an amount of Rs 2 lakh to the Military Hospital, Khadki. The hospital will utilise the funds to help all patients, including NDA cadets and officers.

Heading: Golden moments - Indian Express
Content:
In yet another suicide case, a 27-year-old woman killed herself by jumping from the terrace of a seven-storey under-construction building of the Sinhgad Business School in Erandwane on Wednesday afternoon.

Police have identified the deceased as Snehal Potnis, a divorcee who was a resident of Balaji Nagar area on Pune-Satara Road. No suicide note was found. The reason behind her death is not yet known.

According to the Deccan Gymkhana police, Potnis was working as a receptionist with a private firm on Jangli Maharaj Road. She left her office around 2.30 pm, went to the terrace of the building and jumped off.

A police team led by assistant sub inspector U K Yadav is investigating the case. Police have recorded the statements of a few eyewitnesses. Police said that Potnis got married eight years ago and had a son.

Heading: The Nano effect - Indian Express
Content:
Navratri and Durga Puja have set the celebratory tone in the city that welcomes Dussera with all its auspicious tidings

Fasting ends, feasting begins
Bringing an end to the eight day fast for Navratri was Navmi on Tuesday when at the break of dawn, people performed their kul swami's puja the fast comes to an end. "Tirth is the first thing that we who observe fast are supposed to have. After consuming that we can break our fast," says Deepak Yadav an Infosys executive who ended his fast on Navmi. The fast is preferably is broken by consuming something sweet. "We make phirni, kheer and other delicacies with which we have to end our fast," adds Yadav. While the ones who observe fast end it by savouring something sweet, it is a must to prepare pooranpoli in the later half of the day to be consumed by others. "Like you have sandesh in Bengal we have pooranpoli here for Navmi. All households prepare pooranpoli on Navmi. It is a must to have pooranpoli on this day," says Yadav. Apart concluding the fast Navmi also brings an end to ghatstapana, which is established on the first day of Navratri. "On Navmi we break the ghatstapana which signifies that the festival has come to end," he adds.

The hub
Congress Bhavan has been quite the hub during the puja days, drawing huge crowds for the typically Bengali fare they offer. Kaushik Bhattacharya has been designing pandals for the last 15 years and is the man behind the fascinating set put up in the Congress Bhavan. "The theme this time has been unity hence we have a single backdrop with various idols including those of Lord Ganesh, Saraswati, Kartik and Durga. The design was made using materials such as thermocol, wooden frames and cloth. It took us fifteen days to design the set," adds Bhattacharya. The last of the dandiyas are taking place on Thursday. People can enjoy the end of fest Dandiya Raas at New Club today. The event is being jointly organised by Jazmataaz and New Club. The grand finale of the 10-day dandiya fest Dholi Taro Dandiya will be held at Yash Lawns today.

Gold rush
Irrespective of increase in price of precious metal, people continue to but gold and silver to preserve the tradition and also to make a safe investment. While the first Gold Rush began when gold was discovered in California in 1848, buying precious metals and stones on the occasion of Vijayadashmi has been a tradition for ages. In mythology Kuber, the God of wealth created a shower of gold coins to help Kausta pay off his debt to his guru; today buying gold has become more of an investment along with the reason to commemorate the tradition.

Lately, though with the skyscraping prices of gold and silver combined with a slowing economy, buying gold still seems to be shining all the way. "These days, as the share market is so unstable, I feel gold is the safest thing to invest in at present and buying it on the auspicious day is just for the better," says Nilesh Bafna, a businessman.

Shubhada Barve, customer care officer at P N Gadgil Jewellers, affirms to the sturdy status of gold. Along with the new range of Istaumbul Jewellery, which is 22 karat gold neckpieces, P N Gadgil has also introduced a large variety in other precious metals and stones. "Dussera is the most auspicious day to buy gold. In spite of the fact that two weeks back the price was Rs 11,800 and now it has suddenly leaped to Rs 13,500, there has not been any difference on the sales and with Diwali coming soon customers have already placed orders for jewellery."

"Customers may buy little, but on Dussera, gold is definitely bought as token. Sales are not much affected as festive season is around and people definitely indulge in buying gold during this period," is what they have to say at Ranka Jewellers.

For Hina Maheshwari, buying silver would be the choice this Dussera. "It is the festive time, all of us plan to make an investment in something big and this season I would rather invest in silver because I like it." But Chitra Nair, a housewife says, "I would never stake my money just to preserve a tradition, if there was some occasion or I had a need for it then I would have bought it, but at these prices, I feel it is not necessary."

Keeping the shine of precious metals and stones untarnished, the tradition of Dussera is a symbol of celebration that preserves the old school of thought, which upholds the belief of buying gold on Vijayadashmi brings in prosperity.

Ravan Dahan
Dussera or Vijaya Dashmi, the day of bidding adieu to Goddess Durga, connotes victory of good over evil. It was the day when Lord Ram killed Ravan. Traditionally the celebrations are marked with Ravan Vadh. On this day various Hindu communities get together and burn effigies of Ravan, Kumbhkarna (Ravana's brother) and Meghnath (Ravana's son) with fanfare and gaiety. Chokhi Dhani – the village resort in Wagholi will hold the Ravan Vadh event today, drawing hordes of entries to witness the grand celebrations. The event will start at 8 pm. To mark the Dussera celebrations a cultural show from 5 pm to 11 pm is also organised. "A special team of performers from Rajasthan has been roped in to participate in the various performances like fire dance, ghumar dance, kalbailiya dance, puppet and magic show," says B H Yadav, operational manager, Chokhi Dhani.

Heading: State tunes in to a new ‘sop’ opera, courtesy Nano - Indian Express
Content:
Modi, the politician...

There's more to the Nano hitting the brakes in Bengal and swerving sharp from Left to Right. The Memorandum of Understanding between the Tatas and the Gujarat government could not have been signed at a more opportune moment in Gujarat's political history.

The political symbolism of the Gujarat government bagging the Nano project – which was announced on October 7, wherein he completes seven years as the chief minister – is not lost on anybody. Modi not only outmanoeuvred the Left, the Congress in Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh, but also his BJP counterparts in Karnataka.

The 2002 riots, the indictment in cases in the Supreme Court, denial of visa by the US government, have all been sore points, even as Modi donned business suits to doggedly pursue the development agenda and investment opportunities in successive Vibrant Gujarat meets.

At one stroke, Modi will be riding the Nano to a new respectability and national acceptability, leaving the fading taints of the 2002 riots. The Nano will now not only push Tata's dream of a Rs 1-lakh car for the common man, but also lend credibility to a certain brand of politics that Modi represents.

Success, finally, has rolled in with the Nano factory, with all the hallmarks of typical Gujarati entrepreneurial acumen. The land in Gujarat has been acquired not from farmers, but from a state-run agricultural university. For the Tatas, singed in Singur, it is a great investment decision, the icing on the cake being the near-complete absence of labour unionism, protests and industrial unrest, not to mention the intangible sops from the Gujarat government, which are still carefully under wraps. By coincidence or otherwise, Modi became the first chief minister of Gujarat to have enjoyed an uninterrupted stint in the CM's chair for the longest tenure, the day the Nano deal was inked. He has already bested ex-chief minister Madhavsinh Solanki's record, whose stint as Gujarat's chief minister though was marked by breaks.

While Modi had his record blemished by the 2002 riots, his successive political victories as well as his brand of development agenda has kept him firmly in the saddle so far.

While Modi's taking over as Gujarat's chief minister from his predecessor Keshubhai Patel had not been smooth, it resulted in an ineffectual BJP mutiny in Gujarat that made hardly a dent on Modi's vote base.

Modi's brand of politics, where his persona replaced the party bypassing the avowed party cadre system of Sangh Parivar, has resulted in the formation of a new political party — Mahagujarat Janata Party. Comprising BJP rebels, a tribe that took birth post-2002 riots, they have yet to establish their credentials significantly different from the BJP's own. The fact that the deal has come through in a Lok Sabha election year, and Assembly polls in the neighbouring BJP ruled states of Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, is also lost on any political party. It is not merely advantage Modi, the location of the Nano plant happens to be in L K Advani's constituency. The Congress, however, is still looking for a facesaver. "If the Tatas decided to move its project from Bengal to Gujarat, it was purely an investment decision. It was not linked to the type of politics that the state government follows," Congress spokesman Manish Tewari claimed.

...and the businessman

Express News Service

AHMEDABAD, OCTOBER 8

The world's cheapest car, Nano, is expected to create the biggest opportunity for growth and development in the commercial and industrial sectors in Gujarat. Industry bigwigs in the state have affirmed that the setting up of the manufacturing unit will also set the development track for small and medium scale industries in engineering, auto and software sectors.

"The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) believes that the project would give impetus to the development of small and medium scale

industries in Gujarat, particularly engineering, auto and software," said CII chairman Vimal Ambani.

According to Ambani, the engineering SEZ notified near Ahmedabad on Delhi-Mumbai freight corridor would get a special boost. At present, Rajkot is the hub for auto parts manufacturing units. The coming of Tata at Sanand can possibly lead to the expansion of the industry to Ahmedabad. The auto parts

industry turnover, which at present is nearly

Rs 1,500 crore, is expected to grow significantly in the coming years. Vendors and ancillaries at the Tata site will put the auto parts industry on the fast track of growth.

According to Pankaj Patel, Chairman of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), Nano will bring in more ancillary industries and open up newer avenues for employment. While Gujarat is one of the leading states in the country having the largest number of SEZs, the Nano project remains the showpiece. Besides, it is not just a car manufacturing plant that is coming, the Tatas have also assured that they would contribute to agricultural research and marine biology in the state along with setting up an auto academy and driving schools. This will create more learning opportunities and jobs.

Ratan Tata will also help the state in developing its human resources in various ways. Tatas will form an automobile academy and many ITIs for human resource development in the state. Sixty small and medium scale industries and ancillary industries will move in at the Nano site with Tata Motors.

Chief Minister Narendra Modi, while announcing the arrival of Nano in Gujarat, had said: "Over 60 ancillary industries are going to come together in the same complex. Besides, the second and third tier ancillarisation will have a major impact. The global automotive market stands at around three trillion dollars and Gujarat must take full advantage of this emerging market and industry." The plant, to begin with, will produce 350,000 cars per annum with the capacity being expandable to 500,000 cars per annum. The Nano project, including Tata Motors plant, vendor facilities and service providers will together generate over 10,000 direct and indirect jobs. The state is likely to see development of industries that until now have a minimal presence in Gujarat. Many engineering and designing jobs will also be created.

Heading: Midas touch:Vadodara artists’ works fetch over Rs 19 cr at Sotheby’s auction - Indian Express
Content:
A day after the Tata Motors moved its Nano project to Sanand, a team of senior bureaucrats met in the Sachivalaya on Wednesday to discuss the modalities of various sops offered by the state government to the auto company.

On the other hand, the state government remained reluctant to divulge the contents of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) it signed with the Tatas on Tuesday. When Newsline contacted Principal Secretary (Industries) Gauri Kumar and sought a copy of the MoU, she said, "We cannot divulge the contents of the MoU, as it involves professional confidentiality."

Even Chief Secretary D Rajagopalan refused to provide a copy of the MoU, saying he did not have one with him. Also, none of the officials in the Chief Minister's Office was ready to part with a copy of the vital document.

"We will soon post the contents on the government's official website. Media persons can access this over the Internet," said a senior official. As the government continues to keep the contents under wraps, the Wednesday meeting of senior officials called by Rajagopalan reportedly deliberated at length on the various sops offered by the government to the Tata Motors to set up its Rs 2,000-crore Nano project. Among others, the government is considering offering some concessions to the auto firm in the payment of value-added tax (VAT) to help it maintain a cash flow, said a senior official.

It was also decided at the meeting to expedite the works related to different infrastructure facilities to be created at the Nano Mother Plant site spread over 1,100 acres of land, such as approach road, water, power and effluent discharge system. The Chief Secretary and Principal Secretary (Industries) are coordinating the infrastructure related works.

Although Chief Minister Narendra Modi had, at a joint news conference with Tata chief Ratan Tata here on Tuesday, said the government would sell the 1,100 acres of land to the Tatas at prevailing market rates, officials in the state Revenue department say the land would be given to the auto giant as per the existing "jantri" (a ready reckoner for the land assessment) rates at Rs 360 per square metre.

Sources in the Revenue department said Tata Motors would have to pay only about Rs 157 crore towards the land cost, if it was calculated as per the "jantri" rates prevalent in Sanand. The government has permitted the Tatas to make a staggered payment towards the land cost. The prevailing market price of the same land is estimated at Rs 600 per sq metre.

Meanwhile, under its infrastructure development plan, the government has reportedly directed the Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Ltd (GUVNL) to install a 220 KV-capacity station to supply power for the small car project at the Sanand site. While the Gujarat Water Supply Board has been asked to arrange for 10 million litres per day (MLD) of water for the Mother Plant, the government has directed the GIDC to expedite the work on laying an approach road to connect the car manufacturing plant site with the main road.

AAU looks for land as Tatas arrive at Chharodi centre
Anand Agriculture University (AAU), the land of which the state government has acquired for the Nano car plant, is hoping to get land somewhere else in the state soon so that it can continue with the activities going on at the Chharodi centre.The government has acquired 2,200 acres from the AAU, out of which 1,100 acres have been transferred to the Tata Motors. The remaining portion has been retained by it. The university will need chunks of land in various districts, including Anand, Kheda, Panchmahals, Vadodara, Dahod and Ahmedabad. It is learnt that prior to the acquisition, a lot of activities were going on at the Chharodi cattle farm of the AAU. But now, in the wake of the land transfer, these would have to be relocated elsewhere. Among them, a project for developing high-yielding jatropha (ratanjyot) varieties was underway at Chharodi, where the National Oilseeds and Vegetable Oils Development Board (NOVOD) was funding the project. Another project funded by the Gujarat Livestock Development Board (GLDB) was underway at the site, where the ongoing construction work had to be stopped with the takeover of the land by the state government, it is learnt. During a visit to the spot on Tuesday, the Newsline team found that an ongoing construction work had been stopped. The AAU authorities are at present busy estimating the number of projects that need to be shifted. They are also working out probable losses incurred due to the shifting. AAU Vice-Chancellor M C Varshneya, who is also credited with preparing a weather calendar for farmers at the behest of the state government, refused to comment on the issue saying, "I don't want to discuss this."
—ENS

Heading: BJP MP’s petrol pump vandalised - Indian Express
Content:
In what could give a major boost to the Indian artists, especially from Vadodara, works by three former students of M S University's Fine Arts department have together fetched nearly Rs 20 crore at an auction. The auction was held at Sotheby's Modern and Contemporary Art Sale in Hong Kong on October 4.

The three artists are Chintan Upadhyay, Jagannath Pandya and TV Santosh. Speaking to Newsline over phone, Upadhyay, who is on a tour to Egypt, said, "This is news to me! I am in Egypt and have been travelling for the last one month."

His work 'Together for life whether we like it or not' fetched a whopping Rs 6.5 crore at the auction. In the painting, he depicts the subject of cloning and designer babies through a narrative of Siamese twins.

On the other hand, Santosh's painting 'In God's Name' was sold for Rs 8.9 crore. His work is a continuation of his preoccupation with science and technology and how it is used in the battlefield as a tool of destruction.

Another painting by Panda named 'Desirescape II' was sold for Rs 4.2 crore. In his series of paintings, Panda presents a sort of invasion of modern amenities such as large apartment blocks into a pristine setting of a village.

Heading: Restaurant staff kidnapped, robbed - Indian Express
Content:
Four unidentified men vandalised a petrol pump reportedly owned by Ratilal Verma, a Bharatiya Janata Party MP from Dhanduka and decamped with more than Rs 50,000 in cash after assaulting an attendant there. The incident took place at Shradha petrol pump on the Judges' Bungalow road, late night on Tuesday.

The petrol pump remains in service from 7 am to 11 pm daily and the incident, said police, resulted when an attendant, Durgasinh Rathod, refused to sell petrol to a youth, who had come there with his motorcycle at around 11.30 pm.

Enraged at this, the unidentified youth reportedly beat up Rathod and even called up some of his friends to help him vandalise the station.

Two of them, armed with hockey sticks, chased Rathod to a deserted field nearby where he managed to save himself by hiding. "Five men are accused in the case," Vastrapur police

said.

Rathod returned to the site after half-an-hour and informed the owners about it. Vastrapur police have registered a complaint of trespassing and robbery and are trying to establish the identities of the men with the help of leads given by Rathod.

In an unrelated case of housebreak, cash and valuables worth Rs 94,000 were allegedly stolen from an office premises in Sarthi Square on S G Highway late night on Tuesday.

The owner, Brijraj Singh, a resident of Bopal, lodged a complaint on Wednesday morning against some unidentified persons, accusing them of breaking into his office and decamping with two laptops and Rs 20,000 in cash.

Heading: After Nano, Pujas bring in the Bengal touch - Indian Express
Content:
In yet another case of robbery on the posh C G Road of the city in less than 12 hours, an employee of a prominent restaurant of the city was allegedly kidnapped and robbed of his gold chain and cash to the tune of Rs 5,700 at gunpoint late night on Tuesday.

Ajay Shah (30), who works as a kitchen supervisor at the Choice restaurant on C G Road, was also beaten up mercilessly and is undergoing treatment at the V S Hospital. In his complaint, Shah, who stays in Shahpur, has accused his acquaintances — Nishant, Ravi and Nayan — along with seven others of allegedly kidnapping and robbing him.

According to police, the incident took place at around 10.30 pm when Shah was heading home after work.

Ravi and Nayan, who were following Shah on a two-wheeler, had forced him to ride with them by allegedly threatening him at gunpoint.

The duo took Shah to a deserted place near Shankar Bhavan in Shahpur, where Nishant was waiting with seven other people.

The group allegedly lead by Nishant, Ravi and Nayan started beating up Shah. "They later robbed him of his money and gold chain and fled from the site," said Inspector J M Desai of Navrangpura police.

A profusely bleeding Shah was immediately rushed to V S Hospital, where police recorded his statement on Wednesday morning. All the accused have been booked on charges of assault and robbery. The police are investigating the case.

Earlier, on Tuesday afternoon, one Sneha Vakharia of Maninagar had complained that two unidentified persons robbed her of cash and valuables worth Rs 5.87 lakh.

Heading: Flower power: Bedecked with 45 kg of flowers for garba - Indian Express
Content:
After the arrival of Nano from West Bengal to Gujarat, another asset of Bengal has come to the state — the oriental style of celebrating Durga Puja.
