The Sarbajanin Puja Committee (SPC) of the ONGC Colony, Vadodara has for the first time brought most of the traditional things required for the celebration from West Bengal.

"We have been celebrating Durga Puja in our colony for the last three years. And this year, we have brought some of the rich tradition of West Bengal. One of the most interesting part of this year's festivity is the performance of Mahishasurmardini by a dance troupe from Kolkata," said Asim Samanta, president of the SPC. The artists belong to West Bengal and have already held shows at Ahmedabad and Surat. Motifs of puppets are used in Mahishasurmardani dance.

In other parts of the city, several pandals have been serving Bhog Prasad (khichdi, labda, payesh, misti) during the puja. Even the Dhaki (artists playing dhol along with ghanta and shankha) have been invited from Kolkata to ensure authenticity and add attraction.

The celebrations will culminate on September 9, with a colourful entertainment programme by a local group from Vadodara.

Heading: Festive fervour marks Durga Puja in Surat - Indian Express
Content:
An outfit made of 45 kilograms of flowers is not part of a creation displayed at a fashion show. It is a uniquely styled garba dress, that Naresh Ramchandra Patel wore on the eighth day of the Navratri celebrations, at the United Way of Baroda (UWB) here on Tuesday.

Flowers such as rose, lily and chrysanthemum were used to make the dress. The flowers were stitched together on kurta and pyjama made of jute, said Patel.

Forty-year-old Patel himself weighs about 90 kg. "There was a feeling of pride when I wore this dress and did garba," he said beaming.

Around 2,200 roses of five different colours — red, pink, yellow, green and orange — were used for the dress.

The turban, which is a part of the dress, alone, weighs nearly 3 kg.

The flowers have been stitched so well that even after a long dancing stint, no flower came out of the dress. The back of the kurta has a fringe made with lily.

Expert florists took nearly 12 hours to make this unique dress. "The flowers have been brought from Mumbai and I had to spend Rs 9,500 to get this dress made," said Patel.

"The idea struck me after I visited the Pramaswami Mandir. I saw Lord Ghanshyam wearing a similar kind of outfit. I thought of getting a dress that would look like his," said Patel.

Patel has been participating in garba for the past18 years now. His close associates say that he comes up with something different every year for garba. "I don't even drink water when I start dancing. I am there till the programme ends. I came to the garba venue in an open auto-rickshaw so that the flowers wouldn't crumble," he added.

Heading: ACB traps deputy collector accepting Rs 1 lakh bribe - Indian Express
Content:
The Bengali community of Rander in Surat is busy celebrating the much-awaited Durga Puja with much zeal and fervour.

The celebrations, which began on Sunday was organised by one of the oldest club of the city, Bengal club.

Eminent writer Bhagwati Kumar Sharma graced the inaugural function as the chief guest.

Hardas Roy, president of the club, said: "The motive behind celebrating the Puja here is that many Bengalis live here and are unable to go home during the festival. This celebration makes them feel at home. The community also uses it as a good platform to meet other people who have recently shifted to the city."

Thursday, the last day of the festival, will be celebrated as Dashami.

Roy said that cultural and religious programmes such as Shiv Bandana, Jal Taranga and Mahishamardini are performed during the pujas.

Also, various entertainment programmes such as Sankho and Ulu Dhwoni Pratijogita (Lighting the candle competition), traditional dress and fancy dress competition and acting competition are also held to make the best out of this gathering, he said.

Artists from other states also come here to perform during this time, Roy added.

Heading: Truck loaded with iron plates worth Rs 12 lakh looted - Indian Express
Content:
Officers of the Surat Anti Corruption Bureau (ACB) arrested the deputy collector of Stamps and Duty of Bharuch, along with an advocate, for accepting a bribe of Rs 1 lakh from a land owner, on Tuesday.

Ramesh Savji Bhamrolia, a resident of Navsari contacted the Surat Anti Corruption Bureau office at Nanpura bahumali and lodged a complaint against Deputy Collector of Stamps and Duty of Bharuch, Somji Chawda. Bhamrolia claimed that Chawda demanded a bribe of Rs 1 lakh from him for making the excess stamp duty report nil.

Following the complaint, the ACB Police Inspector, S A Zabha together with his staff members laid a trap against Chawda in his office at Bharuch and caught him and his friend, advocate Girish Makwana accepting the bribe amount from Bhamrolia.

According to the police, Bhamrolia and his friend Magan Pansurya, both residents of Navsari, purchased land, worth Rs 20 lakh and Rs 25 lakh, in Ghadkol village in Bharuch from a farmer, Hanif Malek, in March 2008. Both the purchasers made the land documents and paid the stamp duty of the land.

However, Chawda sent a notice to both the parties, stating that valuation of the land is high and thus they will have to pay some more money. Bhamrolia and Pansurya went to the Stamp and Duty office in Bharuch on Friday and showed the deal papers and documents to Chawda, who further asked them to pay Rs 3 lakh as the due amount.

But, when Bhamrolia asked Chawda to solve the matter by some other way, the latter asked the parties to pay Rs 1 lakh. In return, Chawda promised that he would show the due amount as nil in the report.

Zabha said: "We have found that both the parites had paid the stamp duty earlier. But Chawda sent notices to them to extract more money."

Heading: Crude bomb explodes at Hathikhana, no injury reported - Indian Express
Content:
Driver and assistant beaten up and abandoned in a sugarcane field

Six armed robbers hijacked a truck trailer loaded with iron plates worth Rs 12 lakh and later took the vehicle with them after abandoning the driver and his assistant at Kosamba village in Surat district on Wednesday morning.

According to the police, the trailer, loaded with 21 tonnes of iron plates from a company in Hazira, was on its way for delivery to a company in Vadodara. When the vehicle (GJ-6TT-6416) reached the Bhesan road near Rander on Tuesday evening, a truck intercepted it. Six people came out of the truck and took control of the trailer at gunpoint.

When driver Vinod Kushwaha and his assistant Pintu Jagnarayan retaliated, the robbers beat them black and blue and tied their hands and legs. They abandoned the two in a sugarcane field in Kosamba the next morning.

The police added that Kushwaha and Jagnarayan somehow managed to free themselves and contacted the Rander police. They lodged a complaint of abduction and robbery.

Inspector R H Hadiya said: "Our preliminary investigations suggest that a professional gang is involved in the robbery. The gang might have kept a watch on Kushwaha and his assistant and surveyed the route before committing the crime." He said the trailer is valued at Rs 20 lakh and added that further investigation is on.

Heading: Gaekwad feud resurfaces, this time over construction - Indian Express
Content:
On the eve of Dussehra, a crude bomb exploded in the Mitha Pul Mohalla of Muslim-dominated Hathikhana locality on Wednesday afternoon. Three more such bombs were found next to the blast spot. No one was injured in the blast.

Vadodara Police Commissioner Rakesh Asthana, who visited the spot later, said the contents of the bombs were sent to the forensic laboratory for investigation.

According to the eyewitnesses, the blast took place around 2 pm, damaging a street lamp. The residents immediately informed the police and the area was cordoned off.

"Some people spotted three small crude bombs packed tightly in a piece of white cloth," said a resident.

The Bomb Disposal Squad rushed to the spot and checked the explosives, while forensic experts inspected the spot and collected the traces of explosive material.

Heading: GIDC takes over infrastructure development work in Makarpura - Indian Express
Content:
The divide between the scions of the Gaekwad royal family of the erstwhile Baroda State, Ranjitsinh Gaekwad and Sangramsinh Gaekwad, has once again come out in the open.

Sangramsinh's son Pratapsinh has filed an application under the Right to Information (RTI) Act to the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC), inquiring about the Gaekwads carrying out a new construction in the Laxmi Vilas Palace premises recently.

C B Patel, VMC Town Development Officer, said: "On September 22, Pratapsinh enquired about the Gaekwads constructing new buildings in the palace premises at Moti Baug area. Following this, we served a notice on the Gaekwads, who replied that there are no new constructions in Moti Baug."

Mahendrasinh Chauhan, Administrator, Gaekwad Baroda Golf Club, said, "We have responded to the queries saying that no such activity is going on in the Palace premises."

Heading: VMC serves notices to contractor over stagnant water - Indian Express
Content:
The corporation will look after the repair of storm water drains

Bringing two years of uncertainty to an end, the Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation (GIDC) has taken up the task of ensuring critical infrastructure development in Makarpura.

The decision was taken at a high level meeting between officials of the GIDC, the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) and the Vadodara Chambers of Commerce and Industries (VCCI) on Wednesday.

This comes after one Makarpura Infrastructure Industrial Development Board (MIIDB) failed to make headways in the parleys, even after a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed between MIIDB and GIDC two years ago.

GIDC will look after the repairing of storm water drains and roads.

Jayesh Rao, GIDC Divisional Manager, Vadodara, said: "An advisory committee will be formed comprising VCCI, MIIDB and VMC officials to suggest the GIDC authorities about the repair work."

Rao, however, refused to comment on the MoU signed between GIDC and MIIDB and the reason of delay in the project.

GIDC Managing Director M Sahu was present in the meeting, said an official seeking anonymity. The official added that the project is estimated at Rs 20 crore.

"Fifty per cent of the funds will be contributed by Gujarat industrial development, 35 per cent by the GIDC and the rest 15 per cent will be contributed by the plot holders," the official said.

Confirming the meeting, Das said that the GIDC still needs to consult the higher authorities regarding the decisions taken today.

On the MoU with the MIDDB, Das said: "MIIDB also wanted to sign an MoU with the VMC for tax waiver, claiming that it was moving forward with the infrastructure development. However, there was no progress."

Comprising over hundreds of industrial units, Makarpura GIDC estate has concentration of mechanical industries. Every year, the units suffer huge losses due to flooding as the stormwater drain service remained in a bad shape.

Located on the southern part of the city, the estate forms a getaway for all the rainwater collected in the city and flows downstream through Vishwamitri, river ravine to other rivers. The maintenance of civic infrastructure, which includes roads, storm water drains, streetlights and other amenities, remained a long standing demand of the industrial units.

Heading: No Public Information Officer in Agriculture Department - Indian Express
Content:
Three departments of the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) have issued notices to the contractor of Eros Apartment over the water stagnancy in the Akota area of the city.

This comes after two suspected cases of dengue surfaced in this area, making the VMC to take action against those found responsible for water stagnancy.

According to the VMC officials, it is the stagnant water around the under construction buildings of Eros Apartment that led to the suspected dengue cases.

Narendra Vasava, Assistant Municipal Commissioner, Vadodara city south zone, said, "We have served notices on the contractor (Rashmi Patel) and the

person will be penalised. We are yet to take a decision on the amount of the penalty."

While Patel refused to comment on the issue, VMC authorities said the amount collected as penalty will be spent by the VMC's health department on the affected areas.

Vasava added: "The Health department has been spraying insecticides in the area for nearly one week and if they do not pay the penalty to the corporation we will register a case against them."

The notices, issued on October 4, stated that the Eros Apartment did not abide by the rules of the BPMC Act of 1949 in its construction.

It has resulted in the outbreak of dengue in the vicinity of the under constructed apartment, which may lead to necessary legal action.

Heading: After Nano, hi-tech taxis to say ‘Hello’ - Indian Express
Content:
Issue comes to light after city-based activist files an RTI application to the department

An application filed under the Right to Information (RTI) Act by a city-based activist revealed that there is no Public Information Officer (PIO) in the the Agriculture department of the Gujarat government.

The activist, Rohit Prajapati, had sought the usage information of fertilisers after conducting an independent study on various food products and amount of pesticides in form of DDT and Urea in August this year. In its reply, the department, however, said that the information couldn't be given as there is no PIO in the department.

Prajapati said the department did not have a PIO or any concerned officer to give the information. "We are yet to get the information. The department has assured that they are gathering the data," he said. In the application, Prajapati had stated the amount of DDT and fertilisers found in various food products in the city. "The study was conducted after collecting various food samples from areas across the state," he added.

While corncobs in the state have the highest quantity of pesticides in form of DDT in food items with 7.24 ppm, wheat has the highest quantity of urea with 18.07 ppm.

"As per the reply given by the Agriculture department, there has been no survey done in this regard by the government," said Prajapati.

"It is not just the part per million (ppm) amount of DDT and fertilisers in food products being produced by the farmers, but the issue is about the deteriorating health of farmers being exposed to chemicals," he added.

Heading: Mad rush to make most of the last day - Indian Express
Content:
After the Nano, it is now the turn of the Hello Taxi to say hello to the city. The service will soon be launched to suit the mega city status of Ahmedabad.

Gone are the days when calling a taxi meant an agonising wait. The promoters of the taxi service promise that the response time will be at par with the emergency services.

Himanshu Patel, Chief Executive Officer of Ekta Corporate Services Pvt Ltd, which is launching the service, said, "These metred taxis will be equipped with facilities of global standards. Initially, the Indica Zeta will be pressed into service, as it is more comfortable."

He added that the services will be available 24x7. The service is accessible on a single number with 30 lines.

Elaborating on the functioning of the service, he said that on receiving a call for pick-up, the reservation centre will use its GPS (Global Positioning System) screen to search the nearest available taxi and inform the customer about the time the taxi would take to reach him/her.

Costs will be calculated on kilometre basis, from pick-up to drop-off.

Satellite tracking, economical fare for point-to-point transfer, quick commuting and other features will make these taxis a preferred mode of transport for one and all.

To ensure safety of the passengers, all the taxis will be constantly monitored at the central office, said Patel. Taxis that are connected with GPS will be controlled from the call centre itself. The ignition keys of the taxis can be switched off from the call centre itself in case of any trouble, he said.

Trained and professional drivers will be hired. Also, all the taxis are equipped with a panic button, as part of an emergency control system that intimates about any problem being faced by the customer.

Heading: Civic body pinched by ‘personal’ visits of globe-trotting Mayor - Indian Express
Content:
With the beats of the dhak reverberating through the atmosphere, Kolkata — dressed in crisp puja finery — geared up to complete the last lap of pandal hopping on Navami on Wednesday.

Navami marks the climax of the puja rituals beginning with the auspicious sandhi puja — the ritual that marks the transition from Ashtami to Navami.

While the evening was reserved for visiting the pandals that had not been visited on Saptami and Ashtami, the afternoon was dedicated by the Bengalis for strengthening community relations over sumptuous Navami bhog.

From khichudi, pulao, labra to an array of mouth-watering dishes lined up, the food enthusiast Kolkatans were simply spoilt for choice, as they sat in an idyllic mood, revelling in the spirit of Navami.

With most of the corporate sponsors announcing prestigious awards for best pujas, the pandal-hoppers made a beeline for the award- winning pandals in the evening.

Until now, the north Kolkata pujas had "tradition" as their USP, while south Kolkata pandals dabbled in "theme" pujas and won more accolades. In the tussle between north and south Kolkata, however, the former gave its southern counterparts a close competition.

No wonder, Telengabagan Sarbojanin, Pradip Sangha, Chaltabagan Lohapatty pandals in the north were brimming with crowds and the footfall only increased as night descended.

In a welcome relief, the erratic weather of the last week that had threatened to mar the festivities did not play spoilsport for the puja revellers.

When one section of pandal-hoppers was busy touring the puja-circuit, another section of the city was gearing up to usher in the Navratri mood. The dandiya venues in the city were seen bustling with the young and old alike, who came dressed in their ethnic best.

Popular dandiya venues like Salt Lake Stadium and Netaji Indoor stadium came alive with the strains of the latest chartbusters and psychedelic lights, amidst elaborate security arrangements.

Heading: Police clueless over Sourav’s daughter kidnap threat - Indian Express
Content:
Since becoming Mayor in June 2005 , Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya has visited not less than 25 countries

Mayor Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya may well be called a globe-trotter. Since June, 2005 when he took oath as the mayor, he has visited nearly 25 countries for attending summits and seminars. Of these, nearly eight visits came during July 2007 to July 2008.

He has visited almost every part of the world including China, Hong Kong, Australia, America, England, Indonesia, Japan, Germany, France, Spain, Russia, New Zealand, Finland, Russia, Greece and Egypt. Interestingly, most of the tours were not related to either activities or interests of the KMC.

"For every foreign trip, the mayor stays out of the country for at least eight days. Sometimes the duration increases up to 15 to 20 days. In the last 12 months, he has been out of the city for approximately 100 days," said a civic official. "Besides foreign trips, he also goes out of the city for several purposes including contesting court cases," he added.

Unprecedented foreign trips of Bhattacharya have raised several eyebrows in the KMC. Civic officials, councillors and Opposition leaders do not have any clue about the amount of money being spent to organise the tours. "Besides a few tours that were sponsored by the invitee organisations, all the expenses for the foreign trips have been undertaken by the KMC only," said a senior civic official.

Some of the tours included his visit to Germany in July, 2007 for a seminar "Summer Academy on Social Vulnerability", to Australia for Mayor's Asia Specific Environmental Summit (MAPES) in September, 2007, to Korea for Incheon Metropolitan Sister city Summit in October, 2007, to England for the seminar of Department for International Development (DFID), to Turkey in April 2008 and to China with the Bharat Chambers of Commerce for a goodwill tour in July.

Some of the countries mentioned above, he has visited twice in the last 12 months. Leader of the Opposition Javed Ahmed Khan said: "We always keep on asking why he is visiting abroad so frequently even though the visits are not related with the KMC work. All these trips are for seminars and goodwill missions, where the mayor of the city is not supposed to go."

He added: "Several decisions have been put on hold for the absence of mayor in the corporation. During emergencies, the city mayor usually remains out of reach."

Bhattacharya, however, has a different take. "I visit other countries to project Kolkata on the world map. No mayor of Kolkata has showcased the city at a global platform so far. Kolkata should learn from metropolitan cities of other countries," he said. The mayor added: "We are yet to implement the projects, I have seen in other countries, due to lack of political will and stiff resistance by the people."

The Opposition councillors, on the other hand, slam his remarks. "Instead of working in his office and ensure the development of the city, the mayor prefers to project the city at global seminars," said a councillor. "It does not matter to him that Kolkata does not have urban governance, upgraded drainage and sewerage system, proper footpaths and above all environment management," he added.

The Opposition also pointed out that Bhattacharya never took a team of engineers or MMiC (members mayor-in-council) of various departments with him for introducing them to development projects of other countries.

Former Mayor Subrata Mukherjee said: "In my tenure, I entered into agreements with Greece, Italy and United Kingdom to forge joint development projects between Kolkata and cities of those countries. I never visited a country without any purpose. My visits were to further the interests of the KMC."

He added: "I used to take a team of experts from the KMC including engineers, MMiC and even Opposition councilors to give them an opportunity to learn about the development projects so that they can replicate the technology in the city."

Heading: Environment-friendly carry bags in market soon - Indian Express
Content:
The officers of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) are clueless about the identities of the persons who had sent two letters to former Indian skipper Sourav Ganguly, threatening to kidnap his daughter, Sana.

The case was handed over to the CID after it was found that unidentified miscreants claimed themselves to be the members of terror outfit, Indian Mujahideen (IM). "The letters carried the name of IM," said a CID officer.

Siddhinath Gupta, DIG (Operations), CID, said: "We have examined the handwriting of both the letters and come to the conclusion that the letters were written by one person. We have questioned a few persons whose identity can't be disclosed at this point of time." We are taking the matter seriously, he added.

"The alleged IM members had demanded a ransom of Rs 2 crore in the letter if Ganguly wanted to save his daughter," said a CID officer. "The first letter was sent to his residence in Behala nearly 40 days ago, while the second one reached his house about a week ago. Both the letters were dropped in a letter box of a post office located at Park Street," the officer said.

The letters, which were written in Bengali, have been sent to handwriting experts of the state Question Documents Examination Bureau (QDEB) at

Bhawani Bhaban, the CID officer said. CID officers have spoken to employees of the post office, but they failed to give the police any clue about those who had dropped the letters in the letter box.

It is also learnt that the officers have questioned four residents of Behala. Security of Ganguly's residence and his relatives, including his daughter, has been beefed up and a strong vigil is being kept in areas around his residence, said a CID officer.

"No instruction, however, has been given to Ganguly to restrict his daughter's movement," the officer added. "Though it seems that the letters were sent to create panic in the Ganguly family, we don't want to take any chance. His house has been placed under a surveillance," he said.

Heading: Idol stolen from south Kolkata temple - Indian Express
Content:
As an alternative to hazardous plastic carry bags, Green Energy Corporation Limited (GECL) has developed specialised green tissue paper bags, which it plans to launch in market through retail giants soon.

To make these environment-friendly bags, GECL — an agency established by the state government — has used 100 per cent biodegradable tissue papers. According to the corporation, these bags will have carrying capacity of up to 3 kilograms.

S P Gon Chaudhuri, managing director of GECL, said: "These bags are 100 per cent recyclable and since they will be stitched, their production will save electricity. The bag dissolves in water and the mould can be used again to make new bags."

The department has finished creating 1,000 sample pieces and plans to produce in bulk once the bags find acceptance among the consumers.

"This is a first of its kind initiative taken by a governmental body to check the use of environmentally hazardous carry bags. We will be launching the special bags in the public domain after Pujas. We have already approached Spencer's to use our product in their outlets and they have shown interest in the bags," Chaudhuri said.

"We have been approached by GECL about using green tissue bags in our outlets. But we need to address a lot of issues before we begin using them," said Mani Shankar Mukherji, chief advisor (Corporate Relations), RPG Enterprises Limited.

According to GECL officials, since the material used for making the green tissue paper bags was not available in the state, the raw material for the samples was purchased from a Delhi-based private firm. To develop the product on a mass scale, GECL is in talks with some of the entrepreneurs of the city.

The officials said they have spoken to a number of self-help groups who will make the green tissue bags and colour them with special dyes.

Heading: Civic body puts construction of foot overbridges on hold - Indian Express
Content:
An ashtadhatu (the alloy of eight metals) idol of Lord Parasnath was stolen from a south Kolkata temple on Wednesday morning.

The theft took place at Sri Parasnath Digambar Jain temple located at 9, Alipore Park Place in the Alipore police station area.

A temple priest noticed the missing idol at 6.30 am and immediately informed Niraj Jain — joint secretary of the temple committee. Jain rushed to the spot, and informed the Alipore police station about the incident.

After preliminary inquiries, police sources indicated that the theft was the handiwork of a person who wants the temple to be shifted from the area.

Locals suspect that the culprit is a resident of the area.

They alleged that the temple is located inside an under-construction residential complex and the builders want the temple to be shifted.

"We suspect that some of the builders want to close down the temple. Now it is up to the police to investigate the matter," Jain said.

The investigating officers are clueless why the thieves decamped with the 40-year-old ashtadhatu idol when there were several other priceless idols inside the temple.

Rajesh Subarno, Deputy Commissioner (South) said, "We are investigating the matter. There could be various angles to it." No one has been arrested in this regard so far, he added.

Heading: Women in homosexual relationship surrender - Indian Express
Content:
The Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) will no longer give permission for the setting up of new foot overbridges in the city, as a survey conducted by the civic body has revealed that advertising agencies benefit from these more than the common people.

A senior civic official said: "Foot overbridges have to be set up on the basis of some parameters. But in the city, the bridges have been set up in such places where these are not required. As a consequence, the footbridges do not serve any purpose other than displaying advertisements," said the official.

"We are trying to regulate the installation of foot overbridges without proper planning. At present, we have stopped allowing advertising agencies to set up foot overbridges anywhere in the city," said Mayor Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya.

"We have already cancelled the proposals of setting up foot overbridges at Lindsay Street and Golpark," Bhattacharya said.

Considering the situation, an advertising agency had come forward with a proposal to install escalators or elevators on some of the footbridges in the city's most busy intersections. In line with the proposal, an elevator was installed at the Park Circus crossing in August. It was, however, shut down the very next day of its inauguration.

"There were some technical problems and we were ordered by the civic authorities to close the service. We are hoping that the service will resume after the Pujas," said a security officer deployed at Park Circus foot overbridge.

Bhattacharya also said: "We will not give permission to any advertising agency before making a final decision on the proposals."

This decision by the civic body comes after the state transport department had decided to pull down the footbridges on APC Road and Ultadanga, when it was found that the people were barely using them.

Some people allege that most of the foot overbridges are actually a hub for anti-social elements, who operate not only at night but also during the day. Also, on most occasions, the anti-socials carry out their activities in the presence of traffic police.

"I am scared of taking the footbridge although I know it is risky to cross the busy intersection at Ultadanga. But the overbridge is a hub for anti-social elements," said Sraboni Sarkar, a pedestrian taking the Ultadanga (Hudco) intersection said.

The traffic police, however, have washed their hands off the matter saying they cannot monitor the foot overbridges as they have other important things to do. They say they would take action if they receive any complaint from a pedestrian.

Heading: Door-to-door collection out, Internet in - Indian Express
Content:
Two women in a homosexual relationship, who were on the run since September 22, surrendered at Panchla police station on Wednesday.

Later in the day, they were produced in the court of chief judicial magistrate at Howrah and were subsequently handed over to their respective families.

Both are residents of Panchla area of Howrah.

Following the surrender of the duo, a mob assembled at the Panchla police station to take a look at them.

"We don't know about their relationship. We are also not aware of the reasons for such a behaviour," said a relative of one of the women.

However, the duo came out openly to support their decision. "I wanted to be a boy since childhood. It is a curse that I was born a girl," said one of the women.

According to the sources, both the girls were in relationship for the last three years.

"They surrendered at the police station this morning. Their families had lodged complaints that they were missing. The duo was produced in court to ascertain whether they were forced into the relationship or had left their homes willingly," said Gautam Talukdar, officer in-charge of the Panchla police station.

Relationship between persons of same sex is prohibited under Section 377 of IPC.

Heading: Saplings for visitors at Dum Dum pandal - Indian Express
Content:
Going around one's own locality for collecting 'chanda' (donations) for Durga Puja is passé. In the race between big banners and sponsors, certain puja committees have gained an edge by going online.

After organising the annual Durga Puja for more than 40 years, Behala Nutan Dal Puja committee had decided to go online in 2006. "There were many people involved with our puja who had to leave the country for various reasons. With our website behalanutandal.com in place, they can get a feel of our puja every year. During the pujas, we update the website with the latest photos," said Sandipan Banerjee, convenor of the Puja committee.

He added that since last year, quite a few people have approached them through the website to donate to the puja committee.

Taking a cue, Deshapriya Park Durga Puja also launched its website in August this year. "A number of people across the globe wanted to get an update on the puja and also send donations. That is why we decided to design a website," said Anirban Bose, who is in charge of sponsorships for this year's puja.

Their website, dparkdurgotsab.com, has a detailed donorship form that can be downloaded directly from the website. Besides, it has photos, the puja schedule and even a dress code for the immersion procession on the last day of the festival.

"Our website has been designed by Universal Solutions and it took us around a month to get it in place," added Bose. The puja committee also plans to link their website with Google from next year and will also market their online donation procedure more aggressively.

On Mahalaya this year, Suruchi Sangha of New Alipore also inaugurated their website. "Already a few people who are willing to send us donations have contacted us online from within India. It is a little early to tell, but we expect a much better response next year," says general secretary of the Puja committee, Swarup Biswas.

Bagbazar Sarbajanin and Santoshpur Lakepally Pujas have also made their presence felt on the net.

With branding and marketing being the buzzword for the Durga Pujas now, these websites are expected to go a long way in building a brand image for these decades-old pujas in Kolkata.

Heading: Kumartuli remembers the pioneer artist of modern Durga idols - Indian Express
Content:
At Mall Pally Sarbojonin Durgotsav at Dum Dum in the northern fringes of the city, the organisers practise what they preach. So, while the theme of this puja is war against global warming, the organisers are distributing saplings among puja revellers who come to visit the pandal.

"We are not just trying to create awareness about environmental degradation. We also insist that our visitors take one sapling from us and plant it. The only way to fight environmental degradation is to plant as many trees as possible," Falguni Purokayastha, president of the puja committee, told The Indian Express.

Apart from distributing saplings, messages are being blared out through microphones on the importance of planting saplings. The theme is the brainchild of Partha Roy, an artiste from Belghoria.

The committee officials say the Chandi Puran itself has reference to the Goddess Durga fighting a monster that destroyed trees. "Unless we fight the menace of environmental pollution we will be cursed by our posterity for making the planet inhabitable. That is why we have to take recourse to mythology in which the Goddess is said to have fought a monster called Durgam who was destroying all trees and making the world a barren place," Suprakash Bandopadhyay, secretary of the puja committee, told The Indian Express.

The idols are different from the traditional ones, with all of them, including Durga, carrying saplings instead of weapons. The Asura is also shown surrendering an axe to the Goddess that he used for felling the trees.

While the pandal has been built in the shape of a felled tree, structures resembling housing complexes have been depicted behind the pandal. "Urbanisation is eating into the green cover and we will have to make optimum use of the space available to us for building houses," Purokayastha said.

Heading: This pandal is all for rehabilitation - Indian Express
Content:
G Pal and Sons studio at Kumartuli might seem to be just another atelier, but for many idol makers in this town, it is a reminiscence of legendary artist Gopeswar Pal, whom they remember as one of the most acclaimed artists of all times.

Established in 1926, the studio does not make Durga idols any more, but is still considered a one- stop shop for sculptures and figurines on clay, fiberglass and plaster of paris. Many artists recall Pal as the pioneer of the idea of creating Puja idols as separate structures instead of the traditional single chala.

"Pal was the first artist who came up with the idea of creating idols separately instead of putting them together under a single chala, which was quite popular among idol makers earlier," said D Bhattacharya of Kumartuli Sarbojanin Durgotsav Committee, one of the oldest pandals in the city and perhaps the first to adopt the new form of idol making.

Pal had participated in an art exhibition in 1924 and won a prize for creating a horse's head within 45 seconds. "When Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was the president of Kumartuli Sarbojanain Puja, many idols were destroyed in a fire and Pal recreated them within 24 hours before the Puja was inaugurated," recalled Bomkesh Pal, a relative of the artist.

Pal passed away in 1944 leaving behind the studio, which was at one point of time the only supplier of sculptures to the Ramkrishna Mission.

Heading: Puja goes hip, Manchurian replaces khichuri - Indian Express
Content:
The United Club Puja at Paschim Putiary has recreated an open-air rehabilitation home in its Puja pandal to address the problems faced by criminals sentenced for life in gaining acceptance in the society.

"Life convicts are labeled as criminals even if they repent their misdeeds later in their lives," said Ashish Majumder, media secretary of the United Club.

The club has recreated the Lalgola Correctional Home built by the state government in Midnapore.

"The idea is to spread awareness that no matter how grievous somebody's sin is, the best way to deal with it is through love and forgiveness. If we suppress convicts, ill-treat them and pay them back in their own coin, we push them towards crime," added Shankar Ghosal, an artiste.

To spread their message in an innovative way, the Puja organisers have not put arms in the hands of their idol. The deity holds a lotus and a conch and her hands are extended in blessings.

The entrance to the pandal is graced by a tea shop, a cycle repairing shop and a portico which doubles up as a village school.

"Ten mime artistes from Patharpratima in Canning are playing inmates at the pandal. We are trying to show that inmates can be encouraged to sell tea, work in bicycle workshops or take up teaching in a village school," Majumder said.

Heading: Fresh headache for Dalmiya & Co: Shah Rukh’s franchisee is ‘displeased’ with CAB’s IPL bill - Indian Express
Content:
While Durga Puja is synonymous with the bhog of khichuri and labra that is served to devotees, Salt Lake residents have made a paradigmatic shift.

Khichuri cooked by the traditional thakur is passe. Enter well-trained chefs, as vegetable manchurian, chilli potatoes and kosha mangsho now figure prminently in the menus of most Salt Lake pujas.

On navami, organisers of FD Block Puja served fried rice, Manchurian, pakora, dal and paneer curry to devotees. "We ensure that our residents do not have to cook at home," said S Biswas, secretary of the Puja committee. The budget for this year's feast was a whopping Rs 2.5 lakh as nearly 2,000 people are being served meals everyday, he added.

BJ Block kickstarted its puja with fish kalia, while a mutton gravy and basmati rice with dal and vegetable curry were served on navami.

"We have a food budget of nearly Rs 3 lakh and every day we serve meals to nearly 1,500 people," said puja committee secretary U Dastidar.

"Earlier the women of our colony used to prepare simple khichuri and a vegetable mishmash. Now the number of people has gone up and the menu has been expanded. We give the job to professional caterers now," said Sumit Sarkar, joint secretary of the Labony housing complex puja. Around 3,000 devotees gather for the puja meal daily.

No wonder, Puja committees are issuing food coupons to people, and subscription amount collected from a family ranges between Rs 500 and Rs 1,000.

Heading: Where have all the boys gone? - Indian Express
Content:
Shah Rukh's Red Chillies Entertainment is 'reluctant' to fully reimburse CAB's massive IPL bill of Rs 7.26 crore; Only BCCI's intervention can straighten things out between franchisee and state association, reckon insiders

When Bollywood superstar Shah Rukh Khan dropped in at the Eden Gardens last Saturday to catch up with the CAB's new president Jagmohan Dalmiya, it had appeared that the wrangle over the IPL spending was a closed chapter.

But four days after the goodwill meeting, a key insider in the know of things told The Indian Express that nothing is as it seems. In fact, it has been learnt that Shah Rukh's franchisee Red Chillies Entertainment, which owns the Kolkata Knight Riders, is quite "displeased" with the CAB's massive spending during the IPL carnival in Kolkata last summer.

During the April-May Twenty20 championship, SRK and his production unit Red Chillies had formed a separate company Knight Riders Pvt Ltd, which technically owns the Sourav Ganguly-led IPL team based out of Kolkata.

A reliable source, who was involved with the organising of the IPL matches at Eden Gardens last summer, disclosed that negotiations between the CAB and Shah Rukh's franchisee have hit a roadblock. "At this stage, things are not looking nice, for both CAB and the franchisee. Of course, there's plenty of goodwill between the owners of the Knight Riders and hosts CAB. But the bottomline is, everyone is a professional. There's been huge spending during the IPL from the CAB's side. And they will naturally ask the franchisee to pay up. But again, the franchisee right now is not keen at all to pay so much money. They are displeased with such a huge figure in IPL spending," the source revealed.

The source also pointed out that the problem can only be worked out now in two steps. "First, the CAB has to coolly sit down and neatly complete the process of segregating the bills, that is, mark out which expenses should be reimbursed by Red Chillies. After that, if there's still no solution, both parties have to ask the BCCI to step in and sort things out. But as of now, the franchisee isn't happy with the way things are, and they are just not willing to reimburse the full amount of Rs 7.26 crore," the source said.

The Eden Gardens hosted seven matches of the IPL between April 20 and May 25, and after the external auditing, the CAB's total costs in terms of bills has run into Rs 7.26 crore — a figure way above the stipulated Rs 3.5 crore mark.

The CAB had initially refused to accept a lump sum payment of

Rs 3.5 crore from Shah Rukh's company. The state body is now waiting for the franchisee to reimburse the CAB's entire IPL bill amount of Rs 7.26 crore. This is where SRK's company is raising objections, and they are not keen on settling the entire amount.

In fact, even as members of the new Jagmohan Dalmiya-led CAB administration are blaiming the earlier Prasun Mukherjee regime for overshooting the Rs 3.5 crore IPL budget by over two times, the former police chief has written a strong letter to the CAB, clarifying that the IPL-related expenses were inevitable and that the franchisee is legally bound to reimburse all the expenses.

Heading: Two held for evading VAT - Indian Express
Content:
Blame it on cricket or the absence of a culture on athleticism, Bengalis are woefully dropping off Indian football's radar, and it's only getting worse

Football used to be Bengal's forte. Not any more. The Dempos and the Mahindras are running the show at the national level. And in Kolkata, outstation players are ruling the roost.

Football has been the name of the game in this part of the world ever since Mohun Bagan humbled East Yorkshire Regiment in the IFA Shield final. That was 1911.

Ninety-seven years on, as Mohun Bagan won their 28th Calcutta Football League (CFL) title in 2008, only one Bengali player figured in the list of 14 in their final round match — goalkeeper Sangram Mukherjee was the odd man out.

Why is the 'Bong connection' fading fast in Kolkata football? The legendary Chuni Goswami blames it on the changed psychology of the Bengali middle-class, which doesn't encourage kids to play this sport anymore. Cricket is their joie de vivre.

"There has been a marked change in the last 10 years. Young boys are taking to cricket, not only in Kolkata but also in suburbs and small towns. The general perception is, cricket gives security. It has glamour. And Bengal and the Bengalis have a role model in Sourav Ganguly. This is the precise reason why cricket academies have been fast outnumbering football coaching centres. And football talents have no choice but to share the backstage," Goswami told The Indian Express.

"Secondly, Bengali footballers nowadays seem to have lost their appetite for success. A little bit of prominence, a permanent job through sports quota — and they are easily satisfied. Football is observing a global boom and the positives have started to trickle down in our country. We are now among the Asian elites after qualifying for the 2011 Asian Cup. And the cash has started to flow. But Bengal boys seem to be in a deep slumber," he lamented. Even as the I-League is well underway, the absence of Bengali dominance in the national championship is only obvious.

Mohun Bagan goalie Sangram Mukherjee takes solace from the fact that all the top goalkeepers in the country are of Bengali descent. "Subrata Paul, Sandip Nandy, Subhasish Roy Chowdhury — all three national team goalkeepers have Bengali roots. Then there are others like Abhijit Mondal," he said. But again, this is an isolated lot, a rank minority of sorts.

There was a time when the state leagues of North 24-Parganas and South 24-Parganas used to be the hub of footballing talents. The likes of Subrata Bhattacharya, Manoranjan Bhattacharya, Bhaskar Ganguly and other top stars cut their teeth in competitive football in those popular tournaments. During that time, the Big Three — Mohun Bagan, East Bengal and Mohammedan Sporting — had spotters who loved to do some legwork for the sake of the game. The small clubs used to take pride in nurturing talents. There were coaches like Achyut Banerjee, who gave shape to many a dream.

Now, the big clubs are only interested in names, the smaller clubs have more faith in third-string foreigners rather than in home-grown talents, and quality coaches are at a premium.

Indian Football Association (IFA) secretary Utpal Ganguly admits that there is a lack of co-ordination between districts and the state capital as far as promoting the game is concerned.

"We have started to bridge that gap. The IFA-organised state league is a good platform for the youngsters from the districts. We have to ensure that Kolkata's football fraternity gets a chance to see those players. We are working hard to ensure that good performances don't go unnoticed. It's not possible for Kolkata's clubs to go to the districts and spot talents. The idea is to bring them here. We are also trying to promote football in schools. This is basically to target the middle-class and the upper middle-class," Ganguly told this daily.

The IFA is not doing everything wrong though. It has adopted the Sunderbans Football Academy and is sincerely trying to go to the grassroots. Problem is, they are not marketing the game properly.

Kolkata and its Bengalis still swear by football. An East Bengal-Mohun Bagan clash at Yuba Bharati Krirangan still ensures a full-house. And then again, life comes to a standstill in this football-mad city when Brazil and Argentina face off in the World Cup. The Zidanes and the Ronaldos are massive icons here.

So, it's a real paradox that the talent base is receding. That the pressure of academics is getting big sounds too lame an excuse now. Gen-X Bengalis, perhaps, are not game enough to meet the challenges that football offers.

Heading: With static land prices, buyers become choosy - Indian Express
Content:
Fake bill books seized from Mukesh Kumar, Shiv Kumar

Two persons have been arrested for allegedly evading the Value Added Tax (VAT).

The police claimed that the arrested persons used to make bogus bills to evade tax thus cheated the Taxation Department and caused huge loss to the state exchequer.

The police claim to have seized fake bills books from local businessmen Mukesh Kumar alias Rinku and Shiv Kumar Pandey. The police said the bill books had been printed in the names of some local genuine firms but were being used illegally by the accused.

Giving the details of the case, SP (Detective) Gurpreet Singh Toor said a local hosiery owner Jagan Nath, who runs Hanuman Hosiery factory in the city, had recently been questioned by the Sales Tax department for selling goods worth over Rs 1.20 crore in the last six months but paying the tax for goods worth Rs 21 lakh only.

These revelations raised eyebrows of the hosiery owner who approached the police.

SP Toor said that while investigating the case, the police came to know that Mukesh Kumar and Shiv Kumar Pandey were involved in the evasion of VAT using the fake bill books of Jagan Nath's hosiery. SP Toor said that out of the 18 fake bill books of different firms, seized from the accused, one bill book is also of Jagan Nath's firm.

Toor said that further investigations were on in this case.

Two arrested for dodging sales tax

The police arrested two persons, Ravinder Kumar alias Raju and Manish Kumar alias Mani, for illegally using the sales tax numbers of other firms for ferrying their goods to evade sales tax.

Heading: Anaars and rockets are most dangerous crackers, warns doc - Indian Express
Content:
The auction organised by the Greater Ludhiana Area Development Authority (GLADA) for 16 shops near the Civil Hospital yesterday turned about to be a damp squib as not a single bidder turned up for the auction.

Although approved sites had received a big response in the past, much to the dismay of the officials' potential bidders refused to turn up to at the auction.

Insiders said a slaughter house used to exist at the site years ago, hence buyers are not interested to invest in the location. Moreover, the shops are located in a congested area and have failed to attract buyers.

Approved areas can get buyers only when the strategic location of the area suits the buyer and seller, said S.P Singh, a city-based property dealer.

The reserve price of the area was kept at Rs 54,000 per square yard by GLADA. Sources said that market rates are stagnant in many posh areas, so it is unlikely that GLADA can fetch huge sums for the shops.

Paramjit Singh, another property dealer, said, "The real estate business is no longer a booming business. Prices in many colonies are almost stagnant while in few others, buyers have disappeared because of stringent policies of the government. Approved colonies with a good choice of location are the only mantra to get some business from real estate market these days."

He added,"Prices in approved colonies such as Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar, Rajguru Nagar and Sarabha Nagar are also almost the same as the last year. Hence, the market has not moved much despite a few good auctions of GLADA."

No power for unapproved colonies

On the top of it, the unapproved sites are facing the worst scenario. On the instructions of GLADA, the electricity board has stopped giving new connections to the residents constructing houses in the unapproved colonies.

Following this, more than 50,000 residents of the city are waiting to shift in their houses from unapproved colonies near Dhandra Road and Jassian Road. Interestingly, all of them have got registeries of their plots measuring between 50 square yards and 100 square yards.

Suresh Sood, General Secretary, Indian National Trade Union Congress, said, "We will take up the demand with CM on October 10 in his first sangat darshan in the city. If there is no result then we will intensify our stir. The workers cannot have a dark Diwali without electricity."

He added, "Poor people cannot afford to have houses in approved colonies. "

Kamal Chaitly, President, Ludhiana Property Dealers Association, said, "At present, there is no new buyer in the unapproved colonies. GLADA has set conditions that no colony of less than 75 acres can be made an approved colony and within the city such a huge chunk of land is not available. A few colonies are coming up in the outskirts but everyone cannot go that far. Moreover, they are luxury housing schemes. Earlier, 10 acres was the limit for an approved colony. Government needs to soften its stand as thousands are waiting to shift into their new houses."

Heading: Rare feat at DMCH: endoscopic surgery breathes life into three children - Indian Express
Content:
TO make schoolchildren aware about the hazards of fire crackers, the Dayanand Medical College and Hospital in collaboration with the Burns Association of India (Ludhiana Chapter) is holding interactive sessions and workshops on burns prevention across different schools in the city.

An interactive session and workshop on burns prevention was organised at St Thomas School, Brown Road, today.

Dr Sanjeev Uppal, Professor of Plastic Surgery, Department of DMCH, spoke to the students and gave them tips on how to burst crackers to avoid any accident.

Dr Uppal said children usually like to burst crackers 15 to 20 days prior to Diwali. According to him, 'anaars' and rockets' are the dangerous ones and children should ignite these crackers with safety. He emphasised to burst crackers and fireworks in open spaces and in the presence of elders. He said that clothes should be tight fitting and preferably cotton.

He also suggested keeping a bucket full of water nearby which may be helpful in dousing the flames if somebody accidentally catches fire.

Dr Uppal said that role of parents and elder siblings is very important in educating children. He asked the students to educate at least five people at home after the session. He said that fire is a good master when it is in control but becomes bad master when it goes out of control. He said that last year 42 cases reported to DMC emergency on the day of Diwali and most of them were boys and young men.

Heading: One lakh new gastro cancer cases detected every year in India: experts - Indian Express
Content:
For 10-month-old Harshpreet from Mukerian, 5-month-old Meenu from Jalandhar, and 15-year-old Ashu from Sirsa, it was timely surgical intervention using endoscopic modality which gave them a new lease of life.

The patients had inflammation on the back of their tongues, which was blocking the windpipe, making it difficult to breathe.

The operation was conducted at the Dayanand Medical College and Hospital (DMCH).

According to doctors, swelling at the back of the tongue, in medical terms, is a fluid filled abnormal tissue called 'Vallecular cyst'. The individual speaks in a muffled voice initially when the size is small and later as the size increases, it leads to choking attacks. It becomes an emergency situation necessitating surgical intervention. It sometimes manifests at birth or in later age, say doctors.

The doctors say that children below 18 years are the most vulnerable and surgical intervention is required at an early age. Oral endoscopy and endoscopic-assisted minimal access surgery was utilised even in newborn babies as early as 10 months of age to give them a new lease to life.

The unique endoscopic surgical procedure was undertaken by Dr Manish Munjal, Professor, Department of ENT.

Surgery in the past in newborns, infants, children and even in adults was a procedure undertaken by feeling the obstruction with the fingers and merely decapping the swellings or by cutting through the tissues of the neck to reach the swelling. The traditional surgical procedures, now appropriately labeled 'blind procedures', were associated with unnecessary and excessive bleeding, spillage into the windpipe and lungs, postoperative swelling in the mouth and neck and, breathing problems due to damage to normal tissues. Usually, the patient after the surgery was kept on external supply of oxygen through multiple tubes passed through the mouth or neck for days till the neck tissues had healed. There were unforeseen complications, a long postoperative recovery period, extended hospitalisation and huge expenses involved.

Dr Munjal elaborates that cystic swellings in the patients were operated upon under magnified endoscopic visualisation through their mouth using telescopes that illuminated the depths of the entrance to the windpipe from different angles. The challenge initially was to enter the windpipe by manouevering around the bulky obstructions. Any injury to the cyst would have led to spillage of the fluid of the cysts, inside the windpipe and the patient would have drowned in these fluids. It was all because of the dexterity of the anaesthetists, Dr PL Gautam, Dr Suneet and Dr Shikha Kathuria that the windpipe could be successfully isolated from the mammoth swellings and surgery could commence.

Dr Munjal adds that the huge cysts had been meticulously evaluated radiologically and by imaging studies CT scans as well as MRIs, before venturing utilizing an endoscopic approach. The swelling could burst into the windpipe with fatal consequences and an incomplete removal lead to recurrence. The site of origin of the cysts was identified circumferentially. They were occupying the hollows between the back of the tongue and the beak like tissue at the entrance to the windpipe. The weight of these fluid filled cysts made them fall into the windpipe, something similar to "ice cream scoop in a cone" -effect. The blood vessels lining the cysts were identified and controlled endoscopically, therefore minimising blood loss during surgery, said Dr Munjal.

There was minimal swelling of tissues of the windpipe and the patients were discharged on the third day.

Heading: Employee alleges harassment by DEO - Indian Express
Content:
More than 100 delegates from all over north India gathered at Christian Medical College and Hospital (CMCH) to attend the international Upper Gastro Intestinal (GI), Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery workshop and conference today. The conference was organised by the Department of Surgery at CMCH. The faculty of the conference was from Australia, UK, Vellore, Chennai, Delhi, Chandigarh and Ludhiana. There were three international speakers and more than 10 national speakers.

Earlier in the day, the conference was inaugurated by Dr A.G. Thomas and Dr Sunil Singh, Director and Principal of CMC Hospital, respectively. Both thanked the international and national faculty for taking time out of their busy routines to visit CMC and participate in the conference. Dr A.G. Thomas said that upper GI, hepatobiliary and pancreatic surgery services at CMC hospital were an integral part of surgical services in the hospital and included two out-patient clinics, a dedicated ward, a surgical endoscopy suite, and dedicated operation theatres for laparoscopic and open surgery and special services for patients with liver, gall bladder and pancreatic cancer. There is a special liver cancer clinic and dedicated facilities for surgery for liver cancers.

There has been a sea change in the management strategies for diseases of the gastrointestinal tract in the last decade with many more diseases including cancer earlier considered untreatable now being treated successfully; thus department of surgery has formulated this workshop and conference dedicated to the education and treatment of these problems, said Dr. Rajeev Kapoor, Head of Surgery.

Liver cancer is the one of the most common causes of death from cancer for both men and women in the western world, said Dr Sudhakar Rao, director of surgery from Royal Perth Hospital. Dr Misra, Prof and Head, Surgery, at AIIMS said that in India too there were more than 1,00,000 new cases of upper GI cancer diagnosed each year. Panelists discussed various surgical techniques of treating these patients.

Dr Anderson talked about interventional radiology in hepatobiliary diseases and radiological evaluation of liver lesions. Dr Keith Hine discussed gastrointestinal stromal tumors and evaluation of suspicious esophageal lesions. Dr Wig spoke about indications of surgery in acute pancreatitis and operative management on liver and pancreatic trauma. Other speakers included Dr Sanjay Govil, Dr Satish Jain, Dr Surinder Singh, Dr Kuldeep Singh, Dr A.J. Joseph and Dr Rana A.K. Singh.

Heading: Schools celebrate Dussehra - Indian Express
Content:
A senior assistant at the District Education Office on Wednesday alleged harassment at the hands of Sudesh Bajaj, District Education Officer (Secondary), Ludhiana.

Madanjit Singh, who is also assistant public instructions officer of the Education Department, Ludhiana, alleged, "DEO Sudesh Bajaj has been harassing me ever since she joined here as DEO. Being the incharge of Right to Information (RTI) branch, I have to get many documents signed by her for providing information to the applicants. But she delays my work and do not sign the documents in time. All this leads to sheer harassment as applicants of RTI get delayed information, and then they lodge complaint against the delay to the concerned authorities."

The agitated senior employee of DEO office said, "I have been working in the department for the last 28 years. The DEO (Secondary) unnecessarily delays my work. Yesterday I went to Sudesh Bajaj thrice for getting these documents signed but she scolded me in very rude way and said that she was busy. I handed over my files to one of my colleagues for getting them signed, but Sudesh Bajaj signed his files but not mine."

The Punjab State Sikhya Vibhag Ministerial Employees Union, Ludhiana, has also come out in Madanjit's support. Madanjit, who was complaining of severe headache, was taken to the dispensary in the premises of Mini Secretariat. "His blood pressure was 110-190 when we brought him to the dispensary. Following which the doctor gave him the medicine," said Iqbal Singh, district president of this union.

Iqbal Singh further said, "Madanjit reported us the whole incident of harassment and that is why we are supporting him."

However Sudesh Bajaj, DEO (Secondary), denied all these allegations, saying, "I always sign all the documents well in time. And Madanjit should get his files signed on his own. The other employees are not supposed to get his files signed. He is suffering from blood pressure and should take medicine regularly. My office staff told me that Madanjit had spoken against me and others in the office today. I am going to ask the office staff to give all this in writing for further action."

Heading: Terror funds came from Gulf, routed through banks, hawala and money transfer channels - Indian Express
Content:
REALTY: Stamp duty collection up 24 % between Jan and August, notwithstanding 10 per cent fall in number of transactions

At a time when the realty market has been hit by absolute stagnation, the only aspect that doesn't seem to have been hit is the revenue garnered by the stamp duty department.

Revenue collections from stamp duty on property and land transactions between January and August 2008 have gone up by 24% as against the same period last year. The collections have remained buoyant even as in this period, the average of number of transactions has reduced by 10%, the first such dip in recent years.

Stamp duty being up to 5% of the value of the property, realty analysts state that such high collections prove that even when the market is in the midst of a slump, developers are unrelentingly holding on to prices.

"Until a few months ago the slump was only being talked about and very few builders actually reduced their prices. The real impact will be seen now. The rupee fell to a six year low on Wednesday. The way the stock markets have reacted recently has created negative sentiments in the real estate market which will take at least two years to stabilize," said Sandeep Sadh, CEO of the portal Mumbai Property Exchange. Sadh, like most property analysts, predicts continuing poor sales this Diwali, which is usually the time when maximum property transactions are conducted.

As the tug of war between unremitting developers and buyers waiting for a price crash continues, transaction volumes have hit an all-time low. In the month of August this year there have been only 3,814 property sales transactions, 30% lower than August last year which saw 5,385 transactions.

"During Diwali, developers will be forced to reduce their prices by 20-25% if they want volumes in sales," said Gulam Zia, national director, research and advisory services, at the property consultancy Knight Frank. Zia added that the reason developers do not want to admit to any such plans is because once home-buyers hear of a downslide in prices, they will wait for a further reduction which is what is happening right now.

Amongst the few developers who have decided to slash their rates are Orbit Corporations which has announced a 15% discount for bookings done in Diwali in any of their projects in central Mumbai. A week ago, Wadhwa developers brought down the rates for their under-construction project of two-to-four BHK apartments, duplexes and triplexes at Goregaon by Rs 1,500 per sq ft.

"We brought down the rates last Friday, and post the price correction we sold 50 flats. Developers should realize that they cannot be rigid when the times are tough. If they do not bend when the storm is strong, they will break eventually," said Vijay Wadhwa, chief promoter of the Wadhwa group.

The Maharashtra Chamber of Housing Industry (MCHI), however, still insists the industry has no plans to consider any reduction in rates. "With land and construction cost being high, we have left prices to the individual developers' discretion. The pace of sales is poor at the moment due to the economic growth being slow but things will eventually improve," said MCHI vice president Sunil Mantri who is himself currently offering stamp duty waivers for bookings in his projects.

Heading: IIT-B annual fest to give wings to da Vinci’s dream - Indian Express
Content:
Cops freeze bank accounts from which IM members withdrew money

The Mumbai Police Crime Branch on Wednesday revealed that it has frozen a certain number of bank accounts in the city from which money was withdrawn by some of the alleged Indian Mujahideen (IM) members. According to the police, the IM operatives had been receiving money from Gulf countries through these accounts for the past two years. This is apart from what they had been receiving through the hawala network and the Western Union Money Transfer.

"During interrogations, some of the arrested accused told us that they used to withdraw money from some bank accounts in the city, following which we have frozen the accounts. They are savings accounts in nationalised banks and are in the names of some individuals. Since 2006, money was being deposited by people in Gulf countries and was being withdrawn in small amounts by the IM members. A total of Rs 26 lakh was sent from Gulf countries through proper banking channels to these accounts," said Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria, refusing to divulge further details or the number of accounts frozen.

The Crime Branch has already seized Rs 11.36 lakh in cash from the IM members arrested from Mangalore.

A dedicated team of Crime Branch officers is focussing on the funding received by the IM members, and are investigating the manner in which money was sent to them via hawala and money transfer channels. "If it is found that the people who are holding these accounts were actively helping the IM operatives in receiving funds from outside the country, they will also be booked under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) for aiding and abbetting," said Maria.

Heading: All cases personal disputes, says Gawli’s bail application - Indian Express
Content:
Institute to hold workshop on aircraft that flies by flapping its wings

When Leonardo da Vinci drew a detailed diagram of a man-powered aircraft in 1845, he may not have expected its successors to come this far. For, when the Aerospace Engineering Department of the Indian Institute of Technology—Bombay (IIT-B) begins its annual festival Zephyr on Friday, one of the biggest highlights will be a first-of-its kind workshop on the Ornithopter—an aircraft that flies by flapping its wings.

On Saturday, Ornithopter specialist Nathan Chronister will conduct a two-hour workshop where a few students will be shown how to build and fly such an aircraft.

Around the world, ornithopters have been looked at as an alternate to fixed-wing aircrafts, and its study, design and manufacturing is a hobby among enthusiasts.

An ornithopter can be a light-weight model powered by rubber-bands or a larger model that is radio controlled. "Chronister has also bagged a patent when it comes to ornithopters. They can be of different kinds, including remote-controlled ones," says Aadil Shah, general secretary, Zephyr '08. In order to make the workshop more interesting, Chronister has already sent some model kits to be used at the festival.

Having worked with ornithopters for over 20 years, Chronister owns a company called Ornithopter Zone that allows people to buy kits and use them to create their own aircraft. At the workshop, he will do a slideshow presentation and live demonstration of the aircraft. "The workshop will be attended by 60 people in two slots," says Shah, adding some students could build their own ornithopters and fly them.

Chronister's flying demonstration will feature a 110 scale model of a practical flapping-wing aircraft that he has envisioned for personal transport, which, if it ever comes to be used, will use much lesser amount of fuel. He has also authored Ornithopter Design Manual, a book which is used by hobbyists around the world.

Though there have been some successful manned-ornithopter flights previously, still it continues to be a major interest among people interested in such aircrafts. K Nandakumar from Chennai developed a remote-controlled ornithopter of original design in 2004, which was believed to be the first in India. The micro air vehicle or MAV variant of ornithopters can carry cameras that are controlled through radio.

Also at Zephyr: Daniel Raymer and Tessy Thomas
American aerospace design engineer Daniel Raymer and Tessy Thomas, associate project director of the Agni-III missile, will also be at the festival this year, sharing their experiences with the students. Raymer, who is president of the design and consulting company, Conceptual Research Corporation, has helped design the F-22, B-2, and T-45 bombers.  Raymer would be talking about the projects he has headed and the importance of innovation. Thomas, also known as the 'Missile Woman of India', would be talking about her work as the project director of the upgraded 3000-km range Agni-III. An expert on solid propellant systems, Thomas is one among a team of 200 women working on the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO).

Heading: Andheri reservation centre to be demolished - Indian Express
Content:
Gangster-turned-politician Arun Gawli has sought bail in the Kamlakar Jamsandekar murder case on the ground that the cases cited by the police to invoke the stringent Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) against him were all "personal disputes" and do not amount to activities carried out by an organized crime syndicate.

In a 200-page application, Gawli claimed that the police cited four criminal cases registered against him to invoke MCOCA of which two were property disputes that had been settled. A third case related to assault on a journalist which does not come under Section 307 of the IPC (attempt to murder) and was again a "personal dispute", he claimed.

Gawli's application said that the other accused in the murder case were picked up by the police in April 2008 from a hotel in Kalbadevi, which had been closed for over a year and half. In the bail application, Gawli has challenged the authenticity of the arrests.

Heading: Kasliwal case: State to file reply on steps taken to trace victim - Indian Express
Content:
Other offices on platform 1 of the station will also be demolished, a new building will house these

To make way for the additional line to extend the Harbour line services from Andheri to Goregaon, the Western Railway is planning to demolish some offices including the reservation centre on platform no 1 on Andheri station.

A new building would come up at the Andheri station to house the demolished offices except the reservation centre.

According to the WR officials, the reservation centre would be constructed at a suitable location in Andheri (W).

NC Sinha, Chief Claims Manager, Western Railway, said, "Tenders for the construction of a new building will be finalised this month. The estimated cost of this building would be around Rs 6.5 crore. When the new building would be ready, work of dismantling offices and reservation centre would start."

When asked about the deadline for the new building, Sinha said, "At present I cannot comment on the deadline but it would take more than a year."

An official at Mumbai Rail Vikas Corporation Ltd.(MRVC) said, "New reservation centre would be constructed in Andheri (W) for the convenience of the commuters."

The proposal for extending Harbour line from Andheri to Goregaon was sanctioned in the 2007-2008 budget.

At present, local trains coming from Chatrapati Shivagi Terminal or Navi Mumbai terminate at Andheri station. however,after the extension, the commuters from CST or Navi Mumbai would be able to travel directly to Goregaon PC Sehgal, managing director of MRVC, said, "We are planning to start the work by this December which would be completed in 18 months." With this work, modification of structure at Andheri station will also be done.In place of station offices at platform, track will be laid for the new line.

In Goregaon, two more platforms will be constructed."This entire project will cost Rs 100 crore," Sehgal added.

Heading: Doctors on one-day token strike tomorrow over ‘safety concerns’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court has directed the state government to file a reply regarding the efforts taken to trace the complainant/victim who was allegedly reaped by Abhishek Kasliwal.

Abhishek Kasliwal, accused in the alleged rape of a 52-year-old woman, last week had moved a fresh application before the Bombay High Court seeking relaxation of conditions so that he can come back to Mumbai.

Justice D B Bhosale on Wednesday asked the state to file an affidavit regarding the status of the trial and also what efforts they had made in the past to trace the woman who was supposed to be given protection by the police based on HC directions last year.

Justice Bhosale has also sought copy of the Police Commissioner's report regarding the efforts made to trace the woman which has been filed before the trial court.

Kasliwal, who is in Delhi following court directions, has sought for coming to Mumbai as his work is getting affected and the trial is still pending.

Kasliwal, son of Shree Ram mill and S Kumar's brand owner Ambhuj Kasliwal, contends that there has been no progress in the trial even after the lapse of one year. According to his advocate Shamsher Garud, summonses have been issued to the witnesses and the trial is expected to resume in November.

Kasliwal contends that he has been away from his family and his business venture is getting affected and he has not been able to assist his father in the same.

Kasliwal was arrested on March 12 in 2006 for alleged rape. He got bail in April and was directed to stay in New Delhi and his entry into Mumbai was restricted to avoid any manipulation of evidence. At the time of granting bail on a bond of Rs 50,000, the court had orally observed that in such cases sex with consent was a possibility.

In March 2008, the police was reprimanded by the City Civil and Sessions Court after the court was informed that 52-year-old victim has gone missing and could not be served with the summons to be produced before the court to record her evidence. This happened in spite of a High Court direction in April 2006 that had directed the police to provide protection to the victim until the trial is over.

The trial court, last month, issued notice to the Commissioner of Police seeking a reply regarding the status of the missing victim.

According to the prosecution on March 11, 2006, Kasliwal had offered the victim a lift in his car from Colaba and then allegedly raped her. The victim had lodged a complaint with the police and Kasliwal was arrested and after spending over a month in prison, Kasliwal was granted bail by HC on April 18,2006 on the condition that he would not enter city limits until the trial is over.

Heading: Return Bhosale’s passport: High Court directs DoE - Indian Express
Content:
Doctors across the state will observe a token strike on Friday to protest the "state government's apathy" towards their security concerns. As many as four attacks have taken place in the last two weeks in Malad and Chembur areas of Mumbai and at Beed and Akola in Maharashtra. The outpatient department will not function and doctors will only handle emergencies.

Doctors from IMA, General Physicians Association, Association of surgeons, Association of Consultants, docotrs practising Ayurveda, Homeopathy and Unani will take out a silent march from the Government Dental College to the Collector's office.

Two weeks ago, MNS activists attacked two doctors in Malad after a surgical mop that was left in the abdomen of a woman who was operated upon at a hospital. "A couple of days ago, doctors at Shree Hospital in Chembur were threatened after a patient died within 24 hours of being admitted. Also, there have been reports of assaults in places such as Beed, Amravati and Wanori in the past couple of weeks," said Dr Vijay Panjabi, ex-president, IMA.

"Despite several requests, there has been no move to introduce the promised legislation making assaults on doctors a non-bailable offence. Our demand is to pass the bill along with approval Rs 50,000 fine to the offenders," said Dr Panjabi. He added, "Last December deputy chief minister RR Patil assured us that the ordinance will come in 15 days, its been eight months now yet no law is in place. We revisited him soon after the Malad incident. He gave us a spoken assurance that the bill will come through in next assembly meeting."

Heading: Priority Dispatch: New system to provide telephonic aid to pregnant women - Indian Express
Content:
In a significant relief to Pune businessman Avinash Bhosale, the Bombay High Court has directed the Directorate of Enforcement to return his passport within 15 days provided he fulfils certain conditions.

A division bench headed by Chief Justice Swatanter Kumar has directed Bhosale to furnish statements of all his bank accounts with details of transaction within one week. The court has also directed Bhosale to give an undertaking for cooperating with the investigating agency and also give an authorization letter for securing information from all his accounts.
