Pandit XI 259 for 9 decl. (Rahul Lad 48, Abhishek Raut 52, Tejas Kalyankar 72, Sagar Mule 26, Ravishankar Singh 25 n.o.; Pratik Kar 3-21, Siddarth Chitnis 3-46) vs Vengsarkar XI 70 for 4 (Sagar Pawar 22).

Heading: Krishnai on top - Indian Express
Content:
Get the better of Mumbai Police 35-14 in semi-finals

Air-india booked their place in the finals of the Rajaram Sheth Lad Gold Cup in the Shivneri Sewa Mandal-URL Foundation Kabaddi Festival at the Bhavanimata Kreedangan, Dadar on Thursday.

The airmen proved too strong for Mumbai Police and beat them 35-14 in the first semifinal of the day. They now take on an equally strong Western Railway outfit, who won a closely-contested semifinal against sworn rival Central Railway 25-22.

Air-India aided by Gaurav Shetty and Dinesh Kumar both Asian Games'heroes, proved too much for the city cops. With nothing going right for them the policemen were down 7-16 at the interval with defeat staring at them.

The story was no different thereafter and only some lax play to avoid getting hurt by Air-India gave some semblance to the Police score.

Meanwhile, Central went ahead 10-8 at half time after a nerve wracking first half in which the lead kept changing hands. The clash between the two railway outfits was slow-paced with safety-first measures being employed. The pace picked up after Western aided by raider Kunal Yadav gave a "lona"to their rivals to establish a substantial 17-12 lead.

But the joy was short lived as Naresh Kumar, Central's mainstay in attack accounted for three rivals in one raid. He got one more point to restore parity at 17-17. He then needlessly got out which enabled Western to surge ahead 20-17. Western then trapped rival Arun Patil to put a spanner in their opponent's designs.

Arun and Naresh came back after they were revived. But their final fling raised the tempo and brought their side close at 21-22. With another slip, as Naresh got out caught with only three rivals on court, Central's challenge was over.

Hemant Radke got two points in a raid that ensured Western's win. The others who shone for Western were Ravi Radke, Viabhav Kale and Sainath Kalsekr the corner-man who came up with timely catches.

The Mohan Naik Cup for Division 'A'teams will see favourites Rashtriya Chemicals and Fertilizers (RCF) take on Mahavitaran in the summit clash. RCF swept aside Mumbai Fire Brigade 27-9, while Mahavitaran lived dangerously before turning the tables on Mumbai Postal 28-24. Mahavitaran made a splendid recovery after being down 10-17 at the halfway stage.

Mahavitaran were at the receiving end right through till they found a solution to check the marauding Ranjit Devalkar from the Postal outfit.

The veteran heavyweight was unstoppable till he was trapped with the score at 19-19. Once Mahavitaran went up 21-19, they closed ranks and garnered points through Prashant Bhuwad and Kiran Devadign to seal a good win.

Heading: Out of character - Indian Express
Content:
Himesh Reshammiya got a sexy hairstyle, shaved his chest and got into shape for Karzzz. Still, he can't seem to comprehend why a classic hero must be Adonis-like

Himesh Reshammiya knows that he can never be like Clark Gable or James Dean. He maintains that he isn't an archetypal Hindi film hero, nor can he ever be. This, despite the fact that his second film, Karzzz, is releasing on October 17 with a phenomenal 1,200 prints, there are queues of people waiting to interview him and his film's music is already a sell-out success. "The first criterion of becoming a hero is that you have to be good-looking. That, in itself, disqualifies me," he says.

We aren't going to deliberate on what he looked like earlier, but now, he's got himself a cool new hairstyle, shaved his chest hair and gotten into shape. "You have no idea how tough it has been. I had to go on a strict diet (I didn't work out at all), undergo hair transplant, wear extensions... it was crazy. And still people accuse me of trying to emulate Rishi Kapoor. He is one of the most effortlessly handsome faces of his time. However, I believe that Karzzz is a tribute to Rishi Kapoor from an ardent fan."

With Karzzz, the flashbulbs will be trained on Reshammiya, the actor. "In that sense, Karzzz is my real acting debut. My acting skills will be put to test on October 17. We're treading rather carefully. Bhushan Kumar has spent lots of money to make this film. After careful consideration, we brought the release date forward from December and work is going on at breakneck speed. We're getting ready for the verdict." It's true. Although the 35-year-old has been accepted as entertainer par excellence, he is yet to set the big screen ablaze with histrionics. "This is my attempt to win over my critics," he resolves.

In a creative outburst, he composed the music for Tandoori Nights over a meal of grilled chicken. "I was getting too frustrated controlling my diet, eating boiled, bland and grilled meals. That has found expression in Tandoori Nights. It's doing so well now."

Although Karz, the 1980 original, won Laxmikant- Pyarelal awards, Reshammiya has a feeling that his music may not quite bring home the coveted trophy. "I don't know why I am saying that. I just have a feeling. Anyway, I made Pyarelalji listen to my rendition of Ek Hasina Thi. He loved it. And FYI, I have abandoned my nasal twang in this one, I've sung it normally."

Reshammiya's date book looks quite scribbled in. "I am doing five films, and they are all in the big-budget category. Then, I'm making music for others. I intend to take it easy on films for fear of over-exposure," he says.

Clearly, Reshammiya is the most famous package to come out of Gujarat. He says, "I am a good Gujju boy at home. I refrain from talking about my family because they are media-shy. They are happy being in the background. My 10-year-old, Swayam, is my biggest fan and critic. He's going to give me feedback on Karzzz tonight. You also pray for me, okay?" Okay.

Heading: FACE TO FACE with Anjana Sukhani - Indian Express
Content:
Sharman Joshi has whooped it up in the comedy genre. He now wants to try out a variety of roles

If there is one actor who will never undermine the significance of multi-starrers, it is Sharman Joshi. After playing the role of the affable Sukhi in Rang De Basanti, and the over-ambitious Rahul in Life in a Metro, he now plays Shyam Varma, a call centre employee in Hello. Joshi who has worked with industry bigwigs right from his debut film Godmother, is gung-ho about sharing screen space with some of Bollywood's best yet again, that include Salman Khan and Katrina Kaif.

"With Hello, I have achieved two things: the opportunity to work with a bunch of talented actors and a chance to do a role based on a fictional character. Moreover, Atul (Agnihotri, the director) has taken care to see that everyone has equal screen space," he vouches.

The movie, based on Chetan Bhagat's bestseller, One Night @ the Call Centre, had the entire cast posted at a call centre for a

30-day period. "I read the book a couple of times and then got used to the workings of a call centre. To convert a 300-page book into a 30-page script is a difficult job and there are definitely going to be comparisons with the character in the book," says the 34-year-old actor, who is up for the challenge.

Although Joshi has been considered a versatile actor and a powerhouse performer, he still has to prove his mettle at the box office through a solo hit. But for this cheerful actor, it seems, personal achievement coexists with the movie's success. "All films are multi-starrers in that sense. A single person cannot make a successful film. It is the effort and hard work of many involved."

Joshi, who started off his stint almost a decade ago, comes from a family of distinguished theatre actors. "Both my father and uncle are from the theatre fraternity. And I'd happily return to my theatre roots whenever my film career ceases to satisfy me. At the moment, films are an uplifting experience and I'm totally into them." After playing Shabana Azmi's truant son in Godmother, it was an avalanche of comedies that followed. But he doesn't want to be stereotyped as a comedian. "I am not averse to comedies. Right now, my priority is a good script — it could be of any genre. You get the same offers sometimes but then you have to wait for the right time. If something that I am looking for doesn't come my way, I am okay with just chilling at home."

Clearly, Joshi's date diary looks occupied for the year. Onir's Sorry Bhai and Raqeeb are ready for release and he has begun shooting for 3 Idiots. But at the moment, it is Hello that he hopes will see huge success. "The book had more than 10 million readers. With the movie, we hope to cross that mark," he says, ambitiously.

Heading: Very filmy - Indian Express
Content:
What's on your iPod?
Nothing, because at the moment, my iPod is non-functional.

What's your DVD pick?
I just bought The Bourne Ultimatum; I'm a huge fan of Matt Damon.

Your favourite romantic scene in a movie?
I recently watched P.S.I Love You, and I think that whole movie is so romantic. The whole idea of a man who knows he's dying and wants his wife to get over him soon; I find that very touching.

Which actor would you love to go on a date with and why?
Shah Rukh Khan, because he's so witty and has an amazing sense of humour.

Which dialogue have you mouthed in front of the mirror the most?
I've watched Maine Pyar Kiya more than 45 times, and there are two-three memorable scenes in the movie which I've enacted innumerable times, especially the one where Bhagyashree goes to Salman Khan and says, "Dekho to, mere haathon ki mehendi kaisi lag rahi hai?"

Who inspired you to become an actor?
Nobody inspired me in the beginning. But once I got here, I decided to stick around. But if you ask me who is inspiring me right now, I'd say it's Priyanka Chopra and Kareena Kapoor.

The worst film you ever watched?
Jawaani Deewani. Watching that movie was such torture.

Which film you wish you could be a part of?
Zubeida. I loved that movie. If I were in love, I'd be exactly like Zubeida, where her man becomes the centre of her world.

What makes you an actor?
There's an inbuilt something that makes someone an actor. It isn't enough to want to be one. You have to have the talent as well.

Quiz: From which film is this line: Michael ko maut se dar nahi lagta, maut ko Michael se dar lagta hai. Is liye aane mein der lag rahi hai.
I don't know, but it sounds like a Mithun Chakraborty or Amitabh Bachchan movie.
(Correct answer is Majboor)

Heading: Metro Line 3 faces obstacles in planning stage itself - Indian Express
Content:
Mirror image
Imran Khan is not only following in uncle Aamir's footsteps but he also seems to have donned the same pair of shoes — the similarities just don't seem to end. The lad has been on his toes ever since the release of Kidnap. He has been travelling across the length and breadth of the country in attempt to salvage his film Kidnap. Says Dhilin Mehta, producer from Shree Ashtavinayak Cine Vision, "Imran, like Aamir, believes in doing everything with sincerity and gives his 100 per cent to whatever he does. He was very cooperative and would turn up for all promotional events on time despite his overnight rise to stardom." It won't be long before Imran's mirror has Aamir mamu staring back at him.

Diamonds and baubles
KIM Sharma says that New York is her favourite shopping destination as it houses all international brands. The actress, who's of late only visible at social dos, says that she makes frequent trips to the Big Apple and usually shops at Bloomingdales and Canal Street for clothes and Clay Pot for her sparkling diamonds. But all we wish to know, darling, is: where is all the money coming from?

South speak
ARJAN Bajwa is working hard to impress the South Indian audiences. The model-turned-actor has signed three South Indian films and is now learning martial arts. "The directors down South do not like to use body doubles — the actors are expected to do their own stunts," he explains. Bajwa will star alongside Nagarjuna, NT Ramarao's son Balakrishnan and South superstar Mohan Babu in his forthcoming projects. The actor is also learning the local languages, which seems to be the most difficult task. "Ask me to jump from a 50-storey building; I would find it easier than learning Telegu," he laughs.

Heading: ‘If you didn’t love me a lot, you wouldn’t have killed him’ - Indian Express
Content:
While Line 2 awaits Centre's nod, third corridor faces issues like locating plot for car shed and environmental concerns

Even as the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA), the nodal agency for the Mumbai Metro Rail project, struggles to decide on a model for implementation of the third corridor, obstacles in executing this underground route are gradually beginning to surface.

The MMRDA, which is currently awaiting written communication from the Centre to kick-start work on the second Metro rail route — Charkop-Bandra-Mankhurd— in the city, is now faced with a series of challenges on the third metro corridor between Colaba and Mahim in the planning stage itself. It includes issues like locating the plot for car shed and environmental concerns. "There are many ifs and buts in the third corridor. The Colaba-Mahim route has many issues like a car depot land and environmental issues as there would be huge quantity of debris and muck coming out as we need to go around 50 meters deep for the corridor...where and how to dump this waste, etc," said Ratnakar Gaikwad, Metropolitan Commissioner.

Since the third corridor requires a huge viability gap funding (VGF) of around Rs 9,000 crore, the execution has become quite a task for the MMRDA officials, sources said. "Colaba-Mahim is heavily dependent upon the VGF from financial institution like Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC) on minimal interest rates, regardless of the model taken up for implementation," Gaikwad said.

He added that currently the MMRDA is focusing on starting the work on the second corridor, which is behind the schedule by nearly two years due to the Public Private Partnership (PPP)-DMRC model debate. "There are arguments for and against the PPP and the government-funded models," Gaikwad said, adding that since the Centre could not fund 20 per cent VGF for adopting the model like the Delhi Metro, the MMRDA had to go back on the PPP model for the second route.

Meanwhile, the debate sparked by DMRC chief E Sreedharan regarding a government-funded model for Metro rail projects has had little impact on the think-tank within the Maharashtra government. "The government-funded model is actually a good model, but funds from the Centre are an issue. We're studying the possibility of using land as a resource to fund the remaining Metro corridors that can be done without Government of India's funds," Gaikwad said.

However, the first private player led by Reliance Infra to build the Versova-Andheri-Ghatkopar corridor pointed out that the first route of Delhi Metro, which is on a government-funded model, took five years to complete despite DMRC chief's claims that the first Metro Line, Mumbai Metro One, is progressing at a slow pace. "Despite challenges, Mumbai Metro One Pvt Ltd (MMOPL) is geared up to complete the Line 1 project in three years' time against the concession requirements of five years. Incidentally, DMRC took five years to complete their first section in year 2002," stated K P Maheshwari, Director, MMOPL.

According to Maheshwari, Metro rail construction in Mumbai is challenging given the congested roads and issue of utilities. "Mumbai city, commercial capital of the country, is different from other cities like Delhi, Chennai on various considerations. The road area in the city is approximately seven per cent against 25 per cent in Delhi. All the roads are heavily packed with various utilities like water, sewer, gas, power, telecom lines. The construction work is to be carried out in narrow roads in close vicinity of residential and commercial buildings. The construction activities are to be coordinated with multiple civic agencies. All this put together makes the construction work a big challenge in design and construction and hence not directly comparable to Delhi," Maheshwari said.

Heading: Nose-wheel falls off, plane makes emergency landing - Indian Express
Content:
From calling herself his wife to begging for Emile's forgiveness, Mariah Monica Susairaj's letter to her fiancé is an emotional, urgent missive. Excerpts:

 

On her new version of events on the night of May 6
Dear, I was just going through one case law about self defence. Darling what if I say that night when I was talking to you, I told you he is acting funny and my phone put off and you got worried, called him on his phone then he never let you speak to me properly. And cut the phone. You panicked and left Cochin.
He, after he spoke to his friends, forced me physically and tried to rape me by threatening me with a knife. When he kept the knife aside, I took it and in self defence panicked and stabbed him. I pushed him, locked the door and  locked myself in the bathroom outside. He shouted for a bit and after that I don't know what happened since I stayed in the bathroom when the doorbell rang several times in the morning, I came out scared and saw it was you. So I opened the door and told you what happened and when you went to that room, you saw him dead. So, to save me, to save your wife, you helped destroy the body.
...My head and chest hurt a lot when I have to say or think or write that I was the one who killed him. But this way, we can both save our lives and I am ready for this darling.

 

On coping in jail
I am in a bad state today here, high fever, cold, throat pain, chest pain also. By god's grace I will be fine. I read the papers today.. these paper people don't have anything else to do.
...I am okay darling. You yourself got to see how I am doing. Seems like it doesn't matter to you or bother you any more... I fought with canteen person so he stopped giving me mineral water. I drank tap water one day and have got fever and bad cold. I think it's time I should adjust. God is there I am confident he will take care of me.

 

On their meeting in court
You were looking rather cute ummwaah. Am not sure if we can talk to each other like this or not, but what do I do with this love. I will say it again, I will not leave you ever my baby. Darling why were you rude to my family when you spoke to them? Please let me know before Wednesday if my family can meet you during the mulakaath.
(Later, at the end of the letter, she refers to their meeting once again)
When I did not come to court last time, you wrote "I was not feeling good at all" "why did you not turn up?" "I panicked" "Thank god you're alright"  "I turned up smartly, the husband was waiting". But when I came to court ? !!! No love at all :-( just anger. You didn't even ask how are you Monu? :-( You didn't say love you wife, miss you wife. Huh.

 

On why he should forgive her
I know you're angry because I did not listen to you and because I lied, who understands you better than me? Forgive me once darling. In (Matt 18: 22) Jesus said: "I say not unto thee until seven times, but I until 70 times seven". Will you not forgive me? Have I not forgiven you for all your lies, darling? I told you each and everything... now darling put yourself in my place and view this for once. Even after you being fickle-mind from one year, what did I do? I stayed your wife. You lied to me so much, but I was still very loving and caring. Now don't tell me small sin and big sin. Sin is a sin. If you did not lie to me, I would not have lied to you darling. And if I hadn't lied, you wouldn't have killed him.
...I'm still scared of you. I feel scared when I recall all that you told me after showing the knife. But I know that that anger is because of me. I also know that you need me. Why do I still love you so much after having seen your wild face? Because you are my husband. Please understand. Please give me some love at this point in time.
... However, I know if you didn't love me a lot, you wouldn't have killed him. I know you love me darling. I know whatever you did was for me. I believe you will not desert me. The rest is left in God's hands and in your hands.

What their lawyers say

"I am not aware of such a letter. On the last court date, October 1, when I spoke to Mariah she did not tell me anything about it. If Mariah has actually written the letter then it might be an attempt by her to clear up the doubts which would have been created in Emile's mind after the confession given by her. But since I don't know the exact details it would be premature to comment. If what you are saying about her retracting her confession in court is true, it cannot stand, as a lot of time has passed and now the case has to be fought on merits in court."
— G S Kunnur, Susairaj's lawyer

"I cannot comment as I don't have the letter and whenever Emile has met me, we have mostly discussed the case. His personal life is never discussed. If what you are saying is true, it shows how sharp a mind Mariah has, first she confesses and puts the entire blame on Emile and now after her realisation that she won't go scot-free she is turning to such tricks. Emile has read her earlier confession which is part of the chargesheet but he never shows his emotions. Overall, he is a level-headed person. We are in the process of building our defence. All these developments should not affect it."
— Raja Thakur, Emile's lawyer

Heading: ‘Voice is like the most jealous woman in the world’  - Indian Express
Content:
A Delhi-bound Go Air flight with 117 passengers on board made an emergency landing at New Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGI) on Thursday afternoon after the aircraft developed a technical snag in its landing gear. All 123 on board, including six-member crew, were safe.

According to officials at Mumbai airport, one of the two nose-wheels of the plane came off when it was taking off. It was the bird watchers at the airport who first saw the nose-wheel fall from the plane, they said. "Our safety officers and bird scarers played a crucial role in alerting the Air Traffic Control and airline officials in time so that necessary action could be taken," a spokesperson of the Mumbai International Airport Limited (MIAL) said.

An airline official later said in Delhi: "The pilot noticed the problem mid-air and immediately informed the ATC. After consultation with both Mumbai and Delhi airports, it was decided that emergency landing conditions would have to be put in place."

Accordingly, all arrangements — fire brigades, ambulances and other essential services — were made at the Delhi airport. The aircraft was asked to undertake a low-fly past as Delhi International Airport Limited (DIAL) and Go Air engineers studied the damage from the runway.

Passengers on board the flight were informed of the situation by the crew. "As we were nearing Delhi, the captain announced that we will be landing in emergency conditions. Passengers in the first 11 rows were told to move towards the back for safety reasons," said Praveen Jain, one of the passengers. Calling the experience "harrowing", Jain said the captain's calm reassurances ensured there was no panic on the aircraft. "Everyone was scared but there was no panic, just an uncanny silence," he said. The passengers said the emergency procedure took a little over an hour.

Go Air officials said it was a brand new aircraft which had been delivered only in November 2007.

According to a senior airport official, it was Captain Hardeep Singh's expertise that saved the lives of so many people.

"The reasons for the technical problem will be investigated in cooperation with the agencies involved and the manufacturers," said a Go Air spokesperson. Airbus, the manufacturers, too, issued a statement that said: "Airbus will give all necessary support to the airlines and the authorities."

Heading: Police launch drive to nab thieves who pose as cops - Indian Express
Content:
World famous tenor Placido Domingo, set to perform at Brabourne as part of Mehli Mehta Centenary Concert series, says he's nervous about it

We'll have to end the concert by 10 pm," says conductor Zubin Mehta, "Apparently, there is supposed to be no noise after 10 and, these days, we're classified as noise. But there is no more beautiful noise than Placido Domingo."

The renowned tenor himself demurs and adds to the joke, "We'll just have to sing faster, if we want to cover the whole programme."

Domingo is set to perform at the Brabourne Stadium, Churchgate, as part of the Mehli Mehta Centenary Concert series on October 11 and the handsome tenor, is visibly excited. "It is a great feeling to be here in Mumbai, though this is my first time in India."

Domingo, 67, speaks of his connection with the Mehta family and how honoured he is to be performing at the concert for them. "I didn't hesitate when Zubin asked me to come," he says. "Many people may have heard my records, but this is the first time people in India will be hearing me live. So I am a little nervous about it," he says with disarming modesty.

Domingo, a multiple Grammy winning singer and conductor, has even greater recognition outside of the world of opera. He is one of the famous The Three Tenors, along with Jose Carreras and Luciano Pavarotti, and has performed at several FIFA World Cups and even the recent Beijing Olympics. He has lent the drama and passion in his range to the most famous compositions by Verdi (Otello, La Traviata), Puccini (Tosca, Madama Butterfly), Wagner (Parsifal) and Tchaikovsky (Eugene Onegin), among scores of others.

Mehta is all praise for his long-time colleague and friend for his ability to juggle many roles. "Not many people are aware that Placido is not just a singer and conductor. He's also the music director and the guiding spirit of two opera companies in America. I don't know how he does it. He's also one of the few Latin singers to perform Tchaikovsky's operas in Russian, and that too very fluently."

Domingo says he finds singing to be most challenging. "When I'm conducting, I'm more relaxed because I know I have to lead everybody. But while singing I'm always trembling. The voice is like the most jealous woman in the world. You have to take care of her, pamper her. Every morning I wake up and I ask myself, is my voice still there?"

Domingo is more reticent while talking about his favourite performance to date. "It is so difficult to say. I've had close to 3,500 performances and there have been so many special evenings," he says. "Emotionally, you change over time. So what's happening today feels more special."

Heading: State to get memory clinics to aid elderly patients - Indian Express
Content:
There're over 224 such offenders in the city and they're on the police record for committing such crimes earlier, say police

An increasing number of cheating cases in which impostors have robbed elderly women by posing as policemen involved in investigations, and coaxed them to remove their valuables before decamping with them, has now prompted the city police in the central region to track 50 such offenders after receiving tip-off from the Modus Operandi Bureau of the police.

"Such crimes fall in various categories. Some offenders pretend to be police personnel and tell the victims to remove their ornaments and keep them 'safely inside their bag' during a nakabandi or there is a huge crowd. Some take advantage of the women's greed and tell them that a wealthy 'seth' is distributing valuables to needy and won't give her any, if he sees her valuables. There are over 224 such offenders in the city and they are on the police record for committing such crimes earlier," said Assistant Police Inspector Sadanand Lohar, detection officer, Shahunagar police station.

A few police officials on condition of anonymity said that some police stations in the Central region had received a list of the names and addresses of 50 accused.

The detection branch of the Shahunagar police station received a list of 50 names a few days ago. "Our officials will be visiting the accused's addresses mentioned in the list to ascertain their present status. After tracking the whereabouts of the accused, we will be contacting the complainants in such cases to facilitate identification," said Lohar.

Assistant Police Inspector Suresh Yadav who leads the detection branch in Dharavi police station will also be sending his men after the Dussehra bandobast. "Many such crimes were not registered in Dharavi area as these victims are usually middle-class women rather than slum dwellers. Moreover, the list comprises addresses of the accused from across the city and we will be sending our officials to all these given addresses," said Yadav.

The Kurla police who will also be investigating another set of 50 names registered such a cheating cases in August. "The complainant Rukminibai Sonawane was walking on the street wearing some gold ornaments when she met the accused. He warned her that she would be fined for wearing so many ornaments. She had removed the ornaments and the thief fled the spot soon. Last year, we nabbed one Govind Kale who had committed 15 such crimes. We will be tracking more of such 'bol bachan' cheats," said B Jadhav, Police Inspector (Crime), Kurla Police station.

Additional Commissioner of police (Central region) Sadanand Date denied that such a 'drive' had been kick started. He also stressed that all cheating cases were thoroughly dealt with the police.

Heading: Passport snatching: Probe leads police to major job fraud - Indian Express
Content:
While mental health is largely associated with adolescence, with the rapid rise in senior population across the country, governments have recently acknowledged geriatric mental health as a public issue. As World Mental Health day is observed on Friday, it appears that the mental recession of the elderly is finally getting attention across Maharashtra. 

 Of late the city has seen an increase in the number of memory clinics and slowly these are reaching across to tier two cities and rural Maharashtra. In less than a month, Thane's civil hospital and mental health hospital will have full-fledged memory clinics. "Currently both the hospitals are only screening patients for mental illnesses. There are vacant posts for clinical psychologists as soon as they are filled, both the hospitals will start memory clinics," said Dr Sanjay Kumawat, consultant to the state mental health authority.

Memory clinics help screening for dementia, counsel relatives of patients, help patients recall past events and provide them with techniques to recall things by giving them memory cards. They also provide them with proper medication for certain behavioural problems that may occur in geriatric patients.

The state's first mental health hospital and research center dedicated solely to geriatric mental health care will start at Ambajogai in Marathwada region. "A seven crore project including 100 beds and fully equipped research center on neurological and psychiatric disorders will soon come up in Ambajogai. The government doctors will run the hospital. The project has recently got cabinet approval," said Dr Kumawat.

"Along with memory clinics, the hospitals with the local police are planning to start a 24 hour helpline in Thane, to help the geriatric patients in cases of abuse or neglect," added Dr Kumawat.

 Among the elderly, the major mental illness is dementia. Among people above 65 years, dementia is seen in 15 to 17 percent of the old population whereas the mild cognitive impairment (new learning affected, also delayed recall) affects five to seven percent of the geriatric population.

 Soon memory clinics will come up in mental hospitals at Ratnagiri, Pune, Nagpur, and Thane. Mumbai's BMC hospitals like B Y L Nair, Sion hospital and D Y Patil hospital in Navi Mumbai are successfully running memory clinics.

 The state is also planning a central institute of ageing at Yerwada mental hospital that will offer post graduation course in geriatric mental health.

Over nine percent of the 13 million people residing in Mumbai are elderly. In case of elderly patients, emphasis is often laid on the physical heath while the mental health is ignored. Because of their age, elders get cut off from the social circle and go into a shell. This sometimes leads to depression which may result in a suicide.

"In this age there is strong determination to suicide," added Dr Kumawat.

Heading: Sufficient motive behind Soumya murder, will crack the case: DCP - Indian Express
Content:
In the case of Balraj Kumar, the victim-complainant on whose statement officers of Sahar police station on September 26 nabbed the airport duty supervisor, Aditya Patole, for tricking Balraj and subsequently disappearing into the airport terminal building with Balraj's passport, officials at the Sahar police station have revealed that they have zeroed in on a major fraud operation that has been functioning since the early 90s.

According to sources, a Mumbai-based operator is the kingpin of a flourishing trade in which innocent people are lured into paying money to the tune of Rs 5 to 6 lakh in return for cushy jobs abroad. In this case, Balraj Kumar, a cook by profession from Hoshiarpur in Punjab, was approached by a Delhi based agent named Parminder Singh and was promised an opportunity to work in the United Kingdom for a payment of Rs 5 lakh.

Sources also revealed that during their interrogation of Patole, the police learned that Singh and another Delhi based agent, Raju Pawar, were working for the Mumbai -based operator. Senior Police Inspector of Sahar police station Dilip Patil confirmed that the investigations are on in this regard and confirmed that the Mumbai operator has been identified as Ajit Jagdish Puri, aged about 40. In the entire nexus, Patole's commission was Rs 15,000 for every passport that he snatched from unsuspecting travellers.

Sources also revealed that even the visa stamp and the Lufthansa flight ticket provided to Balraj by the agents turned out to be fake. Patole had been commissioned to trick Balraj and grab his passport so that he would not be able to enter the terminal building, where his fake visa stamp and ticket could certainly be detected.

"Had Balraj gone inside, then he would have surely been detained by immigration thus making the authorities alert of such a nexus and therefore Patole took his passport before hand," said an officer on condition of anonymity. According to him, Balraj was told by Parminder to meet an airport security officer outside gate 2D of terminal 2 of the Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport (CSIA). "Patole, who was supervising ground handling for a foreign airline then, posed as an airport security officer and met Balraj a little further away from gate 2D, where CCTV cameras were not reachable at 11:30 pm on 26 th  September," said the officer. "After Balraj gave his passport to Patole, the latter disappeared into the terminal building leaving Balraj outside. He searched for Patole till morning when he was intercepted by CISF surveillance personnel and then handed over to us," the officer added.

Senior Police Inspector Dilip Patil said that the police were looking at various angles. "We have formed teams who are looking into the matter," he said.

Heading: Sad end to Durga Puja: 12 feared drowned - Indian Express
Content:
Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) H G S Dhaliwal on Thursday said there was sufficient motive behind television journalist Soumya Vishwanathan's murder and that the police would crack the case soon.

"We are very confident of working out the case. There is sufficient motive behind Soumya's death," Dhaliwal told Newsline. He, however, did not disclose if they were working on any new line. The angles they were probing earlier were road rage, attempted robbery and personal enmity. "Dedicated teams of officers from various units of the South district police are continuously working on the case," the DCP said.

According to the police, the bullet recovered from Soumya's body would not help much in the investigation as it was fired from a .312 bore country-made pistol, which is easily available with criminals.

On giving clean chit to Mudit Jain, owner of a BMW car — broken parts of which were found at the crime spot — Dhaliwal said: "After picking up all the plastic pieces on the one-km stretch of the Nelson Mandela Marg, the crime scene was reconstructed. Later, we called in experts to show them a rearview mirror and ask which car it might belong to. They identified it as a BMW piece. We did all verifications and carried out a mock drill near the murder spot to check the radical span of the car and its velocity impact, and to see how fast it can drive through the bushes."

Dhaliwal said they carried out all scientific measures to verify Jain's involvement in

the crime. "The BMW occupant was found to be innocent," he added.

Police sources said according to the circumstances and what those known to Soumya had to say, the possibility of a personal enmity as a motive behind the murder appeared bleak, though they were not ruling out this angle altogether. The police said local criminals and bad elements were under continuous watch. Though no deadline has been set to solve the case, the South district police claimed to have put its best men on the job.

The sources said all forensic reports were likely to be out latest by Monday.

The police are pinning hopes on the forensic details to crack the case.

A journalist with Headlines Today, 25-year-old Soumya was killed on the Nelson Mandela Marg in Vasant Kunj when she was driving back home in the early hours of September 30. The police had initially received a call about an accident and found Soumya's car smashed against the central verge of the road. A postmortem at AIIMS, however, found a bullet in her right skull. The police had said she was shot from a close range.

Heading: A-320 makes emergency landing at IGI, all safe - Indian Express
Content:
IDOL IMMERSION goes awry Rescue teams manage to recover only one body; incidents reported from Burari and Wazirabad

One person drowned and 11 others, including two minors, are feared dead after they fell in the Yamuna river at two different places while immersing the idol of Goddess Durga on Thursday. The incidents occurred in the Burari and Wazirabad. Rescue operations managed to recover only one body.

At both the places, rescue operations have been called off the operation due to bad light and "high water current".

The police said a team of around 40 people had boarded a Tempo from Gali Number 10 in Anand Parbat area to go to Sonia Vihar Pushta in Burari to immerse the idol.

"There were two streams flowing in the jungle opposite Nirmal Bhawan. The volume of water in one was lower but the group stepped into the stream with more water. This ground was slippery and people started falling over each other," a senior police officer said.

The police said there was panic and all tried to scamper back to the bank. With nine among them missing, a call was made to the Loni (Uttar Pradesh) police, which reached the spot at 3.45 pm. They analysed the situation and asked the nearby fishermen to cast their fishing nets.

After around half an hour, the sub-divisional magistrate arrived with his team. A debate over jurisdiction later, the SDM declared the area to be under the Delhi Police. After getting a call at 5.05 pm, they reached the spot and called the fire department and the Municipal Corporation of Delhi's boat club for rescue operations.

While nine are feared dead, the relatives of only three have approached the police with details.

"The three are Aftab, Asif and Pankaj. No body has been recovered yet," said DCP (North) Sagar Preet Hooda.

The six others are Raj Mann (21), Kanhayya Lal (21), Soni (13), Raju (27), Jitender (22), and Dalip (13).

Nizam Ali, father of one of the victims, said: "My son, Aftab, and nephew, Asif, accompany the groups going for idol immersion every year. In fact I go too, but could not make it today. People are saying my son's body has not been recovered. I don't know what to do."

The rescue operations were called off at 8 pm. Officials said the operations would commence on Friday morning.

In another incident, three boys in their 20s drowned in the Yamuna near Wazirabad on Thursday afternoon. After almost a two-hour rescue operation, divers recovered the body of one Jitender. The other two are feared dead. This operation also has been called off for the day.

Heading: On World Post Day, ‘lady postman’ recalls old days and ways - Indian Express
Content:
Even after adding 568 low-floor buses to its existing fleet of 3,100 buses recently, the Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) is suffering a loss of Rs 6 crore a month. The reason for the DTC's fast declining revenue graph: shortage of drivers.

"With none to drive them, almost 250 buses in the morning and 1,000 in the evening cannot come out of the depots. These buses are proving to be white elephants, missing almost 7,000 trips daily," said a DTC official.

The corporation had sent a demand to the Delhi Subordinate Services Board (DSSB) to arrange for 10,000 drivers. But the board has not been able to provide a single candidate. The deadline fixed for the recruitment was July 2008.

Of the 3,021 ordinary buses (DTC's old fleet), only 2,800 come on the roads in the morning shift. Evenings see only 60 per cent — about 1,800 buses — serving Delhi's commuters.

The situation is worse in case of the new low-floor fleet. While only 50 buses can be run in the mornings, the number dips to half in the evening shift. Insiders say nearly 90 per cent of these buses miss the trips — all due to shortage of drivers.

A DTC official said: "The DSSB was requested to provide eligible drivers as soon as possible and the remaining should be called for tests. The request was rejected and the DSSB said all candidates would be sent at one go. Now, it all depends on the availability of drivers. Even if the process starts now, it will take at least another month for them to join duty."

The Delhi government provides Rs 23 crore a month to the corporation. After the implementation of the Sixth Pay Commission report, this allocation will be enhanced by another Rs 15 crore.

The situation on the Capital's roads is chaotic during peak hours in the absence of required number of buses. What is worrying the government is the fact that the expenditure of DTC is expected to increase substantially in the days to come.

The annual maintenance contract of the buses has been awarded to the manufacturing company. The company will charge its fees on 'per-kilometre' basis, which will require shelling out more money, widening the revenue gap. By 2010, the number of buses will be increased to 11,000, of which DTC will have a share of 60 per cent. With the introduction of new buses, the corporation will be requiring 4,000 drivers to run them.

Heading: And quiet go the festive flames - Indian Express
Content:
It wasn't easy being one of the first postwomen in Delhi in the 1980s. Indrawati Deshwal, now 60, took an early-morning train from Rohtak, where she lived then, sorted the mail, changed into her uniform, and walked miles carrying thousands of letters and packages for people who eagerly awaited the "lady postman" in the Gole Market area.

People even stopped by at the Gole Dak Khana to see her. She was one of the only two postwomen in those days. "It was certainly a big achievement. I was the first one to get a government job in my family," said Deshwal, walking down the memory lane on the World Post Day.

In the last 25 years that she has worked in various capacities — she started out as a postwoman and now works as a stamp vender — Deshwal has enjoyed meeting people, making friends and even "reading faces".

In the old Gole Dak Khana building, once called the Alexandra Place built by the British, Deshwal waited for customers on Thursday, as her children waited for her at home on Dussehra. None came.

With telephone and Internet order of the day, people no longer depend on letters. She misses the old days and the old ways.

When she walked in the gullies in her khaki uniform, with a sack of letters, children would call out her name. All of them recognised her. In time, she formed wonderful friendships. "I even helped labourers write letters. Things have now become too impersonal," she said. Back then, she was often given sweets at the Bangla Sahib Gurdwara. "They were so nice. They used to say 'gudiya dak le ke aa gayi'," Deshwal recalled.

Her career as a postwoman spanned five years. "I don't have any complaint against me. Work always came first." A stamp vender now, Deshwal often does not have time for lunch. But she doesn't mind. "With competition growing, I can't afford to let my department down," she said.

The Gole Dak Khana, too, has changed a little. Amid old, dusty files piled up in the corridors, chairs with worn-out tapestry and fans that make whirring noises, the changes are reflected in the new logo that was unveiled a couple of weeks ago and the range of new services on the offer, including instant and electronic money orders.

N K Pal, who has worked at the post office for 12 years, said the new logo represented speed and change. "It's like an aeroplane. Fast. The old one looked like a ship."

"Everything is computerised now," he said, pointing at the new screens. Till 2002, they used to sort out everything manually, Pal said, adding he was "proud to be a part of the evolution".

But nostalgia hits him from time to time. Earlier, lovers would request them to send letters anonymously. "Those days were so much fun. It's only speed posts or company letters now," he said.

Prakash Dagre, a student, walked into the post office with a little packet. It was official, he said. Dagre prefers emails. "Letters take too long to reach."

For Deshwal, however, letters are a symbol of a bygone era. She has kept all the letters she wrote to her husband. Once in a while, she takes them out and shows them to her grandchildren. "I want them to know how things were back then," she said.

Heading: City bids Durga farewell amid tight security - Indian Express
Content:
Normal turnout for Dussehra

Dussehra celebrations on Thursday saw a maximum crowd come out to see the effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnad being set ablaze. Firecrackers lit up the Delhi sky at sundown, as families watched under heavy police cover. The Ramlilas had seen a smaller turnout for the first nine days following the blasts last month.

Satish Verma, joint military secretary of the Indraprastha Volunteer Board, said more than 80,000 people had come to see the final day of the Ramlila. "Today we saw a normal turnout, a turnout that we have come to expect at the Shri Dharmik Lila grounds. The last few days had seen a sharp drop in footfall." The grounds saw a high security cover as political figures such as Vice President Hamid Ansari, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, Congress President Sonia Gandhi and Lieutenant Governor Tejendra Khanna among others came to see the Dussehra celebrations.

Prabhat Dayal brought his three-year-old son especially to see the Ramlila procession that winds through the Chandni Chowk, Nai Sarak and Sitaram Bazar area before reaching the Ramlila grounds. "The savari is an integral part of the Ramlila experience in Old Delhi," he said. Ramlila tableaux, depicting Ram and Ravana, as well as their armies, were taken through the streets. Chariots with Shiva and other gods are also part of the procession.

The effect of last month's blasts was visible ,with a number of Ramlila committees burning a fourth effigy, that of "terrorists", before those of Meghnad, Kumbhakarna and Ravana.

Heading: Fortress Ambience: Gurgaon mall goes all out to thwart terror threat - Indian Express
Content:
The engorged Yamuna was dwarfed by a sea of people on Thursday. Delhi has more than 300 registered samitis, along with numerous smaller, unregistered ones. And residents, Bengali and otherwise, were out in full force to bid goodbye to the goddess.

At pandals across the city, idols were lifted onto trucks to the sound of dhak (drums), cymbals, bells and pipes, as people threw gulal and sindoor in the air and danced. Several thousand people gathered at each of the ghats opened by the government for the immersions.

At the Okhla Barrage in Kalindi Kunj, people had come from as far as Dwarka and Gurgaon for Bijoya Dashami celebrations. More than 700 samitis gathered at Geeta Ghat near Kashmere Gate.

Pradeep Majumdar, secretary of Chittaranjan Park Kali Mandir Durga Puja Samiti, told Newsline that around 800 idols had been immersed in the Yamuna at Kalindi Kunj till 6.30 pm. "More are still coming," he said, adding that many belonged to unregistered samitis and samitis from various parts of Noida and Ghaziabad. "Around one and a half lakh people gather here on Dashami and the number grows every year," he said.

A crane and a forklift were deployed to help people with the immersion at Kalindi Kunj. At Geeta Ghat, however, people dragged the heavy idols across the sand in dozen-strong teams.

Supriya Basu (54) of Gurgaon, who came to Kalindi Kunj with a busload of neighbours and friends, said security arrangements are better this year.

Security arrangements included volunteers drawn from various samitis and trained by the police to manage crowds and deal with bomb threats. Ananda Mukherjee, chairman of the South Delhi Durga Puja Immersion Committee, said the CR Park police station had trained around 20 volunteers from the area for a week. They were posted all over the Kalindi Kunj and Geeta Ghat areas. At Geeta Ghat, CCTV cameras were also installed to keep a check on the crowd. Jagdish Shah of the Joint Procession Committee said: "We have also hired private security."

Heading: Cabinet Secretariat faces CIC flak for refusal to part with information - Indian Express
Content:
At the Ambience Mall in Gurgaon, state-of-the-art technology is at work to pre-empt all possible security threats.

Interestingly, the mall had to be evacuated because of a hoax call about a bomb recently.

The management claims it spends up to Rs 25 lakh a month on the maintenance of security apparatus that includes CCTV cameras, non-linear junction devices, bomb blankets, fire blankets, a dog squad and trained security personnel.

The management have also obtained permission for a vapour tracer worth Rs 15 lakh, which they say they will purchase soon, Brigadier Deepak Kapur (Retd), general manager of operations, said. "The availability of all these security arrangements is a deterrent in itself. We place security before anything else on our list of priorities," he said.

Dog Squad
The mall employs a sniffer dog squad, with dogs trained to detect explosives. The squad has two full-grown dogs that are cared for by individual keepers. There are two puppies, which are undergoing training, and will soon join the squad. The number will increase to eight, as the management is in talks with the Indian Army for the purchase of trained dogs.

Non-linear junction detectors
These devices are used for inspecting the area under vehicles. Usually, the mirror-mounted device cannot check the entire area under a SUV and they fail during the night because of poor lighting. The detectors have a night-vision camera mounted on a trolley, which can see even in poor light. It also has a monitor that displays the area scanned by the camera and acts as a storage device for future reference.

Bomb blanket
These blankets are made of special material that reduce the effect of a blast by absorbing shrapnel. Once an explosive is detected, the blanket is put on it to minimise its effect. The heavy sheet absorbs the blast.

Fire blankets
These are made of materials that don't catch fire. In case of a fire, security staff can enter the area wrapped in the blanket.

Security personnel
There are 20 trained guards, some of whom carry licensed weapons, keeping a vigil inside the mall. Some personnel are in black uniforms like commandos, while others are in plain clothes so as to mingle with the crowd.

Guards
The mall has 300 guards on duty at all entry and exit points, outside stores in the mall and in the parking areas. They are in uniform.

CCTV cameras
The mall has 100 closed circuit Television cameras that are functional round the clock. Most are pan-tilt-zoom enabled and can zoom comfortably up to a distance of as far as two kilometres. The management is planning on adding another 100 to the existing cameras for better coverage.

Walkie-talkies and PA systems
Specially trained personnel and managers with walkie-talkies maintain a communication network. There are public address system speakers at various points that ensure an even reach-out to the visitors.

In-house medical room
There is a doctor and nurse available for first aid in case of an emergency and the mall has a tie-up with a nearby hospital for ambulance services.

Vapour tracer
The tracer will soon be included in the existing security arrangements. It is helpful in detecting any kind of explosive and even narcotics.
Dustbins within the mall premises are sniffed by the dog squad and are emptied at quick intervals; with surveillance cameras keep a close watch.
When asked whether the police encourage malls and housing complexes to have their own security arrangements, Manjit Singh Ahlawat, joint commissioner of police, Gurgaon, said: "We certainly encourage places that are frequented by people to maintain their own security arrangements. We are always there to supplement them whenever they require it." What all facilities require a no objection from the police? "Maintaining a dog squad, CCTV cameras and security personnel don't require any permission. However, weapons need a licence," Ahlawat said.

Heading: Embassy worker alleges forceful eviction, court throws out case - Indian Express
Content:
The Cabinet Secretariat, the country's top agency for coordination among the ministries of the Government, has been left red in the face after facing flak from the Chief Information Commissioner for a "bald refusal" to part with the promotion details of a Delhi-based senior Law Ministry official.

"We are constrained to observe that the manner of disposal of the application of Ms Sushma Jain by so august a body as the Cabinet Secretariat, expected to be a model for public authorities, is nothing less than flippant," Chief Information Commissioner Wajahat Habibullah observed.

Directing the Secretariat to part with the information sought by Jain within the next 10 days, the CIC said non-communication of performance reports of a civil servant, "whether he is in civil, judicial, police or any other service (other than the military), certainly has civil consequences, as it might affect his chances for promotion or get other benefits. Such non-communication would be arbitrary".

Trouble started for Jain, a resident of Kakardooma, when she moved an RTI application with the ministry for the records of an expert committee which had considered her case for promotion as Additional Secretary in the Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice on August 9, 2006.

The ministry merely passed the buck to the Cabinet Secretariat, a body under the direct charge of the Prime Minister, saying the information she sought was "available only with the Cabinet Secretariat".

Jain was, however, left disappointed when the Cabinet Secretary wrote to her on December 27, 2007, saying the RTI application filed by her lacked "clarity", and so was "incapable of a specific reply".

"Your application is non-specific and lacks clarity in the present form; it is incapable of a specific reply," the top bureaucrat replied.

Worse still, an appeal under the RTI with the Joint Secretary, First Appellate Authority, elicited no response initially, but did so after she moved the Central Information Commission (CIC).

In a letter to Jain, First Appellate Authority Rajiv Kumar dismissed her request by merely echoing the words of the Cabinet Secretary, saying her request did not specify the "nature of records" sought.

"It would appear from the disposal of this application that this is simply a determined effort not to provide Ms Jain the information she seeks, rather than finding ways of providing it, which is in fact the underlying spirit of the RTI Act 2005," the CIC noted on its October 6 verdict.

Habibullah, who heard the case, said the Secretariat should have come clean on whether they had the documents sought or, better so, even parted with those records not exempted from disclosure.

"None of these has been done; instead Ms Jain was provided with a bald refusal," the Bench said.

Heading: Youth held for raping minor - Indian Express
Content:
A city court dismissed a complaint of alleged wrongful evacuation filed by a former worker of the Embassy of Sudan against 14 embassy officials asking for registration of an FIR against them, after a police report found nothing unlawful in the eviction after the employee's services were terminated.

His complaint included the name of an assistant sub-inspector (ASI) of the Chanakyapuri police station, who had helped the officials in their "criminal acts".

Mirza, who was working as an electrician and plumber for the embassy, had moved the court alleging that he was forcefully ousted from the official quarter allotted to him in the embassy premises on August 12.

The long list of charges levelled by him against the embassy personnel and the ASI comprised allegations of criminal trespass, wrongful restraint, criminal intimidation and conspiracy.

He pressed for registration of an FIR and a thorough investigation in the matter so as "to secure justice for a man suppressed by the high and mighty". Metropolitan Magistrate Sanjay Bansal had directed the SHO, Chanakyapuri to look into the allegations and file a report.

On October 4, when the SHO submitted the report, the magistrate was shocked at the falsity of Mirza's statements and his attempt to implicate officials without any fault. The report revealed that Mirza was given a notice to vacate the quarter way back in March, informing him unambiguously that his services had been terminated with effect from December 31, 2007, requiring him to comply with the direction.

He was paid terminal benefits as well and the notice complied with all the conditions of the employment, it maintained.

Regarding the role of ASI Tika Ram, the report stated that when Mirza was refused to give up the possession of the quarter even after five months of receiving the notice, embassy officials had sought assistance from the local police. The evacuation took place in the presence of the officer. "I see nothing wrong in it. The allegations of the complainant seem to be an afterthought," held the magistrate after reading the report in detail.

The court said that Mirza was just a licensee residing in the flat by virtue of his employment and as soon as his services were terminated, he had no legal right to continue living there.

"The embassy, which was the employer, had all rights to oust the complainant from the quarter," noted the court, adding the case would have fallen through even otherwise, as embassy officials enjoy diplomatic immunity from prosecution. Rebuffing Mirza for his wrongful endeavour, the court threw out his complaint saying no cognizance could be taken over his false charges.
